quest:100.text: Call of Water. This ritualistic step marks the culmination of the shaman's ordeal at the Brazier of Everfount along the coast of Silverpine Forest. Having shattered the corrupt spirits threatening the spring with a burst of elemental radiance, the shaman stands before an apparition of pure water to receive its communion. Upon reciting the final incantation at the Brazier of Everfount, an explosion of light scours the area of surrounding corruption. The hissed protests of tainted water drops evaporating over elemental flame fade, leaving the immediate shore silent as malevolent minor spirits disperse. In the wake of the spirits' destruction, a Minor Manifestation of Water materializes beside the brazier. Grateful for the ritual intervention, the spirit recognizes the growing burden placed upon the Horde's shamans: though the local taint has ebbed, life in the decaying lands of Silverpine continues to wane, requiring vigilance to preserve.

quest:1007.text: The Ancient Statuette. Talen, an elf camped near the dangerous Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale, seeks recovery of a lost relic. After being ambushed and run aground by vicious naga, he dropped his prized ancient statuette along the surf and needs an adventurer to retrieve it from the ruins. The sunken ruins of Zoram along Ashenvale's northwestern shoreline have long attracted those curious about the ancient night elven past. Talen was navigating the shallows in a small vessel when hostile naga surfaced and tore into him with claw and trident. He managed to scramble ashore with bare provisions to make a hasty camp, but in his desperate sprint for survival, his most precious find was dropped into the sands. The ancient statuette left half-buried on the beach is more than a simple souvenir. Talen considers it the entire justification for braving the monster-infested Zoram Strand. Upon its recovery, he reveals that the drowned city holds centuries of forgotten mysteries, and this delicate carving acts as a vital key to understanding what remains hidden beneath the tides.

quest:1009.text: Ruuzel. Ruuzel is an Alliance quest offered by Talen on the edges of the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale. After recovering an ancient Kaldorei statuette from the coast, adventurers are sent to wrest the Ring of Zoram from the naga leader Ruuzel to unlock its sealed secrets. Before the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart and cast its grand coastal cities beneath the sea, the city of Zoram was governed by powerful night elven nobility. Chief among their regalia was the Ring of Zoram, which Talen believes is the key to the ancient statuette's lock. Following the cataclysm, the ring was lost to the tides for millennia, preserving the secrets of sunken relics from curious eyes. With the recent arrival of the naga on the Zoram Strand, the serpentine invaders began scouring the ruins of their former homeland. Ruuzel, the matriarch leading the local brood, successfully unearthed the Ring of Zoram and carried it off to her sanctuary on an island to the north. Seeking to unseal the statuette dragged from the shallows, the night elf Talen tasks Alliance travelers with hunting down Ruuzel and reclaiming the ancient heirloom.

quest:101.text: The Totem of Infliction. Madame Eva of Darkshire offers to craft a protective ward known as the Totem of Infliction for travelers passing through the shadowed woods. By harvesting remains from the ghouls, skeletons, and venomous spiders haunting the region, she enchants a charm that retaliates against attackers. The task serves as both a grim test of survival and a superstitious safeguard against the pervasive darkness of Duskwood. Within her candle-lit abode in Darkshire, Madame Eva peers past the veil into the fortunes of those who cross her threshold. Sensing impending danger and violence waiting patiently on the horizon, she offers more than mere divination: practical sorcery. By gathering ten ghoul fangs, ten skeleton fingers, and five vials of spider venom from the haunted thickets, an adventurer supplies the raw materials needed to construct a protective ward against Duskwood's ravenous predators. Ghoul fangs steeped in necrotizing hunger, finger bones wrested from restless dead, and potent arachnid venom are woven together by Madame Eva's enchantments. When grasped in times of mortal peril, the totem radiates a magical aura designed to reflect cruelty, inflicting spiritual and physical harm upon anyone foolish enough to strike its bearer.

quest:1010.text: Bathran's Hair. Bathran's Hair is an Alliance quest offered by Orendil Broadleaf at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Desperate to treat a mysteriously afflicted night elf child whose illness transcends the physical body, Orendil sends adventurers north to scour the ancient ruins of Bathran's Haunt for a restorative plant renowned for mending ailments of the spirit. At Maestra's Post, just south of the Darkshore border, the night elf herbalist Orendil Broadleaf faces a troubling medical crisis. A young child in Astranaar has fallen grievously ill, exhibiting symptoms that resist ordinary physical remedies. Convinced that the sickness plagues the child's spirit rather than merely the flesh, Orendil seeks Bathran's Hair, an uncommon restorative herb historically gathered amidst the ancient elven ruins to the north.

quest:1011.text: Forsaken Diseases. Deep in eastern Ashenvale, the night elf scout Kayneth Stillwind watches the encroaching Forsaken with growing alarm. Believing the undead are brewing blights to ravage sacred elven lands, he directs Alliance champions to raid an encampment near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den and secure a sample of their foul concoctions. The night elves of Ashenvale have long contended with satyrs, raging elementals, and orcish logging crews, but the arrival of the Forsaken marks a darker turn. Rather than merely felling timber, the undead arm of the Horde is establishing footholds near ancient ruins and sacred barrow dens. Their presence brings not only war, but the horrific specter of alchemical plague into pristine Kaldorei groves. South of Forest Song, near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, Forsaken apothecaries and scouts have set up a fortified camp. There, amidst brewing caldrons and foul reagents, they bottle untested toxins. Kayneth Stillwind tasks scouts with infiltrating the camp to retrieve an intact Bottle of Disease so its volatile contents can be analyzed before the Forsaken can unleash it across the forest.

quest:1012.text: Insane Druids. Investigating Forsaken incursions in eastern Ashenvale, Kayneth Stillwind uncovers a tragic massacre deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The resident druids were poisoned and slaughtered in their sleep by undead agents, leaving their maddened spirits trapped in torment. Alliance adventurers are tasked with granting eternal rest to their slain leaders to soothe the agonizing spiritual blight. While battling the effects of virulent Forsaken toxins recovered in eastern Ashenvale, the night elf sentinel Kayneth Stillwind was struck by a terrifying waking vision. Beneath the earthen mounds of the nearby Dor'Danil Barrow Den, he witnessed an atrocity: the druids resting within had been quietly poisoned and slaughtered by undead infiltrators. Rather than passing peacefully into nature's embrace, their souls were severed violently from their flesh, warped by unnatural venom into shrieking, errant specters. Driven mad by the unnatural circumstances of their deaths, the druids' phantoms haunt the subterranean chambers of Dor'Danil, unable to find release. To quiet the echoing anguish beneath the earth, Kayneth bids champions to venture into the depths and strike down the lingering spirits of the circle's three venerable leaders: Taneel Darkwood, Uthil Mooncall, and Mavoris Cloudsbreak. Only by laying these tortured figures to rest can the restless den begin to heal from the defilement.

quest:1013.text: The Book of Ur. The Book of Ur is a mission assigned by Keeper Bel'dugur in the Undercity's Apothecarium. Bel'dugur charges Horde champions with infiltrating Shadowfang Keep to recover the arcane treatise of Ur, a deceased mage of Dalaran. The Forsaken seek Ur's extraplanar research, intending to weaponize magical insights he was too scrupulous to exploit. Before the Third War wiped out Dalaran, a brilliant human wizard named Ur dedicated his scholarship to realms beyond Azeroth. Unlike standard Kirin Tor doctrine, which strictly regulated conjuration and outer planar contacts, Ur cataloged entities from other dimensions, including the savage worgen. Despite his curiosity, Ur ultimately hesitated to manipulate these alien powers, deeming them dangerously uncontrollable. That restraint, however, made his written legacy a coveted prize for those who possess no such moral qualms. Archmage Arugal acquired Ur's treatise and used its research before taking up residence in Shadowfang Keep. Arugal lacked Ur's ethical reservations and used the book's contents to summon bloodthirsty worgen into Silverpine, unleashing a curse that devoured Pyrewood and the surrounding valleys. The volume now rests neglected inside the keep's towers, watched over by Arugal's feral pets.

quest:1014.text: Arugal Must Die. Arugal Must Die is a decisive Horde mission issued by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. It tasks brave champions with storming Shadowfang Keep to slay the rogue archmage Archmage Arugal and claim his severed head. Eliminating Arugal is critical for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner to break the worgen menace and secure Silverpine Forest for the Forsaken. While the Forsaken have carved out a base in the Sepulcher, Silverpine Forest remains treacherous and deeply contested. Perched high upon the cliffs overlooking the woods sits Shadowfang Keep, the lair of Archmage Arugal. Driven mad by guilt and dark sorcery, Arugal unleashed the feral worgen upon Lordaeron. His ravenous beasts roam the forest paths, directly hindering Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's efforts to establish a fortified strategic hold over the region. Dalar Dawnweaver recognizes that merely hunting wandering beasts in the forest will never cleanse the land. The heart of the corruption beats within Shadowfang Keep itself. Horde champions must breach the ancient stronghold, fight through Arugal's devoted worgen brood, and confront the mad wizard in his aerie. Bringing his head back to the Sepulcher finally shatters his magical hold over the region, clearing the way for Forsaken supremacy.

quest:1016.text: Elemental Bracers. Water elementals have begun tainting the pristine lakes and streams of Ashenvale, troubling the night elves stationed at Silverwind Refuge. Sentinel Velene Starstrike tasks travelers with collecting intact bracers from these creatures to divine the identity of the rogue spellcaster responsible for conjuring them. The sacred waters of Ashenvale are suffering under an unnatural blight, overrun by rogue water elementals. Unlike the wild spirits that naturally inhabit the world, these entities bear signs of artificial conjuration. To the Sentinels stationed at Silverwind Refuge, the sudden arrival of hostile elementals is an alarming symptom of outside corruption creeping deeper into the forest's pristine waterways. Believing these elementals were deliberately bound and unleashed, Sentinel Velene Starstrike provides a magical divining scroll to unmask the culprit. The spell requires raw reagents tied to the summoned beings—specifically, intact bracers salvaged from the spirits before they dissipate. By focusing the scroll upon these enchanted bindings, the magic reads the lingering arcane signature of whoever originally called the elementals into being.

quest:1017.text: Mage Summoner. Mage Summoner is an Alliance strike mission directed by Sentinel Velene Starstrike from Silverwind Refuge. After investigating corrupted water elementals near Mystral Lake, the Sentinels dispatch adventurers across the border into the Barrens to execute the undead mage Sarilus Foulborne atop Dreadmist Peak. The night elves rarely send scouts southward into the sun-scorched savannas of the Barrens without dire cause. After investigating unnatural disturbances among the water elementals around Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike traces the meddling directly to Sarilus Foulborne, a Forsaken conjurer practicing his arts just across the border. For the Sentinels guarding Silverwind Refuge, letting an enemy sorcerer defile nature right on their doorstep is intolerable. Sarilus Foulborne has taken up roost high upon Dreadmist Peak, an craggy mountain crawling with Burning Blade cultists. From this elevation, he summons and bends ranks of water elementals to his will, mocking night elf authority from within Horde-dominated lands. Taking him down requires braving enemy territory, cutting through his summoned forces, and severing his head as proof that the Sentinels' vengeance reaches beyond the forest line.

quest:1020.text: Orendil's Cure. Orendil's Cure is an urgent delivery errand tasked to Alliance travelers by the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf. After concocting a remedy from rare flora, Orendil sends the courier racing down the woodland roads to Astranaar to save a dying night elf child. In the central settlement of Astranaar, Pelturas Whitemoon watches over his daughter, Relara, as she wastes away from a severe and mysterious sickness. Facing the limits of local knowledge, Pelturas sought aid across the wild forest of Ashenvale, turning to the wisdom of distant herbalists before hope slipped entirely through his fingers. Having successfully procured the necessary components—specifically Bathran's hair—Orendil Broadleaf brews a specialized draught capable of halting the affliction. Entrusting the fragile cure to a passing adventurer, Orendil directs them south and east along the beaten forest highway to deliver the flask before it is too late.

quest:1021.text: Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger!. Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger! is an urgent Alliance quest begun in Ashenvale by the dryad Illiyana. Desperate for aid, she recruits travelers to search for her missing sisters who ventured into the corrupted ruins of Xavian to recover a stolen sacred relic. While resting in Ashenvale, the dryad Illiyana finds herself overwhelmed with worry. A band of her dryad sisters departed into the corrupted northern reaches of the forest on a perilous mission to recover the Branch of Cenarius, a holy relic stolen by the vile satyrs. Though they promised to return swiftly, two days have passed in silence, prompting Illiyana to plead with passing Alliance travelers to track them down before it is too late.

quest:1022.text: The Howling Vale. Assigned by Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow at the Shrine of Aessina, this quest sends Alliance adventurers into the Howling Vale near the Felwood border. The ruined shrine of Mel'Thandris has been overrun by feral wolf-men known as worgen. By consulting the sacred Tome of Mel'Thandris, investigators hope to uncover why these bizarre creatures have emerged in Ashenvale. While night elf sentinels expend heavy resources holding the line against the demonic corruption spilling out of Felwood, a new threat has quietly nested in the northern hills of Ashenvale. The ruined shrine of Mel'Thandris, hidden beyond a cavern path near the Felwood border, has fallen to ferocious wolf-men whose haunting cries echo across the canopy. The area is now known as the Howling Vale, and Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow fears this beastly infestation may herald another disaster for the woodland realm.

quest:1023.text: Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the tragic continuation of the search for Teronis, a night elf sentinel sent to Lake Falathim. Upon discovering his remains on the shore, the task shifts to recovering his research journal and retrieving the glowing gem held by local murlocs before reporting the grim news back to Astranaar. Sent to Lake Falathim by Raene Wolfrunner, adventurers discover Teronis dead along the waterside. Rather than a rescue, the mission turns into salvage and investigation. Among his belongings lies an intact journal detailing his assignment and findings regarding the strange disturbances in Ashenvale. Teronis had tracked a rare, luminous stone to the lake, which fell into the possession of the aggressive murlocs infesting the shallows. Recovering both Teronis' journal and pryed-away gem is necessary to carry forward the late scout's original mission.

quest:1024.text: Raene's Cleansing. This intermediate step in the investigation of Ashenvale's corruption sends Alliance adventurers deep into the sacred groves east of Iris Lake. Entrusted with a recovered Glowing Gem, you must consult the dryad Shael'dryn to learn how to restore Dartol's ancient rod. Following the tragic death of the sentinel Teronis, Raene Wolfrunner examines the field notes he left behind. His research indicates that investigating Ashenvale's troubled furbolgs may require an ancient artifact: a rod crafted long ago by a night elf named Dartol. With only a Glowing Gem in hand, Raene admits her tactical expertise as a huntress is ill-suited to deciphering lost arcane and natural mysteries. Rather than guessing at the remaining pieces of Dartol's Rod, Raene directs travelers northeast toward Iris Lake. Tucked away beside a tranquil moonwell dwells Shael'dryn, a dryad whose natural communion with the forest grants her deep insight into ancient relics. By delivering the gem to her, adventurers hope to uncover the missing components and learn how to reforge the rod.

quest:1025.text: An Aggressive Defense. An Aggressive Defense is an Alliance quest given by Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar. Faced with rampant furbolg corruption along the central thoroughfares of Ashenvale, the night elves are forced to mount an active cull against the maddened Foulweald tribe. The road running east from Astranaar toward the Falfarren River serves as a vital lifeline through Ashenvale, but it has grown exceedingly dangerous. Furbolgs driven mad by demonic corruption have begun raiding travelers directly off the main trail. Rather than simply manning barricades and waiting for the next ambush, Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner dispatches capable adventurers to break the Foulweald camps located just south of the highway. Striking down the Foulweald furbolgs carries a tragic weight for the night elves. The bear-folk were longtime friends and allies of the kaldorei throughout ancient ages, sharing reverence for nature and the wild gods. However, the lingering taint of the Burning Legion's invasion shattered the minds of many tribes, warping peaceful neighbors into bloodthirsty reavers whose violence threatens innocent travelers.

quest:1026.text: Raene's Cleansing. This quest represents a pivotal step in restoring Dartol's Rod of Transformation, an ancient night elf artifact being sought by Raene Wolfrunner. Guided by Shael'dryn at her moonwell, adventurers must venture north toward the foul border of Felwood to recover an iron shaft locked inside a hidden chest. The mission carries a tragic undertone, forcing the Alliance to confront corrupted ancients who guard the key. Following the clues to repair Dartol's Rod, Raene directs the search to Shael'dryn, a knowledgeable keeper watching over a tranquil moonwell deep in Ashenvale. Shael'dryn knows the whereabouts of the rod's iron shaft, yet retrieving it requires confronting the creeping taint threatening the northern woods. The piece lies locked in an old chest tucked away in a quiet glade near the border of Felwood. Reaching the chest requires a wooden key, but the key itself has fallen into the hands of the forest's warped protectors. Along the mountain road running north toward Felwood, treants known as Crazed and Withered Ancients wander in agony. The corruption leaching southward from the demonic wastes has shattered their natural harmony, turning former stewards of the wild into hostile, tormented creatures that must be subdued to reclaim Dartol's relic.

quest:1027.text: Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the search for the final component needed to restore Dartol's Rod, an ancient relic tied to cleansing Ashenvale. Shael'dryn directs travelers toward the fallen druid sanctuary of Dor'Danil to recover the missing iron pommel. The final piece of Dartol's Rod—an iron pommel—was entrusted to the night elf druids dwelling at the Dor'Danil barrow den. Tragically, the sanctuary fell to disaster, and its caretakers were slain. With the druids dead and their refuge overrun, the exact hiding place of the relic was lost, leaving scavengers and wandering oozes to swallow up whatever was left behind in the ruins east of the southern road. Dartol was a now-dead evil wizard, but the rod he created holds transformative powers. Raene Wolfrunner and Shael'dryn seek to reassemble the artifact in the hope that it can help slow the furbolg attacks on Ashenvale's night elves. Securing the iron pommel is the last step required before Shael'dryn can attempt to mend the fractured rod at the moonwell.

quest:1028.text: Raene's Cleansing. This step in the cleansing of Ashenvale tasks you with taking the rebuilt Rod of Dartol to a secluded mountain shrine. Hidden among the ridges southeast of Shael'dryn's retreat, the sacred basin holds the latent magic needed to re-enchant the relic. After assembling the shattered pieces of Dartol's Rod, the dryad Shael'dryn directs travelers away from her moonwell into the untamed slopes to the southeast. The ancient shrines of Ashenvale were often deliberately nestled high in the mountain crags, far from the road and shielded by dense forest canopies. Reaching this quiet sanctum requires navigating unmarked terrain along the rock faces, climbing winding trails known mostly to Sentinels and woodland hermits. The shrine itself rests within a quiet alcove surrounded by vibrant forest. Even dormant, the stone hums with the latent protective magic imbued by the night elves of antiquity. By resting the reconstructed rod inside the shrine's stone basin, the site's dormant power awakens, bathing the glade in a soft resonance and infusing Dartol's creation with pristine enchantment so it may finally serve to cleanse the land.

quest:1029.text: Raene's Cleansing. This step in the long-running Ashenvale investigation sees Dartol's Rod of Transformation fully restored. Entrusted with the completed artifact by the dryad Shael'dryn, you return to Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar to report success and honor the memory of the fallen scout Teronis. After scouring the corrupted reaches of Ashenvale for components and ancient gem fragments, the relic known as Dartol's Rod of Transformation has finally been reforged. Entrusted to the dryad Shael'dryn near Iris Lake, its magical properties were cleansed and renewed. With the craftsmanship complete, she directs you back across the forest roads to Astranaar to present the artifact to Raene Wolfrunner.

quest:1030.text: Raene's Cleansing. This critical stage of Raene Wolfrunner's mission requires the use of Dartol's newly restored rod to disguise an outsider and initiate contact with an uncorrupted furbolg. Southeast of Mystral Lake, an outcast named Krolg offers a rare glimpse into the surviving furbolgs' deep resentment toward the night elves. With Dartol's Rod of Transformation restored, Raene Wolfrunner suspects the late night elf intended to disguise himself in order to safely approach the furbolgs. The woods of Ashenvale have grown perilous, and the madness spreading through the tribes makes direct diplomacy impossible. By harnessing the arcane relic, an adventurer takes on the appearance of a furbolg, hoping to slip past instinctive territorial rage and find someone willing to speak.

quest:1031.text: The Branch of Cenarius. Following a desperate plea from the dying dryad Anilia, an adventurer is tasked with recovering a sacred relic stolen by the vile satyr Geltharis. Reclaiming the Branch of Cenarius means confronting the demon-sworn corrupters lurking in eastern Ashenvale and returning the treasured bough to the dryad Illiyana. Sent into the corrupted folds of eastern Ashenvale to search for missing dryads, Alliance travelers stumble upon Anilia clinging to the very edge of life. With her final breaths, the wounded daughter of Cenarius gestures toward the satyr ruins to the north. Gasping out the name of the satyr who has taken it—Geltharis—she begs with her fading strength for the recovery of the Branch of Cenarius before succumbing to her wounds. The thief, Geltharis, is a vile satyr nested within the ancient elven ruins of Xavian. To the satyr, ancient relics tied to the demigod Cenarius are prized trophies ripe for defilement and demonic mockery. Defeating Geltharis and tearing the branch from his claws is not merely an act of justice for Anilia, but a defense against the spreading taint that the Burning Legion's ancient servants inflict upon Ashenvale's sacred flora.

quest:1032.text: Satyr Slaying!. Grieving the loss of her sister Anilia, the dryad Illiyana at the Shrine of Aessina seeks vengeance against the satyrs lurking in Ashenvale. She asks Alliance champions to cull the corrupted creatures and return with their horns as proof of their downfall. Dryads are typically playful and serene forest spirits, deeply bonded to nature and elusive to mortals. The brutal slaying of Anilia shatters this tranquility for Illiyana, who dwells at the Shrine of Aessina. Pushed past her carefree nature into unfamiliar sorrow, she turns to travelers of the Alliance to strike down the demonic beasts responsible. Satyrs represent a dark, twisted branch of ancient night elf ancestry, irrevocably tainted by demonic energy during the War of the Ancients. Lurking in defiled groves across Ashenvale, these vile servants of the Burning Legion actively prey upon the denizens of the woods. Taking their horns serves not only as proof of vengeance, but strikes a direct blow against the fel presence encroaching upon eastern Ashenvale.

quest:1033.text: Elune's Tear. Pelturas Whitemoon's young daughter Relara remains gripped by a foul and relentless malady, defying the herbal remedies brought from the northern ruins. Desperate for a stronger cure, Pelturas sends an adventurer to Iris Lake to retrieve Elune's Tear, a sacred mineral revered by night elves for its power to wash away corruption. Relara Whitemoon lies bedridden in Astranaar, wasting away from a virulent sickness of unknown origin. Pelturas had placed his hopes on an alchemical draught prepared from Bathran's hair by the apothecary Orendil Broadleaf. While that brew managed to arrest the rapid advance of the affliction, it fell short of cleansing her body entirely. Facing the bitter reality that ordinary restorative magic and wild herbs are not enough, Pelturas turns to the ancient traditions of his people, pleading for aid in securing remedies imbued with divine cleansing light. Before parting ways, Orendil shared darker precautions with Pelturas, naming legendary remedies should the herbal mixture prove insufficient. Foremost among them is Elune's Tear, a luminous, sacred stone found only upon an island resting within Iris Lake, east of Astranaar. Believed to carry the blessing of the Moon Goddess, the stone is said to hold the power to purge deep-seated corruption from living flesh. Recovering it is no gentle pilgrimage, as troubled water elementals patrol the shallows and banks of the lake, fiercely guarding the untouched heart of the water.

quest:1034.text: The Ruins of Stardust. Pelturas Whitemoon's desperate quest to heal his daughter Relara continues in Astranaar. While the sacred stone Elune's Tear calmed her terrifying nightmares, a fierce fever still grips her. Guided by Orendil Broadleaf's botanical knowledge, adventurers journey south to harvest a cooling, luminescent dust settled among ancient night elven stones. Pelturas Whitemoon has spent sleepless nights by the bedside of his daughter, Relara, watching a malignant affliction burn through her. Though offering an Elune's Tear provided a temporary respite from the tormenting dreams that plagued her thoughts, the illness remains deeply rooted. Her body is racked by an intense fever that mundane medicines have failed to quench. With the temple healers pushed to their limits, Pelturas turns once more to ancient, nature-infused remedies to preserve his daughter's life. On the advice of the elder herbalist Orendil Broadleaf, Pelturas looks toward the Ruins of Stardust, located south across the river from Astranaar. The fallen marble columns and archways of this ancient kaldorei sanctuary harbor a peculiar phenomenon: a frosted, shimmering substance that settles over the local foliage. This powdered condensation, colloquially termed stardust, possesses natural cooling properties potent enough to draw out unnatural heat. Pelturas intends to grind the collected residue into a medicinal poultice, hoping its tranquil chill will finally break Relara's burning fever. Harvesting the frosted dust is perilous due to the guardians and wildlife inhabiting the flooded, sunken stones. Water elementals, corrupted or agitated by shifts in Ashenvale's balance, surge around the sunken plazas where the bushes grow thickest. Harvesters must wade into the tranquil-looking shallows while staying alert to sudden ambushes from the murky depths, scouring sparkling bushes for enough clean residue before rushing it back to Astranaar.

quest:1035.text: Fallen Sky Lake. "Fallen Sky Lake" is the emotional culmination of Pelturas Whitemoon's quest chain to save his dying daughter, Relara, in Astranaar. Although her initial fever has broken, her vitality remains dangerously depleted, requiring a celestial moonstone to restore her life force. Players must journey into the untamed waters of Fallen Sky Lake to wrest one of these hoarded stones from a corrupted Shadethicket Oracle. Pelturas Whitemoon has spent agonizing days watching his young daughter, Relara, slip closer to death. While powerful curatives brewed from Bathran's hair and stardust helped break her raging fever, the ordeal left her body hollowed and frail. Time is no longer on her side; Pelturas fears that without supernatural intervention, she has only breaths remaining before her spirit fades permanently into the night. To revitalize the girl, Pelturas turns to the magic of the moonstones—celestial fragments that once fell freely into the waters of Fallen Sky Lake, southeast of Astranaar. Traditionally gathered by the night elves for their restorative properties, these remnants of lunar grace have been claimed by aggressive elemental or corrupted bark, making their collection a matter of blade and spell rather than peaceful harvesting.

quest:1037.text: Velinde Starsong. This quest bridges an eerie investigation in Ashenvale with the military hierarchy in Darnassus. After uncovering unsettling events tied to the vanished night elf commander Velinde Starsong, adventurers are sent across the sea to consult Sentinel leadership regarding her mysterious fate. Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow holds watch in Ashenvale, but she was not the first to shoulder that burden. Before her stood Velinde Starsong, a priestess tasked with containing the demonic corruption bleeding southward out of Felwood. Though initial reports suggested Starsong had the peril well in hand, her defensive campaign gradually unraveled. Then, without warning or formal relief, she vanished entirely, leaving behind an unfinished war and unanswered questions.

quest:1038.text: Velinde's Effects. Velinde's Effects is an Alliance investigation in Darnassus uncovering the fate of Sentinel Velinde Starsong. Directed by Thyn'tel Bladeweaver, adventurers retrieve Velinde's personal journal from a chest in the Sentinels' quarters to learn why the revered priestess vanished. Priestess Velinde Starsong earned immense trust among the night elves through her long, devoted service. When she quietly disappeared from her duties, the Sentinels assumed she departed for personal reasons and anticipated her return. Only when outsiders uncover clues linked to the Tome of Mel'Thandris does Sentinel leadership permit an inquiry into her private possessions.

quest:1039.text: The Barrens Port. The Barrens Port is an Alliance quest given by Thyn'tel Bladeweaver in Darnassus as part of the investigation into the disappearance of Velinde Starsong. Believing Velinde took a ship across the Great Sea to the Eastern Kingdoms, the Sentinels direct you across dangerous Horde territory to the goblin-run harbor of Ratchet to consult Wharfmaster Dizzywig's ledgers. Following the inspection of Velinde Starsong's personal effects, the Sentinels discovered clues suggesting she sought passage across the sea toward the Eastern Kingdoms. Ratchet serves as the only operational maritime harbor in the Barrens, making it the solitary conduit through which a traveler from northern Kalimdor could arrange transport south or east without sailing directly out of night elf territory. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver sends you southward to search the harbor master's shipping ledgers for any sign of Velinde's name. Traveling to Ratchet requires an Alliance operative to brave the heart of Horde-controlled lands. South of Ashenvale, the Mor'shan Rampart and the arid savannas of the Barrens crawl with orcish outriders and Tauren patrols. The town of Ratchet itself, governed by the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel, provides safe harbor under goblin law, where trade supersedes faction rivalries and Wharfmaster Dizzywig keeps careful track of every passenger and cargo crate crossing the docks.

quest:104.text: The Coastal Menace. Captain Grayson's restless ghost watches the rocky coast of Westfall, haunted by the memory of the shipwreck that took his life and the slaughter of the lighthouse keeper's family. He charges travelers with hunting down the vicious murloc chieftain responsible: Old Murk-Eye. Slaying the beast brings a measure of justice to the shore and helps safeguard future sailors. The Westfall Lighthouse stands as the lone guide through the jagged shallows of the southern coast, but its flame has flickered through bloody tragedies. Captain Grayson lost his life when his vessel broke against the rocks in the dark, an accident precipitated when murlocs terrified the lighthouse keeper's family into fleeing their post. Though the family later returned and relit the flame, the reprieve was brief. The shoreline remained stalked by a particularly cunning and ruthless predator. Old Murk-Eye is not merely another wild beast prowling the tide pools. Grayson recounts watching the creature sway the weaker-minded murlocs along the coast, rallying them into a coordinated strike against the lighthouse. The second raid proved fatal, wiping out the keeper's family before Grayson's helpless spectral eyes. To bring peace to the dead and preserve what remains of safety on the Great Sea, the ghostly captain demands Murk-Eye's death and a scale as proof.

quest:1040.text: Passage to Booty Bay. This errand traces the missing Sentinel Velinde Starsong across the Great Sea to the lawless haven of Booty Bay. Following shipping logs uncovered by Wharfmaster Dizzywig, Alliance travelers must journey from Ratchet to the Eastern Kingdoms in search of a goblin caravan driver named Ruzzgot. The search for the night elf Sentinel Velinde Starsong leads away from the familiar boughs of Ashenvale and onto the ocean trade lanes. In the bustling goblin port of Ratchet, Wharfmaster Dizzywig eventually unearths old shipping manifests confirming that Velinde booked passage aboard a vessel named the Black Osprey, bound directly for the pirate haven of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Reaching Booty Bay requires boarding the neutral goblin trans-oceanic ferry running between Ratchet and the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms. Upon arrival, the trail narrows toward Caravaneer Ruzzgot, a goblin transport master Dizzywig recommended to Velinde when she inquired about dangerous overland journeys through the southern wilderness.

quest:1041.text: The Caravan Road. The Caravan Road is an Alliance quest that traces the footsteps of the missing night elf priestess Velinde Starsong. Following information uncovered in Booty Bay, the trail leads north from the perilous jungles of Stranglethorn Vale into the shadowed town of Darkshire. Tracking Velinde Starsong across the world brings adventurers from the forests of Ashenvale all the way to the southern port of Booty Bay. There, Caravaneer Ruzzgot recalls an unusual passenger: a night elf priestess traveling alongside his dusty shipping caravan. Such solitary journeys are rare for her kind, making her journey through the lawless jungle of Stranglethorn Vale stand out in the minds of merchants. According to Ruzzgot, he and Velinde parted company on their trek northward through the jungle, with the priestess striking out toward Duskwood. Her trail points directly to the beleaguered town of Darkshire, where the town's records are meticulously maintained by Clerk Daltry. In an era troubled by supernatural threats, Daltry logs every unfamiliar traveler entering the settlement, making his ledger the next vital link in unraveling Velinde's fate.

quest:1042.text: The Carevin Family. The Carevin Family is a short Alliance investigation quest that connects the mystery of Velinde Starsong to the monster hunters of Duskwood. Guided by town records clerk Daltry, adventurers seeking the lost priestess turn to Jonathan Carevin, patriarch of a family dedicated to culling beasts and fiends. Searching for Velinde Starsong leads away from the ancient forests of Kalimdor and deep into the haunted gloom of Duskwood. Upon arriving in Darkshire, municipal clerk Daltry finds no official log of an elven priestess ever boarding in town. However, mentioning the savage wolf-men seen in Ashenvale immediately catches his ear, as beasts fitting that description have recently begun terrorizing the surrounding woods. Rather than standard town guards, dealing with such unnatural terrors falls to the Carevin family. Renowned locally as relentless hunters of demons, undead, and other horrors, their tracker Calor recently dragged a grisly string of severed wolf-men heads right through Darkshire's streets. Clerk Daltry directs outsiders to Jonathan Carevin, the stern head of the household, to learn what the family knows of these ferocious worgen.

quest:1043.text: The Scythe of Elune. The Scythe of Elune is an Alliance investigation bridging an ancient night elf relic in Kalimdor with the sudden worgen infestation plaguing Duskwood. Sent by Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, adventurers delve into the haunted depths of Roland's Doom to uncover what brought these ravenous beasts to the Eastern Kingdoms. After tracing the enigmatic Priestess Velinde Starsong across Kalimdor and speaking with the Carevin household in Darkshire, travelers find common cause with Jonathan Carevin. The Nightbane worgen have overrun southern Duskwood, pushing out miners and threatening what little remains of the township. Although Carevin does not fully grasp the supernatural origin of these beasts, he recognizes the value of someone willing to root them out, pointing searchers toward Roland's Doom—the very mine where the fiends were first sighted.

quest:1045.text: Raene's Cleansing. Disguised by Dartol's Rod of Transformation, adventurers gain the trust of Krolg, an uncorrupted furbolg near Lake Mystral. Disillusioned with both the arrogant night elves and the corruption rotting his own kin, Krolg asks for the death of the depraved chieftain Ran Bloodtooth so that the furbolgs can police their own. Near the waters of Lake Mystral, Krolg keeps a secluded vigil. Displaced and weary, he carries deep resentment toward the night elves, whose ancient hubris he blames for bringing ruin upon Kalimdor and stirring the dark rot festering in Ashenvale. To reach him, seekers use Dartol's Rod of Transformation to walk among furbolgs undetected. Yet despite his bitter hatred of the kaldorei, Krolg does not seek senseless butchery or innocent deaths. Rather than surrendering entirely to the demonic taint gripping the tribes, Krolg believes his people must remain accountable for their own deeds. The demonic corruption did not originate their flaws—it merely amplified their worst impulses. Ran Bloodtooth embodies this fall: already ruthless and power-hungry before the taint, Ran embraced the darkness eagerly, posing an existential threat to elves and innocent beasts alike. Krolg refuses to let such malice speak for all furbolgs.

quest:1046.text: Raene's Cleansing. This quest marks the final chapter in the search to uncover what befell Teronis and halt the furbolg threat looming over Ashenvale. Bearing Ran Bloodtooth's skull from Krolg, an adventurer returns to Sentinel Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar to report the culmination of their perilous journey. Following the defeat of the fierce corrupted furbolg chieftain Ran Bloodtooth, Krolg sends the champion back to Astranaar. With Bloodtooth's severed skull in hand, you return as proof that the savage threat prowling the forest depths has been decisively struck down.

quest:1054.text: Culling the Threat. Culling the Threat is an Alliance defensive operation issued by Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar. Faced with rapidly multiplying Thistlefur furbolgs directly to the north, the night elves seek to preempt an assault on the settlement by slaying their warlord, Dal Bloodclaw. It reflects the grim reality that former woodland allies must now be culled to safeguard kaldorei homes. Astranaar lies in the heart of Ashenvale, constantly surrounded by danger. Just north of the settlement dwell the Thistlefur furbolgs. Once peaceable dwellers of the ancient forest, they have fallen into madness and aggression like so many of their kin. Sentinel scouts watched their populations swell over recent months, raising fears that a coordinated assault on Astranaar itself was only a matter of time. Rather than waiting for the Thistlefur horde to overrun Astranaar's modest palisades, Raene Wolfrunner commissions travelers to take offensive action. The objective is Dal Bloodclaw, the chieftain whose leadership organizes and emboldens the den. By severing the tribe's head and bringing Dal's skull back to Astranaar, the Sentinels hope to break the furbolgs' coordination and buy precious time for the beleaguered town.

quest:1055.text: Raene's Cleansing. This task marks the completion of the Rod of Transformation at the hidden shrine in Ashenvale. With the sacred artifact assembled, it must be returned immediately to the dryad Shael'dryn at her moonwell sanctuary. The arduous effort to assemble the Rod of Transformation reaches a quiet turning point at the secluded shrine hidden deep within Ashenvale's wilds. Piecing together the shaft, pommel, and glowing gem, and re-enchanting the reconstructed rod at the hidden shrine has restored its magic. The artifact is ready to be returned to Shael'dryn for Raene's investigation of the furbolg attacks. With the assembly complete, word and relic must be delivered swiftly back to Shael'dryn. Stationed beside the calm waters of the forest moonwell, the dryad has guided every step of this restoration effort. Presenting the assembled rod to her not only confirms that the rod's magic has been restored, but also allows the Sentinel defenders to take the next critical steps in defending their besieged homeland.

quest:1057.text: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Reclaiming the Charred Vale is an Alliance quest offered by Keeper Albagorm atop Stonetalon Peak. It charges adventurers with culling the aggressive Bloodfury harpies who occupy the ruined valley of the Charred Vale, clearing a path so druids and caretakers can begin healing the scorched landscape. To the south of Stonetalon Peak lies the Charred Vale, a once-lush alpine haven reduced to ash and smoldering ruins. The devastation began when a mechanized logging and mining army swept through the sacred crags, stripping trees and fueling uncontrolled blazes. For the guardians stationed around Stonetalon, watching ancient woodland succumb to industrial greed is an intolerable wound upon the wilderness. While mechanical fires sparked the ruin, an opportunistic infestation took root in the ashes. The vicious Bloodfury harpies swarmed into the smoking lowlands, establishing nests and aggressively ambushing anyone approaching the valley. Keeper Albagorm and his allies cannot even walk the soil to sow the seeds of renewal, as the Bloodfuries violently refuse passage to all outsiders. Before any meaningful restoration can take place, the roosts of the Bloodfury tribe must be broken. Albagorm tasks seasoned Alliance fighters with carving deep into their numbers—slaying hunters, ambushers, and roguefeathers alike. Thinning their predatory flocks is the vital first step toward reclaiming what belongs to nature and giving the forest spirits room to breathe once more.

quest:1058.text: Jin'Zil's Forest Magic. At the small outpost of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil has captured three night elven scouts in crude iron cages. Rather than executing them outright or holding them for ransom, the eccentric troll tasks Horde adventurers with gathering wilderness reagents from Stonetalon Peak to concoct a gruesome dose of 'forest magic.' In the red-rock defile of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil conducts his craft under the watchful gaze of the Horde. When three night elf captives fall into his clutches, Jin'Zil decides against ordinary butchery, concocting instead a mocking ritual tailored specifically for his captive woodland foes. He directs travelers north into the untamed peaks to collect an array of indigenous parts: thick tree sap, feline whiskers from predatory twilight runners, a shimmering fey dragon scale, and scores of eyes plucked from the local forest coursers.

quest:1059.text: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Reclaiming the Charred Vale is a messenger quest tasked by Keeper Albagorm in Stonetalon Peak. Having temporarily suppressed the local harpies, Albagorm sends an Alliance traveler far south to Feralas to recruit the aid of the druid Falfindel Waywarder. The Charred Vale in southern Stonetalon Mountains remains an ash-choked reminder of catastrophic devastation. While Alliance forces under Keeper Albagorm have struck back against the rampant Bloodfury harpies nesting in the ruins, driving them off is merely a holding action. Albagorm recognizes that physical force alone cannot mend the ravaged earth before the harpies rally and reclaim their dominance. To permanently restore the scorched lands, the grove tenders need mystical intervention beyond their current means. Albagorm dispatches a courier far to the south, skirting past the salt flats and canyons of Thousand Needles to Thalanaar on the border of Feralas. There waits Falfindel Waywarder, a night elf druid reputed to possess the rare power to call forth primordial forest spirits capable of rejuvenating the dead soil.

quest:106.text: Young Lovers. Young Lovers is an Elwynn Forest quest centered on the forbidden romance between Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield. With their rival families locked in a bitter feud, Maybell enlists an adventurer to secretly courier a heartfelt love letter to Tommy Joe by the riverbank. In the pastoral fields of Elwynn Forest, a bitter feud divides two neighboring farming households: the Stonefields and the Maclures. Despite the hostility between their families, young Maybell Maclure has fallen deeply in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield. Unable to visit him openly without igniting family fury, Maybell relies on passing travelers to carry secret correspondence across the boundary lines separating the rival estates. To keep their affection hidden from watchful relatives, Tommy Joe Stonefield spends his hours by the quiet riverbank just west of the Stonefield Farm. Delivering Maybell's letter brings him immense relief and rekindles his longing, making the separation unbearable and setting in motion further clandestine attempts to bring the young lovers together despite the feud.

quest:1060.text: Letter to Jin'Zil. Letter to Jin'Zil is a Horde delivery quest entrusted to adventurers who have slain Serena Bloodfeather in the northern Barrens. Orc rogue Darsok Swiftdagger sends you across the border into the rugged crags of Stonetalon Mountains to deliver word of the harpy matriarch's demise to his old friend, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. After the harpy threat around the northern Barrens is systematically dismantled, Darsok Swiftdagger reveals that the winged raiders were never native to the scrublands. The Witchwing and Bloodfeather broods descended from the rugged ridges of the Stonetalon Mountains to the northwest. Impressed by your prowess in dispatching Serena Bloodfeather, Darsok sends you into those dangerous peaks to carry news of her death to an old acquaintance, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil, residing at the troll settlement of Malaka'jin.

quest:1066.text: Blood of Innocents. Blood of Innocents is an errand undertaken for Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to harvest sinister alchemical components. Seeking to pacify the encroaching Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes dark ingredients gathered from regional bandits. The Horde faces persistent friction in the Stonetalon Mountains, where the rapacious Venture Company ravages the wilderness without regard for the earth or its inhabitants. Rather than dispatching armies to blunt their axes, Apothecary Lydon proposes an alchemical remedy. His plan involves concocting a paralyzing, pacifying agent designed to sap the mercenaries of their aggression, leaving them weak and docile. Brewing such an insidious concoction demands an exceedingly rare and morally questionable reagent: the blood of innocents. Rather than forcing Horde agents to slaughter innocents directly, Lydon capitalizes on the crimes of the local Syndicate. The fallen nobles and cutthroats infesting Durnholde Keep employ rogue shadow mages who harvest innocent blood for their own profane rituals, making them an opportune target for alchemical requisition.

quest:1067.text: Return to Thunder Bluff. This quest charges an operative with carrying a potent chemical agent brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill back across the sea to Thunder Bluff. There, Apothecary Zamah awaits the compound so she can engineer a dispersal apparatus against the Venture Company. It marks a crucial step in the Royal Apothecary Society's clandestine research under the very roofs of their Tauren hosts. After securing the volatile ingredients requested in the Hillsbrad Foothills, Apothecary Lydon successfully synthesizes his virulent concoction. Lydon is thoroughly thrilled to see his biological handiwork tested on live subjects, but the raw toxin alone lacks an effective delivery mechanism. To maximize its effect, the vial must be brought back across the Great Sea to the crags of Mulgore, into the waiting hands of Apothecary Zamah.

quest:1068.text: Shredding Machines. Shredding Machines is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with hunting down two specialized Venture Company logging mechs in Windshear Crag. Directed by the shaman Seereth Stonebreak, players strike against the mechanical deforestation that torments Stonetalon's native spirits. Stationed along the dusty border between the Barrens and the Stonetalon Mountains, the orc shaman Seereth Stonebreak listens closely to the unseen realm. While much of Stonetalon's spiritual voice is drowned out by chaos, one vision came to her with harrowing clarity: man-shaped contraptions tearing through ancient woods with unnatural haste. Marked with the mechanical designations XT:4 and XT:9, these goblin-engineered shredders butcher the timberlands of Windshear Crag, sending waves of distress through the surrounding nature spirits. To stem the devastation, Horde champions venture deep into Windshear Crag, northwest of Greatwood Vale, where the Venture Company operates. Tracking down and wrecking these specific logging constructs deals a sharp blow to the commercial deforestation of the mountains. Though bringing down XT:4 and XT:9 calms the immediate cries of the wounded tree spirits, Seereth warns that unless the Venture Company abandons Stonetalon entirely, far darker atrocities await the land.

quest:1069.text: Deepmoss Spider Eggs. Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet aims to capitalize on an exotic culinary craze sweeping Booty Bay: spider egg omelettes. To supply the lucrative overseas market, he hires adventurers to venture into the Stonetalon Mountains and harvest fresh clutches of deepmoss spider eggs. Booty Bay's high rollers and eccentric pirates have developed an insatiable appetite for spider egg omelettes, sparking high demand for rare ingredients across the Great Sea. Recognizing an easy fortune, Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix has jumped at the chance to supply the southern port. Because the Eastern Kingdoms lack this particular arachnid delicacies, Kalimdor's rugged wilderness provides the perfect supply chain. The harvest requires trekking into the Stonetalon Mountains to find deepmoss spiders. Clutches of their eggs can be discovered clinging beneath the surviving timber of the Venture Company's logging operations in Windshear Crag, or deeper within the web-strewn depths of Sishir Canyon. Gathering the eggs means risking venomous bites and confronting dense infestations that make even seasoned scavengers squeamish. Speed and logistics are critical when moving raw arachnid eggs across the sea before they spoil or hatch. Mebok coordinates closely with Ratchet's Wharfmaster Dizzywig, arranging freight passage on goblin merchant ships bound straight for the docks of Stranglethorn Vale. With the eggs safely packed in crates, Mebok turns a tidy profit on high-seas gastronomy.

quest:107.text: Note to William. "Note to William" is an errand undertaken for Gramma Stonefield in southern Elwynn Forest to help two secret lovers from feuding families. By delivering Mildred's message to the apothecary William Pestle in Goldshire, adventurers seek an alchemical solution to unite young Maybell and Tommy Joe. The Stonefield and Maclure families have lived as neighbors in southern Elwynn Forest for years, yet their bitter feuding has made normal relations impossible. Caught squarely in the middle are young Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure, whose romance must be conducted in utter secrecy. While their parents harbor relentless resentment, Gramma Mildred Stonefield takes pity on the young lovers and seeks an unconventional remedy to unite them. Believing that mundane persuasion will never sway the feuding families, Gramma Stonefield dispatches a courier north to the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Her message seeks out William Pestle, an experienced alchemist and apothecary whom Mildred has known for many years. Taking the missive in hand, William is moved by the plight of Maybell and Tommy Joe, resolving to put his alchemical knowledge to work on their behalf.

quest:1070.text: On Guard in Stonetalon. On Guard in Stonetalon is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers south from Ashenvale into the rugged Stonetalon Mountains. Sentinel Thenysil dispatches travelers to check on her scout friend, Kaela Shadowspear, who was sent into the crags alongside a gnome mage to monitor industrial incursions by the Venture Company. Stationed in Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil keeps a close watch on threats pressing toward the ancient forest. Deeply concerned for her friend Kaela Shadowspear, Thenysil asks passing Alliance champions to track her down. Kaela was dispatched into the Stonetalon Mountains by Sentinel Wolfrunner to survey rising turmoil in the heights, but communication has fallen silent, leaving Thenysil anxious for her safety. Thenysil's concern is heightened by Kaela's assigned companion: a gnome mage deployed alongside her by the Alliance leadership. While the night elves have joined the Grand Alliance out of strategic necessity, many Sentinels remain deeply skeptical of arcane practitioners and tinkering gnomes operating in pristine wilderness. Finding Kaela perched on the bluffs above Windshear Crag reveals an outpost keeping vigil over widespread environmental devastation wrought by the Venture Company.

quest:1071.text: A Gnome's Respite. A Gnome's Respite is an Alliance quest offered by the eccentric tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Overwhelmed by the Venture Company's rapid industrial push into Windshear Crag, Gaxim hires adventurers to cull their loggers and deforesters so he can buy enough breathing room to invent new deterrents. Gaxim Rustfizzle represents the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences. Stationed among the ancient groves of Stonetalon, his stated duty is proving to the nature-worshipping night elves that modern gnomish invention—blending magic, chemical brews, and mechanics—can actively protect their threatened lands. However, the relentless pace of the Venture Company has left him with barely any time to prototype his defensive devices. To stem the tide, Gaxim sends adventurers directly into the smoking operations at Windshear Crag. By targeting the frontline Venture Co. Loggers and Deforesters, travelers give Gaxim the respite he needs to organize his workshop and devise his next line of defense: strategic, controlled high explosives.

quest:1072.text: An Old Colleague. An Old Colleague is an Alliance quest given by the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looking to construct an extraordinarily potent device, Gaxim sends an adventurer all the way across the sea to Ironforge to track down an old acquaintance capable of synthesizing a hazardous explosive concoction. Completing this errand opens the door to procuring the volatile chemical compound known as Nitromirglyceronium. While stationed among the peaks of Stonetalon, Gaxim Rustfizzle conceives of his most ambitious engineering endeavor yet. Creating a mechanism of that scale requires specialized fuel far beyond typical gunpowder or crude oil. Specifically, Gaxim requires Nitromirglyceronium, also designated as NG-5, an explosive mix potent enough to guarantee destructive results should everything go according to plan. Formulating NG-5 is no simple task, and Gaxim knows of only one mind skilled enough to refine it: an old acquaintance named Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac resides far to the east in the gnome quarter of Tinker Town, tucked deep within the mountain stronghold of Ironforge. Entrusted with the long journey, the courier arrives only to be greeted by Lomac's immediate suspicion and paranoid questioning.

quest:1073.text: Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. Seeking an explosive countermeasure against the Venture Company in the Stonetalon Mountains, Alliance adventurers are sent across the sea to Ironforge. There, the eccentric gnome Lomac Gearstrip agrees to brew his volatile invention, Nitromirglyceronium, provided you fetch the necessary alchemical reagents. Gaxim Rustfizzle, stationed high in the craggy passes of the Stonetalon Mountains, needed potent explosives for the most advanced device he had yet devised against the Venture Company. For that, he turned to an eccentric former colleague living in Ironforge: Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac is the creator of Nitromirglyceronium, a substance so inherently unstable and destructive that he finds the prospect of anyone using it hilarious, regardless of who gets blown apart in the process. Despite Lomac's eagerness to see goblin machinery—and possibly the adventurer—blown into pieces, his workshop in Ironforge is entirely out of the finished compound. Before he will brew a fresh batch of Nitromirglyceronium, Lomac demands common alchemical draughts: Minor Mana Potions and Elixirs of Minor Fortitude. In his eyes, forcing an adventurer to gather these ingredients serves a dual purpose, ensuring he has the raw reagents needed for the reaction while proving they possess at least a shred of respect for the craft of alchemy.

quest:1074.text: Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. This errand delivers a canister of volatile NG-5 from the tinker Lomac Gearstrip to Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gaxim requires this unstable chemical to create a potent igniter for several wagons packed with dynamite. The resulting blast forms a critical distraction for Alliance operations in the disputed crags. Gnomish engineering often balances brilliance on the razor edge of catastrophe, and Nitromirglyceronium—or NG-5—is no exception. Lomac Gearstrip hands over the unstable compound with a stern warning: handle it with extreme care, or risk blowing yourself to pieces on the road back to Gaxim Rustfizzle.

quest:1075.text: A Scroll from Mauren. "A Scroll from Mauren" is an Alliance errand carrying word between gnome ingenuity and human arcane craft. The inventive Gaxim Rustfizzle requires a specialized spell to remotely trigger his volatile NG-5 explosives, dispatching couriers to consult with mage Collin Mauren in the heart of Stormwind. Gnomish engineering is legendary for ambitious concepts, but safe execution often requires clever solutions. When Gaxim Rustfizzle set out to design an explosive payload capable of remote activation, mechanical fuses proved insufficient. Rather than relying purely on mechanical timers or trailing cords, Gaxim envisioned a device that would detonate the NG-5 explosives at the push of a single button from a safe vantage point. To bridge the gap between volatile powder and instantaneous trigger, he turned his sights toward arcane magic. To acquire the necessary spellwork, Gaxim directs travelers across the kingdom to Stormwind's bustling Mage Quarter. There resides Collin Mauren, a human spellcaster whose practical understanding of the arcane makes him an ideal partner for ambitious tinkers. Mauren ponders the delicate problem of binding explosive ignition to a distant command, marking the first step in assembling the arcane incantation required to arm Gaxim's hazardous project.

quest:1076.text: Devils in Westfall. "Devils in Westfall" is an Alliance errand undertaken for Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. Tasked with aiding an eccentric experiment by the gnome inventor Gaxim Rustfizzle, adventurers are sent into the desolate plains of Westfall to gather volatile debris from living dust devils. The collected dust provides the raw magical component needed to enchant a specialized messaging scroll. The wizard Collin Mauren is assisting the tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle with an unusual venture, but arcane work requires specialized reagents. To enchant a scroll capable of carrying Gaxim's desired messaging spell, Mauren cannot rely on simple ink and vellum alone. The swirling elemental magic trapped within Westfall's native dust devils provides the exact volatile medium needed to bind the spell into parchment form. Westfall was once the fertile breadbasket of Stormwind, but drought, banditry, and neglect have left the land arid and wild. Swirling dust devils now roam the untamed fields, posing a hazard to travelers and lone homesteaders alike. By defeating one of these living whirlwinds and gathering its residue, adventurers retrieve the focused elemental essence required to bring the mage's enchantment to life.

quest:1077.text: Special Delivery for Gaxim. Special Delivery for Gaxim represents the return leg of an Alliance courier mission between Stormwind City and the wilds of Kalimdor. Collin Mauren provides a specialized Scroll of Messaging to take back to the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. The scroll contains the arcane component needed to construct a remote explosive against local deforestation efforts. Gaxim Rustfizzle's efforts to sabotage the destructive operations of the Venture Company require unconventional solutions. Having concocted an explosive compound called NG-5, the tinkerer found himself lacking a reliable means of remote detonation. Rather than turning to crude fuses, Gaxim enlisted help across the Great Sea, reaching out to Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind to acquire an enchanted Scroll of Messaging.

quest:1078.text: Retrieval for Mauren. Retrieval for Mauren is a quest given by Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. Hearing tales of travelers venturing deep into Kalimdor, the wizard contracts Alliance adventurers to gather crystallised scales from basilisks dwelling in Stonetalon's Charred Vale. Mauren seeks these rare specimens to grind into dust as reagents for his personal spellcraft. Collin Mauren, a wizard residing in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind City, keeps an ear close to the chatter of wandering adventurers. Word has reached him that the distant Stonetalon Mountains in Kalimdor have become a burgeoning hotspot for travelers seeking wild wyverns, unruly elementals, or lucrative deals and clashes with the Venture Company. Rather than seeking riches or glory, Mauren's interest lies in the rare natural wonders reported from the region's harshest corners. Deep within Stonetalon lies the Charred Vale, an ash-choked expanse left scarred by the Venture Company's devastation. According to Mauren's studies, the basin was once known to house a peculiar breed of basilisk. When harvested and crushed into a fine powder, their scales form a potent catalyst for specialized arcane spells he has developed. Unsure whether the creatures managed to survive the harsh transformation of the Vale, Mauren relies on intrepid explorers to harvest a fresh batch of crystallised scales and confirm whether the breed endures.

quest:1079.text: Covert Ops - Alpha. Covert Ops - Alpha is an Alliance infiltration mission directed by the gnome tinker Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. While operating out of the peaks, operatives are tasked with penetrating the Venture Company's lumber mill in Windshear Crag to recover proprietary engineering schematics. Securing these blueprints allows the Alliance to decipher the mechanical vulnerabilities of goblin machinery while co-opting their logging technology. Operating from Windshear Crag, Gaxim Rustfizzle conducts a persistent covert campaign to disrupt the aggressive logging operations of the Venture Company. While goblin deforesters fell the primeval timber south of Cragpool Lake, Gaxim recognizes that wanton destruction alone cannot halt the enterprise. Instead of merely detonating industrial hardware, Plan Alpha prioritizes intelligence gathering, requiring agents to slip past goblin loggers and overseers to seize their core technical schematics directly from the lumber mill. Gnomish interest in the Venture Company extends beyond ecological sympathy for the night elves. The recovered schematics detail the inner workings of heavy-duty goblin loggers, mechanical cutters, and mechanized transports. By studying these blueprints, Alliance engineers can expose critical structural flaws to dismantle future operations—while simultaneously borrowing refined goblin designs to enhance their own mechanical projects back in Ironforge.

quest:1080.text: Covert Ops - Beta. Covert Ops - Beta is an Alliance mission organized by the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Building upon previous sabotage against the encroaching Venture Company, this operation sends an agent deep into Windshear Mine to trigger explosive diversions and extract vital operational letters. The retrieved intelligence serves both gnome curiosity and the territorial defense of the regional night elf Sentinels. Following initial strikes against the Venture Company's clear-cutting operations across Windshear Crag, Gaxim Rustfizzle devises a follow-up operation aimed directly at their logistical heart. Plan Beta follows the same fundamental logic as its predecessor: creating an explosive, chaotic diversion to scatter the goblin operators and mercenaries while an operative slips through the confusion to search the mines for written correspondence. Windshear Mine sits at the far eastern reaches of the crag, serving as the company's regional subterranean base. Digging through rock and harvesting timber, the goblins maintain strict ledgers and communications detailing their supply lines and executive directives. By sneaking inside, setting Gaxim's specialized explosive packs, and seizing the Venture Co. Letters, operatives dismantle the company's security while uncovering their wider ambitions in Kalimdor. While Gaxim approaches the mission with typical gnomish delight for pyrotechnics and clever gadgetry, the mission has serious strategic implications for the night elves. The Sentinels in Stonetalon, led by commanders like Kaela Shadowspear, are hard-pressed battling both the Horde and ruthless industrial exploiters. The intelligence recovered from the mine directly assists the Sentinels in predicting and thwarting the defilement of their sacred woodlands.

quest:1081.text: Reception from Tyrande. Reception from Tyrande is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the embattled slopes of the Stonetalon Mountains directly to the night elf capital of Darnassus. After aiding the Sentinels in securing their precarious foothold in Stonetalon against the Venture Company, you are sent by Sentinel Thenysil in Astranaar to receive formal recognition from High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind herself in the Temple of the Moon. The night elven outposts scattered throughout the Stonetalon Mountains face intense pressure, particularly from the Venture Company ravaging the land. Sentinel Thenysil coordinates efforts from Astranaar, but sustaining these remote bases requires immense resilience. Securing supply lines and intelligence is vital to maintaining an Alliance presence in Kalimdor's interior, making outside aid profoundly impactful to the Sentinels stationed there. Recognizing that your assistance has actively bolstered the Sentinels' grip on the region, Sentinel Thenysil directs you to travel back to Teldrassil. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind grants you a personal audience. Tyrande acknowledges your rising deeds across Kalimdor, welcoming you not merely as a wandering mercenary, but as an allied champion fighting alongside the kaldorei.

quest:1082.text: Update for Sentinel Thenysil. This errand carries word of relief from the crags of Stonetalon back to the night elf outpost of Astranaar. Having aided Kaela Shadowspear and Gaxim Rustfizzle against the encroaching Venture Company, you are tasked with reassuring Sentinel Tara Thenysil that their outpost holds firm. Stonetalon's jagged passes are an isolated and vulnerable frontier for the night elves. With goblin deforestation operations eating away at the crags and polluting the waterways, the outpost manned by Kaela Shadowspear and the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle operates under constant threat. Once the immediate dangers posed by the Venture Company are blunted, keeping the command hierarchy informed is essential. Kaela sends you northeast across the border back into Ashenvale to confirm their survival. In the forested sanctuary of Astranaar, Sentinel Tara Thenysil maintains watch over Ashenvale's interior roads while worrying over scouts deployed into harsher territories. Receiving confirmation that both Kaela and her eccentric engineering partner are alive and actively healing the land offers a rare moment of good news. It proves that despite dwindling forces and multiple hostile fronts, cooperation with Alliance allies can stem the tide of ecological destruction.

quest:1083.text: Enraged Spirits. Enraged Spirits is an Alliance quest given by Kaela Shadowspear in the Stonetalon Mountains. After the Venture Company laid waste to the Charred Vale with fire and heavy machinery, furious fire elementals broke free and overran the blighted basin. Alliance champions are asked to quell these roaming spirits of flame and stone so the wounded land might one day heal under Elune's grace. The Charred Vale was once a lush haven within Stonetalon, but the reckless greed of the Venture Company transformed it into an ashen wasteland. In their drive to log and strip the land of resources, the goblins deployed incendiary devices and heavy machinery that set the entire canopy ablaze. Their destructive meddling did not merely destroy trees; it shattered the fragile elemental balance beneath the earth. The venture did not go as planned for the goblins. The conflagration and deep excavation stirred ancient, dormant spirits of fire, stone, and fury from the depths. These enraged elementals swiftly turned on the trespassers, driving the Venture Company back and claiming the smoldering crater as their own. Kaela Shadowspear laments that until these chaotic elementals are culled, nature can never begin to recover.

quest:1084.text: Wounded Ancients. Wounded Ancients is an Alliance task given by Kaela Shadowspear in the Stonetalon Mountains. Suspecting that goblin munitions drove the local forest guardians mad, Kaela sends adventurers to recover shrapnel lodged in the corrupted treants so the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle can analyze the taint. The forested groves of Stonetalon were long watched over by towering treants, gentle yet ferocious guardians bound to the health of the land. When the Venture Company moved in with buzzsaws, explosives, and strip-mining operations, nature fought back. The treants successfully repelled the invaders from parts of the vale, but victory came at an insidious cost. The defenders did not return to peaceful guardianship; instead, they devolved into hostile, maddened husks. Kaela Shadowspear, an Alliance scout stationed in the mountains, believes the treants' decline is no natural sickness. The gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle suspects the culprit lies in the chemical and mechanical arsenal used by the goblins during their chaotic retreat. By prying corroded shrapnel from the wounded wood-beasts, Gaxim hopes to determine whether Venture Company ordnance is actively poisoning Stonetalon's ancient protectors.

quest:1085.text: On Guard in Stonetalon. On Guard in Stonetalon directs Alliance travelers from Kaela Shadowspear to Gaxim Rustfizzle at their camp near Windshear Crag. Facing rampant despoilment by the Venture Company, an otherwise unlikely pair—a cautious night elf sentinel and an eccentric gnome tinkerer—join forces to safeguard the mountain pass. Night elves and gnomes rarely share common ground, especially when it comes to technology and the natural world. In the crags of Stonetalon Mountains, however, necessity bridges the cultural gulf. With the rapacious Venture Company carving out the wilderness and felling ancient trees, the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear has recognized that pure martial prowess alone cannot overcome industrialized pillaging. Welcoming gnome ingenuity into sacred Kaldorei territory demonstrates just how precarious the situation has become. Gaxim Rustfizzle represents the eccentric pragmatism of the Alliance's smaller allies. While night elf society famously turned its back on arcane excess millennia ago, Gaxim believes that abstaining from magic and technical innovation leaves them vulnerable. By pairing alchemy and engineering with a touch of arcane discipline, Gaxim aims to convince his Kaldorei hosts that practical science can defend nature just as effectively as bow and glaive.

quest:1086.text: The Flying Machine Airport. Tasked by Apothecary Zamah from Thunder Bluff, Horde adventurers hunt down a hidden Venture Company landing pad nestled above Stonetalon Mountains. Carrying an alchemical Toxic Fogger, operatives must slip into the heart of the goblin logging operations to gas their air transit hub. The mission strikes directly at the cartel's communications while underscoring the ruthless methods of the Royal Apothecary Society. While the tauren seek to protect Stonetalon from deforestation and ravaging machinery, the Forsaken bring an entirely different philosophy to the front. Apothecary Zamah readies Apothecary Lydon's toxin to disrupt the Venture Company's logistics. Rather than attacking foot soldiers or loggers directly, she targets the cartel's link to the outside world: a rumored copter pad used to ferry light cargo and messages between Stonetalon and distant corporate offices. Hidden high in the Cragpool Lake area south of the great waterwheel sits the Venture Company's copter pad, perched above the soot and chopped timber. It is small, meant for lightweight flying machines rather than massive zeppelins. Setting off the Toxic Fogger directly upon the pad ensures that any pilot, courier, or mechanic operating the machinery is smothered in toxic vapor before they can alert their commanders.

quest:1087.text: Cenarius' Legacy. Cenarius' Legacy is a Horde task handed out by Braelyn Firehand near Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Frustrated by the natural wards maintained by the night elves and the children of Cenarius, the blood elf mage seeks to cull their numbers at Stonetalon Peak to restore the raw flow of magic. For the Horde, striking at the Cenarion defenders also weakens the regional Alliance presence. Braelyn Firehand resides in the hills near Sun Rock Retreat, festering with frustration at Stonetalon's natural environment. According to her, the druids of the Cenarion Circle and the demigod Cenarius's offspring actively suppress and choke the arcane currents of the land. Describing the process of channeling power here as drawing water with a perforated bucket, she hungers to strip away their natural defenses so raw magical energy can surge unimpeded once again. To weaken this verdant stranglehold, Braelyn enlists Horde champions to venture north to Stonetalon Peak. There, around the ancient kaldorei groves and temple grounds, patrol the Cenarion Botanists alongside the proud Sons and Daughters of Cenarius. Striking down these wardens serves a dual purpose: it dismantles the wards muffling Braelyn's spellcraft and deals a bloody blow to the night elf enclave threatening the Horde's foothold in the mountains.

quest:1088.text: Ordanus. Braelyn Firehand at Sunrock Retreat uses her arcane sight to track down Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius who fled Stonetalon Peak. Believing his people desecrated ancient Highborne ruins, she sends Horde champions across the border into Ashenvale to take his head. Braelyn Firehand arrived in Stonetalon Mountains on orders from her master to reclaim the sacred ruins of Azshara's ancient temples. She found the night elves already occupying the peak, treating the relics of her Highborne forebears as wilderness to be contained. Her chief target, Keeper Ordanus, fled before she could corner him, slipping across the border into Ashenvale. Using her arcane vision, Braelyn scried his hiding place high in a wooden refuge at Raynewood Retreat and enlisted the Horde to finish the hunt. Ordanus is counted among the eldest sons of Cenarius, possessing deep ties to the wild magics of Kalimdor. Night elf guardians moved him from Stonetalon Peak to Raynewood Retreat, seeking to protect him from the arcane forces encroaching upon sacred groves. Defended by loyal Cenarion Vindicators and summoned woodland treants, the keeper represents both the ancient authority of the forest demigod and a living obstacle to Braelyn's vengeance.

quest:1089.text: The Den. The Den is the culmination of a Horde infiltration campaign against night elf druids entrenched on Stonetalon Peak.
