Directed by the blood elf operative Braelyn Firehand, champions delve into the Talon Den's subterranean barrow chambers to crack a layered security system and plunder the druids' hidden relics. Perched upon the highest reaches of the Stonetalon Mountains, the Talon Den serves as an underground redoubt for night elf druids. Carved deep into living stone, these barrow halls are designed to shield meditating guardians and shelter sacred treasures away from prying eyes. Knowing the strategic and arcane value of what rests within, Braelyn Firehand interrogates a captured druid to pry loose the secrets of their defenses.

quest:1090.text: Gerenzo's Orders. At the Venture Company dig site in Stonetalon Mountains, an ousted goblin named Piznik schemes to expose his new boss, Gerenzo. By defending Piznik from camp patrols while he extracts a strange gold-green ore, adventurers help uncover the lucrative secrets behind the company's aggressive excavation. The Venture Company's massive operations within Stonetalon rely on cutthroat competition, where promotions are won through ruthlessness rather than loyalty. Piznik once enjoyed the status of being second-in-command at the excavation until Gerenzo seized power, ousted supervisor Ziz Fizziks, and demoted Piznik to swinging a pick in the dirt. Rather than walking away, Piznik stayed on as an informant under Ziz's instructions, watching Gerenzo's every move and biding his time to strike back at his treacherous new supervisor. Gerenzo's sudden takeover is driven by an obsession with a mysterious gold-green ore running through the Stonetalon rocks. Believing the mineral holds extraordinary commercial value, Gerenzo ordered miners to rip massive quantities out of the earth. Suspecting that Ziz Fizziks's mysterious new employer will pay handsomely for information on the venture, Piznik risks discovery to dig up a pristine sample while reliant on an ally to fend off aggressive diggers, vermin, and overseers who police the operation.

quest:1091.text: Kaela's Update. Kaela's Update is an Alliance dispatch in the Stonetalon Mountains, carrying captured correspondence between frontline operatives. The gnome mage Gaxim Rustfizzle sends the adventurer back to Kaela Shadowspear with intercepted Venture Company letters. The intelligence helps the night elf Sentinels track the goblin cartel's destructive expansion across sacred lands. After assisting the gnome mage Gaxim Rustfizzle in uncovering the movements of the Venture Company, he compiles recovered letters detailing the cartel's operations. Not one to pass up credit, Gaxim sends the player directly back to Kaela Shadowspear, the night elf Sentinel coordinator stationed near Windshear Crag. He makes sure to remind the courier to mention how his magical prowess made the investigation a success. The Sentinels stationed in Stonetalon watch the crags with growing concern. While Horde forces contest the lower trails, the Venture Company's clear-cutting and mining apparatus pose an immediate ecological and tactical threat. The letters recovered by Gaxim grant Kaela valuable insights into the cartel's internal communications, bolstering the Alliance's defensive planning along the ridges.

quest:1092.text: Gerenzo's Orders. Having fought off the dig site's patrols and secured a sample of the strange ore Gerenzo ordered mined, Piznik dispatches adventurers to take the specimen to his contact, Ziz Fizziks. The delivery wraps up a risky act of corporate espionage deep in the Venture Company operations of Windshear Crag. With his cover blown by the fight at the dig site, Piznik knows his time among the Venture Company crew at Windshear Crag has expired. Corporate management in Undermine does not take kindly to internal sabotage, prompting the nervous goblin to orchestrate his escape. Before slipping away to seek a new employer, he entrusts the Unidentified Ore mined under Gerenzo's orders to an outsider, ensuring the prized specimen gets delivered safely without drawing suspicion to himself.

quest:1093.text: Super Reaper 6000. Super Reaper 6000 is a quest offered by the disgruntled goblin tinkerer Ziz Fizziks in the Windshear Crag of the Stonetalon Mountains. Looking to curry favor with his new boss Sputtervalve, Ziz hires adventurers to infiltrate the local Venture Company logging operation and steal the schematic blueprints for a colossal woodcutting machine designed by his rival, the gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. The Venture Trading Company has carved an industrial scar straight into the heart of the Stonetalon Mountains, ruthlessly deforesting Windshear Crag. Yet beneath the smog and spinning blades lies petty corporate rivalry. Ziz Fizziks, a goblin engineer recently cast out of the Venture Company's ranks, has found employment with Sputtervalve. Eager to cement his position and show off his value, Ziz seeks to procure the Venture Company's most prized mechanical asset: the blueprints for their massive automated lumber engine, the Super Reaper 6000.

quest:1094.text: Further Instructions. Further Instructions is a delivery task connecting the chaotic logging operations of the Stonetalon Mountains to the trade hub of Ratchet. The disgruntled tinkerer Ziz Fizziks sends a courier with stolen blueprints and internal documents to his counterpart, Sputtervalve, aiming to turn corporate espionage into personal advantage. When Ziz Fizziks was booted out of the Venture Company's logging operations in the Windshear Crag, he did not leave empty-handed. Bitter over his dismissal, Fizziks snatched up an assortment of sensitive documents, internal manuals, and technical schematics, culminating in the prized blueprints for the experimental Super Reaper 6000. Desperate to find a buyer or ally willing to exploit the data, he sealed the gathered secrets into an envelope marked for Ratchet. The recipient of the stolen documents is Sputtervalve, an engineer stationed within the neutral port of Ratchet in the Barrens. While Sputtervalve harbors little personal affection or trust for Fizziks, the rivalry with the Venture Company makes the offering impossible to refuse. The Steamwheedle-aligned goblins are constantly looking for ways to diminish their ruthless competitor's footprint while happily reverse-engineering any superior mechanical innovations they stumble across.

quest:1095.text: Further Instructions. Further Instructions marks an escalation in goblin corporate politics, ordering the assassination of a rogue gnome engineer hired by Mogul Razdunk. Sputtervalve delivers directives originating from high within Undermine, commanding Ziz Fizziks to eliminate Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle in the Stonetalon Mountains. The Venture Company operates under ruthless profit motives, but hiring outsider talent can spark fierce internal friction. When Mogul Razdunk brought the gnome engineer Gerenzo into the fold, word reached Undermine and ruffled feathers among the ruling Trade Princes. Director Riddlevox instructed Sputtervalve to intervene and handle the situation quietly. Sputtervalve, deducing that the order stems from the highest trade authorities, passes down the dirty work to the operative closest to the scene: Ziz Fizziks.

quest:1096.text: Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. This bounty tasks adventurers with eliminating Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a rogue gnome overseer perched high above Cragpool Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gerenzo has heavily augmented his decaying flesh with gears, clockwork machinery, and artificial limbs. The goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks seeks his mechanical arm as indisputable proof of his demise to earn a coveted promotion from his superiors. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle is infamous even among veteran tinkerers for his gruesome physical transformations. By the account of those who have seen him, his natural flesh appears to be rotting away, patched over by grafted gears, iron plating, and whirring clockwork prosthetics. Perched near the massive water wheel perched high above Cragpool Lake, the gnome watches over operations with mechanical precision and an unsettling disregard for his own mortal biology. Ziz Fizziks, a goblin operating on behalf of Sputtervalve, sees Gerenzo's downfall as his golden ticket out of Stonetalon's backwaters. Lacking the physical prowess to fight up the cliffs or defeat the augmented overseer himself, Ziz enlists an adventurer to take Gerenzo down and recover his mechanical arm. Armed with this trophy, Ziz hopes to demonstrate his worth and secure a transfer to the prestigious Tinkers' Union workshops in Gadgetzan or Undermine. The recovery of Gerenzo's mechanical arm highlights the profound ideological divide between goblin and gnome engineering traditions. While Gerenzo took the extreme gnomish step of amputating failing flesh to integrate complex prosthetics, goblins find the sacrifice baffling. As Ziz points out, true goblin ingenuity wouldn't discard a biological limb—it would simply mount an explosive third arm alongside the other two.

quest:1098.text: Deathstalkers in Shadowfang. High Executor Hadrec dispatches Horde adventurers into Shadowfang Keep to locate two missing reconnaissance agents, Deathstalker Adamant and Deathstalker Vincent. The Forsaken military relies on their gathered intelligence to coordinate an assault against Archmage Arugal and his worgen packs. Breaching the fortress reveals the grim reality of espionage behind enemy lines. Silverpine Forest remains contested ground, with Archmage Arugal's feral worgen holding the towering redoubt of Shadowfang Keep. Seeking to break this siege on their southern borders, the Forsaken command stationed at the Sepulcher organized an intelligence operation. High Executor Hadrec sent two seasoned Deathstalkers—Adamant and Vincent—to infiltrate the fortress and chart its defenses. When days passed without word, Hadrec grew desperate for their field reports, tasking capable Horde champions with entering the stronghold to recover the agents and salvage the mission.

quest:1100.text: Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is an Alliance quest initiated by finding a weathered book held in the hand of a dead dwarf at the base of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. The notes detail his final journey and prompt the finder to deliver the volume west to a night elf druid stationed on the Feralas border. Near the base of the Great Lift, the massive mechanical elevator connecting the Barrens to the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, lies the body of Henrig Lonebrow. Clutched in his hand is a personal journal detailing his travels through this rugged territory. Left behind in a hostile desert dominated by centaur and tauren, his corpse serves as a grim warning of how unforgiving the canyon can be to isolated travelers. Reading through Henrig's journal reveals his intended path and final wish. Rather than leaving his findings to decay in the canyon, the explorer hoped his records would reach friendly hands. Following the road straight west across Thousand Needles leads out of the dry gullies and toward Thalanaar, the night elf outpost guarding the border to Feralas, where the druid Falfindel Waywarder awaits news of the traveler.

quest:1101.text: The Crone of the Kraul. The Crone of the Kraul is an Alliance quest offered by Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, on the border of Feralas and the Thousand Needles. After reading the recovered journal of the fallen dwarf Henrig Lonebrow, Falfindel tasks adventurers with infiltrating Razorfen Kraul and slaying the quilboar crone, Charlga Razorflank. At the secluded night elf outpost of Thalanaar, Falfindel Waywarder grieves for the druid Heralath and the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow. Lonebrow, an Explorers' League traveler captured by the quilboar, escaped Razorfen Kraul only to die on the road, leaving behind a tattered journal detailing the growing menace within Razorfen Kraul. Realizing there is no time to send a runner to Darnassus for military reinforcements, Falfindel turns to passing adventurers to strike directly at the heart of the thorned dens. The target of the expedition is Charlga Razorflank, an ancient geomancer and ruthless matriarch who has united the fractious Razorfen quilboar under her iron rule. From the depths of the Kraul, she marshals a bristling army that threatens neighboring lands. Adventurers must carve through thick thorn mazes, battlement walls, and swarms of fanatical quilboar warriors to corner Charlga and pry her medallion from her lifeless body as proof of her downfall.

quest:1103.text: Call of Water. This quest offers a second chance for shamans completing their spiritual trials along the coast of Silverpine Forest. If a shaman's spirit-sight fades before communing with the purified manifestation of water, Tiev Mordune stands by to rekindle the communion. By providing another Water Sapta, the petitioner can witness the ritual anew and finish their communion. The path to mastering water is fraught with delicate spiritual timings. Shamans drink a potent draught known as a Water Sapta to perceive the spirits lingering around the elemental shrines. Should the draught's magic lapse before the shaman speaks with the Minor Manifestation of Water, they find themselves locked outside the spirit realm, unable to complete their trial. Fortunately, fellow shaman Tiev Mordune lingers on the fog-shrouded shores of Silverpine Forest to assist those whose visions ended too soon. Tiev Mordune, having already conquered the corrupt water spirit lurking off the coast, waits with his gathered ritual remnants. He requires proof of readiness in the form of a fresh Water Sapta from Islen Waterseer in the Barrens. Once presented with the sapta, Tiev casts his gathered bracers and droplets into the shrine's brazier, summoning forth the pure manifestation once more so his fellow shaman can speak with it and seal their elemental bond.

quest:1104.text: Salt Flat Venom. Out on the blinding salt expanse of the Shimmering Flats, gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts searches for unusual ingredients to supercharge his rocket car. Convinced that the intensely saline venom of local scorpids will produce an ultra-hot burning propellant, he tasks passing adventurers with braving the stinging beasts. The Mirage Raceway is an endless battle of high-speed technical supremacy between gnomish precision and goblin audacity. For Fizzle Brassbolts, standard hydrocarbons and clockwork parts simply are not enough to outpace the competition. He envisions a custom fuel mixture tailored to burn far hotter than conventional propellants, driving their rocket cars across the dried salt lake at blistering speeds. Fizzle's breakthrough relies on the dangerous native fauna of the Shimmering Flats. The local scorpids have evolved to survive in an arid, salt-encrusted wasteland, resulting in an exceptionally saline venom. Rather than fearing its deadly toxicity, Fizzle sees it as a raw chemical payload. Once boiled, refined, and treated with exotic catalytic agents, he believes the salty venom will deliver the explosive combustion required to leave the goblin pit crews in the dust.

quest:1105.text: Hardened Shells. At the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats, the gnome tinkerer Wizzle Brassbolts worries his brother's potent new rocket fuel will dissolve their racer from the inside out. To prevent a catastrophe on the salt flats, Wizzle enlists passersby to harvest hardened shells from the local tortoises to craft an impervious fuel tank. Out in the blinding heat of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between gnome and goblin engineers pushes mechanical ambition to reckless extremes. Wizzle Brassbolts and his brother are determined to dominate the Mirage Raceway with their custom rocket car. However, his brother's experimental fuel mixture is showing signs of being far too potent. Fearing that the corrosive concoction will melt straight through the vehicle's standard chassis and tanks, Wizzle scrambles to find a container tough enough to survive the run. Rather than relying on refined metals that might dissolve under chemical strain, Wizzle turns to the natural adaptations of the salt flats. The native tortoises roaming Thousand Needles possess shells remarkably resistant to harsh elements and mechanical wear. By gathering these hardened carapaces, Wizzle hopes to fashion custom fuel tanks resilient enough to hold the volatile mixture without blowing the rocket car to pieces.

quest:1106.text: Martek the Exiled. Fizzle Brassbolts is building a new engine for his car, but he cannot make pistons hard enough to take the strain. He sends you with a letter to a great smith named Martek the Exiled, far off in a camp in the Badlands. After Salt Flat Venom, Fizzle at the Mirage Raceway explains that his new engine should make the car so fast it could fly. All his trials have failed because he cannot make pistons hard enough for the heavy stress. He knows one person who might know how: Martek the Exiled, a great smith who knows more about metal than anyone. Martek is a long way off in the Badlands, camped there with a goblin, and you carry Fizzle's letter to him.

quest:1107.text: Encrusted Tail Fins. Wizzle Brassbolts at the Mirage Raceway fears the rocket car is so fast that friction will tear it apart. To protect it, he needs tail fins from the Saltscale murlocs at the Vile Reef, off the coast of Stranglethorn Vale. Wizzle calls the rocket car the fastest thing on the Shimmering Flats, and worries that friction will tear it apart. The moving parts need a coat of composite that is hard but not brittle, and able to resist salt corrosion, or the flats will eat the car away. Its key ingredient is the tail fins of the Saltscale murlocs, who live at the Vile Reef, off the coast of Stranglethorn Vale. You are asked to bring Wizzle ten of them.

quest:1108.text: Indurium. Martek the Exiled says the Badlands hold a wealth of metal for anyone with the nerve to get it. Indurium is said to stand up to heat and stress, and Martek wants samples to test whether it could serve Fizzle's racecar. Stonevault troggs out in the Badlands are the ones carrying flakes of it. Martek the Exiled tells you he is not out in the Badlands just to avoid company. The region holds indurium, a metal said to stand up to heat and stress, and it might do for Fizzle's car. Martek wants samples to test, and has the forge hot and waiting. The true ore is deep in Uldaman, but Stonevault troggs in the Badlands carry flakes of it now and then. Martek asks for ten. The troggs that have them roam the south-east slope of a rocky clump at Agmond's End, just south of the Valley of Fangs.

quest:1110.text: Rocket Car Parts. Rocket Car Parts is an errand undertaken for the opportunistic dwarf merchant Kravel Koalbeard on the blinding salt pans of the Shimmering Flats. Rather than letting the violently scattered debris of high-speed racer crashes go to waste, Koalbeard pays wanderers to comb the desert floor and recover wrecked mechanisms to resell directly to the rival gnome and goblin pit crews. The Shimmering Flats serve as the proving ground for the fierce technological rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers. High-velocity experimental rocket cars routinely suffer catastrophic malfunctions, leaving twisted gears, cylinders, and jagged sheets of metal scattered wide across the vast white desert. While the pit crews focus solely on building and tuning the next machine, the desert floor has quietly become a scrap yard of experimental engineering. Rather than competing directly on the track, the dwarf entrepreneur Kravel Koalbeard recognized a lucrative middleman opportunity at the Mirage Raceway. Gnome and goblin mechanics burn through parts at a furious pace and are constantly desperate for spare mechanisms to slap onto their vehicles. Koalbeard hires travelers to gather thirty bundles of shattered debris, turning devastating crashes into fresh inventory and neatly profiting off the drivers' misfortunes.

quest:1111.text: Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Kravel Koalbeard, a dwarf at the Mirage Raceway, makes it his business to get people what they need. The gnomes there are waiting on parts that reached Ratchet a week ago, and Kravel cannot go himself. He sends you to Ratchet with his parts order for Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Kravel Koalbeard sees to it that people get the things they need. The gnomes of the Mirage Raceway are waiting on a batch of parts that reached Ratchet a week ago, and Kravel cannot make the journey himself. He asks you to do the legwork, and promises more jobs with serious profit potential if you do. Ratchet lies in the Barrens. Wharfmaster Dizzywig, a goblin, is the one to see, and Kravel says Dizzywig will probably be at the docks. You carry Kravel's Parts Order there.

quest:1112.text: Parts for Kravel. Having brought Kravel Koalbeard's parts order to Wharfmaster Dizzywig, you now carry Kravel's package back to him at the Mirage Raceway on the Shimmering Flats. Dizzywig sends a message along with it: if Kravel wants more special orders, he will have to pay his tab. Wharfmaster Dizzywig gives you a package meant for Kravel Koalbeard, who waits at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats of Thousand Needles. Dizzywig asks you to pass on a warning with it: if Kravel hopes for more special orders, he must first pay what he owes.

quest:1114.text: Delivery to the Gnomes. Kravel Koalbeard now has what he needs, and wants the Delicate Car Parts carried to Fizzle Brassbolts in the Shimmering Flats, who has waited a long time for them. Kravel admits he removed a little piece from Fizzle's order, and suggests you leave it unmentioned. Kravel Koalbeard tells you the parts are for Fizzle Brassbolts, who has been waiting a long time. Kravel confesses he took one little piece out of Fizzle's order, but feels sure it will not be missed. He calls the piece small and worthless, advises you not to bring it up, and asks you to trust him.

quest:1115.text: The Rumormonger. Having done a service for the gnomes, Kravel Koalbeard now wants to do the goblins a favor. He has heard that Nazz Steamboil, the goblin racer pilot, once went by another name, and wonders whether it is a secret worth money. He sends you to Krazek of Booty Bay, who would know. Kravel Koalbeard says the goblins are next in line for a favor. Nazz Steamboil, the goblin racer pilot, once went by another name, he hears, and Kravel wonders why it changed, whether it hides a secret, and whether Nazz cares to keep it hidden. The one who would know the truth, Kravel says, is Krazek, down at the southern tip of Stranglethorn in Booty Bay. Useful information might turn a profit. Look for Krazek at the Salty Sailor Tavern.

quest:1116.text: Dream Dust in the Swamp. Krazek of Booty Bay says that learning about Nazz is quite a favor. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to bring 10 specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, for Krazek's snuff pouch. Bring it back and Krazek will give you the information you seek. Krazek tells you that learning about Nazz is a considerable favor, and that you have already come a long way from the Shimmering Flats for it. While Krazek contacts sources, you are asked to gather something. The choice falls on ten specks of dream dust, taken from dragon whelps in the Swamp of Sorrows, which Krazek would love for a snuff pouch. Once you return with it, the information is yours. Green dragons of the Swamp of Sorrows carry the dream dust. Adolescent whelps and dreaming whelps both have it, and both live in the swamp's south-western corner.

quest:1117.text: Rumors for Kravel. Krazek has found what you came for. After calling in favors, doing plenty of deducing and giving up a rare bottle of elven wine, Krazek wrote a letter about Nazz Steamboil. It is too dangerous for Krazek to use, so you carry it to Kravel Koalbeard, out on the Shimmering Flats, and you are asked not to say where it came from. Krazek tells you what the search cost: some favors were used up, a rare bottle of elven wine was parted with, and a good deal of deducing was done. The result is a letter holding some very interesting bits about Nazz Steamboil. Krazek finds it too dangerous to use, and leaves it to you to do with as you will, as long as nobody learns where it came from. It goes back to Kravel Koalbeard, out on the Shimmering Flats.

quest:1130.text: Melor Sends Word. Melor Sends Word is a summons delivered by Jorn Skyseer in the Barrens on behalf of the renowned hunter Melor Stonehoof. Rising adventurers who have proven their grit across Kalimdor are directed to Hunter's Rise in Thunder Bluff to receive a far more demanding trial. Word travels fast across the plains. As an adventurer cuts their teeth in the Barrens and surrounding lands, notable hunters take notice of those who show true promise. Jorn Skyseer, keeping watch over the crossings and encampments, serves as an emissary for the elders of Hunter's Rise. He intercepts promising hunters and warriors to let them know that Melor Stonehoof, a revered mentor among the tauren, has marked out a specific path for them. Upon climbing the heights of Hunter's Rise in Thunder Bluff, the seeker meets Melor himself. The elder hunter does not offer praise, but rather asks whether the adventurer possesses the resolve to venture into perilous, distant wilderness. Answering the summons unlocks testing grounds that stretch far beyond the safety of Mulgore, pitting hunters against the fiercest predators across the continent.

quest:1131.text: Steelsnap. Steelsnap is a hunting task issued by Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. The hunt departs from traditional tauren reasons for killing, seeking the destruction of a vicious hyena whose pack terrorizes the wildlife of Thousand Needles. Tauren tradition dictates that taking a life must serve a sacred or practical purpose: hunting for sustenance, hunting to uphold honor, or hunting to glean wisdom from the Earthmother. Melor Stonehoof offers this quarry as an exception to the rule. Steelsnap is viewed as an abomination against natural balance—a brutal tyrant that sows senseless violence and fear rather than maintaining the cycle of life. Steelsnap roams the canyons of northern Thousand Needles, lingering south of the centaur enclave at Camp E'thok. Unlike solitary scavengers, this formidable beast draws fierce packmates into his wake, orchestrating attacks that disrupt and cull the more docile wildlife of the canyon floor. Slaying him and retrieving his rib cleanses the needles of his vicious influence.

quest:1133.text: Journey to Astranaar. Journey to Astranaar is an introductory Alliance quest guiding newcomers arriving on the Kalimdor coast to the inland heart of Ashenvale. Directed by Fiora Longears at Theramore, travelers make their way north toward Ashenvale to report to Shindrell Swiftfire in Astranaar. It marks an adventurer's entry into the growing conflicts surrounding the night elves' ancestral forest. Alliance travelers arriving in Dustwallow Marsh aboard the ferry from Menethil Harbor often look for purpose in northern Kalimdor. At Theramore, Fiora Longears directs capable hands to move deeper inland toward Astranaar, the main night elven settlement within Ashenvale. The journey follows winding paths under ancient, shadowed canopies, leading straight into a forest strained by war and unrest. Curiously, Fiora tells travelers not to bother mentioning her name when arriving in Astranaar, stating plainly that Shindrell Swiftfire does not know her. Her role is simply to funnel fresh Alliance talent where it is needed most. Upon arriving, Shindrell readily welcomes any able-bodied defender, acknowledging that while Ashenvale remains breathtaking, it is no longer the peaceful sanctuary it once was.

quest:1134.text: Pridewings of Stonetalon. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim: Concerned about covert Horde attacks, the Sentinels in Astranaar seek to intercept a deadly weapon before it can strike their people. Intelligence from Theramore reveals that orc assassins harvest toxic venom from the wyverns of Stonetalon Mountains for clandestine raids. To protect their fragile border, Alliance scouts are dispatched south to harvest the venom sacs first and starve the enemy of their lethal poison. Though open war has not been declared between the Alliance and the Horde across northern Kalimdor, the peace between them is razor-thin. Skirmishes break out under thick forest canopies, and quiet, deniable strikes have replaced full-scale armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar maintain constant vigilance against covert enemy movements, knowing that complacency could cost them their sanctuary. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim: Intelligence passed from secretive contacts in Theramore brought word of a sinister enterprise underway in the crags of Stonetalon. Orcish stalkers have been gathering venom from wild pridewings around Mirkfallon Lake, using the potent biological agent to coat their blades for fatal ambush raids against Alliance personnel. To blunt the threat, Shindrell Swiftfire directs champions to cull the beasts and seize the venom sacs before Horde agents can harvest them. Ordering the destruction of native beasts weighs heavily on the night elves, who hold deep reverence for Kalimdor's wilderness. Shindrell herself laments that innocent creatures must suffer for a war they have no role in choosing. Yet in the grim calculus of border defense, denying an enemy lethal arms takes precedence over ecological preservation.

quest:1135.text: Highperch Venom. Fiora Longears in Theramore tasks Alliance adventurers with journeying west to the canyons of Thousand Needles. There, atop the elevated bluffs of Highperch, roost dangerous wyverns prized for their exceptionally potent venom. While resting in the island port of Theramore, travelers may cross paths with Fiora Longears. While orcs commonly capture and domesticate wyverns as aerial mounts, Fiora points out a far more clandestine trade: the creature's lethal venom. Certain buyers across Kalimdor value fresh venom sacs far more than the beasts themselves, prompting Fiora to recruit hunters willing to brave long distances and precarious heights. The quarry nests west of Dustwallow Marsh, within the towering sandstone mesas of Thousand Needles. At a roost known as Highperch, the local wyverns possess an unusually concentrated toxin. Reaching their nests requires navigating hostile Horde territory and scaling treacherous terrain, where hunters must slay wyverns to extract intact venom sacs before hauling the prize back to Theramore.

quest:1137.text: News for Fizzle. Martek the Exiled in the Badlands has news about indurium for Fizzle Brassbolts. You carry Martek's message back to the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Martek reports that indurium stands up to heat remarkably well, and believes it suits Fizzle's pistons. Flakes will not do, though: Fizzle needs real indurium ore, dug out of the depths of Uldaman at the northern edge of the Badlands, which Martek names as the true source of indurium. Martek asks you to pass on regards and repeat all of this to Fizzle Brassbolts.

quest:1140.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest represents the sixth chapter in the crusade against the cultists of the Tower of Althalaxx, directed by Delgren the Purifier from Maestra's Post. Delgren deciphers orcish writings recovered from the cult's emissaries to reveal that the warlock Athrikus Narassin has hidden two trapped Highborne soulgems inside demonic satyr strongholds deep in Ashenvale. Champions are dispatched to Night Run and Satyrnaar to shatter these vessels, freeing the tormented ancient spirits and shattering Athrikus's dark source of power. After cutting down the orcish courier Ilkrud Magthrull, Delgren the Purifier puts his controversial studies of the Orcish tongue to good use. While his peers in the Holy Light often scoffed at learning the language of their adversaries, Delgren's pragmatic insight unravels the cult's clandestine trade. The notes reveal that Athrikus Narassin secured two potent soulgems containing the essences of ancient Highborne, hiding them far to the northeast within the defiled groves of Night Run and Satyrnaar.

quest:1142.text: Mortality Wanes. Deep within the hostile briars of Razorfen Kraul, a dying night elf named Heralath Fallowbrook whispers his final plea to passing Alliance adventurers. Stripped of his strength and life, he asks only that his wife's stolen pendant of bonding be recovered and brought home to Darnassus alongside news of his demise. Razorfen Kraul is a perilous redoubt overrun by savage quilboar and dark magic, far from Alliance territory. Among these treacherous brambles lies Heralath Fallowbrook, mortally wounded and fading fast. With his dying strength, he manages only broken whispers, revealing that a brave dwarf named Lonebrow was sent ahead to deliver a warning to Falfindel. Heralath, however, knows he will never leave the Kraul alive. Before succumbing to his wounds, Heralath clings to one final wish: retrieving a token of his marriage. A pendant symbolizing his eternal bond with his wife, Treshala, was torn from him by one of the lair's foul aggressors. He begs any traveler who stops beside him to recover the pendant and carry it all the way across Kalimdor to Darnassus, ensuring Treshala learns the truth of his lonely death rather than waiting in vain.

quest:1143.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks the direct assault on Athrikus Narassin, the ancient dark sorcerer holding the pinnacle of the Tower of Althalaxx. Under the direction of Balthule Shadowstrike, an Alliance operative must breach the ruined keep and execute the cabal's master. Eliminating Athrikus strikes a devastating blow to the demonic worship corrupting northern Darkshore. Perched upon the ruined heights of northern Darkshore, the Tower of Althalaxx has become a foul center of demonic summoning. Balthule Shadowstrike, monitoring the ruin from nearby, determines that the time to act is immediate. At the tower's peak dwells Athrikus Narassin, an ancient and formidable night elven warlock who orchestrates the dark rituals taking place beneath its shattered stone roof.

quest:1147.text: The Swarm Grows. Moktar Krin at Ironstone Camp says Belgrom wants the silithid pushed back into the depths they crawled out of. Moktar's own half-dead war party cannot do it, so Moktar asks you to take on the silithid at the dig site to the south. After The Swarm Grows (2), Moktar Krin says Belgrom considers the silithid a threat and wants them driven back into whatever depths they came from. Having already killed the dwarves the Explorers' League sent, Moktar now has a war party in no state to fight again, and cannot do it without help. The dig site lies to the south, and Moktar expects no more dwarves there. Searchers, hive drones and invaders are the silithid to be killed, and Moktar's party cannot leave until it is done.

quest:1149.text: Test of Faith. The Test of Faith is a spiritual rite administered by the hermit Dorn Plainstalker high above the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. It challenges Horde adventurers to prove their resolve by stepping off a precarious wooden plank into the open chasm below. Dorn Plainstalker dwells in a secluded vantage overlooking the wind-carved spires of Thousand Needles, pondering the facets that make up a living being: the mind, the body, and the spirit. Rather than relying on simple tribal traditions, Dorn administers his own trials to measure what truly lies within an adventurer. He posits that while conviction can take many forms, the essential quality is simply having the fortitude to believe in something strongly enough to risk one's life on it.

quest:115.text: Shadow Magic. Shadow Magic is a desperate task given by Marshal Marris to disrupt the dark arts bolstering the Blackrock invasion of Redridge. Blackrock shadowcasters have brought demon-tainted midnight orbs to the battlefield, weaponizing dark energies against the beleaguered defenders of Lakeshire. Securing and destroying these cursed relics is vital to holding the town's defensive line. While brute force has always been the hallmark of the Blackrock clan, their recent incursions into the Redridge Mountains display a far more insidious threat. The invaders have bolstered their ranks with shadowcasters wielding dark powers. These casters do not rely on sorcery alone; they channel their fel and shadow energies through demon-tainted artifacts known as midnight orbs. The artifacts have inflicted terrible losses upon the local town militia, tilting an already desperate war further in favor of the invaders. Marshal Marris, coordinating Lakeshire's strained defense from the town center, understands that ordinary steel cannot easily overcome dark relics. Allowing the Blackrock orcs to retain their midnight orbs risks the complete collapse of Redridge's eastern borders. By ordering adventurers to slay the shadowcasters and seize the orbs, Marris seeks not to repurpose this dangerous magic, but to have the demonic relics destroyed.

quest:1150.text: Test of Endurance. The Test of Endurance is the second rite in a series of spiritual trials overseen by Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles. Having already proven their courage of spirit, Horde adventurers are tasked with pushing their physical endurance to the limit by infiltrating Roguefeather Den and drawing out the fierce harpy leader, Grenka Bloodscreech. Dorn Plainstalker, dwelling at the Weathered Nook, takes it upon himself to temper young warriors before they venture into the wider, harsher world. Where the initial rite proved that a traveler possessed unshakable faith and steady nerve, this trial tests physical fortitude. In Dorn's philosophy, true readiness requires harmony between spiritual devotion, mental discipline, and the sheer stamina to survive sustained brutality. The chosen arena for this trial is Roguefeather Den, a treacherous cavern tucked within Screeching Canyon west of Freewind Post. Swarming with hostile harpies, the cave poses severe danger to solitary wanderers. To complete the trial, challengers must carve their way deep into the subterranean roost, sabotage the harpies' gathered provisions, and weather the flock's ferocious retaliation until the matriarch Grenka Bloodscreech herself takes the field.

quest:1151.text: Test of Strength. The Test of Strength is the third trial overseen by the tauren mystic Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles. To prove their physical prowess, Horde champions are tasked with hunting down Rok'Alim the Pounder, an ancient, free-roaming rock elemental, and returning with remnants of his shattered form. Long ago, during the reign of the Old Gods, primordial elementals blanketed the surface of the world, serving their dark masters. When those ancient entities were overthrown and sealed beneath the earth, the elemental spirits lost their tether to this realm, largely fading from physical existence unless bound and summoned by modern spellcraft. A few entities, however, were stubborn and potent enough to linger on Azeroth indefinitely without magical anchors. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such relic, wandering the arid canyons of Thousand Needles as a living echo of that primordial age. The local centaur clans gave Rok'Alim his moniker on account of the deafening, earthquake-like crashes produced when his stone fists strike the canyon floor. Anyone foolish or bold enough to stray into his roaming path is hammered into dust. Because Rok'Alim represents raw, unbridled physical mass, Dorn Plainstalker directs initiates to break the beast as a direct measure of their warrior spirit, demanding fragments of the elemental's stony heart as proof of victory.

quest:1152.text: Test of Lore. Following trials of faith, endurance, and strength in Thousand Needles, Dorn Plainstalker directs Horde champions northward to Stonetalon Mountains. There, a wise shaman named Braug Dimspirit waits to administer the Test of Lore. This trial shifts the focus from physical resolve to an understanding of the world's deep history and widespread suffering. In the sheltered refuge of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker pushes initiates through demanding trials meant to test their spiritual conviction, physical endurance, and martial prowess. Yet brute strength and blind faith alone do not make a true champion of the Horde. Dorn recognizes his own boundaries as a teacher and sends those who have proven themselves to Stonetalon Mountains, where an elder shaman can test their intellect and worldliness. The journey takes travelers north across the dry scrub of the Barrens and into the crags of Stonetalon. High in the mountains, near the entrance to Talondeep Path—the cavern cutting through the rock toward Ashenvale—sits the hermitage of Braug Dimspirit. He watches over an embattled frontier where goblin logging ventures despoil the forests and hostile night elves fiercely defend their ancestral borders.

quest:1153.text: A New Ore Sample. Tatternack Steelforge in Camp Taurajo has heard rumors of an unusual mineral deposit carried by kobolds far to the south. Determined to satisfy Warchief Thrall's demand for stronger arms, he sends Horde adventurers into Thousand Needles to secure an unrefined ore sample for testing. Operating out of the dusty outpost of Camp Taurajo, the blacksmith Tatternack Steelforge works under the direct scrutiny of Orgrimmar. Having already supplied weaponry made from local centaur armaments, Tatternack remains driven to prove his craft to Warchief Thrall. When passing travelers refused to sell him a strange piece of ore they looted from a kobold to the south, Tatternack took the refusal as an insult to both his craft and the Horde. The quest takes Horde scouts out of the flat plains of the southern Barrens and into the towering canyon mazes of Thousand Needles. There, subterranean vermin dig through the crags and cliffs. By prying unrefined mineral chunks directly from the local kobold diggers, adventurers return with the raw material Tatternack needs to evaluate whether this new stone can be forged into weapons worthy of Thrall's war effort.

quest:1154.text: Test of Lore. The Test of Lore is a trial set by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to Talondeep Path, testing a Horde adventurer's mind rather than their physical endurance. To pass, the seeker must venture deep into the haunted barrow dens of Ashenvale, recover an ancient tome of dragon history, and study its contents before being quizzed. After proving their physical endurance and unwavering faith across the salt flats and plateaus of Thousand Needles, candidates under Dorn Plainstalker's series of trials are sent north to Braug Dimspirit in the Stonetalon Mountains. Stationed near the mouth of Talondeep Path, Braug dismisses the earlier challenges as simple physical exercises. To truly serve the Horde with distinction, an adventurer requires a sharp and disciplined intellect, prepared to understand ancient histories rather than merely striking down beasts. Braug directs petitioners to venture through Talondeep Path into the forested reaches of southern Ashenvale. There, hidden beneath the canopy south of Splintertree Post, lies the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The subterranean sanctuary is a perilous ruin haunted by fallen night elf druids and the vicious creatures that slaughtered them. Rested upon a stony podium deep in the lower chambers lies the prize: 'Legacy of the Aspects', a rare manuscript detailing the ancient creation and corruption of the great Dragon Aspects.

quest:1159.text: Test of Lore. This leg of the Test of Lore sends Horde adventurers across the Great Sea to the ruins of Lordaeron. Having answered Braug Dimspirit's initial riddle in the Stonetalon Mountains, you are directed to seek a former human scholar among the Forsaken in the Undercity. After proving your mettle and unraveling the history of the Dragon Aspects recorded in the Legacy of the Aspects, Braug Dimspirit admits his own knowledge has limits. Rather than keeping the trial confined to Kalimdor, Braug demonstrates the broad, surprising reach of the Horde's ties by pointing you toward the undead capital beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. In the damp corridors of the Apothecarium dwells Parqual Fintallas. Once an esteemed human chronicler of the northern kingdoms, Parqual's pursuit of knowledge survived the Scourge and his transformation into one of the Forsaken. Confronted by an outsider claiming to have completed the spiritual and physical trials of Thousand Needles, Parqual refuses to believe you are anything more than an opportunistic mercenary until you prove your worth to him directly.

quest:1167.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks the tense pause before confronting Athrikus Narassin at the Tower of Althalaxx. Sent northward by Delgren the Purifier, adventurers reconvene with the scout Balthule Shadowstrike to gather intelligence on erratic, dark occurrences rocking the spire. After purifying corrupted relics and unraveling the cult's grip along Darkshore's border, Delgren the Purifier dispatches you back north to consult his sentinel partner, Balthule Shadowstrike. Before assaulting the sorcerer Athrikus directly, Delgren recognizes the necessity of fresh battlefield reconnaissance, trusting Balthule's tireless watch from the ruins overlooking the tower.

quest:1175.text: A Bump in the Road. Trackmaster Zherin looks after the track at the Mirage Raceway, and the animals out on the Shimmering Flats have grown big enough that their numbers must be kept down before they wander onto it. You are asked to thin out Saltstone Basilisks, Crystalhides and Gazers. A basilisk once collided with a racer belonging to the goblins, the Red Thunder, and in the aftermath Kronkrider took Zherin on to look after the track. Zherin cannot say what the animals out on the Shimmering Flats are eating to get so big, only that their numbers have to be kept down, or one will stray onto the course mid-race. Clearing wreckage is bad enough, and Zherin would rather not pick it out of burnt animal parts as well.

quest:1176.text: Load Lightening. Pozzik, the head goblin engineer out at the Mirage Raceway, needs materials to shave critical ounces off his rocket-car chassis. Rather than relying purely on heavy metal plating, the goblins salvage hollow bones from local desert vultures to build sturdy, ultralight steering and structural rigs. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers is decided by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust is useless if a racer is weighed down by excessive bulk. While gnome teams obsess over intricate gears and brass fittings, the goblin crew led by Pozzik seeks ruthless pragmatic efficiency: stripping out dense iron framing and replacing it with lighter, hollow structural components wherever the frame permits. Rather than shipping expensive, specialized composites out to Thousand Needles, Pozzik turns to the surrounding salt wastes. Salt Flats vultures are plentiful, their skeletons honed by flight to possess hollow, honeycombed cores that provide great tensile strength with almost no mass. By substituting worked vulture bones into the racer's steering rig and minor braces, Pozzik's mechanics aim to keep their machines nimble enough to outmaneuver the gnomes without shaking apart at top speed.

quest:1178.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Pozzik of the goblin racing team is waiting on a prototype fuel regulator that Gazlowe promised a few weeks ago, and it has not come. Gazlowe is usually very prompt, so Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask what happened, since the gnomes are gaining on the team. Pozzik calls the racing team the pride of goblins, and says many people help it in one way or another. Gazlowe hunts down parts from all over the world for the team, and once even came to work on one of their rigs. A few weeks ago Gazlowe said a new prototype fuel regulator would be sent, but nothing has arrived, which is unlike him. With the gnomes gaining, Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask Gazlowe about it.

quest:1179.text: The Brassbolts Brothers. Pilot Longbeard in Ironforge needs a courier to deliver a crate of reinforced siege engine helmets across the sea to Kalimdor. His friends, the Brassbolts brothers, are testing high-speed rocket cars in the Shimmering Flats and urgently need head protection for their accident-prone test drivers. While stationed among his aerial machinery in Ironforge, the dwarven aviator Pilot Longbeard received an urgent request from the Shimmering Flats in southern Kalimdor. His friends, a pair of inventive gnomes known as the Brassbolts brothers, had taken up residence on the vast salt pans to race experimental machinery. Longbeard is tied down by military and piloting duties, leaving him unable to deliver the supplies himself. The Brassbolts' rocket car has turned out to be extraordinarily fast—so fast that their test drivers keep wiping out across the salt beds and suffering severe concussions. Longbeard procures a crate of heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets to protect their craniums. Delivering the crate gives the gnomes the leverage they need to coax reluctant pilots back behind the wheel of their volatile speed machine.

quest:1180.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Gazlowe is back to the matter you came about: the fuel regulator promised to Pozzik has not reached Ratchet. Revilgaz in Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. Gazlowe sends you to Wharfmaster Lozgil there, who can check the cargo records. Gazlowe admits he promised Pozzik a new fuel regulator and still has not received it. Revilgaz of Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. If so, there is not much to be done, but you can at least learn whether it left Booty Bay. Wharfmaster Lozgil, at the far northwestern end of the Booty Bay docks, can look through the cargo records.

quest:1181.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Wharfmaster Lozgil cannot help any further with the missing fuel regulator, and suggests you ask Baron Revilgaz himself. You will find the Baron at the tavern across the harbor in Booty Bay, on the top floor. Wharfmaster Lozgil tells you he cannot be of much more help in tracing the missing shipment bound for Ratchet. If you want to follow it up, he suggests you go to the Baron himself, since if anyone knows Revilgaz's business, it is Revilgaz. He waits in the tavern across the harbor, on the top floor.

quest:1182.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz tells you the Venture Company shredders at Lake Nazferiti in northern Stranglethorn have a new model fuel regulator that Pozzik could use. Foreman Cozzle has proven cleverer than the Baron expected, so Revilgaz sends you to find the blueprints. Baron Revilgaz explains that the Venture Company's shredders at Lake Nazferiti, in northern Stranglethorn, carry a new model of fuel regulator. Pozzik could take advantage of it if he had the details, but Cozzle, the foreman there, is cleverer than Revilgaz gave him credit for. You might have better luck. Revilgaz knows the blueprints are kept in Cozzle's house, almost certainly under lock and key. The Venture Company is based around Lake Nazferiti, in the vale's north-eastern corner. The key is with Foreman Cozzle in the cabin atop the oil tower, and the box holding the blueprints is in the small house near the tower's base. Revilgaz admits the gnome team out there is pretty good, and says the team needs every advantage it can find.

quest:1183.text: Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz has the Fuel Regulator Blueprints ready and sends them to Pozzik on the Shimmering Flats. He gives his regards and adds that Pozzik should not hesitate to ask if he ever needs anything. Baron Revilgaz says you are all set. You carry the blueprints to Pozzik, out on the Shimmering Flats, with the Baron's regards and a message: if Pozzik ever needs anything, he should not hesitate to ask. Revilgaz says he will be waiting for news that Pozzik breaks the track record.

quest:1184.text: Parts of the Swarm. Korran has a message for Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar. You are to carry word back that Moktar is serving well out in Thousand Needles, and that Korran's studies are moving along. After the cracked carapaces taken from the silithid at the Rustmaul Digsite, Korran sends you back to Belgrom Rockmaul in Orgrimmar. Tell Belgrom that Moktar is doing his bidding well out in Thousand Needles. Tell him too that Korran's studies are progressing and that he hopes to learn more soon.

quest:1186.text: The Eighteenth Pilot. Pozzik will be busy fitting the new fuel regulator into the racer designs, but suggests that you help the team further by speaking with Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth, and likes to add modifications to the racers. Pozzik says the fuel regulator is keeping him busy, but you can help the team some more by talking to Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth in fact, and likes to add little modifications of his own to the racers. Pozzik adds that Razzeric is a little off his rocker, so you should try not to seem too surprised.

quest:1195.text: The Sacred Flame. The Sacred Flame is a Horde task initiated by Zangen Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff. Seeking to recover an ancient relic guarded by the Galak centaur in Thousand Needles, Zangen sends adventurers deep into Ashenvale to acquire a sacred moonwell phial from the local dryads. The Galak tribe of centaur inhabiting the canyon floor of Thousand Needles fiercely protects an artifact dating back to the creation of their race. To pierce their defenses and extinguish their sacred flames, Zangen Stonehoof requires water touched by lunar divinity, drawing the tauren's gaze northward to the ancestral forests of Ashenvale. Obtaining pure moonwell water is no simple task. Unblessed vessels cannot hold the sacred liquid without corrupting its virtue, forcing Horde emissaries to hunt the Laughing Sisters near Raynewood Retreat to secure an etched phial. Once retrieved, the phial must be submerged into a moonwell along the western banks of the Falfarren River before being carried back to Mulgore.

quest:1196.text: The Sacred Flame. Following a perilous excursion to an Ashenvale moonwell, a phial of sanctified waters must be ferried south to Freewind Post. The tauren mystic Rau Cliffrunner needs this lunar essence to breach an eternal flame warding an ancient centaur relic in Thousand Needles. Zangen Stonehoof's mission demands swift transit through central Kalimdor. With the etched phial brimmed with purified moonwell water, you are instructed to cross the sun-baked expanse of the Barrens, descend the towering Great Lift, and reach the high mesa settlement of Freewind Post. Waiting perched above the canyon floor is Rau Cliffrunner, who monitors the brazen centaur clans below.

quest:1197.text: The Sacred Flame. The Sacred Flame is the final task in Rau Cliffrunner's investigation into the Galak centaur of Thousand Needles. Armed with blessed waters, a Horde adventurer must penetrate Splithoof Hold, extinguish the tribe's revered brazier, and claim the ancient Cloven Hoof relic. North of Freewind Post lies Splithoof Crag, the heart of the Galak centaur domain in Thousand Needles. Deep within its cavernous den, Splithoof Hold, burns a fire that the centaur hold sacred. After preparing an etched phial filled with purified water, Rau Cliffrunner tasks his allies with penetrating the subterranean stronghold, using the water to momentarily quench the flame, and snatching the prize guarded within: a relic known as the Cloven Hoof.

quest:1198.text: In Search of Thaelrid. In Search of Thaelrid is an Alliance reconnaissance mission dispatched from Darnassus on behalf of the Argent Dawn. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass tasks adventurers with venturing into the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps to locate a missing scout who vanished while investigating a dangerous alliance between naga and cultists. It represents an early encounter with the reach of the Argent Dawn beyond their typical northern vigil. Though the Argent Dawn is most renowned for holding the line against the Scourge in the plague-ridden ruins of Lordaeron, its vigilance extends across Kalimdor. Stationed within Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass gathers whispers and intelligence on unnatural threats emerging across the world. When unsettling reports arose that sea-dwelling naga and the doomsday zealots of the Twilight's Hammer had forged a pact within the flooded chambers of Blackfathom Deeps along the Ashenvale shore, the order recognized the potential catastrophe. To assess the veracity of these coastal rumors, Shaedlass dispatched Argent Guard Thaelrid to quietly infiltrate the subterranean caverns. Weeks passed without word, leaving the Dawnwatcher in the dark with his other scouts committed to separate operations. Fearing that Thaelrid had either fallen in battle or been captured by the dark powers dwelling beneath the waves, he enlists seasoned travelers brave enough to breach Blackfathom Deeps and bring him back alive.

quest:1199.text: Twilight Falls. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus calls upon Alliance champions to strike at the Twilight's Hammer cultists gathered within Blackfathom Deeps. The dark cult has allied with serpent-like naga to occupy the sunken night elf temple along the Ashenvale coast. By gathering pendants from the fallen cultists, adventurers strike a blow against their insidious plans to awaken ancient evils. Beneath the rugged cliffs of the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale lie the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. Once a sacred night elf temple dedicated to Elune and home to a powerful moonwell, it was shattered and plunged into the depths during the Sundering. Today, the sacred waters have turned putrid and foul, overrun by bloodthirsty naga and fanatic cultists who venerate forces far darker than the sea. The Twilight's Hammer is an apocalyptic cult devoted to the chaotic Old Gods, seeking to bring about the return of their primordial patrons and cover the world in madness and ruin. Reports reaching Darnassus confirm that these madmen have joined hands with the naga inhabiting Blackfathom Deeps. Deep within the submerged halls, they conduct blasphemous rituals, using the sunken temple's tainted waters to feed their dark masters' resurgence. Stationed in Darnassus, Argent Guard Manados represents the Argent Dawn's vigilance against all scourges that threaten Azeroth. Recognizing that the depravity within Blackfathom Deeps could unleash horrors upon all civilized races, the order offers recognition and aid to any heroes willing to descend into the flooded labyrinth, cull the cultists, and pry the Twilight Pendants from their necks as proof of their downfall.

quest:1200.text: Blackfathom Villainy. Blackfathom Villainy is an Alliance task given by Argent Guard Thaelrid deep within the ruined subterranean temple of Blackfathom Deeps. To halt the horrific sacrifices fueling an ancient horror, heroes are tasked with executing the cult leader Twilight Lord Kelris and bringing proof back to the Argent Dawn in Darnassus. The flooded cavern now known as Blackfathom Deeps was once a pristine subterranean temple dedicated to Elune. That sacred past was shattered when the corruption of an ancient Old God seeped up through the rock, spoiling the temple's Moon Well and releasing Aku'mai, a voracious servant of that primordial darkness. In the wake of this defilement, the Twilight's Hammer cult forged an unholy alliance with local naga, turning holy halls into a den of ritual murder. Argent Guard Thaelrid ventured into Blackfathom Deeps on behalf of his order, only to be grievously wounded and drained of his strength. Stranded amidst enemies, Thaelrid realizes he cannot finish his mission alone. He implores any brave Alliance travelers who reach him to strike down Twilight Lord Kelris, the sinister cultist orchestrating the sacrifice of innocents to Aku'mai in exchange for dark power.

quest:1221.text: Blueleaf Tubers. Blueleaf Tubers is a retrieval contract commissioned by the goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Seeking to profit from a rare subterranean delicacy, Mizzyrix equips adventurers with trained snufflenose gophers to locate and dig up the tubers buried inside the thorned depths of Razorfen Kraul. Blueleaf tubers are coveted across the world as a rare and lavish culinary delicacy. Despite their high value, harvesting them is notoriously difficult because they do not grow in open fields or standard wild groves. Instead, they are found almost exclusively deep in the sunless earth beneath the southern Barrens, tangled among the labyrinthine roots of Razorfen Kraul. Because the tubers remain completely buried and virtually impossible for ordinary humanoids to spot, the Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix devised an unusual solution. By training native snufflenose gophers—creatures capable of catching the scent of a buried tuber from fifty paces away—Mizzyrix turned vermin into foraging tools. He supplies scavengers with a command stick, a ventilated crate, and an instruction manual to guide the creatures through quilboar territory. Reclaiming the tubers requires delving into the territory of the hostile Death's Head quilboar tribe. Foragers must protect their trained gophers from the feral beasts and thorny briars of the Kraul, commanding the rodents to unearth the hidden bulbs before packing them away for transport back to Ratchet, where Mizzyrix's high-paying foreign buyers await.

quest:124.text: A Baying of Gnolls. Verner Osgood, the stable master in Lakeshire, finds his business under siege by gnolls raiding south from the Redridge foothills. Already strained by Blackrock orc incursions, he asks travelers to clear out the brutes and mystics threatening his livestock. Running a stable in Lakeshire has become increasingly hazardous. Blackrock orcs command the heights of the region, while packs of gnolls roam the surrounding ridges. For Verner Osgood, the situation reached a breaking point when aggressive gnoll raiding bands crept close to the northern borders of his paddocks, preying on any horses that wandered too close to the bluffs.

quest:1241.text: The Missing Diplomat. An urgent discreet investigation begins within Stormwind City after an Alliance diplomat fails to arrive at Theramore Isle. Bishop DeLavey suspects Defias foul play and dispatches trusted operatives to consult Jorgen, a quiet contact stationed in the Valley of Heroes. A high-ranking diplomat departed the Eastern Kingdoms bound for Theramore Isle to conduct sensitive talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore. The envoy vanished before ever making landfall. While royal investigators comb Stormwind for leads, the disappearance has been kept strictly under wraps to avoid widespread panic or tipping off conspirators who might be watching the crown's every move. Believing the Defias Brotherhood is involved in the diplomat's abduction, Bishop DeLavey opts not to rely solely on the king's formal guard. Instead, the bishop reaches out to unofficial and discreet channels, turning to Jorgen, an old acquaintance who keeps a low profile fishing in the Valley of Heroes just inside the city gates.

quest:1242.text: The Missing Diplomat. This errand directs investigators from Jorgen in the Valley of Heroes to Elling Trias, the proprietor of Trias' Cheese in Stormwind's Trade District. Carrying a discreet sealed note, it bridges palace concerns about the missing diplomat into the quiet contacts kept behind the counter of a modest cheese shop. Following initial inquiries into the disappearance of an unnamed diplomat, Jorgen directs trusted operatives to keep their mouths firmly shut and carry a sealed note across the city. The destination is not an official barracks or a magistrate's office, but Trias' Cheese, nestled in the busy Trade District. The secretive nature of the handover hints at how delicate the matter has become, bypassing ordinary guard channels in favor of informal intelligence.

quest:1243.text: The Missing Diplomat. This errand within the investigation of Stormwind's vanished emissary sends you south into the gloomy realm of Duskwood. Acting on leads secured in the capital, master of cheese Elling Trias dispatches you to contact Watcher Backus near Darkshire to uncover traces of Defias activity. Following a frustrating exchange involving Jorgen, cheesemonger Elling Trias decides to leverage his broader network of informants. Rather than squander his own coin sending out professional agents, he directs you to undertake the legwork yourself. You are charged with carrying a sealed missive across the border into Duskwood, a shadowed land beleaguered by beasts, the undead, and worse. Your target is Watcher Backus, a member of the Night Watch patrolling the northern approach to Darkshire. Despite the perils that make Duskwood treacherous for ordinary travelers, Trias relies on Backus as a dependable source of intelligence regarding illicit movements. Presenting the sealed dispatch opens the door to municipal guard records and local gossip concerning Defias Brotherhood operations in the south.

quest:1244.text: The Missing Diplomat. This leg of the investigation directs Alliance agents into the shadows of Duskwood following the trail of Stormwind's vanished emissary. Acting on information from Watcher Backus, investigators must search the derelict farmstead of Addle's Stead to uncover Defias paperwork. After following whisperings of conspiracy outside Stormwind's walls, the search for the missing diplomat reaches the Night Watch in Duskwood. Watcher Backus notes that while Defias bandits usually keep to themselves across the border, an unusually large gathering converged at Addle's Stead several weeks prior. For an organization operating largely out of Westfall, such concentrated activity in the dark woods suggests something critical transpired on that abandoned farmland.

quest:1245.text: The Missing Diplomat. This errand within the sprawling investigation sends you racing back to Stormwind with the recovered Defias Docket. What began as a quiet inquiry into a missing diplomat is steadily uncovering a conspiracy far broader and more perilous than local night watchmen dare touch. Upon recovering the Defias Docket in the shadowed forests of Duskwood, Watcher Backus wants nothing more to do with it. The papers detail schemes far too intricate to be mere banditry or diversionary tactics. Terrified of royal retribution and wary of his own superiors in the Night Watch, Backus urges you to keep his involvement entirely quiet. The documents speak of machinations dangerous enough to end careers or cost lives, leaving the investigator no choice but to carry the dangerous prize directly back to the capital.

quest:1246.text: The Missing Diplomat. This errand leads investigators deep into Old Town to confront a known street brawler tied to suspicious papers. Guided by the cheese merchant Elling Trias, you must seek out Dashel Stonefist and pry answers from him by any means necessary. The trail surrounding the missing diplomat is rapidly shifting from court intrigue to Stormwind's rough underbelly. After examining the coded notes and leads tied to the missing diplomat, Master Trias recalls a key figure connected to the operation: a rough street fighter named Dashel Stonefist, colloquially known as 'Fist'. Rather than rubbing shoulders with nobility in the Cathedral Square, Stonefist frequents the cramped alleys of Old Town. Tracking him down represents the first physical thread pulling the investigation away from the grand halls of Stormwind Keep and into the city's criminal circles.

quest:1247.text: The Missing Diplomat. This step in the investigation of Stormwind's missing envoy follows the interrogation of Dashel Stonefist in Old Town. Having beaten a confession out of the thug, you carry word of a backup abduction plot back to the spymaster disguised as a master of cheese, Elling Trias. Dashel Stonefist is not the kind of operative who takes secrets to the grave, especially once convinced his health is on the line. Cornered in his Old Town alley, Dashel folds and admits that his role in the kidnapping crumbled when the conspirators' initial plan fell apart. Desperate to deflect blame, he points to a clandestine meeting held weeks earlier at Addle's Stead in Duskwood and offers a single lead for their backup operation: an insider operating out of Menethil Harbor known only as Slim.

quest:126.text: Howling in the Hills. Howling in the Hills is an Alliance bounty offered by Verner Osgood in Lakeshire to hunt down Yowler, the fearsome alpha leading the Redridge gnolls. With Stormwind's military stretched too thin fighting the Blackrock orcs to defend the local borders, Lakeshire relies on visiting adventurers to break the gnoll pack's command. Even after culling the lesser gnolls raiding the paths around Lakeshire, their ominous calls continue to echo through the Redridge ridges. Verner Osgood, Lakeshire's hardworking farrier, recognizes that killing scouts and scavengers will never stem the tide as long as their pack leader remains alive. Rising above the rabble is Yowler, an exceptionally cunning and massive gnoll whose calls direct the pack across the hills. Verner tasks adventurers with hunting down the beast and severing his paw to ensure the howling is silenced once and for all. This contract highlights the grim reality facing the eastern borders of the kingdom of Stormwind. With the missing King Varian Wrynn and regency disputes paralyzing high command, royal soldiers are focused almost exclusively on the entrenched Blackrock orc clans in the north. Everyday settlements like Lakeshire are left completely undefended against native menaces like gnolls, forcing townsfolk like Verner Osgood to organize their own bounties to prevent their homes from being overrun.

quest:127.text: Selling Fish. Dockmaster Baren manages the bustling pier at Lakeshire, but finding fresh stock for his trade has grown difficult. He pays travelers to haul in spotted sunfish, a prized local staple of Lake Everstill that has become dangerous to gather due to the encroaching murlocs. Lake Everstill is known throughout the surrounding lands for its spotted sunfish, a delicate catch that remains in perpetual demand among the townspeople and passing merchants. Yet despite the abundance beneath the lake's surface, the town's supplies regularly run thin. With Lakeshire stretched to its limits under various local threats, even basic commerce requires the help of freelance adventurers. Normally, local anglers would have little trouble satisfying Dockmaster Baren's orders. However, the rise of aggressive murloc tribes along the shallows and banks has driven ordinary townsfolk away from the water. Travelers looking to fulfill Baren's request must either cast their own lines while watching their backs, or claim the catch directly from the foraging murlocs that plague the shores.

quest:1274.text: The Missing Diplomat. The Missing Diplomat is the introductory step in one of Stormwind's most critical and sensitive investigations. Brought to your attention discreetly on the city streets, the matter leads directly to Bishop DeLavey in Stormwind Keep. The Church and the crown require capable hands for an issue too perilous to trust to public channels. While traveling through Stormwind, an unassuming altar boy named Thomas approaches trustworthy adventurers with a quiet request. Bishop DeLavey, a respected figure within the Church of the Holy Light stationed at Stormwind Keep, needs an outsider's assistance. The matter is described strictly as delicate and urgent, requiring complete discretion to avoid inciting panic among the populace.

quest:1275.text: Researching the Corruption. Gershala Nightwhisper in Auberdine seeks corrupted brain stems from the creatures infesting Blackfathom Deeps. Disturbed by reports of the blood elves dabbling in demonic magic across the sea, he hopes to study the physiological descent of the naga and satyr to foresee—and perhaps avert—another catastrophic elven mutation. To the night elves of Kalimdor, the ruin of their ancient kin is a living memory etched into monsters. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne succumbed to the allure of demonic energies, warping themselves into horned satyrs or drowning into serpentine naga. Watching the high elves rebrand themselves as blood elves and embrace dark magic strikes Gershala Nightwhisper not as a distant curiosity, but as history doomed to repeat itself. Blackfathom Deeps serves as an ideal specimen ground for Gershala's grim inquiry. Hidden beneath the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale, the subterranean temple ruins crawl with both satyr cultists and coiled naga. By sending an adventurer to harvest brain stems from both monstrosities, he hopes to dissect the biological link between arcane addiction, demonic corruption, and catastrophic bodily transformation.

quest:128.text: Blackrock Bounty. Blackrock Bounty is a defense contract issued by Guard Howe in Lakeshire on behalf of Magistrate Solomon. With Stormwind failing to dispatch reinforcements, the town pays independent adventurers to cull the elite Blackrock Champions massing in the northern mountains. Striking down these battlefield unit commanders is aimed at disrupting the orc clan's coordinated assault on Redridge. Redridge has long fallen under the sovereign rule of the Kingdom of Stormwind, but the Blackrock clan does not honor human borders. Pouring down through the mountain passes leading from the Burning Steppes, the orcs have established heavily fortified encampments across northern Redridge. With King Varian Wrynn missing and the regency in Stormwind withholding royal soldiers, local leaders like Magistrate Solomon have been forced to put up bounties from the town's dwindling coffers to protect Lakeshire. Guard Howe identifies the Blackrock Champions as the backbone of the invading vanguard. Serving as squad leaders and battle-hardened veterans within their warbands, these champions coordinate troop movements and drive the lesser grunt forces forward. By putting a price on their heads, Lakeshire's defenders hope to break the clan's tactical leadership and stall a full-scale push south before the township's outer perimeter collapses.

quest:1302.text: James Hyal. "James Hyal" is an Alliance quest concerning a human settler who sailed to Kalimdor with Lady Jaina Proudmoore's expedition. After setting out to open an inn on the frontier, his family in the Eastern Kingdoms lost touch with him and seeks news of his fate through Theramore's administrative records. During the Third War, countless souls left their ancestral homes in the Eastern Kingdoms to follow Lady Jaina Proudmoore across the Great Sea. Among them was James Hyal, remembered fondly by his kin as a gifted cook. After the fighting subsided and Theramore Isle was founded, James chose to carve out a living on the rugged continent of Kalimdor by opening an inn of his own to serve travellers and fellow settlers. Back in the Eastern Kingdoms, James's brother has grown concerned after receiving no recent correspondence from across the sea. Hoping that James is merely consumed by the demands of managing a bustling roadside taproom, he asks passing travellers to track him down. The first step in finding him lies in Theramore, where Clerk Lendry oversees local records and keeps track of expedition members who have ventured out into the wilderness.

quest:133.text: Ghoulish Effigy. Deep in the gloomy wilderness of Duskwood, the eccentric hermit Abercrombie claims his isolated shack is under siege by the walking dead. To protect his home, he tasks passing adventurers with harvesting ghoul ribs to assemble a bizarre protective scarecrow. Abercrombie lives far beyond the guarded boundaries of Darkshire, isolated amidst the shadowed trees of Duskwood. Out here, wandering ghouls like Flesh Eaters and Bone Chewers roam unchecked. Claiming that ravenous corpses recently battered down his walls, the panicked hermit requests the ribs of these horrors to fashion a deterrent, hoping a grisly effigy will keep the hungry dead at bay. While common sense might suggest running toward the safety of the Night Watch or fortifying his wooden shack, Abercrombie insists on macabre methods. He believes erecting an effigy made from ghoul remains will frighten off other scavenging dead. Though building a scarecrow out of slaughtered undead seems unsettling, travelers in Duskwood often take the eccentric hermit at his word to earn some needed coin.

quest:134.text: Ogre Thieves. Abercrombie, the peculiar hermit dwelling in western Duskwood, asks travelers to venture into the ogre stronghold of Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. He claims that ogres ambushed him while he was foraging and made off with a crate filled with his irreplaceable herbs and tools. Isolated out along the damp roads of western Duskwood, the aged hermit Abercrombie claims he was attacked while gathering supplies in the wilderness. According to him, brutes from the southern ogre mound drove him off, forcing him to abandon a sturdy wooden crate packed with precious herbs and delicate instruments. The Vul'Gol Ogre Mound in southern Duskwood is a fortified hive of hostile ogres who harass unwary wanderers. The crate sits right near the entrance of their cavernous mound, daring outsiders to step past roaring brutes and spell-weaving magi to haul it back to the hermit.

quest:1361.text: Regthar Deathgate. This directive dispatches seasoned Horde champions from major capitals to reinforce an outpost in the western Barrens. The veteran warrior Regthar Deathgate is marshaling capable volunteers for an impending campaign across the mountains into the arid wastes of Desolace. He seeks those willing to carry Horde steel against the entrenched centaur clans terrorizing the frontier. Across Kalimdor, influential leaders of the Horde—including Shadow Hunter Vol'jin, Nazgrel, and seasoned commanders like Belgrom Rockmaul—keep a watchful eye on potential threats along the borders. In the Barrens, an experienced warrior named Regthar Deathgate has established a defensive post guarding the western passes. Recognizing that regional skirmishes require hardened fighters rather than raw recruits, Horde officers direct proven adventurers west of the Crossroads to answer Regthar's call. Regthar Deathgate is stationed within the fortified redoubt bunkered along the ridges west of the Crossroads. From this vantage point, he monitors the western mountain trails that wind into the desolate badlands of Desolace. His mandate is direct and unyielding: assemble an expeditionary vanguard capable of braving hostile terrain to strike directly at the heart of the Kolkar and other warring centaur clans before their violent expansion threatens Horde territory.

quest:1362.text: The Kolkar of Desolace. This quest bridges Horde military operations between the Barrens and the bleak expanse of Desolace. Directed by the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate, Horde champions journey westward across the mountains to reinforce scout Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post. While the Horde contends with marauding centaur packs across the Barrens, commanders like Regthar Deathgate recognize that trimming branches will never kill a tree. The Kolkar clan traces its root strength directly to the desolate crags of Kalimdor's western coast.
