Instead of hoarding his newfound metallurgy, Furen copies down detailed technical diagrams and sends his tested adventurer across continents to find Mathiel, an accomplished smith dwelling high in Teldrassil. Mathiel works his forge on the tree-canopied Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, catering to the Sentinels and fighters who defend the night elven capital. Receiving Furen's notes marks a bridge between disparate crafting traditions: the rugged, subterranean smelting of the Khaz Modan dwarves and the graceful, nature-attuned armorsmithing of the kaldorei.

quest:1704.text: Klockmort Spannerspan. This quest sends an adventurer from Stormwind to Ironforge to deliver trade secrets to Klockmort Spannerspan in Tinkertown. After mastering the art of fire-hardened armor, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard eagerly shares his metallurgical discoveries with his gnomish colleague. It serves as an essential link in the journey of an aspiring warrior looking to test exotic crafting methods. Having successfully forged a set of fire-hardened mail, Furen Longbeard compiles his detailed findings to pass along to a fellow craftsman. Rather than hoarding his newly discovered techniques, Furen trusts you to carry his notes from Stormwind to Ironforge and into the clatter and steam of Tinkertown, where the gnomish blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan plies his trade. Gnome blacksmiths are relatively rare compared to their dwarven hosts, and Klockmort is enthusiastic about pushing the boundaries of traditional metalwork. Upon inspecting Furen's notes, Klockmort becomes wildly excited over the breakthrough, eager to integrate these fiery techniques into his own exotic projects.

quest:1705.text: Burning Blood. Master smith Grimand Elmore in Stormwind tasks an adventurer with venturing into the shadowy forests of Duskwood to recover exotic forge reagents. Intrigued by innovative armorcrafting techniques pioneered by Furen Longbeard, Grimand requires burning blood and a blazing ember stone held by feral worgen to test the process himself. Grimand Elmore, one of the Alliance's most accomplished armorers, rarely concedes that another craftsman might outshine his own methods. Yet, after hearing of Furen Longbeard's unconventional smithing discoveries, professional curiosity overtakes his stubborn pride. Grimand agrees to put Furen's methods to the test by hammering out a bespoke piece of armor. To quench and temper the metal to exact specifications, ordinary water or common coals will not suffice; he demands strange, volatile components found only in the darkened reaches of the south. The quest directs brave smith-aspirants and warriors into Duskwood, specifically toward the forsaken mine of Roland's Doom. The cavern has been overrun by savage Nightbane worgen—lupine beasts whose cursed veins pulse with unnatural, searing ichor. Grimand requires vials of this burning blood, alongside a rare flaming geological core known as a burning rock, held by the pack's ferocious leader, Gutspill. Slaying these beasts and securing their scorching remains allows Grimand to fire his forge with dark, fiery power.

quest:1706.text: Grimand's Armor. "Grimand's Armor" is the culmination of a warrior's training questline under the supervision of Grimand Elmore in the Dwarven District of Stormwind. After proving the viability of Furen Longbeard's metallurgic techniques, the smith crafts a formidable piece of armor capable of absorbing punishing blows in battle. It marks an essential milestone in an Alliance warrior's journey toward mastery. Grimand Elmore, working from his forge in Stormwind's Dwarven District, originally held deep skepticism regarding the bizarre and daring techniques developed by the dwarven master armorer Furen Longbeard. Testing Furen's methods required perilous expeditions into hostile territory to gather rare elemental and beast components. By delivering these vital materials, a warrior allows Grimand to put the dwarf's theories to the fire, turning raw ingredients into a reinforced helm engineered to endure catastrophic impacts. The final product demonstrates that Furen's metallurgic insights were entirely sound. Grimand successfully treats the metal to withstand intense pressure and physical trauma that would warp ordinary steel. Presenting the crafted coif to the warrior who aided him, Grimand acknowledges both Furen's craft and the adventurer's determination, equipping them to hold the frontline against the greatest threats in Azeroth.

quest:1708.text: Iron Coral. Iron Coral is an Alliance quest given by the gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan in Tinker Town, Ironforge. Eager to test newly shared smithing methods on a custom suit of armor, Klockmort sends you to dive for rare searing coral along the coast of the Wetlands. Completing his request allows him to fuse gnomish ingenuity with dwarven craftsmanship. After exchanging insights with the master dwarven smith Furen Longbeard, Klockmort Spannerspan is bursting with inspiration. The eccentric gnome blacksmith wants to combine Furen's metallurgy with his own tinkering ideas to craft an exceptionally resilient suit of armor. To pull off this daring metallurgical experiment, standard mountain ores will not suffice; Klockmort requires an unusual, naturally hardened marine element known as searing coral. Searing coral is a volatile, tough oceanic deposit found in only one specific region: submerged off the coast south of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Retrieving twenty clusters means wading through treacherous marshland waters, braving native aquatic predators, and hauling the dripping harvests back to Ironforge. For Klockmort, however, the prize is well worth the damp excursion, as he intends to smelt and hammer the coral directly into his experimental plating.

quest:1709.text: Klockmort's Creation. Klockmort's Creation marks the successful forging of a specialized suit of armor in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Utilizing an unconventional technique devised by the master armorsmith Furen Longbeard, the gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan shapes raw materials into an extraordinarily resilient piece of gear. Forging heavy armor typically belongs to the great anvils of the Great Forge, but Klockmort Spannerspan operates out of Tinker Town. The creation of this armor represents a collaborative triumph between dwarven metallurgical tradition and gnomish mechanical innovation. By adapting Furen Longbeard's rigorous methods, Klockmort finishes a pair of armored gauntlets engineered to endure punishment that would crush ordinary steel. According to Klockmort, the resulting armor boasts structural integrity so great that a siege engine could roll directly over it without causing permanent distortion. The secret lies in the peculiar treatment of rare components, proving that combining ancient dwarven forging techniques with gnomish ingenuity yields armor capable of withstanding the fiercest frontline battles.

quest:1710.text: Sunscorched Shells. In Darnassus, the armorer Mathiel collaborates with the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard to refine a new mailcrafting technique. He tasks warriors with traveling to Thousand Needles to gather durable wyvern eggshells from the heights of Highperch. Mathiel works out of the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, but his trade takes him far beyond traditional night elven techniques. He maintains correspondence with Furen Longbeard, an accomplished dwarven armorer in Stormwind. Inspired by Furen's metallurgy and armor-smithing discoveries, Mathiel seeks to forge a suit of mail reinforced by natural components capable of withstanding extreme strain. To test this hybrid theory, he requires exotic materials that cannot be found anywhere near Teldrassil. The key to Mathiel's experiment lies far to the south across the sea, in the canyon gorges of Thousand Needles. There, high above the salt flats and red stone mesas, Highperch wyverns nest beneath the blazing Kalimdor sun. Their eggshells harden through constant exposure to blistering heat and altitude. Mathiel intends to pulverize these sun-baked fragments and render them into a resilient lacquer, coating the links of chainmail to create flexible yet exceptionally durable armor.

quest:1711.text: Mathiel's Armor. "Mathiel's Armor" marks the completion of an armorsmithing effort undertaken by Mathiel in the Warrior's Terrace of Darnassus. By combining his own night elven craftsmanship with innovative dwarven metalworking methods devised by Furen Longbeard, Mathiel reforges exotic materials into protective battle gear. The quest represents a fruitful blending of allied traditions in service of Alliance warriors. Night elven armorers traditionally favor methods honed over millennia, relying on harmony with nature, supple leathers, or delicately worked metals. However, the exchange between the night elves and the Eastern Kingdoms has prompted master smiths like Mathiel to experiment. By incorporating newly devised techniques from the dwarven armorer Furen Longbeard, Mathiel manages to meld dwarven metallurgy with elven artistry. Forging this resilient armor required sunscorched eggshells gathered from the Highperch wyvern nests of Thousand Needles. By rendering these sun-hardened shells into lacquer and applying Furen's heat-treatment formulas, Mathiel successfully created a resilient set of leggings designed to withstand brutal frontline combat.

quest:1712.text: Cyclonian. Cyclonian is a mighty wind lord whose defeat has been sought for ages. To challenge him, a champion must gather the components required to summon the elemental and strike him down to claim his whirlwind heart. Defeating the wind lord allows the heart's power to be infused into a formidable weapon. Cyclonian is a raging elemental wind lord whose presence commands reverence and caution. For ages, an attentive watcher has kept vigil over the summoning site, waiting for a combatant possesses enough raw martial prowess to challenge and destroy this tempestuous entity. Calling forth Cyclonian requires a ritual of summoning using rare materials detailed upon a special parchment. Once summoned, the wind lord must be faced in direct combat, testing whether the challenger is truly a champion or merely another victim of his howling gale.

quest:1716.text: Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is a pivotal rite of passage for Alliance warlocks dispatched from Stormwind to learn the summoning of a succubus. Directed by Gakin the Darkbinder, initiates must trek halfway across the world into the hazardous wildlands of the Barrens to seek counsel from Takar the Seer. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder instructs promising warlocks on their next major summons: the succubus. Described as a devourer of souls, a destroyer of hearts, and a dominator of minds, this demonic entity cannot be summoned blindly into Azeroth. It requires a potent lure, specifically an object tied to pure love, to tease it forth from the Twisting Nether so that the practitioner may defeat and bind it. Procuring such a token demands wisdom that Stormwind's covens cannot provide locally. To track down the required catalyst, Gakin sends his pupils across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. Deep in the arid expanse of the Barrens, near the Horde settlement of Camp Taurajo, sits Takar the Seer. For an Alliance warlock, reaching Takar requires braving wilderness heavily patrolled by hostile centaur, quilboar, and Horde warriors, serving as an unstated test of survival before the summoner can even begin preparing the ritual.

quest:1717.text: Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks in Ironforge, directing them south to Stormwind. Gakin the Darkbinder awaits beneath the city's Mage Quarter to oversee their advancement into commanding greater fiends. Demonology remains a practice conducted entirely in shadows across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly keeps tabs on wandering practitioners on behalf of the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock shows sufficient mastery over their initial minions, word travels quickly. Lago passes along the directive: drop whatever business keeps you in the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind's Mage Quarter, beneath the tavern known as The Slaughtered Lamb, Gakin the Darkbinder coordinates the development of the city's warlocks. Gakin views every capable student as a valuable, hazardous investment. Receiving his summons marks the threshold of true demonic binding, beginning the trials required to subjugate a succubus from the Twisting Nether.

quest:1718.text: The Islander. The Islander is an invitation extended by veteran warrior trainers across Azeroth to those who have proven their basic mettle in battle. It directs rising fighters to Fray Island off the Merchant Coast, where an insular brotherhood of warriors tests their peers in raw martial combat. Meeting the chief warrior Klannoc Macleod marks a pivotal step toward mastering advanced combat disciplines. Warrior trainers in capital cities across both the Alliance and the Horde recognize when a student has outgrown basic drills. Rather than formal rank or political loyalty, martial progression demands that combatants measure themselves against true peers. The journey sends warriors away from civilized sparring yards toward a rugged isle isolated in the Great Sea. Fray Island sits east off the Merchant Coast, just south of the goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. It is reached by swimming the waters over submerged sandbar shallows. On this rock, political ties dissolve in favor of martial fraternity; fighters gather under the gaze of Klannoc Macleod, the chief warrior on the isle, awaiting whatever brutal trial he deems necessary.

quest:1719.text: The Affray. The Affray is a brutal martial trial conducted on Fray Island off the coast of the Barrens. Administered by Klannoc Macleod, this arena brawl pits ambitious warriors against waves of island challengers and their champion to prove they possess the mettle required for advanced training. Fray Island stands apart from the struggles of the mainland, serving as a sanctuary for hardy brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not simply teach any wanderer who steps off a boat. To earn his tutelage, aspiring warriors must participate in the Affray, an open trial of martial stamina and battlefield awareness designed to separate true fighters from boastful pretenders. The rules of the Affray are simple and unforgiving. By stepping onto the central iron grate among the gathered spectators, a warrior signals ringmaster Twiggy Flathead to begin the contest. Challengers enter the ring one after another, testing the initiate's endurance. Those who survive the preliminary fighters face the island's heavyweight champion, Big Will, whose defeat is the sole condition for earning Klannoc's respect.

quest:173.text: Worgen in the Woods. Calor, a disillusioned former guardsman stationed in Darkshire, tasks adventurers with culling the sinister Nightbane Shadow Weavers prowling Duskwood. By taking the hunt to Brightwood Grove and the Rotting Orchard, outsiders can prove their mettle to Master Jonathan Carevin's monster hunters. The Night Watch struggles constantly against the undead, spiders, and outlaws pressing against Darkshire's borders. For some, like Calor, the official guard proved too slow and complacent to cleanse the land. Leaving the Watch behind, Calor threw in his lot with Master Jonathan Carevin, dedicating his blade to the total eradication of heresy and corruption. But Carevin does not accept just anyone into his circle; those seeking to aid their cause must first prove they can survive against the woods' most ferocious horrors. The proving ground lies in Brightwood Grove and the blighted Rotting Orchard, where feral lupine beasts known as worgen hold dominion. Among them, the Nightbane Shadow Weavers harness dark magics to blind and ensnare their victims before tearing them apart. Calor sends aspiring hunters to cut down these spell-weaving beasts, both to test an outsider's resolve and to thin out a threat whose origins remain deeply unsettling to Darkshire's defenders.

quest:1738.text: Heartswood. Heartswood is an Alliance warlock quest that sends practitioners deep into Ashenvale to recover the branch of an ancient, tragic tree. Sent by the hermit Takar the Seer on behalf of Gakin the Darkbinder, warlocks seek this romantic relic as a potent bait to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. According to Takar the Seer, the Heartswood tree sprang from the spot where two night elf lovers, Anathera and Latherion, fell together during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Nourished by their final breaths and eternal devotion, the tree grew as a pure emblem of undying romance. To mortal senses it is a sacred tragic monument, but to practitioners of the dark arts, concentrated emotional energy makes potent magical fuel. Succubi feed upon mortal passions, desire, and emotional torment. Takar realizes that ordinary temptations pale in comparison to an artifact suffused with thousands of years of pure, undying devotion. A piece of the Heartswood provides Gakin the Darkbinder with the exact catalyst required to bait one of these cunning demons across the Nether into the summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

quest:1739.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation ritual for Alliance warlocks seeking to command a succubus in Stormwind. Using the enchanted core obtained from the Heartswood, the practitioner enters the summoning circle beneath The Slaughtered Lamb to drag forth and physically overpower the demon. Once defeated, the demon's will is chained, binding its servitude to the summoner. Hidden beneath the floorboards of The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter lies a cavernous crypt dedicated to forbidden arts. Far from the watchful eyes of the city watch and the Cathedral of Light, the city's covert warlock enclave conducts its most dangerous rituals here. Summoning circles etched into stone channel the raw forces of the Nether, allowing ambitious initiates to pierce the veil between worlds. Summoning a succubus requires far more than merely chanting incantations. A warlock must bring a focus—in this case, the prepared Heartswood Core—and cast a ritual of breach at the circle. Succubi are known to corrupt, seduce, and overwhelm even fortified minds. To establish absolute mastery, the summoner must cut the beast down in single combat, banishing its physical form back to the Twisting Nether while securing its true tether.

quest:174.text: Look To The Stars. Look To The Stars begins Viktori Prism'Antras's endeavor to gaze past the eerie canopy of Duskwood. Believing that a scientific answer beyond arcane superstition explains the forest's dark curse, Viktori recruits you to gather components for a telescope designed by his gnomish associate. Amid the gloom and fear shrouding Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras takes a distinctly unconventional view of Duskwood's misfortune. Rather than attributing the land's corruption purely to black magic, curses, or restless dead, Viktori suspects that greater truths await high above the canopy. With the aid of blueprints drawn up by his gnomish partner, Cog, he sets out to build an optical device capable of peering into the heavens. To commence assembly on the stargazing apparatus, Viktori needs a sturdy frame. Following Cog's specifications, he asks travelers to procure a machined bronze tube. This first step relies directly on the ingenuity of mortal mechanics rather than spellcraft, highlighting Viktori's stubborn insistence that practical craft and observation might shed light where mysticism has failed.

quest:1740.text: The Orb of Soran'ruk. The Orb of Soran'ruk is a warlock rite of passage assigned by the hermit Doan Karhan in the southern Barrens. Aspiring practitioners track down broken demonic relics across Azeroth to reconstitute a vessel binding the essence of a disgraced demon. Within the hierarchy of the Burning Legion, failure carries an eternal punishment. When lesser demons fall out of favor with their demonic masters, their spirits are bound and imprisoned within crystalline orbs. These artifacts are then distributed to the Legion's mortal conjurers and warlocks to serve as conduits of raw, subjugated power. Even when shattered into shards, the demonic essence entrapped within retains potent magical strength. The orb of Soran'ruk did not remain whole. Shattered into fragments, its remnants found their way into dark corners on both major continents. One half was shattered further, held by the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer within the damp caverns of Blackfathom Deeps in Ashenvale. The larger intact half made its way across the sea to Silverpine Forest, claimed by one of the sorcerers within the haunted ruins of Shadowfang Keep. Doan Karhan, a lifelong scholar of Legion orbs who previously assembled the Orb of Zargain, uses the recovered shards to reconstruct Soran'ruk into a functional implement.

quest:175.text: Look To The Stars. Following the blueprints provided by the tinker Cog, Viktori Prism'Antras seeks a reflective surface to assemble his observatory telescope in Darkshire. He directs travelers to southern Duskwood to locate Mary, a local woman remembered for carrying a looking glass. Having secured a bronze tube for his telescope, Viktori Prism'Antras turns to the next requirement outlined in Cog's blueprints: a reliable mirror to direct and reflect light through the device. Rather than forging fine silvered glass from scratch amidst the shortages plaguing Darkshire, Viktori recalls Mary, a local resident known across the region for always carrying a looking glass. Mary's former residence lies deep in southern Duskwood, just north of the haunted Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Seeking her out takes adventurers past the safe patrol borders of the Night Watch and into blighted groves teeming with ravenous wolves, feral spiders, and wandering undead.

quest:1758.text: Tome of the Cabal. Tome of the Cabal sends an aspiring Alliance warlock from the heights above Ratchet back to the Library of Ironforge. To summon and dominate a ravenous felhunter, the summoner must locate a legendary manual written by the first warlocks who ever conquered the beast. Subjugating an imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus requires ritual, but a felhunter poses an entirely different hazard. Felhunters do not merely serve the Burning Legion; they actively hunt and devour arcane energy. A standard summoning circle will crumble before one, draining the summoner's magic before a binding can even take hold. Strahad Farsan, watching over Ratchet from his redoubt in the Barrens, knows better than to let an amateur try such a binding unprepared. To safely draw forth and bind a felhunter, an acolyte requires the arcane formulas compiled within the Tome of the Cabal. Authored by the earliest mortal cabal of warlocks who successfully broke a felhunter without outside aid, the manuscript details the specific geomancy, materials, and binding runes necessary to withstand the creature's hunger. Unfortunately for Strahad and his circle, their copy of this masterwork was lost long ago. Unable to provide the text himself, Strahad dispatches Alliance warlocks across the Great Sea to the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. There skulks Krom Stoutarm, an itinerant dwarven warlock who spends his twilight years combing through ancient manuscripts and library records. If any trace of the lost grimoire remains recorded in the Eastern Kingdoms, it rests buried in Krom's meticulous catalogs.

quest:177.text: Look To The Stars. This quest sends adventurers to recover Blind Mary's discarded looking glass for the astronomer Viktori Prism'Antras. The fragile mirror fell into the hands of an Insane Ghoul that wanders the desolate Tranquil Gardens Cemetery in southern Duskwood. Before the creeping gloom overran Duskwood and turned her into a weeping spirit, Blind Mary treasured an ornate looking glass. Following the horrific incident that claimed her sight and sanity, she cast the keepsake into the dirt behind her family barn. The reflective mirror is exactly what Viktori Prism'Antras needs to build his grand telescope in Darkshire, but it was snatched away into the shadows long before the astronomer dreamed of studying the heavens. The mirror was scavenged by an Insane Ghoul that prowled behind the ruined farmsteads. Driven south by restless hunger, the wretched undead creature carried the looking glass into the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, haunting an abandoned chapel amid the overgrown tombstones. Reclaiming the delicate lens means navigating the flesh-eating horrors that infest the southern woods to pry Mary's lost treasure from rotting claws.

quest:178.text: Theocritus' Retrieval. Theocritus' Retrieval begins when an adventurer in Redridge finds a magical trinket carried by the local gnolls, only to hear a distant voice echoing through it. The speaker is Theocritus, High Mage of Tower of Azora, who has successfully intercepted the gnolls' mystical network and urgently requests the pendant be brought to him for study. While fighting off the savage Shadowhide gnolls across the Redridge Mountains, travelers sometimes stumble across an enchanted trinket known as a Shadowhide Pendant. Instead of guttural barking or curses, touching the object triggers a calm, disembodied voice belonging to Theocritus, a human mage residing in Tower of Azora across the border in Elwynn Forest. The transmission is the result of long, painstaking research aimed at breaking into the dark sorceries directing the gnoll packs.

quest:1782.text: Furen's Armor. Furen's Armor marks the culmination of an aspiring warrior's quest to assist the master smith Furen Longbeard in Stormwind. By gathering spider fangs, chimaera horns and a vial of phlogiston, the adventurer helps Longbeard forge a resilient suit of fire-hardened mail. In return for their aid, Longbeard rewards the warrior with the finished mail and pledges to share his newfound metallurgical techniques across the Alliance. Furen Longbeard, an esteemed dwarven armorer stationed in Stormwind, has dedicated his craft to pushing the limits of Alliance defensive metallurgy. By commissioning a stalwart adventurer to track down scarce fangs, horns and phlogiston, Longbeard sought to test advanced techniques in tempering mail against searing heat and crushing impacts. The resulting craftwork proves to be a tremendous success, solidifying Longbeard's standing as one of the Alliance's foremost armor crafters. Upon presenting the newly finished fire-hardened mail to the adventurer who gathered the materials, Furen expresses deep gratitude for the partnership. The experiments did more than produce a single durable suit; they expanded his understanding of protective smithing. In the communal spirit of Ironforge and Stormwind artisans, Longbeard resolves to dispatch his notes and discoveries to fellow Alliance smiths, ensuring that his breakthrough strengthens frontline fighters across the faction.

quest:1791.text: The Windwatcher. The Windwatcher is an instructional summons directing seasoned warriors to seek out a reclusive troll shaman far to the north. Having proven their mettle in the trial of the Affray and mastered the berserker stance, warriors are directed to seek a weapon equal to their growing fury. Upon surviving the brutal endurance trial of the Affray on Fray Island, warriors earn the fierce discipline of the berserker stance from Klannoc Macleod. Yet raw martial discipline demands an arm of equal renown. Recognizing this, Klannoc sends promising fighters away from the coast of the Barrens, pointing them across continents to seek out a solitary craftsman capable of forging an extraordinary armament. The quest directs travelers deep into the contested valleys of northern Lordaeron, specifically the mist-shrouded borderland between the Alterac Mountains and the blighted Western Plaguelands. Resting beside the river flowing north past Tarren Mill, the troll hermit Bath'rah the Windwatcher lives in isolation among stone ruins. Bath'rah is no ordinary hermit: he is both a gifted weapon crafter and a wielder of potent elemental shamanism, waiting for warriors determined enough to forge something truly monumental.

quest:1793.text: The Tome of Valor. The Tome of Valor is a foundational trial for Alliance paladins coming into their own. Directed by paladin mentors in Stormwind and Ironforge, initiates are challenged to prove that their courage and devotion to protecting the innocent match their martial prowess. To wield the Holy Light in battle requires more than heavy armor and martial discipline. As young paladins reach greater heights in their training, instructors in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries demand proof of their inner resolve. The lessons of the Tome of Valor test an initiate's readiness to confront terrifying evils—from dragons to demons—without faltering or abandoning those who cannot defend themselves. Bravery under mortal threat is considered as essential to a holy warrior as their weapon and shield. Through the trials laid out in the Tome of Valor, paladins learn that raw strength is hollow without an unwavering vow to shelter the helpless. Facing genuine peril ensures that when darkness falls upon the Alliance, its defenders will stand firm rather than break.

quest:1795.text: The Binding. The Binding is the culminating rite for warlocks seeking to command a felhunter. Overseen by the enigmatic summoner Strahad Farsan above Ratchet, the ritual uses the restored Tome of the Cabal to rip an aggressive demonic predator from the Nether and force it into subjugation through trial of combat. Perched on the bluffs overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet, Strahad Farsan conducts some of the most dangerous demonological trials on Kalimdor. After a warlock gathers the disparate fragments and reagents needed to piece together the ancient Tome of the Cabal, Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays down an inner glyph of containment while his loyal acolytes channel through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle, ensuring whatever horrors emerge remain isolated from the settlement below. Calling upon the incantations inscribed in the Tome of the Cabal, the initiate opens a bridge into the Twisting Nether. Felhunters are ravenous demonic hounds that naturally hunger for arcane power and feast upon magical energy. The summoned beast cannot be merely sweet-talked or gently enthralled; it must be violently subdued and broken in combat before it will recognize the warlock as its rightful master. Surviving the clash proves a summoner's readiness to wield the hound against enemy spellcasters.

quest:1796.text: Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. Menara Voidrender tasks aspiring warlocks in the Barrens with procuring a set of Robes of Arcana as the base garment for a potent magical garment. This marks the initial step in crafting the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe, establishing the foundational vessel needed to withstand dark enchantments. Before dark magic can be bound to cloth, the garment itself must be worthy of bearing such power. Menara Voidrender instructs warlocks seeking greater power to procure a set of Robes of Arcana. As Menara explains, the capacity of any magical relic relies on the skill, rarity, and effort woven into its base materials. Mundane rags would unravel under the strain of deep enchantments, making a finely stitched, receptive garment indispensable. While Menara expresses particular admiration for practitioners capable of weaving the garment with their own hands, she values ruthless ambition above pride. Whether a warlock sews the silk themselves, commissions a talented artisan, or bargains on the market, the outcome remains the same: a completed robe ready to be remade into a specialized tool of fel mastery.

quest:1798.text: Seeking Strahad. Seeking Strahad is an Alliance warlock quest that sends practitioners of the dark arts from Stormwind City across the Great Sea to the Barrens. There, beneath the gaze of the goblin port of Ratchet, they seek the expertise of Strahad Farsan to learn the summoning of felhunters. It marks a warlock's passage into the higher, more dangerous tiers of demonic subjugation. Within the subterranean enclave of the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder oversees the development of budding warlocks. Yet mastering the predatory felhunter demands materials, relics, and rites beyond what the modest cellar in the Mage Quarter can provide. Recognizing his pupil has grown in power, Gakin directs them away from the safety of the kingdom toward Kalimdor, initiating a journey that bridges the secret circles of human demonology across continents. The destination is the arid hills overlooking the goblin harbor of Ratchet. There dwells Strahad Farsan, a human warlock and a peer of Gakin's within their clandestine cabal. Operating out of neutral territory allows Strahad relative freedom from the prying eyes of Alliance magistrates, church inquisitors, and Horde sentries alike. His presence in the Barrens serves as an anchor for ambitious summoners ready to wrest control over mana-draining demons.

quest:180.text: Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore. Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore is a local bounty posted in Lakeshire by Magistrate Solomon. It calls on adventurers to hunt down Lieutenant Fangore, the vicious chieftain of the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching upon the Redridge Mountains. Eliminating him strikes a direct blow against the renegade sorcerer Morganth, whom the gnolls serve. Lakeshire sits in a desperate position. With Stormwind's army stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn mysteriously absent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon has left frontier settlements like Redridge to look after themselves. The Shadowhide clan has grown increasingly bold, raiding trade routes, burning farmsteads, and pressing right up against the town's perimeter. Magistrate Solomon relies on posted bounties to draw mercenary blades where royal soldiers will not march. Lieutenant Fangore is not merely a marauding beast; he operates as an enforcer for Morganth, a rogue dark wizard lurking in the hills of Redridge. Under Fangore's command, the Shadowhide gnolls coordinate their strikes rather than fighting as disjointed scavengers, threatening to completely sever Lakeshire from Elwynn Forest. Striking off Fangore's paw provides Magistrate Solomon with proof that Morganth's brute vanguard has been broken.

quest:1801.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest sends Horde warlocks on a journey from Strahad Farsan's encampment in the Barrens to the Undercity in search of ancient demonological lore. To summon and bind a felhunter, an initiate must track down the lost Tome of the Cabal, starting with a cartographer named Jorah Annison. It marks a critical step in mastering higher demonic summoning. Summoning a felhunter is no minor trick of fel magic; the predatory beasts devour magical energies and resist standard summoning circles. Strahad Farsan explains that to draw one forth, an initiate requires the aid of specialized circles and an ancient grimoire known as the Tome of the Cabal. Authored by the first order of warlocks ever to bind a felhunter without outside aid, the book contains the exact rites and seals required to enslave such a dangerous demon. Because copies of the Tome of the Cabal have long been lost to the warlocks in Kalimdor, Strahad directs his student across the sea to Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Though nominally employed as a royal cartographer mapping Lordaeron, Annison possesses an extraordinary depth of knowledge regarding ancient and obscure texts. As Annison himself confesses, he despises the simple trade of mapmaking and hungers far more for rare histories, occult narratives, and treatises on dark magic.

quest:1802.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest tasks an Alliance warlock with tracking down the scattered, ruined halves of a singular grimoire known as the Tome of the Cabal. Recovering the missing pages from distant lands is essential for deciphering the dark rites necessary to bind a felhunter. Only a single copy of the Tome of the Cabal was ever scribed, and its violent history ensured it did not stay intact. Torn apart and vandalized, its remnants were scattered to entirely different corners of the world. One portion, a tattered manuscript ripped straight from the binding, somehow found its way across the sea into the rugged canyons of Kalimdor, falling into the hands of the centaur clans. The remaining section was intended for transport by sea from the shores of Lordaeron down to Khaz Modan, but the vessel foundered before reaching its port. Reassembling the grimoire demands surviving two treacherous perils. The sea-lost pages washed ashore off the Hillsbrad coast west of Southshore, where scavenged debris and waterlogged relics fell into the grasp of shoreline murlocs near Azurelode Mine. Meanwhile, recovering the arid half requires infiltrating Splithoof Hold in Thousand Needles, delving deep into centaur caverns to reclaim the manuscript from an ancient chest. Only by uniting these disparate halves can Krom Stoutarm inspect the lost text before it returns to Strahad Farsan.

quest:1803.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest tasks Horde warlocks with reuniting the severed halves of the ancient Tome of the Cabal for Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Once kept within the kingdom of Lordaeron, the grimoire was torn apart and scattered across the world before being lost entirely. Tracking down its damp and tattered remnants requires braving hostile waters in the Eastern Kingdoms and deep centaur territory in Kalimdor. The Tome of the Cabal was once preserved within the library walls of the old kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point, the sinister grimoire was deliberately vandalized, stripped of nearly half its pages, and sundered into two pieces. The remaining formal text was slated for transit south to the dwarven halls of Ironforge, but fate intervened: the transport wrecked along the rocky coastline west of Southshore, leaving the pages to rot in the shallows under the watchful eyes of scavenging murlocs.

quest:1804.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest marks the final preparation for Alliance warlocks seeking to command a felhunter. After piecing together the fragmented Tome of the Cabal, the warlock must gather rods of channeling from Dragonmaw orcs in the Wetlands and return to Strahad Farsan overlooking Ratchet. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Krom Stoutarm meticulously bound the tattered and mouldering remnants of the Tome of the Cabal back together. Reluctant to surrender such a rare piece of dark scholarship, the dwarf scholar extracts a promise of a future copy before passing along a fresh missive from Strahad Farsan. The tome contains the rites required to breach the Nether, but raw parchment alone cannot conduct the necessary ritual. Before Strahad's acolytes can assist with binding a demon as ravenous as a felhunter, they require focus implements to stabilize the summoned energies. Krom directs the warlock to the Wetlands, where spellcasters of the Dragonmaw clan wield rods of channeling. Prizing these foci from the hands of hostile orcs provides the conduit Strahad's circle needs to control the rift.

quest:1805.text: Tome of the Cabal. This quest marks the final preparatory leg in a Horde warlock's journey to summon and command a felhunter. Having helped Jorah Annison restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal, the practitioner must travel into hostile territory to seize three Rods of Channeling before bringing the components to Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. In the Undercity, the Forsaken scholar Jorah Annison examines the fragments of the recovered Tome of the Cabal, piecing together its eldritch passages. While pleased with the rare intellectual bounty, Jorah delivers an urgent directive sent by Strahad Farsan. To bind a demonic predator like a felhunter, raw knowledge is not enough: a warlock must possess precise instruments of power capable of focusing violent demonic energies into a binding circle. Strahad requires three Rods of Channeling, specialized conduits carried by the renegade orcs of the Dragonmaw clan. Far from the Horde's heartlands, these Dragonmaw dwell amid the ruins of Angerfang Encampment in the sodden marshes of the Wetlands. Hunting them down demands entering contested lands ruled by hostile clan remnants who despise the modern Horde just as readily as they butcher Alliance explorers.

quest:1806.text: The Test of Righteousness. The Test of Righteousness culminates at Jordan Stilwell's forge outside Ironforge in Dun Morogh. After gathering perilous components from across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, a paladin waits while the smith crafts a mighty warhammer. It marks the transition of an apprentice into a recognized champion of the Light. Master smith Jordan Stilwell plies his craft outside the gates of Ironforge. While he admits to a touch of envy toward wandering paladins, he takes profound pride in supporting the cause through his hammer and anvil. Once presented with rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines, Stilwell fulfills his promise to forge a weapon worthy of a true defender. The finished warhammer is christened Verigan's Fist in honor of Bosch Verigan, an honored dwarven paladin and dear personal friend of Jordan Stilwell. By passing this sacred weapon into a young champion's hands on behalf of himself and his wife, Stilwell ensures that the memory and valor of his fallen friend endure against the darkness threatening Azeroth.

quest:181.text: Look To The Stars. This quest marks the final chapter in Viktori Prism'Antras's endeavor to assemble a stargazing device in Darkshire. With the telescope structure otherwise built, Viktori sends travelers to the dangerous Vul'Gol Ogre Mound to retrieve a lens large enough for his contraption: a monocle worn by the ogre Zzarc'Vul. Throughout the construction of his stargazing telescope, Viktori Prism'Antras has relied on plans drafted by the gnome engineer Cog Glitzspinner. While brass tubes and sturdy mountings could be scavenged or assembled from local supplies, the apparatus required an exceptionally massive focusing lens. Standard magnifying glasses and optical components from Stormwind traders simply lacked the diameter called for by Cog's ambitious design, leading Viktori to look toward an unlikely and perilous alternative.

quest:1824.text: Trial at the Field of Giants. Trial at the Field of Giants is a warrior rites quest issued by Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo. As part of their training, martial aspirants are dispatched south into the swarming mounds of the Field of Giants to slay alien insectoid invaders. Candidates must harvest several still-twitching antennae and rush them back before the biological proof goes dormant. Warrior trainers among the Horde rarely accept mere martial competence without testing fortitude and urgency. Ruga Ragetotem challenges growing warriors at Camp Taurajo to prove themselves against an unfamiliar adversary. Aspirants are not just ordered to slay the encroaching creatures; they must sever fresh antennae and return to Taurajo within half an hour before the harvested tissue ceases twitching, demanding rapid navigation of the southern Barrens. The targets of the trial are the silithid hives burgeoning in the Field of Giants, nestled beneath massive fossilized ribcages. These crawling, chitinous insects are recent arrivals to the Barrens, disturbing the tauren hunters and shamans who watch the savannas. Ruga notes with dread that their presence bodes ill for Kalimdor, making the extermination test serve a dual purpose: proving a young warrior's combat instincts while gathering intelligence on a looming ecological menace.

quest:1825.text: Speak with Thun'grim. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze, an acclaimed orc blacksmith camping in the Barrens. Having proved themselves through demanding physical trials, warriors are invited to have custom armor forged in recognition of their valor. The quest serves as the crucial bridge connecting general warrior testing with the crafting of Brutal Armor. After proving their mettle against the silithid hives during the Trial at the Field of Giants, Horde warriors earn more than simple praise from Ruga Ragetotem. Word of their endurance and martial prowess quickly reaches Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc smith who maintains a camp perched on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Recognizing a warrior worthy of his craft, Thun'grim sends word that he wishes to fashion them an exceptional suit of battle mail. Thun'grim Firegaze does not forge for ordinary soldiers. For an armorsmith of his reputation, steel must match the spirit of the one who carries it into battle. Reaching his camp signifies that a warrior has advanced past simple militia drills and is ready to undertake the grueling, specialized tasks required to gather rare crafting reagents across Kalimdor.

quest:1838.text: Brutal Armor. Brutal Armor is a Horde warrior rite of passage overseen by the near-blind smith Thun'grim Firegaze in the northern Barrens. Seeking to craft armor worthy of a rising champion, Thun'grim sends seasoned warriors across distant lands to gather rare reagents and exotic smelting agents. Fulfilling his scroll begins the forging of a complete set of brutal battle gear. Perched along the craggy hills of the northern Barrens, the veteran orc smith Thun'grim Firegaze listens closely to the winds of war. Though his eyesight is failing and clouded, his reputation at the forge remains unmatched. Having heard rumors of a warrior whose strength and valor outpace ordinary soldiers, Thun'grim decides to craft an enduring set of mail that can withstand the harshest clashes of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Forging armor of this caliber requires far more than common ore. Struggling by firelight with weak eyes, Thun'grim pens an exacting scroll detailing the components required for the core chestpiece. The task demands common refined iron alongside rare smoky iron ingots carried by burrowing kobolds, powdered azurite worked by miners across the sea, and a volatile vial of phlogiston. Only a warrior willing to endure far-flung trials can hope to see the suit brought to life.

quest:1839.text: Ula'elek and the Brutal Gauntlets. This quest directs rising Horde warriors from the heights of the Barrens back to the coast of Durotar. Sent by the blacksmith Thun'grim Firegaze, you must seek out the Darkspear craftsman Ula'elek in Sen'jin Village to forge your Brutal Gauntlets. After proving their valor throughout the Barrens and taking up the task to assemble the Brutal Armor set, warriors are directed eastward by Thun'grim Firegaze. Rather than forging every piece on his own mountain perch, the veteran orc smith relies on a network of skilled artisans across Horde lands. To craft heavy mail gauntlets suited to an advancing champion, he sends fighters down to Durotar's rocky southern shores. In Sen'jin Village, the troll armorsmith Ula'elek works among his Darkspear kin. Far from being caught unawares, Ula'elek reveals that Thun'grim had already sent word of your deeds—and more importantly, the spirits themselves had observed your triumphs in battle. For a warrior earning a place among the Horde's elite, craftsmanship and spiritual acknowledgement walk hand in hand.

quest:1840.text: Orm Stonehoof and the Brutal Helm. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thunder Bluff to consult with Orm Stonehoof, an artisan smith. Recommended by Thun'grim Firegaze, Orm possesses the specialized craft required to forge the Brutal Helm. After proving their mettle and assembling pieces of the Brutal Armor in the Barrens, warriors are directed higher into the mesa city of Thunder Bluff. Thun'grim Firegaze, an accomplished armorsmith himself, recognizes his limits and refers his champions to Orm Stonehoof. Orm's craft is renowned throughout Kalimdor, specifically his ability to mold resilient battlefield helms from rare, savage trophies. Orm makes his home and workplace on the high bluffs of Mulgore, standing near the tranquil waters beneath the city's towering central totem. When a warrior arrives carrying word from Thun'grim, Orm steps away from routine work to discuss the demanding components needed to forge headgear truly worthy of the Horde's front lines.

quest:1841.text: Velora Nitely and the Brutal Legguards. This quest directs seasoned Horde warriors from the Barrens across the sea to the Undercity in Lordaeron. There, the Forsaken armorsmith Velora Nitely uses her retained mortal craftsmanship to forge specialized Brutal Legguards. It represents a vital step in assembling a durable set of armor for the Horde's front-line champions. After proving their mettle to the veteran smith Thun'grim Firegaze atop his vigil in the Barrens, warriors are tasked with assembling the fabled Brutal Armor. Thun'grim cannot fashion the entire suit alone and directs aspiring champions to skilled allies across the Horde. For the greaves, he sends them eastward across the Great Sea to the subterranean kingdom of the Forsaken, seeking an artisan whose work was revered long before the fall of northern humanity. Before her demise during the Scourging of the north, Velora Nitely was renowned as one of the preeminent armorsmiths in the Kingdom of Lordaeron. Despite the loss of her mortal life and the corruption of her homeland, death failed to diminish her metallurgical mastery. Now plying her trade in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity, she turns her ancient human craft toward aiding the Horde's warriors, maintaining a dry, macabre wit about her undead condition.

quest:1842.text: Satyr Hooves. Satyr Hooves is a quest given by the troll craftsman Ula'elek in Sen'jin Village. In pursuit of forging a pair of empowered brutal gauntlets, warriors must journey north into Ashenvale to hunt satyrs and harvest their magically bloated, uncloven hooves. To forge armor capable of rivaling the most brutal forces on Kalimdor, the Darkspear craftsman Ula'elek looks beyond mundane iron and leather. He directs aspiring warriors north to the ancient woods of Ashenvale, where lingering demonic corruption festers within the local satyr covens. According to Ula'elek, the satyrs in northeastern Ashenvale sustain themselves by leeching the forest's latent purity and twisting it into foul power. Those demons that have gorged themselves the deepest on this borrowed life manifest abnormal, swollen hooves that have lost their natural cloven split. Ula'elek intends to drain this concentrated magical energy and weave it directly into the gauntlets he crafts.

quest:1843.text: Brutal Gauntlets. Brutal Gauntlets is the culmination of an artisan's craft for seasoned Horde warriors. After gathering rare components across distant lands, the craftsman Ula'elek fashions a formidable pair of handguards designed to bring honor to both the maker and the bearer. Forging armor fit for a seasoned frontline warrior is more than simple metalworking—it is a spiritual undertaking for Horde artisans. Ula'elek, a craftsman residing in Durotar, pours his lineage and skill into shaping these brutal gauntlets. By employing hardened trophies harvested from dangerous adversaries, he constructs armor tailored to withstand ferocious blows while enhancing the wearer's offensive might. In orcish and troll traditions, fine arms and armor carry the prestige of the forge and the spirit of the maker into battle. When Ula'elek presents the finished gauntlets to a warrior, he entrusts them with the legacy of his ancestors. A champion who wears them into combat is expected to display courage, martial discipline, and strength worthy of the craftsmanship.

quest:1844.text: Chimaeric Horn. As part of the warrior rite to craft the Brutal Helm, Orm Stonehoof tasks an aspiring champion with journeying into the ruined Charred Vale. There, the warrior must hunt a maddened chimaera matriarch to claim her galvanized horn as both an act of mercy and proof of strength. Orm Stonehoof is willing to forge the legendary Brutal Helm for Horde warriors, but martial tradition demands that the wearer prove their mettle first. Orm does not simply ask for raw metal or coin; he demands proof of martial prowess and a willingness to confront the grim scars left behind by devastating conflict. The quest directs warriors to the southwestern reaches of the Stonetalon Mountains, into the ashen desolation known as the Charred Vale. Once lush and green, the valley was burned into a smoking wasteland. The surviving beasts wandering its soot-covered craters are twisted by agony and fury, particularly the mighty chimaeras that make their nests amid the dead trees and searing steam vents. Slaying a chimaera matriarch serves two purposes in the tauren smith's eyes. It claims the hardened, galvanized horn required for crafting the headpiece, but it also ends the creature's torment. By felling the matriarch, the warrior acts both as an executioner and an instrument of mercy for a wild spirit driven mad by the destruction of its home.

quest:1845.text: Brutal Helm. Brutal Helm marks the culmination of an arduous warrior trial overseen by Orm Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff. Having collected rare beast trophies across Kalimdor, an aspiring warrior is recognized with a formidable horned helm as a testament to their strength. Orm Stonehoof serves as a stern smith in Thunder Bluff, guiding Horde warriors through grueling rites of passage. These trials demand proof of martial capability, pushing initiates into treacherous territory to hunt ferocious creatures and claim rare trophies. Only those who have met Orm's exacting standards are granted audience for the completion of their armor. By bringing the rare chimaeric horn to Orm Stonehoof, the warrior proves their resolve against the wilderness. In recognition, Orm presents the Brutal Helm—a heavy, menacing piece of mail crafted to honor the beast and bolster the wearer in frontline combat. As he bestows it, Orm invokes the blessings of the Earthmother, looking forward to the greater deeds the warrior is bound to undertake across Azeroth.

quest:1846.text: Dragonmaw Shinbones. Dragonmaw Shinbones is a Horde warrior quest directed by the armorer Velora Nitely in the Undercity. To craft the resilient Brutal Legguards, warriors are dispatched into the southern Wetlands to harvest exceptionally thick shinbones from the hostile Dragonmaw orcs. Forging armor fit for a seasoned frontline warrior demands unorthodox materials. When tasked with fashioning Brutal Legguards, the Forsaken armorer Velora Nitely specifies a structural brace constructed from thick, resilient bone. Rather than utilizing common beasts, she directs aspiring warriors toward the Dragonmaw orcs of the Wetlands, whose dense skeletal builds provide the necessary resilience to withstand heavy blows in combat. Harvesting bone from the Dragonmaw is only half the ordeal. Velora instructs warriors to manually test every bone taken in the field; any specimen brittle enough to snap in bare hands is utterly useless for the forge. Warriors must scour the renegade encampments along the Wetlands' crags, breaking weak bones until eight genuinely sturdy examples survive the test of strength.

quest:1848.text: Brutal Hauberk. Brutal Hauberk marks the culmination of an arduous rite of passage for Horde warriors in the Barrens. After gathering rare materials and proving their mettle against dangerous foes across the lands, warriors present their bounty to the reclusive smith Thun'grim Firegaze. In return, he hammers out a rugged suit of mail designed to withstand the harshest battles. Perched along the craggy hills of the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze does not forge armor for just anyone. The reclusive orc demands that aspiring warriors travel far and wide to harvest tough beast parts, rare metal, and alchemical reagents before he even lights his bellows. The finished hauberk is not merely protective gear; it is an enduring badge of endurance and grit recognized by veteran fighters throughout the Horde. Thun'grim's task is purposefully punishing. True Horde arms and armor are expected to bear the sweat and blood of their wearer from the moment of their inception. Handing over the finished Brutal Hauberk, the smith offers no flowery praise—only the expectation that the armor will be proven in brutal combat and return bearing stories of blood and honor.

quest:185.text: Tiger Mastery. At the northern safari camp in Stranglethorn Vale, the hunter Ajeck Rouack offers to train adventurers in the discipline of big cat stalking. She starts newcomers against the younger tigers prowling near the camp to test basic hunting and tracking prowess. Having learned the art of hunting tigers from her father when she was a girl, Ajeck Rouack shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition following Welcome to the Jungle. She insists that tracking and slaying the youngest felines is the essential foundation before any hunter can advance to greater quarry. Young Stranglethorn tigers are often found in the jungle close to the expedition camp. Rouack demands that ten of these beasts be hunted down to prove sufficient skill before she agrees to provide any further training.

quest:186.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack escalates her hunting trials. Having seen your early promise with young stalkers, he now sends you into the jungle to fell mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Following your initial success against younger predators, Ajeck Rouack seeks to test your growing skills against more seasoned beasts. She directs you back out into the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale to hunt down ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers before you can pursue even greater challenges.

quest:187.text: Tiger Mastery. Deep in the jungle at Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack raises the stakes of his hunting trials. He demands the death of ten elder Stranglethorn tigers to prove your prowess before the final test. Following the earlier hunts, Ajeck Rouack asks you to pursue ten elder Stranglethorn tigers across the wilds. He considers these beasts both the most elusive to track and the fiercest to overcome. Felling ten of them serves as the prelude to a concluding trial, after which he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

quest:188.text: Tiger Mastery. Ajeck Rouack offers the ultimate challenge in his series of hunts within northern Stranglethorn Vale. After weeks of tracking an elusive beast, he challenges you to seek out the tiger Sin'Dall and bring back her paw. Having completed the earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers, you are offered one last challenge by Ajeck Rouack at Nesingwary's Expedition. The hunting camp has tracked an extraordinarily elusive tiger known as Sin'Dall across the jungle for weeks. Ajeck challenges you to track her down, fell the beast, and claim her paw as indisputable proof.

quest:189.text: Bloodscalp Ears. Kebok in Booty Bay is losing guards and agents to jungle clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe. Worried about climbing expenses and answering to Baron Revilgaz, he offers coin to any adventurer willing to hunt down the trolls and return with proof of the kill. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Kebok faces a serious operational dilemma. The local trolls in Stranglethorn Vale have been killing his agents in the jungle, and he has lost many of his best guards in skirmishes with them. With the casualties mounting, so too are the costs, leaving him frantic over how to explain them to Baron Revilgaz. Rather than allowing the losses to accumulate further, Kebok turns to outside help. He offers monetary compensation to travelers who head into the jungle, cull the Bloodscalp trolls, and bring back fifteen of their severed ears as undeniable confirmation of their demise.

quest:19.text: Tharil'zun. Marshal Marris places a bounty on Tharil'zun, the cunning leader of the Blackrock outrunners harassing the roads near Stonewatch Keep. Striking him down serves as a critical step in breaking the Blackrock clan's hold over northern Redridge. Bringing his severed head back to Lakeshire marks a hard-fought victory for the embattled town watch. The winding pass between Lakeshire and Stonewatch Keep has become a gauntlet of sudden ambushes. Blackrock outrunners and renegades prowl the rocky ridges, cutting off scouts and threatening any reinforcements attempting to push toward the fortress. Marshal Marris identifies Tharil'zun as the commander orchestrating these coordinated strikes, declaring his elimination necessary to prevent Lakeshire from being entirely hemmed in. Tharil'zun represents a dangerous breed of battlefield leader: vicious, crafty, and capable of coordinating the disparate orc raiders into an effective raiding force. Taking his head inside the shadow of Stonewatch requires cutting through entrenched Blackrock outposts. His death breaks the cohesion of the outrunner patrols, clearing a path for the Alliance to confront the garrison entrenched within the keep itself.

quest:190.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition offers a trial to those seeking to prove their prowess as big-game stalkers in Stranglethorn Vale. To join Hemet's hunting company, adventurers must first demonstrate their basic tracking ability by taking down ten young panthers. Within the wild expanse of northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary has assembled a seasoned band of big-game huntsmen. Sir S. J. Erlgadin tells anyone who wants a part of the hunt that they must first prove themselves an able panther hunter. Before Erlgadin entrusts anyone with greater game, he issues an entry test: finding and slaying ten young panthers. Simply finding the beasts is only half the challenge.

quest:191.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin demands that you prove yourself worthy of the big game hunters at Nesingwary's Expedition. Following your initial cull of younger beasts, he challenges you to track down and slay ten fully grown panthers in the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. After dispatching the young panthers around the jungle, Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks you to raise your sights. To show that you deserve to keep company with seasoned big game hunters, you are sent out to hunt ten mature panthers, which are far tougher and more dangerous than their younger kin.

quest:192.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition challenges big game hunters to track and bring down the deadliest panthers in Stranglethorn Vale. Following your earlier trials, you must now seek out and slay ten Shadowmaw Panthers. Sir S. J. Erlgadin considers Shadowmaw Panthers to be the most dangerous cats prowling the jungles of Stranglethorn. Proving your mettle as a true stalker requires crawling through the dense underbrush to track down ten of these elusive beasts, whose ferocity makes them far harder to kill than to find.

quest:1938.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic is a quest given by High Sorcerer Andromath in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. He charges adventurers with recovering a forbidden, magically sealed tome from the renegade mage Morganth, who fled with it to the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Long ago, three promising mages studied together within the Wizard's Sanctum of Stormwind. Over time, one of them, Morganth, succumbed to the temptations of dark arts and shadow magic. Despite desperate warnings from his peers urging him to turn away from such corrupting power, he refused to abandon his obsession. He was formally banished from the city's magical order, but he did not leave empty-handed—he stole a dangerous work penned by Ur, an infamous archmage whose studies ventured beyond orthodox arcana. Morganth established a new redoubt far from Stormwind's scrutiny, seizing the Tower of Ilgalar in the heights of the Redridge Mountains. High Sorcerer Andromath cannot allow such hazardous knowledge to remain in the hands of an outcast practicing forbidden sorcery. Tasking Alliance adventurers with breaching the tower's defenses, Andromath seeks the recovery of the tome before its wards fall.

quest:1939.text: High Sorcerer Andromath. High Sorcerer Andromath is a short summons directing Alliance mages to report to the summit of the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind. High Sorcerer Andromath stands as one of the kingdom's preeminent archmages outside the ruined city of Dalaran. Within the Mage Quarter of Stormwind, apprentice coordinator Jennea Cannon directs promising casters upward to the peak of the Wizard's Sanctum. High Sorcerer Andromath, one of the most senior practitioners of the arcane operating actively in the southern kingdoms, specifically requests an audience with emerging magi ready for weightier responsibilities. With the northern magocracy of Dalaran ruined in the Third War and its surviving wizards consumed by the work of rebuilding it, practitioners like Andromath hold vital strategic importance. Without easy access to the libraries of the Violet Citadel, the Alliance relies directly on senior archmages stationed within Stormwind to study ancient threats and direct research into shadowy, forbidden arts.

quest:194.text: Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

quest:1940.text: Pristine Spider Silk. Pristine Spider Silk is an initiation task for rising Alliance mages entrusted by High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind. To earn a garment fitting an adept's station, the spellcaster is dispatched into the darkened woods of Duskwood to harvest prime silk from carrion recluses. The gathered spools are delivered to tailor Wynne Larson in the Mage Quarter to prepare enchanted robes. Within the Wizard's Sanctum, recognition is measured not only by mastery over the arcane but in the regalia worn by its practitioners. High Sorcerer Andromath recognizes when a student has graduated from mere apprentice work and directs them to commission vestments proper to an adept. Rather than simply purchasing finished goods, the mage must prove both field competence and discernment by gathering pristine, unblemished silk directly from perilous beasts. The required material cannot be found in conventional merchant stalls. It must be carefully extracted from the venomous carrion recluse spiders stalking the haunted gloom of Duskwood. Once eight prime samples are gathered, they are brought across the city to Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter, where tailor Wynne Larson stands ready to spin the delicate threads into a robe of arcane significance.

quest:1942.text: Astral Knot Garment. Astral Knot Garment is the culmination of a dedicated crafting endeavor in Stormwind City. After braving the wilds to gather rare spider silk, an adventurer presents the materials to the skilled tailor Wynne Larson. The result is a fine, magical weave suited for both treacherous journeys and high-society gatherings. In the bustling Mage Quarter of Stormwind, tailors and seamstresses cater to the arcane elite and visiting nobility alike. Wynne Larson is one such artisan, renowned for her ability to weave pristine spider silk into durable, enchanted vestments. Known for a playful sense of humor, she jokes about keeping extra scraps of precious silk for her own wardrobe before delivering her expertly tailored creations. The Astral Knot Garment is prized by cloth-wearing spellcasters who demand both resilience and refinement. Woven from delicate yet hardy silk gathered from dangerous arachnids, the garment is designed to withstand the rigors of combat while maintaining the polished appearance expected at formal banquets within Stormwind Keep.

quest:1943.text: Speak with Deino. "Speak with Deino" is a summons directing promising Horde mages to seek out a skilled practitioner in Orgrimmar. Deino, a troll mage operating out of the Valley of Spirits, requires an adept to undertake critical work on behalf of their craft. Answering her call opens the path to deeper magical study and vital tasks across Kalimdor. As practitioners of the arcane hone their abilities within the Horde, instructors recognize when a student is prepared for more demanding ventures. Mentors like Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity point developing mages toward Orgrimmar. There, tucked away in the troll-dominated quarter, more specialized knowledge and perilous errands await. Deino makes her home within the Darkbriar Lodge in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits. Among the Darkspear, dedicated practitioners of the arcane are relatively rare compared to witch doctors and priests, making Deino a notable authority in the capital. She works not just for local concerns, but for the broader interests of the Horde's arcane practitioners, seeking ambitious mages willing to brave distant perils.

quest:1944.text: Waters of Xavian. Waters of Xavian is a Horde mage quest offered by Deino in Orgrimmar. Seeking to plumb ancient elven secrets, she tasks her apprentice with traveling to the ruins of Xavian in Ashenvale to draw a sample from its highest waterfall. Within the dark crevices of the Valley of Spirits, the troll mage Deino seeks out lingering reservoirs of primal arcane energy across Kalimdor. Her gaze turns to Xavian, an ancient night elf city hidden deep in the eastern canopy of Ashenvale. Legends among scholars whisper that the city was steeped in magical knowledge before the Sundering, and its waters are said to retain potent arcane properties that modern casters yearn to dissect. Reaching the source of these waters is no simple errand. Xavian no longer belongs to peaceful elven sages; it has fallen into ruin and is now overrun by feral, corrupt satyrs who fiercely guard their territory from outsiders. Prying mages must navigate past Satyrnaar and tread through dangerous waterways, avoiding both prowling beasts and demonic sentinels to fill Deino's flask at the base of the city's towering waterfall.

quest:1945.text: Laughing Sisters. Laughing Sisters is a Horde quest that sends mages into the heart of Ashenvale to gather enchanted locks of hair from wild dryads. The material is destined for Kil'hala, an experienced troll tailor at the Crossroads, to spin into an empowered mage robe. Hunting the daughters of Cenarius underscores the relentless friction between Horde spellcasters and the native defenders of the ancient woodland. Following their efforts to secure water from Xavian, rising mages are directed by Deino in Orgrimmar to assist in crafting their own enchanted vestments. Arcane tailoring of this nature demands materials imbued with raw magical essence. Dryad locks, naturally suffused with the primeval vitality of the forest, hold the necessary qualities to thread intricate magical garments capable of shielding and augmenting a caster's powers. To harvest these locks, mages must venture south toward Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale. The laughing sisters—nimble, woodland dryads allied with the night elves—guard these groves fiercely against encroaching woodsmen and outsiders alike. Because these woodland fey would never willingly surrender their hair to Horde spellcasters, the harvest is inevitably paid in blood beneath the canopy of ancient trees. Once gathered, the locks are carried south across the border to the dusty settlement of the Crossroads in the Barrens. There, the troll tailor Kil'hala receives the tribute without remorse. While acknowledging the loss of the woodland creatures with a touch of irony, Kil'hala wastes no time putting the enchanted strands to practical use, recognizing that power in the Horde often requires unyielding resolve.

quest:1946.text: Nether-lace Garment. Nether-lace Garment marks the completion of tailor Kil'hala's specialized crafting work in the Barrens. By weaving the gathered hair of dryads into refined cloth, the tailor crafts an enchanted garment fit for spellcasters. Kil'hala, working out of the Crossroads in the Barrens, undertakes the delicate process of fashioning nether-lace. Requiring rare and magically resonant components—specifically the locks harvested from the dryads known as laughing sisters in Ashenvale—the tailor binds natural woodland enchantment directly into comfortable, durable cloth. Beyond simply practicing his trade, Kil'hala has personal motivations for ensuring the quality of the garment. He is particularly keen on currying favor with Deino, a respected troll mage residing in the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. By crafting exceptional garb for aspiring practitioners, Kil'hala hopes to secure and maintain Deino's good graces.

quest:195.text: Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

quest:1950.text: Get the Scoop. Magus Tirth has locked a crucial spellbook inside his magically sealed strongbox, but he cannot recall the activation phrase to open it. To retrieve the tome, you must locate his missing apprentice somewhere around the Shimmering Flats racetrack and pry the forgotten words from him. Magus Tirth is an eccentric spellcaster dwelling on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. While he possesses the esoteric knowledge and tomes that advancing mages desperately seek, dealing with him requires patience. Tirth relies heavily on an assistant to manage mundane details, including the spoken passwords guarding his arcane repositories. When tasked with retrieving a book of power, visiting practitioners quickly learn that Tirth has locked the volume away behind magic words that have slipped his mind entirely.

quest:198.text: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek in Booty Bay hires a courier to haul miscellaneous goblin supplies north to Lieutenant Doren's camp. Local troll aggression has halted routine shipments, requiring an outside hand to ensure the goods reach Private Thorsen near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren and his outfit stationed near the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood rely on regular shipments arranged through Krazek. Persistent attacks from local trolls have made standard delivery hazardous, prompting the goblin merchant to contract an independent courier. The package must travel all the way up the jungle road, with Private Thorsen designated to receive it either in their camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

quest:1999.text: Tools of the Trade. Tools of the Trade is an initiation mission for Horde rogues given by Mennet Carkad in the Undercity. Ordered by Lord Varimathras, agents must obtain lockpicking gear and infiltrate Ambermill to recover sensitive Kirin Tor reports detailing Dalaran's current state. Following the interrogation of one of their prisoners, the Deathstalkers learned that vital intelligence concerning the ruins of Dalaran lies hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and the human mages guarding the village guard their communications fiercely. Under the orders of Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad directs promising operatives to bypass Kirin Tor sentries and secure the Dalaran Status Report. Unlike straightforward assassinations, this mission serves as a practical proving ground in infiltration and lockpicking. Operatives are outfitted with specialized thieves' tools from Estelle Gendry before marching into hostile Kirin Tor territory. Cracking the secured chest in Ambermill demonstrates that an operative has progressed beyond raw street brutality into an indispensable espionage asset for the Forsaken.

quest:2.text: Sharptalon's Claw. Sharptalon's Claw is a trophy quest representing the defeat of the ferocious hippogryph Sharptalon in Ashenvale. Taking the creature's severed talon back to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post proves your skill and protects Horde supply lines through the ancient forest. As the Horde attempts to carve out resources in Ashenvale, the native fauna proves just as perilous as the night elven sentinels. Sharptalon, a notoriously aggressive hippogryph, haunted the canopies and paths winding toward Splintertree Post. The beast preyed upon vulnerable peons and couriers traveling between the forward logging camps and the outpost, severely hampering Horde operations in the region. Under the guidance of the tauren huntress Senani Thunderheart, Horde stalkers are tasked with clearing out the deadlier predators lurking beneath Ashenvale's canopy. Carving the massive talon from Sharptalon serves as undeniable evidence that the sky-terror has fallen. Delivering the trophy to Splintertree Post earns honor among the outpost's defenders and brings relief to the frightened laborers who must walk the woods.

quest:20.text: Blackrock Menace. Marshal Marris of Lakeshire tasks adventurers with culling the aggressive Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. By seizing their battleworn axes, the town's defenders hope to break the siege tightening around the settlement. Lakeshire finds itself hemmed in on multiple fronts, but none pose so dire a threat as the Blackrock orcs spilling over from the fiery Burning Steppes. Having pushed south into Redridge, these veteran raiders have seized strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps the townspeople effectively penned inside the settlement, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads. Marshal Marris, commander of the beleaguered Lakeshire guard, cannot spare a detachment to assault their positions outright. Instead, he enlists roaming adventurers to bleed the invaders' forward scouts and foot soldiers. By demanding their crude, battleworn axes as proof of death, Marris seeks to thin the invaders' numbers both around Stonewatch to the north and in the rugged pockets of southeastern Redridge.

quest:200.text: Bookie Herod. Lieutenant Doren fears a spy among his own men after Kurzen discovered Thorsen's secret. To uncover how the secret slipped out, an investigator must infiltrate Kurzen's Compound and recover the records kept by Kurzen's logistics officer. Following the discovery of Thorsen's secret, Lieutenant Doren suspects that a traitor operates within their midst. The intelligence leak threatens their operations, and finding the traitor has become an urgent concern. Thorsen maintained a line of communication directly into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer.
