Because Herod knows how Kurzen's Compound is run from day to day, Doren believes the officer's written records hold the truth about how the operation was exposed. Reaching Bookie Herod's paperwork requires venturing into Kurzen's Compound. During Doren's time serving under Kurzen, Herod kept his office on the top floor of the compound's lone two-story house. There, among supply requisitions and missives from Colonel Kurzen himself, lie the documents that could trace how the secret was betrayed.

quest:201.text: Investigate the Camp. Investigate the Camp is an expedition task originating in Booty Bay to scout a newly established hunters' campsite in Stranglethorn Vale. Commissioned by Krazek, it tasks travelers with confirming rumors that the legendary dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary has arrived near Lake Nazferiti. Reports circulating through the docks of Booty Bay speak of an expedition of big-game hunters encamped in the northern jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Word has reached Krazek that the camp lies along the river just past the Venture Company's busy mining claim near Lake Nazferiti. In a lawless jungle teeming with dangers and competing interests, unexplained armed encampments always demand a watchful eye. What makes this particular expedition notable is the rumored presence of Hemet Nesingwary himself. The renowned dwarven marksman is known throughout the lands as an elite explorer with influential ties. Krazek prefers to take no chances with powerful figures operating in the hinterlands, sending scouts upriver to confirm whether the legendary hunter has truly arrived.

quest:203.text: The Second Rebellion. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks help against the overwhelming forces of Colonel Kurzen. Outnumbered ten to one by a cunning tactician, the rebels must rely on swift, covert strikes to survive. Cutting down Kurzen's jungle fighters is the first step toward relieving the relentless pressure on their refuge. The soldiers at the Rebel Camp face dire odds against Colonel Kurzen. Yohwa explains that the Colonel is a brilliant military tactician whose force outnumbers the rebellion by at least ten to one. Unable to wage an open war of attrition, the rebels have no choice but to adopt the Colonel's own covert tactics, launching quick incursions into his encampment to thin his ranks and escaping before heavy reinforcements can retaliate. To stem the tide, Yohwa asks you to push east into Kurzen's stronghold and eliminate a sizable contingent of his jungle fighters. Thinning out these foot soldiers eases the pressure bearing down on the Rebel Camp.

quest:204.text: Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks to blunt Colonel Kurzen's military advantage by targeting his medical support. The renegades rely on powerful remedies and toxins concocted by their practitioners, leaving the resistance fighters desperate to turn those same concoctions to their own advantage. Colonel Kurzen has bolstered his jungle force with numerous medicine men who heal his forces and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extracts. To turn the tide of the conflict, Sergeant Yohwa directs adventurers into the Kurzen Compound to scavenge those vital supplies. Securing their jungle remedies will help treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp, while capturing a sample of their venom fern extract will enable the resistance to study the toxin and manufacture their own cures.

quest:2040.text: Underground Assault. Underground Assault is an Alliance quest offered by Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. Tasked with aiding the displaced gnomes, adventurers venture into the Deadmines to salvage an intact power core from a goblin shredder. This stolen component is destined to power drilling machines intended to spearhead the liberation of Gnomeregan. Following the catastrophic fall of Gnomeregan to the primitive troggs, surviving gnomish tinkerers have been forced into exile across Khaz Modan and Stormwind. Rather than wallowing in defeat, engineers like Shoni the Shilent are already devising mechanical operations to breach their lost home. The primary obstacle is the dense, subterranean rock surrounding the technocratic city, requiring massive tunneling engines known as gyrodrillmatic excavationators. Lacking the necessary localized power grids in human lands, the gnomes have turned their sights to an unlikely and volatile alternative: goblin heavy machinery operating in the criminal underworld. Deep within the twisting shafts of the Deadmines in Westfall, Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood employs goblin engineers to manufacture war machines, including a fully operational goblin shredder. Shoni directs Alliance operatives to infiltrate this foundry, destroy or dismantle the lumbering automaton, and recover its specialized heart—the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. By commandeering the potent goblin power supply, the exiled gnomes gain the raw mechanical output needed to bore through the subterranean perimeter and launch a counteroffensive to reclaim Gnomeregan.

quest:2078.text: Gyromast's Revenge. Gelkak Gyromast seeks payback against the local murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship along the Darkshore coastline. To carry out his vendetta, the eccentric captain sends adventurers to reactivate his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Stranded upon the misty strands of Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast refuses to accept defeat at the hands of the shore-dwelling murlocs. Having salvaged the pieces needed to fuel his schemes, the eccentric captain sets his sights on complete retaliation against the tribe and their chief. Rather than wading into the surf with cutlass in hand, Gelkak relies on heavy engineering to exact his vengeance, entrusting a winding key to any landlubber brave enough to handle his mechanical subordinate.

quest:2098.text: Gyromast's Retrieval. Shipwrecked on the misty coast of Darkshore, the eccentric gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast seeks aid to restore his mechanical first mate. His vital winding key was shattered upon the rocks and scavenged by the local wildlife and murlocs. Recovering the three pieces is the first step toward getting his crew back in working order. Gelkak Gyromast is an odd sight along the gloomy sands of Darkshore: a gnome pirate stranded far from the typical sea routes of the South Seas. According to Gelkak, his vessel met an unfortunate end just off the coastline after being attacked and sunk by aggressive threshadons. Washing ashore amid the flotsam, he found himself utterly marooned and separated from his trusty crew. Gelkak's most pressing concern is not provisions or gold, but his first mate. Activating and operating this companion requires a specialized key, which shattered into three distinct fragments when Gelkak crashed onto the rocky shoals. Before he could gather the fragments, the indigenous wildlife—scuttling reef crawlers on the beach, towering foreststriders near the woods, and scavengers from the local Greymist murloc tribe—snatched the shiny metal pieces away.

quest:213.text: Hostile Takeover. Gelriz has been muscling out the moguls appointed by the trade princes and now makes a move on the most notorious pirate of all, and Baron Revilgaz will not stand for it. In response, Kebok in Booty Bay directs adventurers to steal strange blue crystals that Venture Company geologists have been finding near Lake Nazferiti. Gelriz has stepped over the line by shoving aside moguls chosen by the trade princes and making a move on the most notorious pirate of all. Baron Revilgaz refuses to permit such insolence, instructing Kebok to handle the intrusion however he sees fit. Kebok's chosen response is outright theft, targeting the strange blue stones that Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing. Venture Company geologists operating around Lake Nazferiti have taken a keen interest in these unusual crystals. Kebok wants eight samples brought back to Booty Bay, unconcerned with how they are acquired so long as they end up in his hands.

quest:215.text: Jungle Secrets. After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions. Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

quest:2158.text: Rest and Relaxation. Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road. After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey. Innkeeper Farley takes pride in his establishment's hospitality, operating under the motto of providing rest and relaxation for the tired and cold. Adventurers who mention their referral can take advantage of Farley's good graces, settling by the open fire to enjoy a warm meal, sturdy ale, and a much-needed respite before journeying further into Elwynn.

quest:219.text: Missing In Action. Missing In Action is an Alliance escort mission in the Redridge Mountains to rescue Corporal Keeshan from Blackrock orc captivity. After his regiment was wiped out in the hills, Keeshan was knocked unconscious and dragged into a cave fortress. Guiding the wounded soldier safely back to Lakeshire helps the local garrison confirm the grim fate of their missing men. The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as Blackrock orcs descend from the northern peaks. Patrols sent out by the town guard frequently run into ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's unit suffered the worst of it. Outnumbered and overwhelmed, most of the soldiers in his regiment were cut down on the spot. Keeshan survived only because a crushing blow knocked him cold before he could be executed, allowing the orcs to drag him back to their cave as a prisoner. Battered, concussed, and held deep within enemy territory, Keeshan could not make the trek back down the mountain alone. Escorting him down to the safety of Lakeshire takes him past swarming orc warbands that occupy the ridgelines. Reaching Lakeshire alive brings sorely needed relief to Marshal Marris, who has been trying to piece together what happened to the missing regiment while bracing Lakeshire for further attacks.

quest:220.text: Call of Water. This leg of the shamanic trial tasks an initiate with bringing purified water back across the Barrens to Islen Waterseer. Prepared and blessed by the recluse Brine, this vial contains the catalyst required to distill a spiritual sapta. Once brewed, the draught will reveal the elemental spirits dwelling in the distant waters of Silverpine Forest. After trekking across the southern Barrens and fulfilling the trials set by Brine, a shaman initiate receives a Vial of Purest Water. Filled from pristine springs and consecrated by Brine's secluded rites, this vessel represents the pure potential of the element. Carrying it safely back to the eastern coast where Islen Waterseer keeps vigil is the vital link connecting Brine's rustic wisdom with the formal rites of the totem. Upon receiving the pure water, Islen explains that mortal eyes cannot easily behold the elusive spirits of water. To commune with them, an initiate must consume a specialized brew known as a sapta. The liquid brought from Brine will serve as the potent foundation for this draught, opening the shaman's senses to forces hidden from common sight. Yet, as Islen cautions, communion is only half the journey; the spirits themselves demand testing.

quest:221.text: Worgen in the Woods. As the Nightbane pack encroaches further upon Darkshire, Calor tasks adventurers with striking down the pack's primary rank-and-file stalkers. These ferocious Dark Runners have overrun the nearby Rotting Orchard, threatening to completely surround the besieged town. While scouts first encountered lone worgen weaving shadowy magic on the fringes of the forest, Calor's rangings revealed a far more urgent tactical threat. Larger, swifter beasts known as Nightbane Dark Runners have massed in the Rotting Orchard just southwest of Darkshire. Rather than merely lurking beneath the canopy, these predators form the bulk of the pack's numbers, establishing a staging ground within striking distance of the village gates.

quest:222.text: Worgen in the Woods. As the Nightbane pack tightens its grip on Duskwood, Calor directs adventurers to strike against their deadliest ranks. Taking the fight directly to their southern dens and mines, defenders push back the feral threat encroaching on Darkshire. The worgen infestation haunting Duskwood is far from mindless chaos. Having carved out territory in the dark expanse south of Darkshire, the beasts known as the Nightbane have begun establishing fortified camps. Calor watches their bonfires flicker in the distance with growing dread, noting that the creatures have occupied deep caves and abandoned mining shafts. Among them, the Vile Fangs and Tainted Ones represent the most vicious breeds, displaying ferocious savagery and a tenacity that threatens to overwhelm the town's perimeter.

quest:223.text: Worgen in the Woods. This errand delivers Calor's letter of recommendation to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, concluding your pursuit of the savage worgen haunting Duskwood. Impressed by your prowess against the beastly invaders, Calor points you directly to a man fighting deeper threats among the shadows. Having culled the Nightbane pack stalking Roland's Doom and the shadowed glades, you earn the hard-won respect of Calor. Stationed on the darkened frontiers of the woods, Calor is rarely eager to hand out compliments, let alone formal introductions. Handing over a faded scrap of parchment, he directs you to deliver his word directly to Jonathan Carevin in Darkshire, remarking that if they had more fighters of your caliber, their small cohort might finally eclipse the town's beleaguered Night Watch. Jonathan Carevin operates within Darkshire under tremendous strain, wary of outsiders and perpetually pressed for time. The town faces onslaughts not only from slavering worgen, but also from unresting undead, shadowy demonic forces, and traitorous cultists aiding the corruption from within. Receiving Calor's glowing endorsement breaks Carevin's cold demeanor, confirming you as a trustworthy blade dedicated to preserving the Light against the suffocating terrors of Duskwood.

quest:226.text: Wolves at Our Heels. Wolves at Our Heels is an Alliance quest offered by Lars at Sven's Camp in western Duskwood. Tasked with hunting the rabid and starving dire wolves stalking the surrounding woods, travelers help clear immediate wilderness threats so Sven and Lars can focus on their vendetta against the necromancer Morbent Fel. Tucked away along the western hills of Duskwood near the Westfall border, Sven Yorgen and his companion Lars maintain an isolated outpost. Living away from Darkshire leaves them entirely reliant on their own foraging and hunting to survive. However, carrying fresh game through these dark woods makes Lars an irresistible target for the ravenous predators stalking the shadowed riverbanks and underbrush. The local packs of starving and rabid dire wolves roam primarily to the north and east of the camp toward the river. By culling these frenzied beasts, travelers lift an immediate siege on Lars's hunting efforts. Thinning out the wolves frees both men from constantly fighting for their daily bread, allowing them to turn their full attention toward the necromancer Morbent Fel, who lurks further east.

quest:2282.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a pivotal training assignment given to Alliance rogues by Lucius in Lakeshire. Dispatched to the nearby mill with a set of thieves' tools, initiates are tasked with infiltrating an area under Blackrock orc scrutiny to crack a locked chest and retrieve a token of thievery. In Lakeshire, rogue instructors do not bother with abstract lectures when a locked chest can teach the lesson faster. Lucius sends promising operatives northeast along the road to Alther's Mill, equipping them with their first set of thieves' tools. To earn their formal Certificate of Thievery, novices must slip into the abandoned mill, pick open Lucius's personal lockbox, and bring back the token cached within. While Alther's Mill was once an ordinary lumber outpost, it has recently drawn the dangerous attention of the Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. Lucius gleefully treats the encroaching warmongers as an added layer of practical examination. Prowling through enemy-held territory to pick locks undetected is precisely the kind of trial SI:7 expects its agents to survive.

quest:23.text: Ursangous's Paw. This quest represents the proof of felling Ursangous, one of the most ferocious and legendary predators prowling Ashenvale. Bringing the beast's severed paw to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post earns honor among the Horde's trackers. As part of the Ashenvale Hunt, trackers operating out of Splintertree Post are tasked with pursuing the ancient beasts that dominate the dense forest canopy. Ursangous ranks among the fiercest of these apex predators, known for killing numerous travelers and warriors who crossed his path. Taking down such a beast is no small feat, and claiming his paw serves as undeniable physical proof that the mighty creature has finally met his match.

quest:230.text: Sven's Camp. Sven's Camp is an Alliance quest in Duskwood that uncovers a crucial clue regarding the tragedy at the Yorgen homestead. By unearthing a buried, untitled journal from a mound of loose dirt on the abandoned farm, adventurers piece together who witnessed the slaughter of Sven Yorgen's family. Sven Yorgen was away when dark riders struck his farm, returning only to find his family murdered and his farm in ruins. Consumed by grief and vengeance, he sent allies to search the wreckage of the homestead. Hidden beneath a mound of freshly turned earth, a small, dirt-stained book lay buried where a shadowy figure had hastily hidden it.

quest:235.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. Issued by Warcaller Gorlach in Orgrimmar, this directive summons budding Horde adventurers northward beyond the Barrens into the ancient forests of Ashenvale. Players are directed to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to participate in the ongoing hunt and reinforce the Horde's expanding frontier. Orgrimmar buzzes with martial fervor, but the young city requires vast amounts of timber, meat, and secure trade routes to sustain its growth. Warcaller Gorlach serves as the voice of the Horde's high command, directing seasoned wanderers and new blood alike toward active campaigns. For warriors coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, the ancient woodlands of Ashenvale represent the next testing ground for both glory and survival. Crossing the northern border of the Barrens brings travelers directly into Ashenvale, where the Horde maintains two primary bastions: Splintertree Post nestled in the eastern woods and Zoram'gar Outpost along the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations at Splintertree Post, organizing trackers and hunters to tame the beast-choked canopy and push back against hostile night elven sentinels disputing the Horde's claims.

quest:2359.text: Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower is a covert SI:7 infiltration mission assigned to Alliance rogues in Westfall. Operating on intelligence from Agent Kearnen, agents must pickpocket a key, break into a heavily guarded Defias outpost, and retrieve sinister documents linked to unnatural experiments. At the southeastern edge of Westfall, near the river and north of the Dagger Hills, stands a lonely stone spire claimed by the Defias Brotherhood. While the Brotherhood's human thieves and brigands are common across the plains, Agent Kearnen noticed strange developments after weeks of solitary surveillance. A bizarre shipment recently arrived directly from the shadowed woods of Duskwood, escorted by monstrous, deformed sentries unlike any ordinary highwaymen.

quest:24.text: Shadumbra's Head. This quest represents the proof of victory over Shadumbra, a notoriously ferocious nightsaber stalking the western paths of Ashenvale. Taking the beast's severed head back to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post fulfills a key trial of the Ashenvale Hunt and secures travel routes toward the Zoram Strand. Shadumbra is no ordinary predator among the towering trees of Ashenvale. The great nightsaber stalked the wilderness west of Splintertree Post, preying upon Horde scouts and couriers attempting to journey toward the Zoram Strand. Her speed, stealth, and sheer savagery made travel on foot perilous, leaving Splintertree's defenders on edge whenever patrols moved west. As part of the Ashenvale Hunt, the tauren huntress Senani Thunderheart challenges Horde champions to track and fell the forest's apex beasts. Presenting Shadumbra's head is not merely a grim display of prowess; it serves as undeniable proof that the roads have been made safer and that the hunter has mastered one of Kalimdor's deadliest native stalkers.

quest:240.text: Return to Jitters. Return to Jitters concludes Chef Grual's culinary errand in Duskwood. Having prepared his infamous 'crab' cakes using the gooey legs of the local venom web spiders, Grual sends you back to the starving, terrified hermit at Raven Hill. Delivering the meal finally satisfies Jitters' desperate hunger. Duskwood is short on conventional livestock and sea life, leaving Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to improvise with whatever the blighted forest provides. His renowned 'Dusky Crab Cakes' contain no actual crab meat at all, relying instead on gooey legs harvested from the venom web spiders creeping through the wood. Grual considers this resourceful cooking; anyone with a delicate stomach might view it with horror. Jitters spends his days huddled at Raven Hill, utterly consumed by fright and paralyzed by whatever horrors drove him out of the woods. Weak with terror and unable to muster the courage to hunt or forage for himself, his empty stomach only amplifies his distress. Receiving the warm cakes brings a rare moment of relief to the trembling vagrant, who is far too hungry to question what kind of 'crab' Chef Grual used.

quest:245.text: Eight-Legged Menaces. Eight-Legged Menaces is a militia contract issued by Watcher Dodds in Duskwood. With the western border overrun by aggressive venom web spiders, the understaffed Night Watch relies on wandering adventurers to cull the brood before more guards are caught in their webs. Along the western road linking Westfall to Duskwood, the dense canopy gives way to tangled thickets choked with webbing. Pygmy venom web spiders now infest the brush in swarms, threatening travelers and encroaching upon the fragile defensive lines maintained by the Night Watch. Stationed far from the safety of Darkshire, Watcher Dodds finds himself desperately short on troops. Commander Althea Ebonlocke cannot spare reinforcements to secure remote outposts when undead and worgen press against the township itself. Left isolated, Dodds has already watched comrades fall victim to the spiders, discovering men hanging upside down in the canopy as paralytic venom slowly liquefied them for feeding.

quest:2458.text: Deep Cover. Deep Cover is an undercover assignment given to promising Horde rogues by Shenthul in Orgrimmar. The mission dispatches the operative to the Venture Company drilling grounds at Sludge Fen to establish secret contact with an embedded agent of the Shattered Hand. The Shattered Hand operates as the clandestine intelligence and assassin guild of the Horde, quietly guarding Orgrimmar's interests through ruthlessly practical means. For an entire year, the guild labored to slip an operative into the hierarchy of the rapacious Venture Company. That asset, Taskmaster Fizzule, managed to ingratiate himself into their industrial drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen. Operating deep within mercenary lines leaves no margin for error. Because Fizzule maintains a ruthless persona to satisfy his corporate overseers, any unannounced visitor risks immediate attack. To verify their identity, arriving rogues must fire twin flares from a designated signaling gun within sight of his tower, approach quietly, and perform the secret salute of the Shattered Hand before receiving his report on the Venture Company's escalating schemes.

quest:2460.text: The Shattered Salute. The Shattered Salute is an initiation ritual overseen by Shenthul within the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. By learning this distinct sign of recognition, budding rogues are taught how to safely identify fellow operatives of the Shattered Hand in the field. Within the dark tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow, the Shattered Hand operates as the clandestine intelligence and assassination arm of Thrall's Horde. Given the dangerous and secretive nature of their assignments, operatives cannot rely on overt banners or standard military heraldry. Shenthul instructs newly inducted rogues in the Shattered Salute, a specific gesture meant to serve as an unmistakable, silent signal among allies. Mastering the salute is not merely a ceremonial exercise; it is vital tradecraft. Rogue agents sent into perilous territory or tasked with infiltrating rival factions must verify contacts without alerting bystanders or targets. Shenthul insists that an operative be able to recognize and mirror the gesture effortlessly before entrusting them with covert fieldwork.

quest:247.text: The Hunt Completed. The Hunt Completed is the culminating moment of Senani Thunderheart's great beast trials in Ashenvale. By felling Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon, a Horde champion proves their strength, tenacity, and primal prowess in a contested forest. Senani Thunderheart, stationed among the Horde forces in Ashenvale, tests travelers not merely by their loyalty to the warchief, but by their understanding of wild survival. The Ashenvale Hunt targets three legendary predators stalked beneath the ancient boughs: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the fierce hippogryph Sharptalon. Felling all three and securing their trophies proves a hunter's blood flows true in the challenger's veins. For the tauren, the hunt is a sacred act of balance and respect, even amidst an active warfront. By overcoming Ashenvale's apex terrors, a hunter honors the spirits of the land and earns the ancestral blessings of Thunderheart. The hunt concludes with a formal commendation and a token of favor, cementing the champion's reputation throughout the forest.

quest:2478.text: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. This critical assignment tests a Horde rogue's stealth, thievery, and combat skills against a rogue Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens. Operatives infiltrate an oil tower, assassinate Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, and seize a potent chemical concoction for the Shattered Hand. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company maintains an isolated drilling tower. Under orders from Taskmaster Fizzule, an embedded Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, rogues are instructed to use classic underworld methods rather than outright assault. Fizzule asks rogues to pickpocket a key directly off Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him before mounting an ascent through heavily altered workers and sentries.

quest:2479.text: Hinott's Assistance. Hinott's Assistance is an urgent journey undertaken by Horde rogues suffering from a debilitating tropical toxin. Contracted during an infiltration mission in the Barrens, the affliction requires the specialized expertise of Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill. Seeking his aid promises both a life-saving cure and instruction in the art of concocting deadly poisons. Following the daring infiltration of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen, rogues find themselves afflicted by Zanzil's altered mixture. The poison wreaks havoc on the body, dulling reflexes and threatening life itself. Recognizing the severity of the affliction, rogue trainer Shenthul in Orgrimmar admits that local remedies are inadequate and directs the poisoned operative across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms. The search for a cure leads south through the continent of Lordaeron to the village of Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills. There resides Serge Hinott, an apothecary whose fascination with virulent brews makes him ideally suited to analyze the exotic sample. While ordinary healers recoiled from Zanzil's venom, Hinott treats the deadly compound with professional glee, eager to dissect the foul concoction and instruct worthy rogues in brewing their own venoms.

quest:248.text: Looking Further. Looking Further is an Alliance espionage mission directed by the wizard Theocritus via an enchanted conduit. To investigate tensions between the rogue mage Morganth and the Blackrock orcs, you must infiltrate the watch tower beside Stonewatch Keep and plant an enchanted glyph inside an unnoticed container. From his sanctum in Elwynn Forest, the wizard Theocritus maintains a vigilant watch over eastern Redridge through scrying magic. While monitoring the Tower of Ilgalar, he detects sudden contention between the renegade human warlock Morganth and the Blackrock orcs entrenched in Stonewatch Keep. Rather than working together against the Kingdom of Stormwind, these hostile factions are locked in conflict over an unknown prize, prompting Theocritus to intervene before the balance shifts.

quest:2480.text: Hinott's Assistance. Hinott's Assistance is the culmination of a Horde rogue's journey to overcome Zanzil's deadly creeping poison. Waiting upon apothecary Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill, the afflicted operative receives an antidote to the toxin alongside foundational training in alchemical venomcraft. After contracting a virulent, mind-altering toxin during an assignment in the Barrens, Horde rogues are directed north to Tarren Mill to consult Serge Hinott. A Forsaken chemist of singular focus, Hinott displays professional awe toward the poison concocted by the jungle troll exile Zanzil. While unconcerned with the troll's identity or lineage, Hinott openly commends the brew's vicious efficacy, eager to study its mechanism before formulating an antidote.

quest:249.text: Morganth. Morganth is the climactic quest concluding a long investigation by the mage Theocritus into a sinister rival perched in Redridge. Entrusted with stopping a dark warlock seeking an ancient relic of horrific power, adventurers must breach the Tower of Ilgalar and put an end to his machinations. From his sanctum at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, the mage Theocritus kept a vigilant scrying eye trained upon the crags of Redridge. What he observed confirmed his deepest anxieties: the warlock Morganth, holed up in the Tower of Ilgalar, was actively seeking the legendary Scythe of Elune. Realizing the warlock stood on the precipice of securing this dark might, Theocritus called upon bold Alliance champions to intervene before Morganth's shadow fell across the entire kingdom of Stormwind. The Tower of Ilgalar looms high above the Redridge basin, infested with gnolls and twisted arcane energies. Morganth awaited at its summit, wielding shadow magic and guarding his research. Confronting the warlock required ascending through hostile grounds to cut down the caster directly and claim his Pendant of Shadow as undeniable proof that the spire had fallen and the threat was broken.

quest:25.text: Stonetalon Standstill. Stonetalon Standstill is a Horde assignment given by Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post to secure the vital passage toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Befouled water elementals in Mystral Lake have brought supply transports to a halt, prompting the Horde to cull the hostile spirits and scout an elven gazebo overlooking nearby Alliance movements. Maintaining the Horde's foothold in Ashenvale requires a constant flow of lumber, supplies, and messengers moving between the forest and the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. The Talondeep Path serves as this critical artery, skirting past the western shore of Mystral Lake. When the waters violently churned to life with hostile elementals, travel stopped dead in its tracks. Transport caravans found themselves battered by enraged water spirits, prompting Mastok Wrilehiss to demand swift action before logistical lines collapse entirely. Mystral Lake is no longer a peaceful woodland refuge. The elementals that drift through its depths have become befouled, aggressive, and unpredictable, striking indiscriminately at anyone attempting to traverse the surrounding trails. Culling these watery fiends—and breaking the reign of the greater spirit Tideress—is essential to restoring a semblance of safety. Yet the origins of their taint remain an ominous riddle amidst the wider turmoil gripping Ashenvale's sacred groves. Beyond subduing the lake's angry spirits, the Horde recognizes a strategic opportunity in Mystral Lake's central island. An ancient night elf gazebo sits upon the islet, commanding a clear vantage point across the water toward the nearby night elf settlement of Silverwind Refuge. By scouting the structure, Horde scouts assess whether the ruins can serve as a forward observation post, ensuring Splintertree's commanders can keep a close eye on their Kalimdor rivals without being detected.

quest:251.text: Translate Abercrombie's Note. Translate Abercrombie's Note is an Alliance quest in Darkshire that tasks an adventurer with carrying an indecipherable letter to the town's resident scholar. Lord Ello Ebonlocke cannot make sense of the hermit's missive, relying instead on Sirra Von'Indi's knowledge of obscure scripts. It marks the moment Darkshire's leadership begins to look closely at the hermit's strange letter. When Abercrombie dispatches a sealed letter to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, the town leader expects an eccentric plea or bitter ramblings from the cemetery hermit. Instead, the parchment is inscribed in strange, cryptic writing that defies standard Common script. Lacking the scholarly training to decipher ancient or esoteric languages, Mayor Ebonlocke refuses to dismiss the letter out of hand, knowing that even mad hermits can pose a hazard in Duskwood. To crack the cipher, Ebonlocke directs travelers across the square to Sirra Von'Indi. Sirra is Darkshire's scholar of esoteric lore, well-versed in ancient arts and forgotten tongues. Though Sirra scoffs at Abercrombie's sanity—quipping that anyone dwelling beside a haunted graveyard must have rotted brains—he takes the parchment seriously enough to begin the painstaking process of transcription.

quest:253.text: Bride of the Embalmer. "Bride of the Embalmer" is a perilous task assigned by Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire. Having pieced together the disturbing truth behind the legendary Embalmer, town leadership sends you into the haunted cemeteries of Duskwood to find his resurrected wife's resting place. By tearing the alchemist's living heart from Eliza's cursed remains, you aim to strip him of his unholy power. For years, parents in Duskwood told their frightened children the tale of the Embalmer. According to the folktale, he was once a kindly alchemist whose mind shattered following the tragic demise of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to cheat mortality, he turned to foul sorceries and took the ultimate sacrifice: carving out his own beating heart and placing it into his wife's chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke long dismissed this as mere village folklore, but recent revelations have proven that the Embalmer walks among them, his foul handiwork festering beneath the graveyard dirt.

quest:254.text: Digging Through the Dirt. Digging Through the Dirt marks the grim culmination of the hunt for the Embalmer's missing heart in Duskwood. Deep in the ravenous quiet of Raven Hill Cemetery, a disturbed mound of earth conceals a buried horror that refuses to stay dead. Amid the countless weathered headstones of Raven Hill Cemetery sits a patch of recently turned, semi-loose soil marked with the name Eliza. While many graves in Duskwood lie desecrated by scavengers or feral ghouls, this earth was placed with deliberate intent. Digging past the topsoil reveals the splintered timber of a buried coffin, sealing away whatever remnant the Embalmer sought to hide away from the light of day.

quest:256.text: WANTED: Chok'sul. A bounty posted in Thelsamar by Magistrate Bluntnose calls for the death of Chok'sul, an ogre warlord menacing northeastern Loch Modan. Believed to be organizing the assaults against local settlements and critical infrastructure, bringing his head secures a handsome reward from the town's leadership. While troggs and wildlife constantly test the borders of Loch Modan, the arrival of organized ogres represents an escalation that the local dwarven mountaineers cannot ignore. Settling into encampments along the rugged northeastern reaches of the valley, these brutes have moved beyond simple scavenging. According to local scouts and town authorities, their raids are focused, persistent, and dangerous. Thelsamar's Magistrate Bluntnose identified Chok'sul as the mastermind coordinating the violence against the town, the nearby dwarven excavation site, and the Stonewrought Dam itself. Fearing catastrophic damage to the valley's prized engineering feat and civilian lives, the magistrate placed a bounty upon the ogre chieftain: dead through any means necessary, with his severed head required as proof.

quest:261.text: Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade, at Nijel's Point, says his order is at war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. He asks you to prove your allegiance by destroying thirty undead ravagers in the Valley of Bones. Brother Anton speaks bluntly. He says the Scourge must be halted before it swallows the land and pulls the world into darkness, and the Scarlet Crusade has pledged itself to that fight. If you are with them, he wants your courage and allegiance shown by destroying thirty undead ravagers. They are found south of Anton, in the Valley of Bones. Succeed, and the Crusade will welcome you.

quest:262.text: The Shadowy Figure. Haunted by the massacre of his family, the hermit Sven Yorgen tasks you with discovering the identity of a mysterious stranger seen lurking near his farm on that fateful night. Armed only with an enigmatic book recovered from the ruins, you must consult the residents of Darkshire to trace the stranger's footsteps. Sven Yorgen lives in hiding along the desolate hills of Duskwood, broken by the horrific butchery of his family. While he originally placed blame on the mysterious black riders terrorizing the woods, his memory remains tormented by another detail: a quiet, shadowy figure who was lurking nearby on the night of the massacre. Desperate for answers, Sven entrusts you with the only physical clue recovered from the wreckage—a strange book left behind at the ransacked farm. With no direct leads to pursue in the perilous wilderness, the trail points back east toward Darkshire. Sven hopes that someone among the superstitious locals might recognize the curious volume. Darkshire harbors its share of oddities and mediums, most notably Madame Eva, whose occult senses and divinations allow her to peer beyond ordinary mundane sight to read the spiritual impressions clinging to mysterious relics.

quest:265.text: The Shadowy Search Continues. Following Madame Eva's divination, this investigation leads from her parlor to Clerk Daltry in Darkshire. It centers on tracing the origins of the journal recovered from the ruins of Sven Yorgen's ransacked farmstead. After examining the dirt-stained journal salvaged from the tragedy at Sven's farm, Madame Eva discerned that while its author was an outsider, the physical volume itself came from within Darkshire. Clerk Daltry frequently sells blank ledgers and tomes to traveling scholars, spellcasters, and record-keepers. By following the trail of local commerce, investigators seek a mundane paper trail to identify an otherwise elusive and sinister trespasser lurking in the gloomy groves of Duskwood.

quest:266.text: Inquire at the Inn. Inquire at the Inn is an Alliance quest in Darkshire that continues the investigation into the mysterious stranger connected to Sven Yorgen's ruined farm. Directed by Clerk Daltry, adventurers take a recovered journal to the Scarlet Raven Tavern to question Tavernkeep Smitts about who stayed there. After Clerk Daltry finishes examining the tattered book recovered from Sven Yorgen's farm, he suggests that any stranger visiting Darkshire would almost certainly have passed through the local tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern stands across town as Darkshire's only gathering hall and lodging house, making it the most sensible place to track down transient visitors.

quest:268.text: Return to Sven. This quest marks the moment Sven Yorgen finally learns the truth behind the brutal massacre of his family at the Yorgen Farmstead. After tracking down the runaway Jitters, you return to Sven's isolated camp on the edge of Westfall carrying the vagrant's completed journal. The journal promises answers to the questions that have haunted Sven since the attack. When Sven Yorgen's farm was attacked, Jitters fled into the woods in terror, leaving behind only an incomplete diary amidst the slaughter. Terrified of Sven's wrath and haunted by what he witnessed, Jitters hid deep within Duskwood. When confronted, he hands over his completed journal willingly, desperately hoping that providing the full story of the attack will spare him from having to face the vengeful farmer in person.

quest:269.text: Seeking Wisdom. Seeking Wisdom is an Alliance errand carrying Jitters' Completed Journal from the embattled camps of Duskwood into the safety of Stormwind City. Sven Yorgen sends adventurers to consult Bishop Farthing at the Cathedral of Light, hoping holy counsel will reveal how to destroy the shielded necromancer Morbent Fel. Duskwood suffers under lingering curses, ravenous undead, and the growing indifference of Stormwind's royal court. Sven Yorgen, a broken-hearted survivor camping near the borders, knows ordinary strength cannot pierce the dark wards of the necromancer Morbent Fel. Armed with the assembled diary of the vagrant Jitters, Sven urges traveling heroes to petition the church rather than the crown, sending them north along the road to the Cathedral of Light.

quest:270.text: The Doomed Fleet. The Doomed Fleet is a journey northward dispatched by Bishop Farthing in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. Seeking a way to defeat the powerful necromancer Morbent Fel, heroes are sent across Khaz Modan to the drowned wreckage off the coast of the Wetlands. Conventional steel has proven ineffective against the dark wards shielding Morbent Fel at his retreat on the Forlorn Rowe. To pierce such necromantic defenses, Bishop Farthing instructs adventurers that they must forge a weapon bound to the Holy Light. The key component is Lightforge Iron, a rare and consecrated metal whose strikes carry holy truth, cutting through sorcerous protections that turn aside ordinary blades. Unfortunately, Lightforge Iron is not kept in ready supply in besieged Duskwood. Farthing recalls that years ago, the Third Fleet of the island nation of Kul Tiras met catastrophe along the treacherous shores of the Wetlands north of Ironforge. Aboard one of those sunken galleons was a shipment of the precious ore. Adventurers must travel all the way to Menethil Harbor to consult Glorin Steelbrow, a dwarven contact who knows the marshes and their shipwrecks best.

quest:2745.text: Infiltrating the Castle. Master cheese monger and intelligence broker Elling Trias directs you into the royal seat of Stormwind Keep. Your objective is to rendezvous with his fellow operative Tyrion, who has spent weeks watching the corrupt nobleman Lord Gregor Lescovar from the keep's gardens. When you bring your findings to Elling Trias in his Trade District cheese shop, he quickly grasps the gravity of the Defias threat nestled deep inside the kingdom's governance. Legal channels will not suffice to expose or punish someone as deeply entrenched and protected as Lord Gregor Lescovar. Trias offers a dangerous route forward: delivering extrajudicial justice within the very walls of Stormwind Keep to permanently sever the conspiracy. Trias does not work alone in the high halls. For weeks, an operative named Tyrion—a clever gnome adept at concealment—has staked out the keep's courtyards and manicured royal gardens. Tyrion has watched Lescovar's movements, noting who enters his chambers and when the traitor confers with his covert Defias contacts. Reaching Tyrion without arousing the suspicion of the Royal Guard is the vital next link in the chain.

quest:275.text: Blisters on The Land. Blisters on The Land is an Alliance quest offered by Rethiel the Greenwarden along the eastern ridges of the Wetlands. Sensing an unnatural sickness stirring the swamp, the lone bog beast warden tasks travelers with culling the diseased Fen Creepers that stalk the waterways. Putting these shambling plant horrors to rest is Rethiel's attempt to break the swamp's rising fever. From its grove amid the marshes, Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the soggy expanse of the Wetlands. The marshes have never been gentle, but recently an unnatural sickness has begun to spread through the mire. Rethiel perceives this affliction as a growing fever in the earth itself, one that causes wild nature to warp into mindless, shambling monstrosities. The primary symptom of this rot is the rise of Fen Creepers—decaying elemental masses of swamp vegetation that shamble along the waterways. Rethiel describes them as diseased blisters swelling upon the surface of the land. Because their tormented existence only spreads agitation through the marsh, the Greenwarden charges passing allies with destroying them so their tangled remnants can settle harmlessly back into the mud.

quest:276.text: Tramping Paws. Tramping Paws is an Alliance task given by Rethiel the Greenwarden at the Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands. Troubled by the surging Mosshide gnoll population near the Gate of Algaz, the bog beast protector tasks adventurers with culling their numbers before their fires and trampling paws ruin the bog. For many years, the Mosshide gnolls inhabited the Wetlands without utterly overwhelming its natural order. Lately, however, their pack numbers have exploded south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and pawprints trample rare fen flora, and their crude logging strips vital groves to feed their campsite blazes. Left unchecked, the burgeoning packs threaten to degrade the fragile marsh ecology. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the marsh with an eye for balance rather than civilization. To the Greenwarden, the issue is not that gnolls exist, but that their runaway population outstrips what the Wetlands can support. By driving Mosshide gnolls and mongrels back into manageable numbers, adventurers help preserve the wetlands and earn the reluctant approval of an ancient wilderness guardian.

quest:277.text: Fire Taboo. Fire Taboo is a task assigned by Rethiel the Greenwarden along the marshy roads of the Wetlands. Tormented by the suffering of the local forest, the bog beast sends travelers to strip the Mosshide gnolls of the crude flints they use to ignite and burn living wood. By depriving the gnolls of fire, Rethiel hopes to spare the bog's ancient boughs from being consumed. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the wilds of the Wetlands, maintaining a profound spiritual kinship with the trees of the marsh. While the natural cycle of rot and renewal belongs in a swamp, the deliberate destruction of the timber cuts deep into Rethiel's spirit. To a living spirit of the marsh, hearing the groans of living boughs chopped down and cast into hearthfires is an agony Rethiel can no longer endure in silence. The Mosshide pack ravages the wetlands for warmth and territory, felling green trees rather than gathering fallen deadwood. To curb their expansion without a prolonged war of attrition, Rethiel targets the key tool of their destruction: the crude flints used by the stronger gnolls. By stripping the pack of fire-making implements, Rethiel renders them unable to burn the felled timber. Rethiel personally shatters each collected stone and casts the dust into the sea, ensuring those sparks will never ignite the forest again.

quest:288.text: The Third Fleet. Sitting outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons drowns his memories in dwarven mead. He is the lone survivor of Kul Tiras's Third Fleet, a proud naval force incinerated off the coast of the Wetlands by orc-enslaved red dragons during the Second War. First Mate Fitzsimmons spends his days slumped outside Menethil Harbor's Deepwater Tavern, nursing an unending hangover and memories he cannot shake. Once an officer aboard the Wave Mistress—a ship-of-the-line sailing under the maritime banner of Kul Tiras—he now trades his grim memories for flagons of dwarven mead. Anyone willing to buy him another drink receives an eyewitness account of one of the Second War's most devastating naval slaughters. During the Second War, the Third Fleet sailed along the shores of Khaz Modan when disaster struck from the skies. The Dragonmaw clan, having subjugated the red dragonflight at Grim Batol, unleashed dragonfire upon the unsuspecting warships. Fitzsimmons recalls helpless wooden hulls burning beneath towering plumes of flame, dragging entire crews into the deep. Fitzsimmons alone survived to wash ashore, leaving his fallen brothers behind in the watery graveyard now known as the Doomed Fleet.

quest:289.text: The Cursed Crew. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the sole living survivor of the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, asks for mercy on behalf of his lost brethren. Trapped by a dark relic hidden aboard their sunken ships off the Wetlands coast, the drowned sailors and marines wander the wrecks as restless undead. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras foundered along the jagged shores north of Menethil Harbor, its tragedy did not end beneath the waves. While First Mate Fitzsimmons managed to wash ashore alive, his fellow crewmen met a fate far worse than death. A mysterious and terrible treasure hidden deep within one of the hulls unleashed an eerie sorcery upon the dying sailors, binding their souls to the sea-battered timbers and denying them the peace of the grave.

quest:290.text: Lifting the Curse. First Mate Fitzsimmons believes that the restless curse binding his fallen crewmates stems from a dark artifact secured aboard their wrecked ship, the Intrepid. To set his brethren free, an adventurer must face the ghost of Captain Halyndor, take the strongbox key, and recover the relic from the submerged hull. First Mate Fitzsimmons survived the tragic fate of the Third Fleet, but the memory of his comrades haunts his waking hours and his dreams. He remains convinced that the undeath gripping his shipmates is tied to a mysterious, malignant object locked away inside the strongbox of his old vessel, the Intrepid. Overseeing the wreck is the spectral remnants of Captain Halyndor, who even in death fiercely guards the key to the vessel's deepest secrets.

quest:2904.text: A Fine Mess. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, an injured goblin named Kernobee lies battered among troggs after being ambushed by Dark Iron dwarves. Rescuing him uncovers unsettling intelligence about Dark Iron involvement in subterranean drilling machinery, which must be relayed all the way to Booty Bay. While navigating the dangerous inner chambers of Gnomeregan, adventurers discover Kernobee stranded in the dormitory area. Severely beaten and groggy, the goblin survived capture by Dark Iron dwarves who left him behind to perish among the feral troggs. Finding a friendly face is his only chance of surviving the trek back through the contaminated corridors.

quest:292.text: The Eye of Paleth. This quest sees an adventurer recover a blackened, pulsating gem known as the Cursed Eye of Paleth from the flooded wreckage of the Intrepid. Recovered at the behest of the haunted sailor Fitzsimmons, the malevolent artifact must be brought to Menethil Harbor so the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow can divine how to purge its blight. Beneath the treacherous waters of the Baradin Bay, resting inside the locked strongbox of the sunken vessel Intrepid, lies no ordinary treasure. The chest yields a blackened orb pulsing with an unsettling radiance: an Eye of Paleth. Rather than gleaning sacred light, this particular stone has been warped into an engine of suffering, heavily tied to the restless spirits and doom that claimed the sailors of the Third Fleet.

quest:2922.text: Save Techbot's Brain!. Tinkmaster Overspark tasks Alliance adventurers with retrieving the memory core of Techbot from the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. The once-helpful mechanical assistant suffered severe brain polarization during the city's fall, causing it to run amok. Overspark hopes recovering its core will allow him to reverse the damage and restore his beloved creation. Before the disaster that claimed Gnomeregan, Techbot served as a marvel of gnomish ingenuity. Designed by Tinkmaster Overspark, the automaton aided researchers with countless integrated gizmos and an encyclopedic repository of technical knowledge. However, the chaos of the trogg invasion and the venting of toxic radiation did not spare the machine. A stray electrical surge jolted Techbot's delicate internal architecture, completely polarizing its positronic brain into a volatile negatronic state. Trapped within the contaminated halls of Gnomeregan, Techbot now wanders in a manic frenzy, attacking anyone in sight. Despite its violent malfunction, Overspark refuses to write off his prized assistant as scrap. He recruits capable operatives to track down the berserk automaton, extract its memory core from the metal chassis, and deliver it safely to Ironforge so the Tinkmaster can unravel the polarization and repair Techbot's mind.

quest:2923.text: Tinkmaster Overspark. This errand directs Alliance adventurers in Stormwind to Tinker Town in Ironforge, where Tinkmaster Overspark is mourning a tragic malfunction. Brother Sarno sends word that Overspark's mechanical creation, Techbot, has gone rogue amidst the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. Reaching the Tinkmaster is the first step toward recovering the wayward construct's memory core. Brother Sarno, tending to travelers in Stormwind City, shares word of an unfortunate dilemma brewing among the gnomish refugees. Tinkmaster Overspark—one of the brilliant minds behind Gnomeregan's wonders—is distraught over the corruption of Techbot, a once-helpful mechanical servant that served the tinkerers faithfully before the city fell into ruin. The quest dispatches helpful souls via the Deeprun Tram up into Ironforge's bustling enclave of Tinker Town. There, Overspark desperately seeks adventurers brave enough to plunge back into the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan to salvage what remains of Techbot's faculties before the construct causes irreparable harm.

quest:2924.text: Essential Artificials. Essential Artificials is an Alliance quest offered by Klockmort Spannerspan in Ironforge's Tinker Town. Tasked with plumbing the depths of the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, adventurers must recover crucial universal components that were abandoned during the gnomes' desperate evacuation. When the trogg invasion overwhelmed Gnomeregan and toxic radiation flooded its corridors, the fleeing gnomes could only carry what was immediately at hand. Among the countless marvels left behind were supplies of essential artificials—specialized, nigh-universal mechanical components prized by tinkers and crafters. Now operating out of Tinker Town in Ironforge, master tinker Klockmort Spannerspan finds his groundbreaking new experiments stalled without them. These vital devices are housed within heavy, steam-powered storage units known as artificial extrapolators located deep within the fallen city. Salvaging them requires braving irradiated halls crawling with mutated leper gnomes, malfunctioning defense automatons, and feral troggs. Recovering a cache of twelve components allows Klockmort to resume his critical work, pushing gnomish innovation forward despite their exile.

quest:2925.text: Klockmort's Essentials. Klockmort's Essentials is a summons carrying urgent word from the night elf Mathiel to his gnome friend, Klockmort Spannerspan. Unable to abandon his duties to travel to Dun Morogh, Mathiel enlists passing Alliance travelers to answer Klockmort's plea for help in Ironforge. The call directs adventurers into Tinkertown to prepare for a perilous venture into the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. Word travels far even in troubled times. When Klockmort Spannerspan found himself in need of bold allies for a mission into Gnomeregan, he reached out across the sea to his night elf acquaintance, Mathiel. Mathiel, bound to his own post, cannot journey to the mountain kingdom himself, but he refuses to leave his friend's plea unanswered. Instead, he appeals to capable Alliance adventurers visiting him on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus to make the trek to Dun Morogh on his behalf. Klockmort Spannerspan operates out of Tinkertown, the bustling refugee district of Ironforge where displaced gnomes have gathered since the catastrophic fall of their underground city. Amid the whir of gears and clouds of steam, Klockmort is formulating plans to retrieve vital machinery left behind in Gnomeregan's contaminated corridors. Taking Mathiel's referral leads adventurers directly to Klockmort's workshop, enlisting them in his reclamation efforts.

quest:2926.text: Gnogaine. Gnogaine is an Alliance quest offered by Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. In an eccentric attempt to synthesize a cure for the leper gnomes—or perhaps concoct an extraordinarily potent beverage—Ozzie tasks adventurers with venturing toward Gnomeregan to gather radioactive fallout from glowing troggs. Ever since the fall of Gnomeregan, refugees like Gnoarn have fixated entirely on exterminating the trogg invaders and reversing the radioactive affliction that mutated their brethren. In contrast, Ozzie Togglevolt and his partner Razzle Sprysprocket take a somewhat less orthodox approach from their workshop in Kharanos. While purporting to pursue a cure for the leper gnomes, Ozzie openly admits their experimental formula might just as easily end up being a recipe for remarkably strong rum. To refine their concoction, the inventors require raw toxic residue directly from the epicenter of the catastrophe. Equipping adventurers with a leaden collection phial, Ozzie sends them toward the breached tunnels of Gnomeregan. There, roving irradiated invaders and pillagers—troggs saturated with leaking waste—glow with the sickening green energy needed to charge the flask.

quest:2927.text: The Day After. The Day After is an Alliance quest that bridges the survivors in Ironforge with researchers stationed in Dun Morogh. Gnoarn, lamenting the catastrophic radiation leak that cost him his legendary hair and his homeland, sends adventurers to assist Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos as he searches for a solution. Gnomeregan's downfall took a deeply personal toll on every survivor, and Gnoarn is no exception. A refugee in Ironforge's Tinker Town, Gnoarn mourns not only the mechanical wonderland stolen by trogg invaders, but also his prized gnomefro—a glorious mane lost in an instant when a bolt of toxic fallout blasted him. Driven by lingering fury toward the troggs and a desperate hope to recover the city, he directs sympathetic travelers to colleagues who might still possess the scientific prowess to salvage what remains. Rather than surrender to despair, Gnoarn points Alliance champions toward Kharanos, where inventive minds have begun tackling the fallout. Chief among them is Ozzie Togglevolt, working alongside his partner Razzle Sprysprocket. Ozzie remembers the horrifying moment of the catastrophe vividly, recalling how Gnoarn's locks fell out in clumps while madness and thirst for vengeance took hold. Now, in the relative safety of the snowbound town, Ozzie turns his engineering genius toward analyzing the contamination in hopes of finding an antidote.

quest:2928.text: Gyrodrillmatic Excavationators. Deep in the Dwarven District of Stormwind, Shoni the Shilent is preparing a fleet of massive tunneling machines intended for transit to Dun Morogh. Stalled by a shortage of mechanical parts, she dispatches adventurers into the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan to harvest intact gears and innards from rogue automatons. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, gnomish engineers work tirelessly to support their displaced kin. Among them is Shoni the Shilent, who oversees an ambitious subterranean venture: a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators destined for Dun Morogh. The project faces a critical bottleneck, as she lacks the necessary components to get the massive digging rigs operational. Rather than forge new parts from scratch, Shoni looks directly to the source of gnomish high technology: the lost city of Gnomeregan. The ruins and surrounding tunnels crawl with malfunctioning defense bots, mechanical sentries, and clockwork laborers roaming unchecked. Venturers are sent to pry apart these rogue machines and haul two dozen bundles of robo-mechanical guts back to human lands. Bringing back two dozen mechanical guts provides enough scrap to patch together exactly one excavationator. With nearly four hundred machines remaining in her fleet, Shoni's dream of mass subterranean transport remains a monumental, agonizingly slow endeavor. Even so, every functioning machine represents a small step toward regaining ground lost in the cataclysm of Gnomeregan.

quest:293.text: Cleansing the Eye. Cleansing the Eye is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the murky Wetlands south to the human capital of Stormwind. After recovering the cursed orb known as the Eye of Paleth, travelers must seek the aid of Archbishop Benedictus to purge its lingering taint. The Eye of Paleth recovered from the marshlands does not shine with holy clarity. Instead, it is steeped in an unsettling shadow, bearing the residual sorrow and trauma of the terrible tragedy that unfolded where it was lost. The dwarf Glorin Steelbrow recognizes the power of the orb, but admits he lacks the divine craft to lift such a heavy affliction. Because the Eyes of Paleth were originally fashioned by human priests of the Holy Light, only their highest order possesses the knowledge to undo the defilement. Glorin directs adventurers to journey to the kingdom of Stormwind and present the darkened orb to Archbishop Benedictus, leader of the Church of the Holy Light. Benedictus recognizes the immense danger of an unpurified relic and takes it upon himself to restore its sacred luminance.

quest:2930.text: Data Rescue. When the gnomes evacuated their irradiated capital, massive archives of vital technical knowledge and records were left behind. Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge recruits daring operatives to infiltrate Gnomeregan and retrieve a high-security Prismatic Punch Card. Navigating through layers of computerized clearance, couriers must punch their way through progressively fortified terminals deep within the ruined city. The sudden fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and deadly radiation forced the gnomish populace to abandon centuries of advanced research, schematics, and civic logs. Scattered throughout the technological corridors are Matrix Punchograph terminals, the automated data hubs that regulate security clearances and file storage. For exile leaders like Master Mechanic Castpipe, recovering these punch-encoded archives from the ruined depths represents one of the highest priorities of the refugee community in Tinker Town. Gnomish data protocol demands rigorous clearance before granting access to central mainframes. Operating the system requires starting with a basic White Punch Card found among the wreckage outside the inner gates. Inserting it into a Matrix Punchograph 3005-A in the Train Depot produces a Yellow card, which must then be carried into the Dormitory's 3005-B terminal for a Blue upgrade, advanced through model 3005-C for a Red card, and finally brought down into the Engineering Labs to encode the coveted Prismatic Punch Card.

quest:2931.text: Castpipe's Task. Castpipe's Task is an Alliance summons directing capable adventurers to seek out Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge. Castpipe is coordinating perilous salvage operations into the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan to extract vital mechanical and technical records. It serves as an official briefing that points mercenaries toward deep-retrieval missions inside the fallen city. Following the tragic fall and subsequent radioactive quarantine of Gnomeregan, the surviving gnomes took refuge in Ironforge's Tinkertown. While their grand home remains overrun by troggs and irradiated constructs, crucial operational records and mechanical schematics are trapped deep within the city's surviving computing arrays. Recognizing that these files could prove invaluable to reclaiming or understanding what went wrong, Master Mechanic Castpipe began actively enlisting intrepid outsiders willing to brave the toxic halls. Word of Castpipe's venture is spread by figures like Gaxim Rustfizzle of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences. Though Castpipe is not a member of this esteemed academic body himself, fellow gnomes respect his technical acumen enough to endorse the effort. Rustfizzle's own calculations put the likelihood of Castpipe's mission having true strategic value at an encouraging eighty-four percent, motivating travelers to report to Tinkertown for orders.

quest:294.text: Ormer's Revenge. Ormer's Revenge begins the retributive campaign of Ormer Ironbraid, an explorer stranded high above the Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. After unearthing ancient fossilized bones, the dwarven dig team inadvertently drew packs of ravenous mottled raptors that slaughtered their companions and trapped the survivors on a rocky bluff. The Whelgar Excavation Site was meant to be a triumph for dwarven archaeology, exposing massive prehistoric remains buried beneath the Wetlands muck. Instead, unearthing the colossal bones caught the attention of the marsh's native raptors. Drawn by the disturbance, packs of mottled predators swarmed the dig site, catching the excavators off guard and tearing through their ranks. Only a handful of dwarves survived the initial slaughter. Ormer Ironbraid, Merrin Rockweaver, and Prospector Whelgar managed to scramble up a bluff overlooking the pit, but they remain pinned by aggressive packs below. Driven by raw grief and boiling anger, Ormer refuses to merely hide. Bound by duty to guard the trembling Prospector and Merrin, he enlists able travelers to thin the surrounding Mottled Raptors and Mottled Screechers as the opening salvo of his vengeance.

quest:2945.text: Grime-Encrusted Ring. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, adventurers can recover a jewelry piece heavily caked in toxic filth and hardened muck from a Dark Iron dwarf invader. Discovering its true identity requires using the Sparklematic 5200, an industrial cleaning automaton found inside the Dormitory sector. Once scrubbed clean, the ring reveals personal markings that launch a journey to return or refashion the heirloom. Gnomeregan's corridors are swimming in toxic sludge, oil, and radioactive fallout, so it is no surprise that items dropped in the fighting become coated in impenetrable sludge. Slain Dark Iron dwarves infiltrating the city often carry heavily soiled trinkets, chief among them this grime-encrusted band. The crust is far too tough for mundane hand-washing, completely obscuring whether the metal beneath is copper, gold, or junk.

quest:2947.text: Return of the Ring. After scouring away layers of subterranean sludge in Gnomeregan's automated cleaning apparatus, an adventurer uncovers a pristine golden ring bearing the seal of Ironforge and the initials 'TdK'. Tracing those markings leads up to the bustling artisan alleys of the dwarven capital to locate its eccentric creator. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, ancient machinery still whirs in defiance of the trogg invasion. Feeding a grimy, caked bauble into the Sparklematic 5200 strips away years of irradiated toxic grime, revealing a polished Brilliant Gold Ring thrumming with arcane potency. Stamped along its inner band is the distinct hallmark seal of Ironforge, alongside three neatly engraved initials: 'TdK'.

quest:2949.text: Return of the Ring. After scouring away the filth of Gnomeregan in the Sparklematic 5200, an adventurer uncovers a ring bearing the seal of Orgrimmar and the engraved letters 'NOG'. Tracing the piece back to the Horde's capital leads directly to the goblin engineer Nogg, who has his own curious theories about the city's fall. Gnomeregan is an Alliance city deep in Khaz Modan, making the recovery of a ring bearing the official seal of Orgrimmar entirely unexpected. Once processed through the gnomes' Sparklematic cleaning rig, the bauble sheds its thick layer of subterranean sludge, revealing a surge of magical power and the partially legible letters 'NOG'. Whether crafted in Kalimdor or brought along on an ill-fated expedition, the trinket clearly has roots in the Horde capital.

quest:295.text: Ormer's Revenge. Ormer's Revenge is an Alliance task given by Ormer Ironbraid at the ruined Whelgar Excavation Site in the Wetlands. With the initial scout raptors culled, Ormer demands the slaughter of the heavier Mottled Scytheclaws and Razormaws that drove his expedition from the pits. Ormer Ironbraid's grudge against the raptors running rampant over the Whelgar Excavation Site is deeply personal. After thinning out the smaller juveniles that overran the upper camp, he turns your blades against the adult predators prowling the lower dig site. The Mottled Scytheclaws and Razormaws represent the core threat to any hope of reclaiming the archaeological effort, tearing through dwarven prospectors and leaving the trenches littered with shattered crates and abandoned picks. The excavation pits have effectively turned into a raptor nesting ground. As Ormer broods on the ridge overlooking the dig, he directs capable adventurers down into the mud to strike directly at the mature beasts. While Prospector Whelgar and his crew hope to salvage ancient relics, Ormer is entirely consumed by vengeance, demanding a hefty tally of dead scytheclaws and razormaws before he considers taking on the apex terror of the site.

quest:2951.text: The Sparklematic 5200!. Deep within the ruins of Gnomeregan, the Sparklematic 5200 is an automated cleaning device that continues to function amidst the chaos. By feeding it a grime-encrusted object scavenged from the subterranean halls along with a nominal coin fee, adventurers can restore salvaged trinkets, gems, and scrap to pristine condition. It stands as a vibrant testament to the enduring ingenuity and eccentricity of gnomish engineering. Amidst the radioactive fallback and trogg infestation consuming Gnomeregan, a pocket of surviving gnomes maintains a secure perimeter near an extraordinary invention: the Sparklematic 5200. Built to scrub the harsh subterranean filth off salvaged valuables, this sturdy contraption promises to put the 'shine back in shine-tastic.' Even while subterranean monstrosities pound on the bulkheads, the machine sits ready for commercial operation. The cleaning mechanism is anything but gentle. Once an adventurer deposits a grime-caked relic alongside three silver coins, the Sparklematic surges into a violent, churning frenzy. The entire iron apparatus groans, vibrates, and lurches from side to side as it strips away toxic sludge, irradiated grease, and rock dust. Moments later, it expels whatever was buried beneath the muck, ranging from precious minerals to mechanical components.

quest:2952.text: The Sparklematic 5200!. Deep within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan sits the Sparklematic 5200, an automated cleaning contraption designed to scrub toxic filth from recovered salvaging. Operating the machine strips heavy grime from soiled objects and packages whatever is salvaged in a decorative gift box. Gnomish engineering often prizes efficiency and whimsy in equal measure. The Sparklematic 5200 was built to handle toxic and contaminated refuse, scouring away grime and caustic residue through automated cycles. Once loaded and paid, the contraption rattles through its cleaning routine before emitting a cheerful ding, neatly wrapping whatever remains into a present tied with a bow. Since the fall of Gnomeregan to the troggs and the subsequent radiation disaster, countless personal effects and technological scraps were smothered in industrial mire. Adventurers who feed grime-encrusted objects into the machine can reclaim lost gemstones, raw ores, and long-lost valuables that were swallowed up when the city was vented.

quest:2953.text: More Sparklematic Action. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan stands the Sparklematic 5200, an automated cleaning apparatus left behind during the city's evacuation. For a small fee of silver, this machine vigorously scrubs salvageable curiosities from the muck and radioactive sludge coating the fallen capital. The Sparklematic 5200 represents the ingenious automated infrastructure gnomes installed throughout Gnomeregan before the trogg invasion and subsequent fallout. Even with toxic waste and hostile automatons filling the corridors, this contraption still performs its exact programming whenever provided with three silver coins and a grime-encrusted artifact. When engaged, the Sparklematic lurches wildly while dousing and scrubbing the inserted relic in potent gnomish cleaning solvents. Once the cycle finishes with a cheerful chime, it dispenses a neatly packaged box containing whatever salvage was preserved beneath the corrosive trogg slime and toxic filth.

quest:296.text: Ormer's Revenge. Ormer's Revenge is the culmination of Ormer Ironbraid's campaign to avenge the dwarven excavators slaughtered at the Whelgar Excavation Site. Convinced that a cunning beast named Sarltooth spearheaded the savage raptor assault, Ormer sends an adventurer to slay the pack leader and claim his talon as proof. Following the slaughter of the Explorer's League diggers at the Whelgar Excavation Site, Ormer Ironbraid watched the teeming raptors from his ridge and observed a beast that dwarfed the rest. Known as Sarltooth, this particularly large and vicious raptor perched above the dig works, directing or leading the pack that drove the dwarves out. To Ormer, the beast was not merely wildlife, but the instigator of an attack on King Magni Bronzebeard's subjects. Ormer demands capital justice for the massacre, instructing adventurers to climb the high paths of the excavation walls and put an end to Sarltooth. By retrieving one of the beast's formidable talons, the fallen workers are avenged, sending a harsh message across the marshes that attacks against dwarven expeditions will not go unanswered.

quest:2962.text: The Only Cure is More Green Glow. Following earlier inconclusive tests on surface troggs, Ozzie Togglevolt tasks adventurers with retrieving pure, high-potency radioactive fallout directly from inside Gnomeregan. His ultimate goal is to understand the toxic radiation that devastated his people and concoct a cure for the afflicted leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt's preliminary trials outside the city were a failure. The irradiated troggs roaming Dun Morogh carried insufficient and impure residue, leaving his lab in Kharanos with more questions than answers. To engineer a true remedy for leper gnomes, Togglevolt concludes that scientific integrity demands a fresh, concentrated sample directly from deep within the city's toxic belly. Obtaining fallout of sufficient potency means braving Gnomeregan itself. The lower depths around the Hall of Gears and Clean Zone teem with irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes spawned by the disastrous venting of radioactive waste. Extracting this unstable ooze into a heavy leaden phial is hazardous work: the fallout rapidly degrades, making containment extremely volatile and time-sensitive.

quest:2996.text: Seeking Strahad. Seeking Strahad is an essential rite of passage for Horde warlocks who have outgrown their basic summoning arts. Instructed by Gan'rul Bloodeye in the shadowy clefts of Orgrimmar, practitioners must travel south to Ratchet to study beneath a renegade human summoner. Within the dark crevices of the Cleft of Shadow, the orcish warlock trainer Gan'rul Bloodeye guides young practitioners in the treacherous art of commanding the Nether. Eventually, an apprentice warlock reaches a threshold where tribal tutelage is no longer sufficient. Gan'rul acknowledges that more volatile entities require specialized instruction, pointing his pupils outside the city walls to a figure possessing deeper mastery over dark arcana. The tutor chosen by Gan'rul is Strahad Farsan, a human sorcerer dwelling in an isolated tower overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet. Despite the enduring hatred between the Horde and humankind, warlocks exist in a realm beyond conventional faction loyalties. Power, discipline, and ritual knowledge supersede ancestry, and Strahad cares far more for an apprentice's inner hatred and aptitude for subjugation than the color of their skin.

quest:3001.text: Seeking Strahad. Seeking Strahad is an undertaking entrusted to Horde warlocks by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity. Halgar directs his pupil across the Great Sea to the dusty hills above Ratchet, where a human sorcerer holds the keys to deeper, more dangerous summonings. It marks the transition from foundational shadowcraft to the demanding art of conjuring a felhunter. Carendin Halgar, the Forsaken warlock trainer who oversees the dark arts in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, recognizes when an initiate has outgrown basic instruction. Rather than keeping his pupils within the bounds of Lordaeron's ruins, he commands them to seek out Strahad Farsan. Halgar warns that while Strahad is a living human, he is far from weak and must not be treated as an enemy. For warlocks, the pursuit of demonic mastery routinely supersedes racial and factional boundaries. Strahad operates in relative neutrality high on the bluffs overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens.
