From his perch near the stone watchtower, he looks down on the bustling sailors, mercenaries, and merchants below with mild disdain, mocking their blissful ignorance of the twisting nether. Strahad does not mind the distrust or simmering hatred in the eyes of Horde practitioners who arrive at his feet; instead, he regards that raw malice as a potent fuel to be shaped into dark authority.

quest:303.text: The Dark Iron War. At the northern edge of the Wetlands, Motley Garmason mounts a desperate defense to reclaim Dun Modr from the Dark Iron clan. After enemy saboteurs shattered the Thandol Span and seized the town, the Ironforge Mountaineers are left holding a tenuous line while waiting for reinforcements that may never arrive. Dun Modr once stood as Ironforge's proud bastion guarding the southern end of the Thandol Span, the colossal bridge connecting Khaz Modan to Lordaeron. When Dark Iron saboteurs and demolitionists detonated the bridge's archway, they severed Alliance transit and swiftly overwhelmed the stronghold. Motley Garmason and a handful of surviving defenders managed to pull back just far enough to establish an observation camp, but without immediate counterattacks, the entire northern gateway risks permanent Dark Iron dominion. With dwarven regiments deployed to distant Alliance battlefields, Motley's small detachment has been largely left to fend for itself. His scouts attempt to signal Ironforge for relief, but communications have faltered and promised reserves are nowhere to be seen. In an attempt to buy time and disrupt enemy entrenchments, Motley orders surgical strikes directly into Dun Modr's ruins to thin the ranks of Dark Iron engineers, tunnelers, and front-line soldiers before they can push further south into the Wetlands.

quest:304.text: A Grim Task. Following the devastating Dark Iron assault on Dun Modr and the Thandol Span, Longbraid the Grim seeks vengeance for fallen kin and lost soldiers. He tasks brave travelers with tracking down and slaying the elusive Dark Iron warlock Balgaras the Foul, taking his ear as proof of the deed. The northern reaches of the Wetlands have seen intense fighting between the Mountaineers of Ironforge and infiltrators from the Dark Iron clan. During the siege, the town of Dun Modr was overtaken, and the western bridge of the Thandol Span was shattered. Longbraid the Grim lost not only many loyal soldiers in the assault, but also his own brother, leaving him determined to see the enemy paid back in kind. Reconnaissance by scouts like Roggo revealed that the Dark Iron contingent occupying Dun Modr is commanded by a warlock known as Balgaras the Foul. Rather than meeting his foes face to face, Balgaras cowers in hiding while ordering his soldiers to carry out his dark designs. Longbraid hopes that cutting down Balgaras will break the backbone of the Dark Iron force, allowing the survivors of Ironforge to secure the vital passage northward.

quest:305.text: In Search of The Excavation Team. In Search of the Excavation Team begins with Tarrel Rockweaver in the Wetlands, who is distraught over a sudden silence from his wife, Merrin. Assigned to the prestigious Whelgar Excavation Site to the east, she has missed two weeks of regular letters, prompting fears that disaster has struck the expedition. Travelers are tasked with venturing into the marsh to locate the dig site and ascertain her safety. While stationed in the soggy expanse of the Wetlands, Tarrel Rockweaver anticipated steady correspondence from his wife Merrin. Operating out of the dwarven dig known as the Whelgar Excavation Site, Merrin had maintained weekly dispatches describing their work. When two full weeks passed without a single word, Tarrel grew convinced that calamity had overtaken the camp. With official dwarf authorities stretched thin, he relies on passing scouts to brave the perils of the marshes to see if the diggers still draw breath. The Whelgar Excavation Site represents a typical dwarven endeavor to unearth ancient Titan relics and Titan-forged history buried in the muck of the Wetlands. However, digging into prehistoric strata in wild territory frequently exposes crews to untamed beasts and hostile subterranean threats. Reaching the site requires heading eastward into territory far removed from the relative safety of the main roads, where whatever disrupted the diggers' letters still lingers.

quest:306.text: In Search of The Excavation Team. This errand delivers word of a disastrous dinosaur attack at the Whelgar's Excavation site back to Menethil Harbor. Merrin Rockweaver writes a hasty letter to reassure her anxious husband, Tarrel, while recounting how the expedition was overrun. After locating the remnants of the excavation team cowering near the ridge overlooking the dig site, Merrin Rockweaver provides a hasty report. Unearthing rare artifacts alongside massive prehistoric fossils proved fatal when packs of native mottled raptors swarmed the diggers. The sudden ferocity left most of the crew dead and the survivors cut off from civilization. Returning to Menethil Harbor brings grim comfort to Tarrel Rockweaver. Knowing his wife and at least two companions survived thanks to the courage of a defender named Ormer eases his mind, though the slaughter of so many colleagues weighs heavily on the town's frontier spirit.

quest:3099.text: Tainted Scroll. The Tainted Scroll is an early quest in Deathknell that directs newly awakened Forsaken warlocks to their trainer, Maximillion. Through this missive, Maximillion invites the initiate to embrace power and dark servitude as a means of securing genuine freedom. Shortly after newly risen Forsaken begin clearing out mindless Scourge remnants around Deathknell, an ominous missive arrives bearing the seal of Maximillion, the local warlock trainer. The scroll beckons the recipient to contemplate the nature of servitude and autonomy before returning to the ruined settlement to speak with him directly.

quest:3100.text: Simple Letter. The Simple Letter is an introductory directive that guides novice warriors to trainer Llane Beshere at Northshire Abbey. It marks the beginning of their formal martial instruction and urges them to assist the troubled citizens of the valley. The Simple Letter serves as an initial introduction for aspiring warriors arriving in Northshire Valley. Directed to Llane Beshere, the resident warrior trainer at Northshire Abbey, the letter prompts newly arrived fighters to make contact with their instructor, familiarize themselves with their surroundings, and prepare for the demands of martial life. Although Northshire Abbey enjoys protection under the watchful presence of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the peaceful facade of the valley belies deeper trouble. As Beshere notes upon receiving the letter, the surrounding residents face numerous plights that require able-bodied protectors, urging fresh recruits to master their weapons and step forward in defense of the realm.

quest:3101.text: Consecrated Letter. The Consecrated Letter is an introductory summons carried by initiates of the Holy Light arriving in Northshire Valley. It directs the bearer to report to their class trainer at Northshire Abbey to begin their training and embrace their role as a visible symbol of faith. The Consecrated Letter marks the formal beginning of an initiate's journey in Northshire Valley. Addressed to newly arrived wielders of the Holy Light, the document calls the bearer to seek out their trainer at Northshire Abbey to formalize their instruction and accept their responsibilities within the Kingdom of Stormwind. Upon presenting the letter, the initiate is reminded of the weight carried by their vocation. The Holy Light shines visibly within those who channel it, making them immediate symbols of hope to allies and clear targets for their adversaries. The trainer emphasizes that such power demands disciplined conduct and an awareness of one's public example. Beyond spiritual obligations, the letter establishes an ongoing relationship between student and mentor. As the initiate tests their mettle against the local threats confronting Northshire, they are expected to return regularly to the abbey grounds to unlock deeper understandings of combat and divine grace.

quest:320.text: Return to Bellowfiz. Return to Bellowfiz is a short delivery quest in Dun Morogh where an adventurer brings a cask of local Evershine to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It concludes a local favor, rewarding the thirsty driver with a welcome drink. Return to Bellowfiz is an errand in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. After aiding with local hunting, an adventurer receives a freshly brewed cask of Evershine with instructions to carry it straight to Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot. It is a straightforward favor that highlights the informal camaraderie and mutual support that keep the cold frontier running. Steelgrill's Depot serves as a busy center of mechanical testing, vehicle maintenance, and gnomish craft just outside Kharanos. For pilots stationed out in the freezing winds, nothing hits the spot quite like a draught of strong local drink. Pilot Bellowfiz wastes no time upon delivery, eager to uncork a bottle on the spot and enjoy the fruits of local labor.

quest:321.text: Lightforge Iron. Lightforge Iron is an Alliance salvage task given by Glorin Steelbrow in Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are sent to scour the wreckage of the Flying Osprey, an elven destroyer carrying rare sacred metal that was lost alongside the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras during the Second War. While most of the sunken hulls littering the Wetlands coastline belonged to the famed Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, one vessel was distinct: an elven destroyer christened the Flying Osprey. Bound from Lordaeron, the ship sought safety in numbers alongside the naval fleet, carrying a precious cargo of Lightforge iron. Unfortunately, convoying with war galleys did little to spare it when the Dragonmaw clan's enslaved red dragons descended from the sky, setting the fleet ablaze and plunging both soldiers and sanctified metal beneath the tides.

quest:322.text: Blessed Arm. Having salvaged lightforge ingots from the wreck of the Flying Osprey in the Wetlands, an adventurer is directed to carry the precious metal to Stormwind City. There, the master dwarven smith Grimand Elmore awaits to fashion the raw metal into a tool capable of confronting the necromancer Morbent Fel. Lightforge iron is not an everyday trade metal found in standard market stalls. Renowned for its resonance against foul and unholy entities, it demands a smith who understands its temper and quirks. After the shipment was recovered from the wreck of the Flying Osprey off the Wetlands coast, Glorin Steelbrow packed the reclaimed ingots into a sturdy crate, knowing of only one artisan in the southern kingdoms suited to work such extraordinary material: master weaponsmith Grimand Elmore. Situated amidst the soot and clatter of Stormwind's Dwarven District, Grimand Elmore maintains one of the city's finest anvils. When presented with the recovered shipment, Elmore notes that years have passed since he last hammered lightforge iron. Intrigued by the heroic errand and eager to strike a blow against the necromancer Morbent Fel, the veteran artisan readily agrees to lend his hammer to the cause.

quest:323.text: Proving Your Worth. Proving Your Worth is a crucial step in Sven Yorgen's campaign for revenge in western Duskwood. Before allowing an adventurer to confront the necromancer Morbent Fel directly, the grieving hermit demands proof that they can overcome the undead legions infesting Raven Hill Cemetery. Sven Yorgen hides in a secluded camp north of the howling woods, consumed by grief and fury over the slaughter of his family. He has pieced together that the shadowy Dark Riders who razed his homestead were allied with a sinister necromancer named Morbent Fel. Though Sven hungers for retribution, he is not reckless enough to throw an untried recruit directly into Fel's grasp. He demands a display of sheer combat mastery against the skeletal forces occupying Raven Hill Cemetery. To satisfy Sven, adventurers must push deep into the necropolis of Raven Hill, south of Forlorn Rowe. The mausoleum and the surrounding grounds crawl with restless corpses bound by Fel's foul magic: sword-wielding Skeletal Raiders patrol the tombstones, while Skeletal Warders and Healers tend the darker chambers beneath the earth. Clearing this vanguard is a bloody chore, especially with horrors like the vengeful phantom Mor'Ladim prowling the cemetery paths.

quest:324.text: The Lost Ingots. The Lost Ingots is an Alliance task in the Wetlands to recover consecrated metal from a shipwreck. After finding only a single bar in a sunken chest, travelers must hunt down the local Bluegill murlocs who looted the remaining shipment. Off the misty shores of the Wetlands lies the shattered wreckage of the Flying Osprey. Sent to retrieve precious Lightforge iron for the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow, seekers discovered that the cargo hold's waterlogged chest was nearly empty. The ravenous local Bluegill murlocs had already scavenged the rest of the vessel, taking the gleaming ingots for themselves. Lightforge iron is no ordinary ore; it is rare, specialized metal attuned to work sacred smithing craft. Allowing it to rot in murloc encampments is unthinkable for a dwarf of the Light. By hunting down the Bluegill raiders swarming the shallows near the broken hull, adventurers prise back the scattered bars so Glorin Steelbrow can see the iron hammered into a weapon.

quest:325.text: Armed and Ready. Armed and Ready marks the culmination of forging a weapon specifically designed to strip away the unholy defenses of the necromancer Morbent Fel. Having secured Grimand Elmore's craft, the adventurer carries Morbent's Bane back across the river to the vengeful Sven Yorgen in Duskwood. Morbent Fel's grasp on the Raven Hill cemetery seemed unbreakable. Conventional steel shattered or deflected harmlessly off the dark wards shrouding the necromancer. Overcoming such vile magic required a specialized artifact: Morbent's Bane. With the metal shaped by Grimand Elmore in the Dwarven District of Stormwind and properly consecrated with sacred power, the ward-breaking relic is finally complete and ready to sever Fel's connection to unlife.

quest:328.text: The Hidden Key. Tucked away in the binding of Bookie Herod's ledgers is a small brass key alongside notes referencing a secure strongbox. Locating this container deep within the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound may reveal how Private Thorsen was betrayed. Searching through Bookie Herod's ledgers yields no direct mention of Private Thorsen, but it reveals something else: a small brass key concealed inside a book's binding. Scraps among the paperwork make passing mention of a secure strongbox tucked away inside the Stockpile, the cavern complex at the rear of Kurzen's Compound. Opening that container might reveal how Thorsen's cover was blown. Reaching the strongbox requires delving into the cave system behind the compound. Heavy, bronze-bound, and sturdily constructed, the chest sits among stacked crates in the cave.

quest:329.text: The Spy Revealed!. Inside Bookie Herod's strongbox lies a damp piece of parchment detailing the daily routines of Private Thorsen. Bearing only the initial M, this correspondence suggests an informant has embedded themselves among the rebels in northern Stranglethorn Vale. The muddy note is meant for Lieutenant Doren. Opening the strongbox reveals not just valuables, but an itinerary tracking Private Thorsen. The barely legible writing recounts his patrol routes, his companions, and his daily activities around the Rebel Camp, marked only with the signature -M. Such detailed observations could only come from someone living alongside Thorsen, pointing to a traitor within the rebel camp.

quest:330.text: Patrol Schedules. Following the discovery of an incriminating message signed only by an initial, Lieutenant Doren seeks to identify the traitor within the Rebel Camp. By cross-referencing duty rosters, duty records can reveal who shared patrol routes with Private Thorsen during the previous week. The recovered note bears only the initial M, which provides little on its own to expose the conspirator aiding the Kurzen forces. However, the author mentions sharing regular duty paths alongside Private Thorsen throughout the previous week. Lieutenant Doren directs you across the Rebel Camp to speak with Corporal Sethman, the soldier responsible for maintaining duty logs, to identify who walked alongside Thorsen.

quest:331.text: Report to Doren. After obtaining the patrol information, Corporal Sethman directs you back to Lieutenant Doren. Delivering these findings brings crucial military intelligence directly to the rebels' commander in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Corporal Sethman reminds you that Lieutenant Doren wants a direct report on the patrol information. You must bring what you learned back to Doren.

quest:335.text: A Noble Brew. Deep within the shadowed recesses of the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Zardeth of the Black Claw schemes against the city's nobility. An inquisitive peer, Lord Wishock, threatens to uncover the warlock enclave beneath the tavern, prompting a quiet gathering of rare and potent reagents to neutralize the threat. Beneath the streets of the Mage Quarter, the warlock coven operating out of the Slaughtered Lamb enjoys a precarious secrecy. That secrecy is jeopardized by Lord Wishock, a member of the House of Nobles who has caught wind of the dark magic simmering below the city. Wishock has begun lobbying his peers for a full investigation, which would bring the city guard and royal scrutiny down upon the coven.

quest:336.text: A Noble Brew. A Noble Brew is the culmination of a covert scheme orchestrated from the shady cellar beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind. Operating at the behest of Zardeth of the Black Claw, an unwitting or uncaring courier delivers a potent concoction known as Black Claw Stout to Lord Baurles K. Wishock inside the Royal Keep. Lord Baurles K. Wishock is a nobleman who frequents the Hall of Petitioners in Stormwind Keep, preaching self-importance and the future of the kingdom. Yet beneath his aristocratic posturing lies an open secret known to the patrons of the Slaughtered Lamb: by night, Wishock frequents the tavern's upper rooms, drinking heavily and running up massive tabs he never settles. Worse still in the eyes of the establishment, he spends his days petitioning to shut the tavern down entirely.

quest:3369.text: In Nightmares. In Nightmares is a Horde quest that tasks an adventurer with carrying a disturbing relic, the Nightmare Shard, to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem atop Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Originally recovered as a glowing fragment from the Wailing Caverns, the shard reveals a deeply unsettling corruption seeping into the Emerald Dream. After examining the strange crystal retrieved from the depths of the Wailing Caverns, Falla Sagewind recognizes that it is made from the pure essence of the Emerald Dream. Yet the vision dwelling inside is dark and chaotic, bearing the hallmark not of peaceful slumber, but of a waking nightmare. Reluctant to speak openly about such alarming omens, she entrusts the shard to you with instructions to seek out Thunder Bluff's most venerated elder druid, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem.

quest:337.text: An Old History Book. Recovered from the blighted soil and monstrous dens of Duskwood, this battered tome bears the official stamp of the Royal Library of Stormwind. Titled 'The History of Stormwind,' it vanished prior to the kingdom's reconstruction following the First War. Returning it restores a lost chronicle to Head Librarian Milton Sheaf and begins an effort to preserve Southern human history. Discovered among the hostile undead and brutish ogres roaming Duskwood, this mud-caked volume is a rare surviving artifact from the era before Stormwind's destruction. Bearing the kingdom's formal library seal on its opening page, it was checked out decades ago—before the Horde razed the capital—and was presumed lost forever amid the fall of the south. When brought back to Milton Sheaf in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep, the book is recognized as an invaluable treasure destined for the rare books archive. Years of exposure in the haunted wilderness have left its pages badly degraded, and the find spurs Sheaf to recover more lost knowledge, looking north to Southshore, the town closest to the ruined kingdom of Alterac and its abandoned libraries.

quest:3370.text: In Nightmares. Following the discovery of a strange glowing shard, Falla Sagewind recognizes that the artifact contains the pure essence of the Emerald Dream tainted by dark visions. She dispatches an adventurer to Darnassus to deliver the disturbing relic directly to the elder druids of the Cenarion Circle. The glowing shard recovered from the depths of Wailing Caverns proves far more dangerous than simple crystal. Upon inspecting it, Falla Sagewind identifies it as an embodiment of the Emerald Dream's purest essence. Yet rather than reflecting the verdant harmony of the natural world, the stone twists with unsettling, fearful visions. Shaken by what she sees, Falla refuses to delve deeper herself and insists the shard must be safely transferred to senior leadership within the Cenarion Circle.

quest:34.text: An Unwelcome Guest. An Unwelcome Guest is a local task in Lakeshire where resident Martie Jainrose seeks retribution against Bellygrub, a destructive wild boar. The beast has rampaged through her garden and trampled her seasonal daffodils, prompting a bounty on the creature's tusk. In the lakeside town of Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose tends to her domestic grounds amidst the gathering shadows over the Redridge Mountains. Her quiet routine is shattered by a persistent local terror: a notoriously aggressive wild boar that has repeatedly invaded her garden. Having trampled her prized patch of daffodils beyond recovery for the season, the distraught resident turns to capable travelers to put an end to the rampaging animal. The beast responsible is known to the locals as Bellygrub, an apt title coined by Lakeshire's town guard leader, Marshal Marris. Bellygrub spends the bulk of his time rooting and foraging through the brush in the fields southwest of the town. However, his voracious appetite and boldness often draw him dangerously close to civilized homes, culminating in the complete ruin of Martie's floral beds and demanding his definitive removal.

quest:343.text: Speaking of Fortitude. "Speaking of Fortitude" is an Alliance errand within Stormwind City begun by Brother Kristoff in Cathedral Square. Preparing a sermon titled "Fortitude of the Spirit," Kristoff enlists an adventurer to visit the Royal Library within Stormwind Keep and ask Head Librarian Milton Sheaf for a specific technical text. Brother Kristoff, one of the priests stationed in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, seeks to deliver a sermon on the Fortitude of the Spirit. Rather than drawing solely from clerical scripture, Kristoff looks to the craft of metalworking to illustrate the temper and resilience of faith. Specifically, he requires a treatise known as "The Stresses of Iron" to quote during his address, hoping its lessons on enduring pressure will resonate with his congregation. Stormwind Keep houses the Royal Library, the central repository of knowledge, history, and civic treatises for the kingdom of Stormwind. Because the collection spans countless shelves and centuries of work, Kristoff directs messengers to Milton Sheaf, the head librarian. Sheaf prides himself on knowing the archive by heart, making him the only practical guide for tracking down obscure craft manuscripts among the keep's sprawling vaults.

quest:344.text: Brother Paxton. Brother Paxton is an errand that sends adventurers from Stormwind's royal archives out to Northshire Abbey. Librarian Milton Sheaf directs searchers there to track down a borrowed dwarven mining treatise that never found its way back to the city shelves. When researchers come looking for rare technical lore within Stormwind City, the head librarian Milton Sheaf often finds his collection scattered. A notable treatise on metallurgical techniques, 'The Stresses of Iron' by dwarven prospector Margulf Blaggon, is missing from the capital's shelves. Rather than being misplaced in the capital, it was loaned out months ago to the clerics of Northshire Abbey for transcription. The task of transcribing and preserving literature falls to Brother Paxton, the caretaker of the abbey's library. While the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics values knowledge, manual hand-copying of lengthy technical manuscripts is painstaking and slow. Caught red-handed with the overdue tome, Paxton admits he has yet to finish duplicating Blaggon's work, stalling the recovery of the original manuscript.

quest:345.text: Ink Supplies. Ink Supplies is an Alliance errand on behalf of Brother Paxton, a monastic scribe residing in Northshire Abbey. Needing a specialized mineral component to brew his fast-drying ink, Paxton sends an adventurer east into the embattled township of Lakeshire to secure Rethban ore from Foreman Oslow. Brother Paxton takes immense pride in his literary craft, refusing to rely on standard inks for vital transcriptions like The Stresses of Iron. Instead, he brews a custom recipe noted for its resistance to smearing and its rapid drying time. The formula's chief flaw is that it dries out even in the pot if left unattended too long. Replenishing his stock requires raw Rethban iron ore, a distinctive mineral mined in the rocky reaches of the Redridge Mountains. When travelers arrive in Lakeshire carrying Paxton's humble requisition, they find the settlement in no condition to indulge a distant monk. Foreman Oslow oversees the strained town laborers, who are wholly occupied with shoring up barricades, rebuilding ruined structures, and bracing against ongoing raids from the Blackrock orcs. Oslow has neither the men nor the patience to dig ore for Stormwind's scribes, leaving outsiders to brave the perilous Rethban Caverns on their own.

quest:346.text: Return to Kristoff. Return to Kristoff concludes Brother Kristoff's search for the elusive tome, The Stresses of Iron. After journeying through Redridge to fetch ore for special ink and waiting on Northshire's scribes, the adventurer finally brings the borrowed volume back to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind. Brother Kristoff, stationed in Stormwind's Cathedral Square, needed access to a specialized metallurgical volume known as The Stresses of Iron. The pursuit of the work sent couriers across human lands, leading first to the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep and then deep into Northshire Abbey. At the abbey, Brother Paxton was busily copying the text by hand, delayed by a shortage of Rethban ore needed to craft scribe's ink. With the ore retrieved and the copy complete, Paxton finally surrenders the original volume for its return to the city. In a kingdom constantly pressed by outside threats, the quiet work of Northshire's copyists remains vital to preserving civic and spiritual lore. Brother Paxton's request to apologize to Librarian Milton Sheaf highlights how thin the abbey's resources have worn. Valuable books must be meticulously duplicated stroke by stroke using mineral-rich inks before they can be released back into Stormwind's care, turning a simple book request into an arduous logistical errand.

quest:347.text: Rethban Ore. Foreman Oslow directs adventurers into the Rethban Caverns of Redridge to retrieve a peculiar dark mineral. While too soft to forge reliable armor or weapons, its unique pigmentation makes it indispensable to the scribes of Northshire Abbey for crafting specialized ink. Rethban Ore is named after its discoverer, Bart Rethban. Unlike common iron or copper, this ore holds little value at an armorer's anvil—when smelted down, the resulting metal lacks the tensile strength required for sturdy weapons or plate. Its true value lies in its raw, dark, flat coloration, which monks and scribes prize as a pigment base for rich manuscript dyes. The primary deposits of the mineral lie within the Rethban Caverns, nestled in the northern mountains of Redridge. Unfortunately for the stoneworkers of Lakeshire, the local miners have abandoned the cavern. A fierce band of Redridge gnolls has seized the tunnels, putting gnoll drudgers to work chipping away at the rocky veins for their own crude purposes. Brother Paxton, a monk residing within the quiet walls of Northshire Abbey, depends on this pigment to reproduce historic texts. His current undertaking—a transcribed copy of the treatise 'The Stresses of Iron'—has ground to an abrupt halt without the proper dye, sending messengers and adventurers deep into gnoll-infested territory to secure the raw stone.

quest:349.text: Stranglethorn Fever. Deep within Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa claims to know how to draw out the beast known as Mokk the Savage. Before communion with the spirits can begin, the witch doctor requires a Gorilla Fang as an offering. Once the ritual commences, defending the troll from agitated jungle beasts is necessary to lure the creature forth. Witch Doctor Unbagwa possesses the ritual knowledge needed to summon Mokk the Savage out of the surrounding jungle. To begin the incantation, the witch doctor demands a Gorilla Fang. Communing with the spirits carries a heavy risk, as the ritual chant draws the attention of other gorilla beasts in the vicinity, demanding protection while the magic does its work.

quest:350.text: Look to an Old Friend. Master Mathias Shaw directs an investigator to seek out an unconventional contact in Stormwind's Trade District. Because noble corruption shields powerful traitors from standard legal justice, the spymaster reluctantly relies on the intelligence network of the city's finest cheesemonger.

quest:3513.text: The Runed Scroll. The Runed Scroll is a curious document tied with a silvery ribbon found in the wilds of Kalimdor. Its formal appearance suggests military or administrative communications originating from the night elves across the border. Discovering it leads Horde scouts directly to the Mor'shan Rampart to warn the guards of northern activity. Wrapped tightly with an ornate silvery ribbon, the scroll immediately marks itself as something foreign to the rough leathers and parchment favored in the Barrens. Its fine craft and script point toward the night elves nestled beneath the dense canopies of Ashenvale just to the north. In a territory contested along every ridge and road, an intercepted missive is of paramount strategic value to the Horde's front lines. Rather than sending the scroll across the plains to the Warchief in Orgrimmar, any adventurer with battlefield sense recognizes the urgency of local command. At the Mor'shan Rampart, stationed right where the red dirt of the Barrens yields to the lush forests of Ashenvale, the orc warrior Kadrak maintains watch over border incursions. Delivering this scroll provides the Rampart's outpost with crucial intelligence regarding night elf troop movements.

quest:3514.text: Horde Presence. Horde Presence is a military strike commissioned by the orc Kadrak at the border of the Barrens and Ashenvale. Prompted by an intercepted missive, the Horde sends a champion high into Stonetalon Peak to eliminate the dryad Rynthariel and plant a Horde banner directly inside the Talon Den. Guarding the northern boundary of the Barrens, Kadrak stands watchful against encroachments from the Alliance and the night elves. When a messenger carrying a runed scroll is cut down, Kadrak decodes the missive and traces its origin to Rynthariel the Keymaster, an influential dryad stationed in Stonetalon Peak. Rather than merely defending the mountain passes, Kadrak chooses an aggressive response to deter any future scouts from probing Horde territory. The mission sends Horde warriors deep into the Talon Den, a cavernous redoubt overlooking Stonetalon Peak. Slaying Rynthariel strikes a direct blow against local night elf coordination, but the act is punctuated by planting Kadrak's Horde banner within the cave itself. By leaving their red standard fluttering in the heart of dryad territory, the Horde intends to signal clearly that incursions into the Barrens will be answered with decisive violence.

quest:359.text: Forsaken Duties. Forsaken Duties is a reconnaissance mission assigned by Magistrate Sevren in Brill to assess Scourge activity along the eastern perimeter of Tirisfal Glades. It establishes the constant threat posed by the Scourge slipping past The Bulwark and endangering local settlements. Magistrate Sevren oversees the security of Brill and the surrounding countryside, keeping a nervous eye on the eastern borders of Tirisfal Glades. With the Scourge swarming across the Western Plaguelands, Sevren requires constant reconnaissance from frontline sentries to ensure undead horrors do not slip past the perimeter unnoticed. Travelers willing to assist are dispatched south and east down the main thoroughfare to gather an urgent tactical assessment from Deathguard Linnea. Stationed at an eastern outpost along the road, Deathguard Linnea observes the frontier firsthand. Her findings confirm the magistrates fears: while the fortified position at The Bulwark successfully holds off the main Scourge host, small groups of undead manage to bypass the defenses on occasion. These stray forces have begun congregating around the nearby Balnir Farmstead, posing a localized but dangerous threat to Tirisfal Glades.

quest:373.text: The Unsent Letter. Found upon the corpse of Edwin VanCleef deep within the Deadmines, this sealed missive is addressed to Baros Alexston, the City Architect of Stormwind. Its delivery pulls back the curtain on the personal grievances and history binding the Defias leader to the city's master builders. When Edwin VanCleef falls aboard his juggernaut in the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, he leaves behind more than a broken rebellion. Tucked into his clothing is a newly penned, sealed letter. Strangely, the Defias kingpin did not address it to one of his criminal lieutenants or shadowy financiers, but to an official inside the heart of the kingdom he swore to destroy: Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect.

quest:3765.text: The Corruption Abroad. Argos Nightwhisper, a night elf envoy visiting Stormwind, seeks capable adventurers to cross the Great Sea and aid his brother in northern Kalimdor. His brother Gershala studies spreading ecological decay in Darkshore, where fresh hands are desperately needed. While Stormwind contends with internal turmoil and regional unrest, representatives from the distant kaldorei lands can be found wandering its stone streets. Argos Nightwhisper came seeking seasoned champions willing to look beyond human borders. The kaldorei are relatively new allies to the Eastern Kingdoms, and formal military aid is scarce, leaving family members and researchers to recruit whatever independent champions answer the call. The destination Argos points toward is Auberdine, a misty port town resting on the fog-shrouded coast of Darkshore. There, his brother Gershala conducts vital research into an ominous malaise afflicting the local wildlife and flora. Answering the summons means a long voyage from Stormwind Harbor across the Great Sea, marking a traveler's first real foray into the ancient wilderness of Kalimdor.

quest:377.text: Crime and Punishment. Crime and Punishment is an Alliance bounty originating in Darkshire that demands the extrajudicial execution of a grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Councilman Millstipe issues the contract after the House of Nobles overrides Duskwood's death sentence for Dextren Ward. Carrying out the hit satisfies local vengeance while delivering a sharp warning to the capital's negligent aristocracy. Duskwood already suffers beneath a shroud of creeping horrors and official indifference from the capital. When Dextren Ward was caught digging up fresh corpses from the Darkshire cemetery to sell to the necromancer Morbent Fel, the town's ruling council showed no mercy. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced the grave robber to beheadment. However, before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles intervened, claiming Ward as an imperial prisoner and transferring him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade. To Councilman Millstipe and the grieving citizens of Darkshire, sparing Ward from the headsman's block was an intolerable insult. The nobles in their secure city showed complete disregard for the torment suffered by frontier families whose dead relatives were fed into Fel's dark craft. Frustrated by Stormwind's bureaucratic meddling, Millstipe recruits daring mercenaries to infiltrate the riotous Stockade, assassinate Ward in his cell, and sever his hand as proof of execution.

quest:378.text: The Fury Runs Deep. This quest represents Motley Garmason's bitter quest for vengeance against the Dark Iron dwarf Kam Deepfury. Deepfury masterminded the assault on the Thandol Span, which claimed the lives of Bronzebeard defenders, including the brother of Longbraid the Grim. Dissatisfied with Stormwind's political detention of the culprit, Motley enlists an adventurer to enact dwarven justice inside the Stockade. The northern reaches of the Wetlands bleed from perpetual clashes between the Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and the insurgent Dark Iron dwarves. When the Thandol Span came under attack, the sabotage cost vital dwarven lives, including the brother of Longbraid the Grim. Intelligence gathered by Roggo revealed that Kam Deepfury planned the deceitful strike. Instead of facing execution on the front lines, however, Deepfury ended up secured inside the Stormwind Stockade—held as a political prisoner rather than executed for murder. Stationed at Dun Modr, Motley Garmason refuses to allow Stormwind's political calculations to shield a war criminal. To Motley, human bureaucracy has placed decorum above blood debts. Bound by duty to remain at Longbraid's side in the Wetlands, Motley tasks trusted champions to march deep beneath the human capital, brave the rioting Stockade, and claim Deepfury's severed head to settle the clan's score once and for all.

quest:386.text: What Comes Around.... What Comes Around... is an Alliance quest offered by Guard Berton in Lakeshire, who is infuriated by the political delays surrounding an orcish war criminal. Players are directed into the Stormwind Stockade to execute Targorr the Dread before corrupt nobility can arrange his escape. Targorr the Dread gained infamy in the Redridge Mountains serving as supreme executioner under General Gath'Ilzogg, chieftain of the Blackrock orcs entrenched at Stonewatch Keep. Renowned for savage cruelty even among the Blackrock invaders, Targorr personally oversaw the torture and execution of numerous defenders of Redridge. Following his eventual capture, he was transferred to the capital's high-security prison, the Stormwind Stockade, and condemned to death for his atrocities against the realm.

quest:387.text: Quell The Uprising. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind, the high-security Stockade has fallen into total chaos. Following a coordinated breakout led by incarcerated members of the Defias Brotherhood, Warden Thelwater is urgently commissioning adventurers to cut down the rioting inmates and restore order before the capital learns how compromised the facility truly is. The Stockade was built to contain the most dangerous criminals, conspirators, and outlaws threatening the Kingdom of Stormwind. However, a sudden, violent uprising orchestrated by imprisoned Defias operatives has wrested control of the cell blocks directly from the guards. With the prison thoroughly overrun and corridors choked with armed felons, normal protocol has collapsed entirely. Rather than mounting a structured retaking, prison authorities are relying on visiting champions to fight their way through the riots. Warden Thelwater's command to execute Defias prisoners on sight reflects both sheer desperation and an effort of self-preservation. Suspecting foul play behind the coordinated mutiny, the warden fears that if the broader nobility or the House of Nobles discovers the facility is out of hand, his post will be forfeit. By decreeing death as the immediate penalty for insurgency, Thelwater hopes brute force will break the inmates' spirits and quell the rebellion before word leaks past the canal gates.

quest:388.text: The Color of Blood. The Color of Blood is a personal task given by Nikova Raskol, a grieving grandmother living in Stormwind City. Consumed by anger over the murder of her young grandson inside the city's prison, she hires adventurers to venture into The Stockade and claim the Defias gang's trademark red bandanas as retribution. When Stormwind's regular military forces were deployed away to distant fronts, local defense fell upon volunteer recruits and the city's youth. Nikova Raskol's grandson, Mac, was only fourteen years old when he took up arms as a guard within The Stockade. Tasked with watching hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood, the young guard was thrust into an intensely dangerous environment far beyond his experience. Behind bars, the captured Defias inmates began ripping apart their provided wool prison blankets, fashioning the shredded fabric into makeshift red bandanas. These crude garments served as identifying gang colors, signaling their continued loyalty to the Brotherhood even inside prison walls. When young Mac reprimanded the prisoners and tried to enforce discipline, the inmates stabbed the boy in the back, leaving him dead on the stone floor. Devastated by Mac's pointless death, Nikova seeks cold revenge rather than official bureaucracy. She dispatches brave adventurers into the depths of The Stockade to cull the rioting prisoners and bring back ten of their cherished red bandanas—symbols dyed the color of her grandson's spilled blood. Presenting these blood-colored trophies offers a grim sense of closure to a broken family.

quest:389.text: Bazil Thredd. Following the discovery of an unsent letter recovered from the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston directs investigators to Bazil Thredd, the Defias leader's right-hand man. Thredd is currently locked beneath the streets of Stormwind in the high-security Stockade prison, holding crucial insight into the Brotherhood's lingering plots. When presented with evidence from the Deadmines, Baros Alexston admits his own shared history with Edwin VanCleef. Both were leading craftsmen in the Stonemasons Guild tasked with rebuilding Stormwind from the ashes of the First and Second Wars. After finishing the kingdom's magnificent white walls and towers, the nobility refused to pay the masons their promised wages. While select senior members were offered cushy bureaucratic posts to quiet them, VanCleef refused to abandon the rank-and-file laborers, leading a violent riot out of the city and founding the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:391.text: The Stockade Riots. The Stockade Riots is an Alliance quest issued by Warden Thelwater at the gates of Stormwind's prison. To quell the ongoing uprising and prove your loyalty to the city guards, you are ordered to descend into the chaos and execute the riot's ringleader, Bazil Thredd. Deep beneath the cobblestones of the Mage Quarter, the Stockade has descended into utter lawlessness. Criminals, Defias insurgents, and violent cutthroats have broken containment and seized the cell blocks, turning the facility into an impenetrable war zone. Warden Thelwater and his guards are clinging desperately to the entrance, entirely unable to push inward and restore order through ordinary means.

quest:392.text: The Curious Visitor. Following the containment of the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater reveals a troubling discovery regarding the insurgent leader, Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, Thredd had been receiving regular visits from a mysterious man holding legitimate papers under the name Maelik. Bazil Thredd spent the early years of his captivity in the Stormwind Stockade abandoned by his former comrades, or so the guards believed. That changed months before the prison riot, when a quiet visitor began meeting with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized paperwork, and gave his name as Maelik. Warden Thelwater, realizing these visits likely coordinated the bloody uprising that followed, gathers a physical description and sends adventurers to consult City Architect Baros Alexston to uncover who this visitor truly was.

quest:393.text: Shadow of the Past. Shadow of the Past is an Alliance investigation quest leading from City Architect Baros Alexston to Master Mathias Shaw, head of SI:7. Following inquiries into a mysterious visitor who spoke with the imprisoned Defias leader Bazil Thredd, the trail shifts from public construction scandals into Stormwind's covert intelligence network. After questioning Warden Thelwater regarding suspicious visitors to the Stockade's chief prisoner, Bazil Thredd, investigators hit a dead end with Baros Alexston. While the city architect cannot identify the mysterious figure, he points toward the one man whose business is knowing every secret whispered in the capital: Master Mathias Shaw, leader of the secretive intelligence agency SI:7.

quest:394.text: The Head of the Beast. Following the assassination of the treacherous Lord Gregor Lescovar, this assignment directs you from Elling Trias to Master Mathias Shaw in Old Town. Reporting the death of Lescovar cements your standing with Stormwind's clandestine intelligence network. In the hidden chambers of Old Town, Master Mathias Shaw oversees the kingdom's covert apparatus through SI:7. Receiving word of Lescovar's demise, Shaw recognizes your skill and ruthlessness, warmly praising your efficiency and thanking you for the great service you have done the people of Stormwind.

quest:395.text: Brotherhood's End. Brotherhood's End marks the aftermath of the clandestine strike against Lord Gregor Lescovar within Stormwind Keep. With the treacherous nobleman dead, Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston, cautioning you to keep quiet about who actually struck the killing blow. Baros Alexston, the City Architect who once helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, greets the news of Lescovar's demise with profound relief. Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort were marked targets for Edwin VanCleef's vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat of retribution hanging over the kingdom's architects and nobility has finally passed.

quest:396.text: An Audience with the King. "An Audience with the King" is the culmination of the long investigation into the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall and the Deadmines. Carrying the final report prepared by City Architect Baros Alexston, heroes journey to Stormwind Keep to lay the threat to rest before the realm's highest authority. Yet reaching the throne room reveals that royal affairs in the capital are not as straightforward as they seem. After the defeat of Edwin VanCleef and the dismantling of the conspiracy beneath Moonbrook, the City Architect Baros Alexston compiles an official dossier for the Crown. Alexston insists that the adventurer who broke the guild's criminal enterprise should be the one honored before the monarch. Carrying the detailed report across the grand canals to Stormwind Keep, the messenger arrives expecting an audience with the sovereign of the realm.

quest:401.text: Wait for Sirra to Finish. This brief pause marks the moment Sirra Von'Indi deciphers the cryptic note delivered from the reclusive hermit Abercrombie. As he puts quill to paper in Darkshire's Town Hall, an ominous dread settles over the room, hinting that the hermit's words are far darker than expected. After receiving the mysterious note penned by the hermit Abercrombie, Sirra Von'Indi requires only a short spell to decipher its text. As a resident scholar aiding the Night Watch and town leadership, he undertakes the task without realizing immediately what horrors the message conceals.

quest:4021.text: Counterattack!. Following the systematic elimination of their local chieftains in the Barrens, the Kolkar centaur mount a desperate retaliation out of Desolace. An invading force marches directly upon Regthar Deathgate's outpost west of the Crossroads, culminating in a fierce confrontation with Warlord Krom'zar. The campaign against the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens struck deep into their tribal leadership. With Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark dead, the remaining centaur found themselves shattered and without direction. In response to this humiliation, word traveled west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. Rather than scattering into the scrubland, a fresh contingent of hardened Kolkar warriors rallied and crossed into the Barrens, burning for blood and retribution against the fledgling Horde encampments.

quest:442.text: Assault on Fenris Isle. Assault on Fenris Isle is the climactic military directive issued by High Executor Hadrec to eradicate the Scourge stronghold in Silverpine Forest. To break the Lich King's grip upon Lake Lordamere, Forsaken agents are sent to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. For weeks, Fenris Isle has stood as a poisonous blister in the heart of Lake Lordamere. While the Forsaken secured the western roads and established their presence at the Sepulcher, the Scourge entrenched themselves inside Fenris Keep. Commanded by the powerful necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, this island outpost threatened not only Silverpine Forest but the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity itself. High Executor Hadrec recognizes that the Forsaken will never truly hold Silverpine while a servant of the Lich King conducts vile experiments right off their eastern shores.

quest:4542.text: Message to Freewind Post. Message to Freewind Post is a Horde quest tasking travelers with carrying urgent dispatches from Brave Moonhorn near the border lifts down into Thousand Needles. The missive warns Cliffwatcher Longhorn of intensifying centaur raids against local caravans. It also raises early concerns regarding the suspicious, standoffish behavior of the neighboring Grimtotem clan. Standing watch near the canyon's western approaches, Brave Moonhorn keeps a vigil over the roads leading down into Thousand Needles. With centaur aggression abruptly spiking, communication between border sentries and the regional leadership is vital. Moonhorn entrusts passing Horde adventurers with carrying an urgent dispatch southeast to Cliffwatcher Longhorn, the commander stationed atop the mesa settlement of Freewind Post. Upon receiving the message, Longhorn confirms the dire situation: a recent supply caravan was intercepted and slaughtered by marauding centaur, leaving Freewind Post in desperate need of retaliation and defense. Just as concerning is Moonhorn's parting caution to avoid the local Grimtotem tauren, whose uncharacteristically bizarre and hostile demeanor hints at deeper rifts brewing across the arid flats.

quest:455.text: The Algaz Gauntlet. The Algaz Gauntlet is an urgent military mission to fight through Dun Algaz, a critical mountain pass linking Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have entrenched themselves in the tunnels, threatening to sever Ironforge's vital lifeline to Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are tasked with cutting down the orcish vanguard and delivering word of the invasion to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz serves as the solitary overland mountain pass carving through the crags between Loch Modan and the marshy basin of the Wetlands. For the dwarves of Ironforge, this stone corridor is essential for trade, troop movements, and supplies heading to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's primary coastal port in the region. Should the pass fall, Ironforge's connection to the western seas is effectively strangled, leaving isolated outposts cut off from dwarven reinforcements. While remnants of the Dragonmaw clan have long haunted the hills and ruins of the Wetlands following the Second War, their sudden, organized push into Dun Algaz marks an aggressive escalation. Instead of lingering in their marshland enclaves, Dragonmaw scouts and grunts have seized the tunnels and fortified the pass. Mountaineer Rockgar enlists brave Alliance travelers to shatter this blockade by slaying the encroaching orcs and carrying word of the assault directly to Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor.

quest:4581.text: Kayneth Stillwind. This quest sends an Alliance courier from Astranaar eastward to the ancient outpost of Forest Song. Carrying a scouting missive from Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire, travelers seek out the druid Kayneth Stillwind to help him monitor the spread of corruption across the ancient woods. In the town of Astranaar, Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire stands watch over the western half of the forest. Word reaches her from the druid Kayneth Stillwind, stationed far out in Forest Song near the eastern reaches of Ashenvale. Deeply concerned by shifting wildlife behaviors and dark omens stirring along the coasts and woodlands, Kayneth requested a formal appraisal of the region's security. Swiftfire drafts her observations into a sealed note, trusting an able-bodied traveler to convey the dispatch safely across the treacherous central forest. Reaching Forest Song requires enduring the wilderness of Nightsong Woods, an area threatened by encroaching satyrs, hostile wildlife, and Horde excursions from the south. At the shrine of Forest Song, Kayneth Stillwind studies the delicate balance of Ashenvale's natural spirits. Reading Swiftfire's reconnaissance confirms his grim suspicions: the tainted influence creeping through the forest is neither isolated nor fleeting, and the druids will require further aid to confront the wickedness taking root.

quest:463.text: The Greenwarden. "The Greenwarden" is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing travelers deeper into the marshes of the Wetlands. Sent by First Mate Fitzsimmons from Menethil Harbor, adventurers venture northeast into the swamp to seek out a mysterious entity rumored to dwell among the beasts. Around the docks of Menethil Harbor, sailors and wanderers trade breathless stories of a beast lurking out in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons paints the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs, warning gullible seekers that stepping off the dry road means being bitten in two by 'ol' Greenie.' To the dockside folk, anything massive lurking out in the murky waters is just another man-eating hazard of the marsh.

quest:464.text: War Banners. Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor tasks Alliance champions with striking an encampment of Dragonmaw orcs northeast of the town and claiming their war banners. The remnant orcs, broken and scattered after the Second War, have begun gathering strength once again in the bogs of the Wetlands. During the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan subjugated the red dragonflight from the mountain fortress of Grim Batol. When their foul control broke, the liberated dragons turned upon their captors with ferocious vengeance, hunting the orcs nearly to extinction. What few survived fled Grim Batol into the high mountains east of Whelgar's Excavation, hidden away from the red flight's wrath. Though long believed broken beyond repair, the Dragonmaw have resurfaced. Northeast of Menethil Harbor, these savage survivors have raised an active war camp and planted their crimson standards in the marsh. Recognizing the danger of an aggressive orc force so close to the harbor town, Captain Stoutfist wants their ranks culled and their proud war banners torn down as proof of their defeat.

quest:465.text: Nek'rosh's Gambit. Nek'rosh's Gambit is an urgent strike mission commissioned by Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor. Learning that Chieftain Nek'rosh has constructed siege engines to bombard the vulnerable port town while reinforcements remain cut off at Dun Algaz, the Alliance sends brave volunteers deep into the marshes to burn the Dragonmaw catapults before an assault can begin. While Alliance adventurers were clashing with Dragonmaw raiding parties, dwarven scouts uncovered the clan's true ambition. Chieftain Nek'rosh has overseen the construction of full-scale siege catapults in the wetlands encampments. His goal is bold and catastrophic: to march his war engines to Menethil Harbor and batter down the fortress walls, wiping out the Alliance's primary shipping hub on the western coast. Menethil Harbor's peril is magnified by the choke point at Dun Algaz. Heavy skirmishes and greenskin activity in the mountain pass effectively isolate the lowlands from Ironforge's main garrisons. Without immediate aid from Khaz Modan, Captain Stoutfist cannot spare a defensive detachment to guard the perimeter, making a preemptive sabotage of the catapults the harbor's sole chance for survival. Armed with Dwarven Tinder, scouts must push directly into the heart of the Dragonmaw encampment. Setting the bulky timber engines ablaze robs Nek'rosh of his artillery, leaving his warriors exposed and denying them the firepower needed to crack Menethil's defenses before the warlord himself can be confronted.

quest:466.text: Search for Incendicite. Pilot Stonegear at Steelgrill's Depot seeks samples of volatile incendicite ore discovered in the Wetlands. Believing its explosive properties could revolutionize artillery munitions, he tasks miners with venturing north to extract the dangerous mineral from a secluded cave. Word of a rare and unstable mineral known as incendicite has reached the siege engine pilots and mechanics at Steelgrill's Depot. Rumors place rich veins inside a cavern northwest of Algaz Gate in the sodden marshlands of the Wetlands. Highly reactive and hazardous to handle, incendicite has developed a reputation for detonating in the faces of careless miners. Where others see a mining hazard, Pilot Stonegear sees military potential. If refined properly, incendicite could serve as a devastating propellant or payload for dwarven artillery, producing cannon shells capable of shattering fortified defenses. Stonegear aims to procure raw samples so courageous, or foolhardy, researchers can begin testing smelting techniques without leveling the depot.

quest:467.text: Stonegear's Search. Stonegear's Search is an Alliance directive directing adventurous travelers to Pilot Stonegear at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. The enthusiastic siege engine operator has caught wind of an exotic mineral and seeks a daring explorer to track down fresh fuel for his tank's ordnance. Dwarven siege engines are legendary feats of engineering, but their operators are rarely content leaving well enough alone. Word around Ironforge and Loch Modan quickly spreads that Pilot Stonegear, stationed just outside the capital, is scheming to boost his war machine's punch. Whether pointed his way by Pilot Longbeard or Mountaineer Kadrell, travelers are recruited simply to meet the ambitious pilot and hear his proposal. Pilot Stonegear makes his workshop at Steelgrill's Depot, the proving ground and staging yard tucked along the road just east of Kharanos. Amid clanking gears and spewing steam, Stonegear keeps watch for prospectors brave enough to pursue a volatile, rare ore known to ignite his tank's firepower to devastating new heights.

quest:468.text: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Report to Mountaineer Rockgar is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers north from the guard posts of Loch Modan toward Dun Algaz. Mountaineer Kadrell dispatches capable travelers to join Rockgar, who is organizing a vital expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the gateway passage connecting the dwarven homeland to northern territories. Dun Algaz represents the crucial artery between Loch Modan and the marshy expanses of the Wetlands. Built into the northern mountain ridge, the fortified pass has long guaranteed safe passage for trade, messengers, and military detachments moving between Ironforge and Alliance settlements further north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps a close watch on travellers passing through, recruiting hardy volunteers to reinforce the northern outposts.

quest:469.text: Daily Delivery. Daily Delivery is an errand on behalf of the dwarven hunter Einar Stonegrip, who asks travelers heading toward Menethil Harbor to deliver cured crocolisk hides to the local tanner. Rather than facing domestic friction at home, Einar relies on passing adventurers to keep his supply line moving. Out in the marshlands, Einar Stonegrip makes his living hunting the local wildlife, particularly the aggressive crocolisks that lurk along the waterways. While he gathers plenty of valuable skins, delivering them requires a trip home to Menethil Harbor. Reluctant to confront his wife Sida during a rough patch in their marriage, Einar prefers to stay in the field and hand his parcels off to passing travelers instead. The destination for these hides is James Halloran, a tanner operating within Menethil Harbor. Halloran relies on regular deliveries from local hunters to craft boots and cure leather for merchants and sailors passing through the port. Having noticed Einar's week-long absence, the tanner easily deduces the marital spat behind the proxy delivery, musing that his own wife might need to intervene and smooth things over with Sida.

quest:470.text: Digging Through the Ooze. While paying her regular respects at Ironbeard's Tomb, Sida was startled by the foul oozes prowling the barrows and threw her bag to distract them. Unable to face the creeping sludge again, she asks brave adventurers in Menethil Harbor to track down the creature that swallowed her belongings. Sida, a traveler residing in Menethil Harbor, regularly ventures northeast into the Wetlands to pay homage at Ironbeard's Tomb. On her latest visit, she found the ancient barrow crawling with foul, dripping oozes. Panicking at the sight of the shapeless horrors, she hurled her satchel at one of them. The creature simply engulfed the bag whole, though the distraction gave Sida just enough time to flee back to the safety of the port town. The burial site of the storied dwarven hero Ironbeard rests near the contested stronghold of Dun Modr. Despite its historical reverence, the surrounding marshland is prone to corruption, drawing amorphous acidic slimes that consume anything unfortunate enough to cross their path. Sida cannot remember which specific monstrosity swallowed her prized belongings, leaving travelers to scour the tomb grounds and carve through the creeping blight to recover her drenched satchel.

quest:471.text: Apprentice's Duties. Apprentice's Duties is an Alliance contract offered by tanner James Halloran in Menethil Harbor. After sending his young apprentice into the marshes only for the boy to be mauled by giant crocolisks, Halloran hires a capable adventurer to finish the dangerous harvesting job and settle the score. Tradesmen in frontier ports like Menethil Harbor must rely on local raw materials, but the surrounding bogs are unforgiving. James Halloran sent his young apprentice into the marshes to skin giant Wetlands crocolisks. When the youth failed to return, Halloran tracked him down and found him horribly mauled by the predatory beasts. Although the local midwife believes the apprentice will survive, the boy was maimed and lost a leg in the attack. Needing his stock replenished and seeking a measure of retribution against the beasts that tore into someone he considers like a son, Halloran enlists traveling adventurers to venture north along the coast, clear past the murloc hovels, and hunt down the giant crocolisks.

quest:472.text: Fall of Dun Modr. Dun Modr, the northern dwarf fortress overlooking the Thandol Span, has succumbed to a violent assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. A severely wounded survivor in Menethil Harbor seeks an Alliance adventurer to venture north and discover if commander Longbraid the Grim and any remnant of the garrison survived. Dun Modr has long anchored northern Khaz Modan, guarding the vital road and bridge connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands across the Thandol Span. Following an ambush at the bridge itself, the garrison scrambled back to regroup within the fortress walls. Before defensive lines could be reestablished, Dark Iron forces struck in overwhelming numbers, slaughtering the defenders and forcing a desperate evacuation. Harlo Barnaby, a young soldier among the defenders, fell gravely injured when a stray axe struck his back during the chaotic retreat. Believing his wounds fatal, Longbraid the Grim and the remaining troops strapped Barnaby to their last surviving horse and dispatched him south to Menethil Harbor. Barnaby survived the ordeal, but awoke in the harbor tavern racked by survivor's guilt, entirely unaware of whether any of his comrades made it out of the massacre alive.

quest:473.text: Report to Captain Stoutfist. Report to Captain Stoutfist is an Alliance military directive in Menethil Harbor. Following initial skirmishes against the Dragonmaw clan at Dun Algaz, Valstag Ironjaw sends proven combatants inside the harbor's keep to coordinate deeper defense efforts. Captain Stoutfist commands the local garrison and is organizing direct strikes against the entrenched orcs across the Wetlands. While dwarven mountaineers have long monitored the narrow mountain passes of Dun Algaz, the resurgence of the Dragonmaw clan cannot be contained to the borders of Loch Modan alone. Valstag Ironjaw recognizes that these orcs are pressing outward, establishing encampments and threatening the entirety of the marshlands. Securing the pass is merely the opening move in a larger campaign to safeguard the road to Ironforge. Deep inside Menethil Keep sits the war room, where Captain Stoutfist oversees the defenses of the Alliance port. Facing attacks from Dark Iron saboteurs, local beasts, and marsh murlocs, the captain relies on capable volunteers to counter external military threats. Valstag's recommendation confirms that you are hardened enough to take on direct orders against the Dragonmaw war machine.

quest:4736.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. This quest sends promising Alliance warlocks across the sea to the arid Barrens in search of Menara Voidrender. Operating out of Strahad Farsan's tower above Ratchet, Menara offers seasoned practitioners the chance to craft specialized tools and garments to bolster their control over demonic forces. Briarthorn, an associate lurking in Ironforge's darker corners, recognizes when a warlock has advanced beyond basic demonology without succumbing to corruption. Rather than keeping his pupils cloistered under the mountain, he points them outward toward Kalimdor, commending their discipline and urging them to seek instruction from an artisan far more skilled in practical felcraft. Perched on the bluffs overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet stands the solitary tower of Strahad Farsan. In a world deeply suspicious of dark spellcraft, practitioners of the fel often discard racial and political boundaries to survive. Menara Voidrender stays at Strahad's sanctuary precisely for this reason, collaborating with warlocks of every allegiance to ensure their perilous craft remains sharp and their summoned fiends firmly bound.

quest:4737.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Zevrost, a cynical warlock trainer lurking in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, directs seasoned practitioners to seek out Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. Despite his harsh warnings about the inevitable price of demonic corruption, he points ambitious warlocks toward an expert mentor capable of fashioning powerful arcane vestments. Deep beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks operate under a veil of uneasy tolerance. Zevrost is among the more bitter tutors in the dark arts, quick to sneer at ambitious acolytes striving for mastery. In his eyes, anyone delving deeper into fel magic is merely racing toward their own enslavement. He insists that it is only a matter of time before demonic addiction overtakes the practitioner completely, reducing even the most disciplined scholar into a thrall of the Twisting Nether. Despite his contemptuous predictions, Zevrost concedes that other practitioners do not share his dreary outlook. Word has reached Orgrimmar of Menara Voidrender, a skilled warlock stationed on the bluffs overlooking the neutral goblin port of Ratchet. Menara seeks promising disciples to aid in crafting specialized implements to harness their arcane might. For warlocks eager to push their craft further, this summons marks the beginning of forging the legendary Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. Upon finding Menara high above Ratchet, the nature of warlock society becomes starkly apparent. Menara observes that warlocks must set aside racial and cultural rivalries to support one another, as the demons they bargain with harbor no prejudice and show no mercy to anyone who falters. Sharing expertise and fashioning protective vestments is not done out of noble charity, but as a practical necessity to survive the hostile entities they bind to their service.

quest:4738.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. An Alliance warlock seeking to craft powerful vestments is directed by the Mage Quarter's covert practitioners to seek out Menara Voidrender across the Great Sea. Stationed high above the neutral port of Ratchet, Menara trains dark spellcasters across faction divides in the dangerous arts of binding and artifact creation. Within the dark crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, warlock trainer Demisette Cloyce is known for her strict, unsparing standards. When an aspiring warlock reaches the threshold of weaving significant items of power, Demisette rarely believes they are truly ready. Nevertheless, higher authorities within the cabal mandate the student's advancement, dispatching them far from the safety of the capital to prove their mettle. The destination is the arid hills overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. There, Menara Voidrender maintains her laboratory in a stone tower. Isolated from the strict laws of Stormwind and the watchful eyes of Orgrimmar, Menara accepts apprentices regardless of race or political allegiance, knowing that the fiends and demonic entities warlocks contend with harbor equal malice toward every mortal soul.

quest:4739.text: In Search of Menara Voidrender. This quest sends promising Horde warlocks from the shadowy quarters of the Undercity across the sea to Ratchet. Atop a hill overlooking the port, the mentor Menara Voidrender awaits those prepared to craft powerful arcane garments. In the Forsaken capital of the Undercity, Kaal Soulreaper observes the growing talent of practicing warlocks. Recognizing that a practitioner has grown past rudimentary hexes and impish thralls, he urges them to seek specialized instruction across the Great Sea. The craft of demonic control leaves no room for hesitation, and only skilled mentors can ensure a warlock's survival against the volatile powers of the Nether. Perched upon a high bluff overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet stands Strahad Farsan's tower. Here, far from the watchful judgment of city guards, practitioners like Menara Voidrender gather to tutor younger initiates. Warlocks of diverse backgrounds put aside tribal and political enmities under the harsh reality of their discipline: the demons they bargain with will consume human, orc, or Forsaken without prejudice if their will falters.

quest:474.text: Defeat Nek'rosh. Defeat Nek'rosh marks the culmination of the Alliance campaign against the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. With their siege engines sabotaged, adventurers are ordered to strike down Chieftain Nek'rosh directly to secure Menethil Harbor. Bringing his severed head back to Captain Stoutfist shatters the orcish threat to the coastal port. The Dragonmaw orcs have long plagued the marshlands of Khaz Modan, entrenched within their fortified encampments and threatening the sea lanes of Menethil Harbor. After discovering and burning the clan's catapults, the defenders of the marsh strike straight at the head of the serpent. Chieftain Nek'rosh, commander of the local warband, stands as the final obstacle to breaking the siege. His demise strips the remaining Dragonmaw raiders of their tactical coordination. Returning Nek'rosh's severed head to Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor marks an enormous victory for Ironforge's garrison. Deprived of both their heavy siege weaponry and their chieftain, the Dragonmaw are dealt a blow from which they are unlikely to quickly recover. For the beleaguered port, which serves as the Alliance's primary lifeline between Lordaeron and Khaz Modan, the chieftain's fall ensures the docks and trade vessels remain safe from sudden assault.

quest:4767.text: Wind Rider. Wind Rider is a Horde quest offered by Elu atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Aspiring to become a wind rider himself, Elu tasks adventurers with climbing into the craggy heights of Highperch to gather wild wyvern eggs to bolster the Horde's aerial mount reserves. Across Kalimdor, the Horde relies heavily on wind riders to ferry couriers, scouts, and warriors across vast distances. At Freewind Post, a young tauren named Elu aspires to join their esteemed ranks. With the demands of the expanding Horde outpacing the availability of mounts, Elu has been charged with helping procure new wyverns to supply the master wind riders, offering eager travelers a chance to assist in this vital effort. Highperch rises atop the towering mesas of Thousand Needles, serving as a prime nesting ground for wild wyverns. Gathering viable eggs requires braving the cliffs and facing the fiercely protective adults that patrol the roosts. By securing these clutches, Elu hopes to prove his dedication and begin the rigorous process of hand-raising and training wyverns for the Horde's flight masters.

quest:4770.text: Homeward Bound. Homeward Bound is a Horde quest that tasks adventurers with rescuing Pao'ka Swiftmountain, a young tauren naturalist stranded in the wyvern nesting grounds of Highperch. After getting separated and lost while studying the dangerous beasts, Pao'ka must be escorted safely down the cliffs back toward Whitereach Post. Pao'ka Swiftmountain accompanied the elder Motega Firemane to Thousand Needles to study the unique wildlife of the canyon floor and its towering stone pillars. Driven by curiosity and overconfidence, Pao'ka crept alone into the heights of Highperch to observe the local wyverns firsthand. The territorial beasts drove him off, leaving the young scholar stranded, terrified, and hiding among the crags for days. Highperch is thick with aggressive wyverns fiercely guarding their clutches and high roosts. Escorting Pao'ka back to level ground requires carving a path straight through the nesting predators. Unprepared for open combat, the panicked youth relies entirely on passing Horde travelers to fend off the swarming wyverns until he reaches the relative safety of the canyon path leading east.

quest:480.text: The Weaver. The Weaver is a strike mission assigned by Shadow Priest Allister in the Sepulcher to halt Dalaran's magical operations in Silverpine Forest. A Dalaran archmage, Ataeric, is directing efforts to reactivate a powerful ley energy node in the region. By slaying the archmage and claiming his staff, the Forsaken disrupt Dalaran's occult ambitions and secure their grip on the surrounding lands. Following preliminary investigations into Ambermill and Dalaran's movements in Silverpine Forest, the Forsaken learned of a hazardous development: the wizards are attempting to harness and reactivate a dormant ley energy node. Left unchecked, access to such concentrated arcane power would allow Dalaran to fortify their position and threaten the Undercity's dominion over the southern reaches of Lordaeron.

quest:4821.text: Alien Egg. Rumors among the tauren of Freewind Post speak of a bizarre, foreign egg guarded fiercely by wild serpents on the canyon floor. Hagar Lightninghoof tasks Horde adventurers with tracking down and retrieving the specimen before whatever lurks inside breaks free. Word reached Freewind Post of an unusual egg spotted deep in the serpent dens that dot the canyon floor beneath the towering stone needles. The serpents native to the canyon watch over the egg as though it were their own brood, striking out at any traveler who ventures too close. Intrigued and wary of what might threaten the local hunting grounds, Hagar Lightninghoof asks brave scouts to locate the clutch, bypass the slithering sentries, and secure the oddity for study.

quest:484.text: Young Crocolisk Skins. James Halloran, a prominent tanner based in Menethil Harbor, contracts travelers to supply fresh skins from the marsh's juvenile crocolisks. His cured hides enjoy international maritime demand, making reliable hunting essential to his trade. Supplying these softer materials earns his trust and opens the way to further leatherworking chores. Menethil Harbor is an essential maritime hub connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to distant continents, but it also supports a bustling local economy built around the resources of the surrounding marshland. James Halloran has established an international trade by tanning and curing the tough hides of the region's abundant reptilian predators. Merchants and ships sailing out of Menethil carry Halloran's leather goods to distant ports, creating constant pressure on his workshop to maintain a steady inventory. While veteran trappers like Einar provide regular hauls of mature hides, tanning specialized luxury goods requires far softer leather than fully grown marsh crocolisks can yield. To fill this shortage, Halloran relies on passing adventurers to wade into the shallow bogs right outside Menethil's palisades. Sourcing intact skins from juvenile beasts requires careful hunting, ensuring the hides remain intact enough to endure Halloran's meticulous curing process.

quest:4841.text: Pacify The Centaur. Pacify the Centaur is a retaliatory hunting mission issued by Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post. Charged with clearing the threat gathering beneath the canyon spires, Horde adventurers strike deep into the Galak centaur encampments of Splithoof Crag. Perched upon its precarious desert mesa, Freewind Post grants the tauren a commanding vantage over the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. However, that high ground offers little peace when hostile enemies mass directly beneath the ropes and elevators. The Galak centaur have established a sprawling war camp nestled directly north along the canyon wall at Splithoof Crag, directly menacing supply lines and tauren movement through the needles. To counter the growing danger, Cliffwatcher Longhorn sends capable Horde travelers to thin the Galak ranks through unsparing violence. Rather than merely defending the access lifts, the tauren believe the only way to safeguard Freewind Post is to break the centaur vanguard in their own camp.
