Taking down their scouts, beast-wranglers, and windchaser mystics is meant to blunt any concerted assault on the post before it can begin.

quest:4865.text: Serpent Wild. Serpent Wild is a Horde quest in Thousand Needles that connects the discovery of strange alien eggs to ancient tauren legends. Following an unsettling revelation at Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof dispatches adventurers northwest to Motega Firemane at Whitereach Post to confront the awakening of Arikara. When strange, unnatural eggs began appearing in Thousand Needles, local tauren feared an ecological disaster. However, inspecting the artifacts reveals something far older and more ominous than ordinary predators: signs pointing to the vengeance spirit Arikara. Stunned by the horrifying confirmation, Hagar Lightninghoof realizes the canyon faces a mythical threat long thought relegated to fireside lore. Recognizing that the threat surpasses simple physical defense, Hagar urges immediate council with Motega Firemane. Stationed northwest along the canyon floor at Whitereach Post, Motega serves as a watcher and spiritual guide versed in the traditional omens of the Needles. His guidance is essential if the Horde hopes to understand and appease or destroy the rising vengeance spirit.

quest:4881.text: Assassination Plot. Assassination Plot is a Horde quest initiated by recovering intercepted centaur orders in Thousand Needles. The orders reveal an impending strike targeting the tauren Kanati Greycloud at his hunting camp by Whitereach Post. Thousand Needles has long been contested terrain dominated by warring centaur clans and dangerous wildlife. When the tauren brave Kanati Greycloud set up a hunting camp at Whitereach Post, the small post southwest of the Great Lift, the local centaur viewed it as an audacious intrusion into their territory. Rather than merely driving game away, the centaur resolved to eliminate Greycloud entirely to discourage any further Horde expansion through the canyon.

quest:490.text: Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg is an Alliance quest authorized by the Sentinels to curb the aggressive furbolg population corrupting Teldrassil. Shayla Nightbreeze recruits adventurers outside Darnassus to hunt the corrupted beasts and collect their fangs as proof of deed. On the road outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze acts on direct orders from the Sentinels to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. Once peaceful inhabitants of the ancient forests, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading corruption that stripped away their reason, turning them into vicious threats to the safety of travelers and the natural sanctity of Teldrassil. To curb the Gnarlpine aggression, hunters are dispatched across the boughs of the World Tree to cull their ranks and collect their fangs as proof. The bulk of their corrupted population resides in two major strongholds: Ban'ethil Hollow, set south of the road west of Dolanaar, and the ruins of Starbreeze Village toward the east.

quest:4904.text: Free At Last. Free at Last is a rescue mission atop the windswept spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Lakota Windsong, a tauren woman held captive by Arnak Grimtotem, needs protection as she flees her captor's stronghold and returns to her friend Thalia Amberhide at Freewind Post. The Grimtotem clan's aggressive presence in Thousand Needles is not limited to skirmishes over land. Arnak Grimtotem sought to take Lakota Windsong as his bride, but when she refused his advances, he chose violence. Arnak returned in the night, struck down Lakota's brother when he tried to defend her, and dragged her away to Darkcloud Pinnacle. Perched across the high wooden suspension bridges above Thousand Needles, Darkcloud Pinnacle is swarming with hostile Grimtotem warriors. Escorting Lakota requires navigating the descent while fighting off waves of Grimtotem bandits intent on recapturing her before she reaches the canyon floor. Once safely down from the pinnacle, Lakota makes her way back to the safety of Freewind Post. Her companion, Thalia Amberhide, receives the news with immense relief but deep mourning for Lakota's fallen brother, offering his remaining belongings as a token of gratitude to those who brought her home alive.

quest:493.text: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills is a Horde courier task connecting the Forsaken research efforts in Silverpine Forest with their outpost in Tarren Mill. Entrusted with sensitive notes from Apothecary Renferrel, the traveler journeys south into the disputed Hillsbrad Foothills to deliver vital biological research to Apothecary Lydon. This dispatch reflects the intense pressure Lady Sylvanas Windrunner places upon the Royal Apothecary Society to produce a weapon of mass devastation. Since breaking free from the Lich King's iron grip, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has harbored a single-minded ambition: the development of a New Plague engineered to eradicate both living enemies and the Scourge. To achieve this, the Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from the Banshee Queen. Because distance isolates their laboratories, researchers scattered across Lordaeron must continuously share raw chemical data and test findings to accelerate their sinister breakthrough. Apothecary Renferrel, operating out of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, directs couriers to deliver his recent findings to his colleague, Apothecary Lydon. The trek winds south through the shadowed pine woods and down into the open, rolling pastures of Hillsbrad Foothills. There, nestled beneath the Alterac Mountains, lies Tarren Mill—a vital Forsaken hub and laboratory staging ground.

quest:494.text: Time to Strike. "Time to Strike" is a Horde reconnaissance mission that transitions scouts across the Hillsbrad Foothills border to the military hub of Tarren Mill. Delivering Deathstalker Lesh's coded signal to High Executor Darthalia marks the transition from quiet surveillance to coordinated offensive operations against the local human populace. Perched along the high ground near the border between Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the movements of human settlers and militia in the valley below. The Deathstalkers operate as the eyes and ears of the Undercity, surveying enemy settlements before any military deployment. Rather than risk abandoning her watchpost, Lesh entrusts passing Horde travelers to relay her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

quest:496.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon pursues the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate to engineer lethal concoctions against the living. To advance his morbid experiments, he enlists travelers to harvest animal reagents from the surrounding foothills. While Tarren Mill serves as a military stronghold for the Forsaken in the Hillsbrad Foothills, it also functions as an active research station for the Royal Apothecary Society. Stationed amidst the scenic greenery, Apothecary Lydon despises the pristine countryside and yearns to see the human settlements poisoned and conquered. To manufacture his experimental 'Elixir of Suffering', he requires local biological agents known for their potency and virulence. Developing alchemical plagues demands precise ingredients. Lydon directs hunters into the wilds surrounding Tarren Mill to collect the tongues of native Gray Bears alongside rare ichor secreted by Moss Creepers. Once refined through unholy alchemy, these organic fluids form the foundation for a lethal mixture intended to eradicate living trespassers across Hillsbrad.

quest:4966.text: Protect Kanati Greycloud. Protect Kanati Greycloud is a Horde quest at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Warned that centaur assassins have targeted the tauren Kanati Greycloud, adventurers must make a stand beside him and repel a squad of Galak assassins. While stationed among the towering sandstone spires of Whitereach Post, the tauren Kanati Greycloud learns from intercepted centaur orders of an assassination plot directed squarely at his life. The Galak tribe of centaur, relentless in their hostility toward the nomadic tauren and their Horde allies, are not content merely raiding supply paths; they seek to eliminate those who settle in their canyons. Realizing the attack is imminent and suspecting the enemy forces might outnumber his initial estimates, Kanati asks travelers at the post to fight alongside him. When the Galak assassins strike, Kanati stands his ground, relying on allied blades and spells to break the ambush before the centaur can claim their prize.

quest:499.text: Elixir of Suffering. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon brews a venomous concoction intended to further the Royal Apothecary Society's sinister work. To confirm its lethality, he orders an immediate live trial on his unfortunate companion nearby. Apothecary Lydon works tirelessly out of Tarren Mill to develop chemical weapons capable of fulfilling the Dark Lady's grand ambitions: a blight that will annihilate both the living humans of the Alliance and the undead horrors of the Scourge. Once the necessary reagents are gathered and steeped, Lydon mixes the foul brew into what he dubs the Elixir of Suffering, eager to witness its raw potency before deploying it on a broader scale.

quest:5.text: Jitters' Growling Gut. Stranded and terrified in the ruins of Raven Hill, the paranoid vagrant Jitters is desperate for real sustenance after subsisting on weeds and insects. He begs passing adventurers to travel east to Darkshire and convince Chef Grual to prepare a hot batch of his famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill has become a den of ravenous undead and lurking beasts, leaving the eccentric hermit Jitters trapped in hiding for weeks. Prowling through dilapidated shanties under perpetual gloom, he has survived solely on dirt-dwelling grubs and wild weeds. Starved of civilized comfort, his nerves and stomach are pushed to their absolute limits. Desperate for any reminder of safety, Jitters dreams of the seasoned patties crafted at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He sends travelers across the haunted road to seek out Chef Grual, hoping Grual will agree to whip up a batch of Dusky Crab Cakes to quiet his violently growling gut.

quest:501.text: Elixir of Pain. Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this assignment tasks Horde adventurers with harvesting mountain lion blood to brew a lethal new concoction. It highlights the Royal Apothecary Society's grim dedication to perfecting their New Plague while despising the natural vitality of the Hillsbrad Foothills. While stationed inside Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon finds little joy in the surrounding landscape. Looking out past his window at the blooming meadows and brisk mountain air of Hillsbrad, he views the region's enduring life as an offense. Like many within the Royal Apothecary Society, his personal devotion is bound to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the perfection of the New Plague, an engineered scourge intended to bring death to the living and retribution to their enemies. To engineer his latest poisonous mixture, Lydon turns to the local fauna prowling the foothills and the slopes toward the Alterac Mountains. Believing that mountain lion blood possesses specific properties vital for crafting what he calls an Elixir of Pain, he sends agents into the wilds to claim ten vials. The collection serves as the foundation for the Society's ongoing chemical trials along the contested southern front.

quest:502.text: Elixir of Pain. Commissioned by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, this quest tasks Horde agents with testing a newly brewed biological concoction known as the Elixir of Pain. The Forsaken apothecary selects Stanley, a pet dog belonging to Farmer Ray in the Hillsbrad Fields, as an unsuspecting test subject. Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon conducts experiments on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Utilizing fresh blood gathered from the local wildlife, Lydon concocts a volatile mixture he dubs the Elixir of Pain. Rather than relying purely on theoretical alchemy, the society requires empirical field data to observe the physiological effects of their experimental poisons and mutagens. To evaluate the draught without alarming the human defenders of Hillsbrad, Lydon directs his agents to target the northern farm in Hillsbrad Fields. There lives Stanley, a seemingly harmless pet dog kept by Farmer Ray. Approaching the unsuspecting canine with the draft poured into an open hand, the agent administers the dose under the guise of an ordinary treat.

quest:503.text: Gol'dir. Krusk has gone through the documents you procured and concludes that Gol'dir is kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has languished in captivity far too long and needs to be freed. Krusk, in Tarren Mill, has gone through the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to Gol'dir being kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Krusk says the captivity has dragged on far too long and Gol'dir needs to be freed. Gol'dir is held in the top room of the inn at Strahnbrad, and the inn is packed with Syndicate. A Rusted Iron Key opens the lock, and Jailor Borhuin carries it; Borhuin may be in any building of the town.

quest:5042.text: Agamaggan's Strength. Agamaggan's Strength is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By exchanging red Blood Shards harvested across the Barrens, travelers are granted the potent physical might revered by the Razormane tribe's greatest warriors. It fuels Mangletooth's bitter hatred of the rival Bristleback quilboar. The quilboar revere the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan, whose spilled blood is said to have formed the thorny red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. To the quilboar, drawing upon these crystals is a sacred rite, imbuing their front-line fighters with terrifying physical might. While held captive in Camp Taurajo, the elder Razormane shaman Mangletooth is eager to impart this strength to Horde champions, claiming your foes will cower just as they do before the Razormane's most formidable champions. Mangletooth's generosity is entirely driven by spite. Captured and caged by the orcs and tauren, the old quilboar harbors a searing grudge against the rival Bristleback tribe, the enemies of his own Razormane. Since he cannot break his chains to slaughter them personally, he uses the ancient gifts of Agamaggan as currency, rewarding anyone who decimates the Bristleback tribes and strips their lands of their sacred Blood Shards.

quest:5043.text: Agamaggan's Agility. Agamaggan's Agility is a repeatable blood shard ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering crystalline blood shards mined from the earth of the Barrens, travelers are blessed with the unerring swiftness and accuracy of the quilboar's ancient boar god. Throughout the Barrens, strange crimson minerals known as blood shards jut from the soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition teaches that these crystals were formed from the spilled blood of Agamaggan, the Great Boar Ancient who perished fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked inside a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth retains the knowledge to channel this dormant divine power for anyone willing to supply the stones. Quilboar hunters and scouts pride themselves on ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. In exchange for four blood shards, Mangletooth invokes the latent energy of the fallen demi-god, infusing the petitioner with the predatory instincts and supple grace of his people's best stalkers. Though he grunts with disdain at outsiders, Mangletooth honors his pact, weaving Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

quest:5044.text: Wisdom of Agamaggan. Wisdom of Agamaggan is a repeatable Horde quest offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By presenting blood shards gathered across the Barrens, spellcasters can partake in the ritualistic magic of the ancient boar god Agamaggan. Held prisoner by the Horde at Camp Taurajo, the quilboar Mangletooth trades the magical secrets of his race for crimson crystals known as blood shards. According to quilboar belief, these shards crystallized from the spilled blood of Agamaggan, the towering boar Demigod who perished in the War of the Ancients. Mangletooth claims the geomancers and shaman of his tribes rely on these shards to channel divine power into their rituals. While other offerings coax physical resilience or swiftness from the shards, the ritual of Wisdom focuses strictly on intellect and arcane capability. For the exchange of four blood shards, Mangletooth invokes the boar god's spirit on behalf of the player, wishing them cunning in their confrontations before parting with an ominous reminder of mortality.

quest:5045.text: Rising Spirit. Rising Spirit is a ritual blessing offered by the captured Razormane geomancer Mangletooth at Camp Taurajo. In exchange for blood shards wrested from his Bristleback rivals, Mangletooth channels the ancient power of Agamaggan to invigorate a champion's willpower and spiritual fortitude. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, the Razormane elder Mangletooth possesses deep knowledge of quilboar geomancy and ancestral magic. While other tribes may boast of raw combat ferocity, Mangletooth takes immense pride in his people's spiritual devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. He teaches that an unbroken spirit is what sustains a warrior when strength alone falters in battle, driving champions onward when defeat seems certain. To invoke this spiritual elevation, Mangletooth demands blood shards—crystallized fragments steeped in the ancient blood of Agamaggan that seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. By bringing him shards harvested from across the Barrens, particularly from his Bristleback enemies, you provide the raw spiritual conduit needed for him to weave a blessing of rising spirit that bolsters your will.

quest:5046.text: Razorhide. Razorhide is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering him blood shards infused with the life essence of the Ancient boar god Agamaggan, warriors and wanderers can gain a powerful blessing of hardened skin and resilience before heading into combat. The quilboar trace their ancestry and power directly to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who perished battling the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood soaked into the soils of the Barrens, calcifying into crystalline blood shards that still thrum with ancient power. Even though the quilboar remain sworn enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth—held in a cage at Camp Taurajo—is willing to trade their sacred knowledge in exchange for these precious fragments. Natural quilboar physiology grants them thick hides and protective quills, but tribal warriors invoke Agamaggan's blessing of Razorhide to further shield themselves from enemy blades and claws. By channeling four blood shards, Mangletooth mimics this tribal rite for outsiders, magically bolstering an adventurer's defenses so their bones remain unbroken and their skin resists trauma in the wilds.

quest:5052.text: Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Mangletooth, a captive Razormane quilboar held at Camp Taurajo, reveals the sacred origin of the blood shards scattered throughout the Barrens. Imbued with the fallen demigod Agamaggan's life essence, these red minerals grant potent ancestral magic to anyone skilled enough to channel them. In exchange for the shards, the spiteful prisoner offers to share the primal boons of his god with the Horde. According to quilboar lore, the blood of the Ancient Boar God, Agamaggan, did not merely cause giant thorn mazes to erupt across the arid plains when he fell ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. His divine blood seeped deep beneath the soil, infusing the subterranean minerals and crystallizing into blood-red stones. The quilboar revere these shards as sacred remnants of their creator, harvesting them from both mineral seams and holy grounds to serve as totems of battle and sorcery. Caged at Camp Taurajo by the tauren, Mangletooth harbors a bitter grudge against his own kind, claiming his tribe betrayed and cast him out. Deprived of his freedom and his connection to the magic of his people, he eagerly strikes a bargain with adventurers. By exchanging blood shards, Mangletooth bypasses his captivity to channel Agamaggan's power directly into Horde champions, gleefully unleashing them as an instrument of vengeance against the very quilboar who turned their backs on him. In his captivity, Mangletooth speaks reverently of the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south: Razorfen. To the quilboar tribes, the sprawling briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs are literally formed from the fallen demigod's colossal skeleton and tusks. He warns that Razorfen Downs rests within Agamaggan's gaping maw itself—a holy threshold said to devour and crush any intruders who enter without the Boar God's favor.

quest:506.text: Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir, freed from the Syndicate, has information for Krusk in Tarren Mill. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, visited Gol'dir and spoke of making slaves of the orcs who stand against him, and brought a girl named Elysa who wore the pendant the Warchief desires. A day or two ago, the head of the Syndicate paid Gol'dir a visit. His name was Aliden Perenolde, and he styled himself lord of the land. He confided that he meant to enslave the orcs who resisted him, just as his father and the despised Blackmoore, his mentor, once planned. Gol'dir sends you to bring this to Krusk in Tarren Mill, and will make his own way after settling his business where he is. More important, Perenolde brought his mistress, a slight girl named Elysa. Around her neck hung the pendant the Warchief desires.

quest:5062.text: Sacred Fire. Sacred Fire is a Horde rite of passage that bridges the jagged canyons of Thousand Needles with the heights of Thunder Bluff. To summon and banish the vengeful wind serpent Arikara, hunters must gather rare Incendia Agave from the Boiling Pool so that Magatha Grimtotem can enchant it into ritual powder. The monstrous wind serpent Arikara cannot simply be tracked across the canyon floor; she must be called. Motega Firemane instructs hunters to prepare the sacred fire of life, an ancient ritual flame that acts as a beacon to the spirit beast. Feeding this fire requires more than ordinary kindling, calling for the rare Incendia Agave that sprouts only around the scalding waters of Thousand Needles. Incendia Agave thrives near the Boiling Pool, a geothermally heated lake tucked below Darkcloud Pinnacle. Harvesting the spiky succulent requires braving the blistering waters and the volatile steam elementals that drift through the mists. Many bushels grow submerged beneath the surface, demanding resilience from any hunter sent to gather them.

quest:5064.text: Grimtotem Spying. Cliffwatcher Longhorn tasks Horde champions with infiltrating Darkcloud Pinnacle to discover what the elusive Grimtotem clan is plotting. Three unknown couriers were spotted visiting the mesa, leaving guarded correspondence scattered across their mountaintop village. Uncovering these secret notes exposes a brewing scheme that threatens the tauren settlements of Thousand Needles. Freewind Post sits precariously on high spires, but its defenders must constantly look over their shoulders at their hostile cousins. The Grimtotem clan has long maintained a tense, resentful stance toward the Horde, clinging to their isolationist strongholds atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn noticed a shift in their behavior when three mysterious agents arrived over successive weeks, conferring with clan leadership in secret. Longhorn suspects these emissaries carried marching orders or alliances meant to undermine Thunder Bluff's presence in the canyon. Darkcloud Pinnacle is a fortified network of sheer mesas connected by wooden rope bridges. Penetrating the village requires braving dense patrols of hostile Grimtotem warriors and shamans. Longhorn's scouts confirmed that the mysterious messages were locked away in separate chests spread across the outpost's central dwellings and outer bluffs. Securing the three secret notes requires sneaking or fighting across the entire settlement to snatch the clan's private communications from under their watchful eyes.

quest:5088.text: Arikara. "Arikara" is the culmination of an ominous task given by Magatha Grimtotem in Thunder Bluff. Warning that an ancient wind serpent may be stalking High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the elder shaman sends Horde adventurers to summon and slay the beast upon the burial spires of Thousand Needles. After securing refined Incendia powder, Magatha Grimtotem enchants the reagent to serve as a summoning catalyst. She warns that ancient tauren traditions have shifted too rapidly under the new Horde alliance, provoking the vengeance of Arikara, a ferocious wind serpent spirit. Magatha directs heroes southward into the windswept canyon of Thousand Needles, instructing them to throw the powder onto a ritual pyre situated among the elevated burial sites of Darkcloud Pinnacle.

quest:509.text: Elixir of Agony. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon enlists Horde adventurers to gather toxic fungi from an overrun farmstead in Hillsbrad Foothills. These virulent Mudsnout Blossoms serve as vital raw material for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim chemical experimentation. The resulting concoction is meant to aid Lady Sylvanas's long-term design to eradicate both the living and the Scourge. While the Scourge ravages the north and the Alliance clings to towns like Southshore, the Forsaken pursue their own calculated solution: the development of a tailored, lethal plague. Operating out of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon labors under the mandate of the Dark Lady. Though personally cynical about the tedious toil of alchemy, Lydon diligently gathers potent organic toxins from the surrounding countryside to brew elixirs capable of speeding along the mutual destruction of Sylvanas's enemies. South of Tarren Mill and east of the river lies Nethander Stead, an abandoned human farmstead now overrun by the vicious Mudsnout gnolls. Amid the filth and neglected soil, strange and foul-smelling mushrooms known as Mudsnout Blossoms flourish. These large, pungent growths hold concentrated organic poisons prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. Procuring them requires cutting through gnoll packs or quietly weaving past their ramshackle camps.

quest:513.text: Elixir of Agony. This errand carries Apothecary Lydon's freshly mashed Mudsnout Composite from Tarren Mill straight to the heart of the Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell requires the plant mash to treat it with a colloid of decay, furthering the Forsaken's development of a new plague. In the ongoing efforts of the Royal Apothecary Society, regional researchers frequently send their raw discoveries back to Undercity for specialized refinement. Apothecary Lydon has mashed down local Mudsnout Blossoms into a composite, but bringing it to lethal fruition requires the advanced reagents kept only in the capital's laboratory. Master Apothecary Faranell works under tremendous pressure within the Apothecarium. Caught between the ever-present shadow of the Scourge in the north and aggressive human populations to the south, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has demanded a potent new plague to defend their people. Receiving Lydon's composite provides Faranell with exactly the kind of toxic breakthrough the Dark Lady expects.

quest:5147.text: Wanted - Arnak Grimtotem. Wanted: Arnak Grimtotem is a Horde bounty posted at Freewind Post demanding the execution of a violent Grimtotem exile. Arnak is targeted by the local authorities for murder and kidnapping on the mesas above the canyon. While tensions between the mainstream tauren of the Horde and the reclusive Grimtotem tribe are perpetually strained, Arnak took matters far beyond political friction. Branded an outcast, Arnak murdered a tauren and abducted the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong. In response to these heinous acts, Cliffwatcher Longhorn of Freewind Post sanctioned an open bounty calling for the rogue tauren's death. Arnak took refuge upon the high crags of Darkcloud Pinnacle, an extensive network of rope bridges and mesa encampments occupied by the Grimtotem clan near the entrance to Razorfen Downs. Trapped upon these windswept heights alongside Arnak is his captive, Lakota Windsong, awaiting rescue from anyone brave enough to fight across the Grimtotem bridges.

quest:515.text: Elixir of Agony. This errand continues the development of the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague, dispatching a courier from Undercity back to Tarren Mill. Master Apothecary Faranell enriches Lydon's Mudsnout mixture with his own decaying compounds, demanding coastal reagents and alchemical draughts to catalyze the lethal brew. When Apothecary Lydon's field work produced a potent composite from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered at gnoll-held Nethander Stead, he sent it straight to the Apothecarium in the Undercity. Master Apothecary Faranell, head of the Royal Apothecary Society, immediately recognized the concoction's grim potential. Delighted by its toxic properties, Faranell added his own specialized colloid of decay to the mixture before outlining the catalysts required to weaponize it fully. Activating the volatile contaminating agents requires precise reagents that Lydon must assemble in Tarren Mill. In addition to a restorative draught of Strong Troll's Blood to feed and stabilize the chemical reaction, Faranell requires organic components harvested from the southern shoreline of Hillsbrad: scales stripped from the serpentine Daggerspine naga and eyes carved from the coastal Torn Fin murlocs.

quest:5151.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Following a deadly centaur ambush on a merchant caravan in Thousand Needles, the goblin tinkerer Wizlo Bearingshiner was left as the sole survivor. Desperate to reclaim his prized invention, he hires adventurers to breach the wreckage, unlock an iron cage, and wrest the gizmo from the neck of a fearsome caged predator. Caravans venturing beneath the towering sandstone spires of Thousand Needles run a perilous gauntlet. Hostile centaur prowl the canyon floor, fiercely guarding their territory and raiding any travelers bold enough to pass through. When one such trade caravan was overrun just north of Whitereach Post, the centaur slaughtered the travelers and plundered the wagons, leaving only the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner to limp back to safety. In the chaos of the raid, the centaur looted nearly every valuable scrap, but they gave one ruined wagon a wide berth. Bound inside a sturdy transport cage was a ferocious, enraged panther with Wizlo's prized hypercapacitor gizmo fastened directly around its neck. Daunted by the predator's snarling fury, the centaur abandoned the cage intact, forcing Wizlo to entrust its key to brave mercenaries capable of slaying the beast and reclaiming his gadget.

quest:516.text: Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a Horde quest directed by Shadow Priest Allister from the Sepulcher. Agents of the Forsaken have caught wind of a hidden conclave of Scourge massing inside a secluded cave tucked into the southern Silverpine hills, aiming to strike them down before an offensive can begin. Word reached Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher that mindless servants of the Lich King were massing deep within southern Silverpine Forest. Left unchecked, these Scourge forces posed an immediate threat to Forsaken operations throughout the region. Rather than waiting for the assault to land, Allister directs scouts to take the initiative and eliminate the gathering horde inside their secluded lair before they can mobilize. Beren's Peril itself is an obscure cavern network carved into the hills south of the Dalaran-aligned settlement of Ambermill. The treacherous terrain makes the cavern easy to overlook, approached only by navigating around the southern slopes. Within its shadows dwell the Ravenclaw drudgers and guardians, entrenched remnants of the plague whose destruction helps ensure the Forsaken maintain their tenuous hold over the forest.

quest:517.text: Elixir of Agony. This quest is the fourth chapter in Apothecary Lydon's relentless development of a devastating Forsaken poison in Tarren Mill. With the deadly Elixir of Agony finally brewed, Lydon dispatches Horde champions to Dun Garok to steal a keg of dwarven Shindigger Stout for delivery. In the damp reaches of Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon works tirelessly on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society and Lady Sylvanas. Having gathered lethal ingredients from across Hillsbrad, his new concoction is complete. Lydon has no interest in wasting such a potent strain on trivial creatures like frogs or stray dogs; he seeks a real, tangible test against living adversaries. To stage his experiment, Lydon needs an inconspicuous delivery vehicle. South of Hillsbrad, the Ironforge dwarves have fortified the stronghold of Dun Garok. Lydon directs agents of the Horde to infiltrate the underground barracks and mess halls, slipping past dwarven rifles and axes to purloin a prized keg of Shindigger Stout.

quest:518.text: The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara wants the Crushridge ogres thinned out before any real blow is struck against Mug'Thol, whose ogres now hold the Ruins of Alterac. You are sent to cut down Crushridge maulers. Mug'Thol and the Crushridge ogres have taken the Ruins of Alterac. Melisara says it will be hard to punish Mug'Thol while so many ogres stand around. First their numbers must be reduced, and only after that will the next move be made. Your part is to hunt the Crushridge maulers.

quest:527.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. Battle of Hillsbrad is the opening strike in the Forsaken campaign to eradicate the human settlement of Hillsbrad. Handed down by High Executor Darthalia under orders from Varimathras, this mission targets the farmers and infrastructure of the northern Hillsbrad Fields to sever the town's food supply. Tarren Mill stands as the southern spearhead of the Forsaken empire, facing an entrenched human populace clinging to the Hillsbrad Foothills. High Executor Darthalia operates under strict directives straight from Varimathras in the Undercity. Her strategy is total attrition: before marching directly on the heavily defended town of Hillsbrad, she orders the systematic disruption of its agriculture. Striking the northern fields deprives the human militia of critical provisions while sowing chaos across their homesteads. The broader campaign against the human presence in Hillsbrad serves a grim tactical purpose. While the Forsaken armies pin down and bleed the local defenders, the Royal Apothecary Society works tirelessly to concoct a new plague capable of eradicating the living and Scourge alike. High Executor Darthalia views these early skirmishes—and the deaths of local landowners like Farmer Ray and Farmer Getz—as necessary steps to suppress the human infestation until that ultimate weapon is ready to deploy.

quest:528.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. Battle of Hillsbrad is a Forsaken military mission directed by High Executor Darthalia from Tarren Mill. Following the initial strikes on the northern human farms, Horde operatives are sent south to slaughter the fleeing Hillsbrad Peasants seeking refuge in the orchards. The campaign against the human presence in Hillsbrad Foothills moves with cold deliberation. After Horde forces strike the northern farms, panic sweeps through the settlement. Rather than taking up arms, many laborers flee southward into the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad Fields, hoping to hide from the advancing undead. High Executor Darthalia views their terror not with mercy, but as a strategic opening to break Hillsbrad's remaining labor force and morale completely. Under direct orders from Tarren Mill, champions of the Horde hunt down these displaced laborers in the fields. Deprived of protection, the peasants are systematically eliminated to choke off Hillsbrad's food supply and shatter civilian resolve. For Darthalia and the Forsaken, every human felled tightens the grip of death around the surviving township, ensuring that Lordaeron remains firmly in the hands of the Forsaken.

quest:529.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. This operation represents a critical phase in the Forsaken campaign to conquer the Hillsbrad Foothills. High Executor Darthalia orders the destruction of the local smithy in Hillsbrad Fields to cut off the weapons arming the stubborn human populace. The Forsaken push across the Hillsbrad Foothills faced fiercer resistance than High Executor Darthalia anticipated. The rural humans refused to simply scatter or yield to the Deathstalkers and soldiers sent from Tarren Mill. Investigation revealed that the local peasantry were not fighting with simple pitchforks and scythes; they were actively being outfitted for war right in the fields. At the southwest edge of the Hillsbrad Fields, Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices worked tirelessly at their forge, turning raw ore into blades and armor for the militia. By dispatching an operative to eliminate Verringtan, butcher his apprentices, and seize their stockpiled iron shipment, Darthalia aimed to cripple the settlement's defense while redirecting their metal toward the eventual assault on Southshore.

quest:530.text: A Husband's Revenge. A Husband's Revenge is the conclusion to a tragic tale of past betrayal carried into undeath. Raleigh Andrean, a Forsaken residing in the Undercity, charges travelers with tracking down his former friend Valdred Moray, who murdered his wife in life. When Raleigh Andrean received the engraved ring carried from Silverpine Forest, it rekindled memories of his mortal life that undeath had mostly withered away. Among those memories was a profound betrayal: his close friend, Valdred Moray, had murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. While the chill of the Scourge and subsequent Forsaken existence dulled Raleigh's capacity for grief and love, his thirst for retribution remained entirely intact.

quest:532.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. This critical phase of the Forsaken campaign against Southshore's surrounding holdings targets the civic leadership of Hillsbrad town. Directed by High Executor Darthalia from Tarren Mill, Horde forces strike at Magistrate Burnside, his council, and their administrative records to completely shatter human governance in the foothills. Even after suffering severe casualties across their fields and patrols, the human defenders of Hillsbrad cling to their remaining civil authority. High Executor Darthalia recognizes that ordinary peasants and militia rally behind their civic leaders. To ensure the town completely collapses, Forsaken operatives are dispatched directly into the Town Hall to execute Magistrate Burnside and five of his councilmen, severing the chain of command. Beyond physical assassinations, Darthalia seeks the total psychological and administrative dismantling of Hillsbrad. Operatives must burn the Hillsbrad Proclamation, a revered political document that symbolizes the settlement's charter and pride. Alongside its destruction, the town registry is seized, depriving the surviving Alliance loyalists of their official records and citizen registries while giving Undercity intelligence detailed insight into the local populace.

quest:5321.text: The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade, a recently awakened Druid of the Claw, struggles to remain awake on his journey toward Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Entrusted with his Horn of Awakening, travelers must shepherd the lethargic druid along the forested border, rousing him when he drifts into slumber and defending him against wild furbolgs and sinister cultists. For millennia, the Druids of the Claw slept within barrows, communing with the wild spirits across the Emerald Dream. Though the Third War demanded their awakening, shaking off centuries of hibernation does not come easily to every mind. Kerlonian Evershade set out south from Darkshore toward Ashenvale to rendezvous with Liladris Moonriver, but exhaustion overtook him shortly into his trek. Finding himself helplessly prone to sudden naps along the wilds, he relies on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep his feet moving. The path connecting Darkshore to Ashenvale is far from tranquil. As Kerlonian meanders southward, his vulnerable state invites aggression from the surrounding wilderness. In Twilight Vale, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs stalk the roadway, while farther south into Ashenvale, members of the shadowy Dark Strand cult lurk in ambush. Escorting the groggy druid requires a vigilant watch, as Kerlonian will simply lie down to sleep wherever he stands unless forcefully roused with the horn.

quest:533.text: Infiltration. In Tarren Mill, Krusk at last hears word and rumor of Gol'dir, an orc held prisoner by the Syndicate. The humans keep moving their captive about, so Krusk has narrowed the search to the Syndicate's large camp, just to the north of town, and wants you to bring back whatever information you can find. Krusk has begun to hear word and rumor of Gol'dir. The Syndicate's humans keep moving the orc about, but the search is narrowing to their large camp, just to the north of Tarren Mill. Krusk sends you there to lay hands on whatever information you can and carry it back. Krusk fears that with each day Gol'dir's prospects darken.

quest:536.text: Down the Coast. Down the Coast is an Alliance task given by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore. Deeply unhappy with his frontier transfer from Stormwind, the guard lieutenant prefers drinking ale to patrolling and hires adventurers to clear out the Torn Fin murlocs encroaching along the Western Strand. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle was reassigned from the polished stone streets of the Stormwind city guard to the remote, salty port of Southshore. Finding the town dreary and its fishy harbor odor unbearable, Orinelle spends his days nursing drinks at the local inn rather than patrolling the frontlines. When ordered by Marshal Redpath to protect Southshore from the surrounding dangers, Orinelle chooses to subcontract his duties to passing sellswords instead. The task itself focuses on the Western Strand, the coastline stretching west from Southshore. While Orinelle scoffs at the threat of 'overgrown fish,' the Torn Fin tribe of murlocs poses a genuine hazard to coastal travel and local shipping. Gathering in tightly packed camps along the breakers, their tidehunters and mystical oracles readily ambush anyone straying too far from town walls, making clearing the shoreline a bloody undertaking.

quest:5361.text: Family Tree. Cliffwatcher Longhorn asks you to carry a report to Nataka Longhorn, Cliffwatcher's brother, who is stationed in Desolace. Word of unusual centaur activity is meant to reach Ghost Walker Post. Nataka, Cliffwatcher's brother, holds a posting at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. A year has passed since Cliffwatcher last wrote, and in that time the centaurs have been behaving unusually. Nataka should hear of it, and you are asked to carry the report. The way runs to Stonetalon Mountain, which lies north of the Crossroads, then west into the Charred Vale. From there it turns south into Desolace, where a road runs south to Ghost Walker Post.

quest:5381.text: Hand of Iruxos. Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village says the Burning Blade holds a Demon Box, and that something powerful called the Hand of Iruxos is kept inside. At Mannoroc Coven, the Burning Blade makes use of it to open demon portals. Taiga sends you to Thunder Axe Fortress to fetch the box. Taiga Wisemane wants the flow of demons into our world stopped. You are given a demon pick, to be used on the red crystal inside Thunder Axe Fortress, which opens the way to the Demon Box. The box and the pick are to be brought back to Taiga in Shadowprey Village.

quest:5386.text: Catch of the Day. Cooked fish has not been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long time, and Nataka Longhorn would like that to change. Nataka rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers around, yet all the centaur activity leaves little time for the journey. You are asked to go in Nataka's place and bring back two Bloodbelly fish. No cooked fish has been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long while. Nataka Longhorn rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers, but with so much centaur activity there is little time to make the journey. So you are asked to go there, talk with the local fisherman Jinar'Zillen, and return with two Bloodbelly fish, Nataka's favorite. The road south of the post bends west and brings you to the troll village.

quest:539.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. This campaign order from High Executor Darthalia directs Horde agents to strike deep into Azurelode Mine, a vital iron excavation south of Hillsbrad Fields. By eliminating Foreman Bonds and his crew, the Forsaken aim to sever iron shipments to Alliance armories and seize the tunnels for themselves. Having seized the Hillsbrad Town Registry during earlier raids, High Executor Darthalia identified Azurelode Mine as a linchpin of human military endurance in the region. The mine operates just south of the contested fields, continuously extracting rich veins of iron ore to supply Alliance weaponsmiths and armories. Leaving it untouched would allow Southshore's forces to rearm and bolster their garrisons, rendering Tarren Mill's prior victories moot. To completely break production, Darthalia targets both leadership and labor. Horde forces are ordered to eliminate Foreman Bonds, the human overseer running the excavation, along with a significant portion of his workforce. Striking into the dark shafts sends an unmistakable message to Southshore: neither their supply lines nor their isolated labor camps are beyond the Forsaken's reach.

quest:54.text: Report to Goldshire. Report to Goldshire marks an adventurer's formal transition from the sheltered grounds of Northshire Valley into the broader jurisdiction of Elwynn Forest. Bearing dispatches from Marshal McBride to Marshal Dughan, recruits are granted Acting Deputy Status amid growing regional neglect from Stormwind's nobility. Having proven their mettle against local troubles within Northshire Valley, recruits are officially released from Northshire's local guard by Marshal McBride. In recognition of their service, McBride prepares transfer papers directing them south past the border gates along the road into Goldshire, transferring their responsibilities to the wider expanse of Elwynn Forest. Upon arrival in Goldshire, Marshal Dughan accepts McBride's dispatches and formally assigns the recruit the rank of Acting Deputy within the Stormwind Marshals. Yet Dughan's welcome comes with a grim warning: Northshire is a peaceful garden compared to the dangers roaming Elwynn, especially with Stormwind's royal army tied up in political maneuvering for distant nobles rather than protecting home ground.

quest:540.text: Preserving Knowledge. Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore sends you into the Ruins of Alterac, where ogres have settled among the precious books left behind. Tomes the ogres looted must be recovered, and one above all: a worn leather book holding The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Ogres have made their home in the ruins of Alterac, and Dibbs dreads what they might be doing to the books still there. You are to go in, hunt for the tomes the ogres have looted, and recover whatever you can. Dibbs would search the ruins too, but fears old bones would not survive the climb into the mountains. Among all the tomes, Dibbs most wants one book: the worn leather volume containing The Arm of Gri'lek. Dibbs is bent on learning the ancient troll lore inside, and the Ruins of Alterac were the last known home of an intact copy.

quest:541.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. This critical phase of the Forsaken campaign in Hillsbrad targets the dwarven stronghold of Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia dispatches Horde champions to dismantle the dwarven garrison assisting the local humans and execute their commanding officer, Captain Ironhill. Having pressured the human farmers and town militia across the foothills, High Executor Darthalia turns Tarren Mill's fury against Ironforge's military contingent. Dwarven troops have taken up arms in support of Southshore, reinforcing the human presence in Lordaeron. To Darthalia, this solidarity is an obstacle that must be shattered, proving to the Alliance that aiding the human remnants will bring only devastation. Tucked against the ancient ramparts of Thoradin's Wall in southeastern Hillsbrad, Dun Garok serves as a heavily fortified dwarven bastion. Storming the outpost requires breaking through ranks of disciplined mountaineers, crack riflemen, and battle-hardened priests. The assault culminates in the death of Captain Ironhill, breaking Ironforge's forward tactical command in the region and leaving the remaining human enclaves isolated.

quest:5421.text: Fish in a Bucket. Jinar'Zillen of Shadowprey Village in Desolace likes to do as little as possible. Many shellfish traps sit below the village docks, and anyone who gathers the shellfish from them will be repaid with something worth having. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village, and would far rather someone else did the collecting. Anyone willing to take on that work is promised something they want in return: one fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

quest:544.text: Prison Break In. Magus Wordeen Voidglare is in Tarren Mill on research but now faces a crisis. A few months ago four Forsaken fled the Undercity after stealing artifacts from a secure vault, and Sylvanas wants them back. Voidglare came to Tarren Mill to research and now must resolve a crisis. Four Forsaken turned their backs on their brethren and, worse, stole from the Dark Lady. They broke into a secure vault and took four artifacts the apothecaries required for certain studies. Sylvanas wants them returned. The thieves ran from the Undercity to Dalaran, where the wizards put them in quarantine at the Lordamere Internment Camp. You are to find the traitors, take back the artifacts and report to Voidglare in Tarren Mill. There are four: a Bloodstone Wedge, Marble, Shard and Oval. Dermot has the wedge, Ricter the marble, Alina the shard and Kegan Darkmar the oval.

quest:545.text: Dalaran Patrols. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill cares nothing for why the wizards of Dalaran raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. What matters is that the ruined outskirts beyond the dome may conceal treasures of real magical worth, while the wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. Voidglare wants those patrols thinned. After Prison Break In, Voidglare turns to the wizards of Dalaran, who raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. Some say it shelters them from the violence of the age; others say they simply wanted solitude to study and plot. Voidglare does not care which. The ruined outskirts beyond the dome may conceal treasures of real magical worth, but the wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. You are to hunt six Dalaran Summoners and twelve Elemental Slaves, then return to Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

quest:546.text: Souvenirs of Death. Souvenirs of Death is a quest given by Deathguard Samsa in Tarren Mill to Horde champions campaigning against the human settlements of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Envious of those sent to the front lines, Samsa asks for thirty human skulls taken in battle to add to his morbid collection. While High Executor Darthalia directs the full military might of the Forsaken against the Hillsbrad human settlements, Deathguard Samsa finds himself stranded on sentry duty in Tarren Mill. Harboring a bitter jealousy toward those dispatched to raid, burn, and pillage, Samsa views the open slaughter of the living as an enviable privilege denied to stationary town guards. Unable to leave his post, Samsa indulges his hatred by collecting the skulls of Hillsbrad humans slain across the ongoing campaign. Rather than serving an arcane ritual or a tactical strategy, his request for thirty skulls is a purely personal indulgence—trophies of a war he longs to fight firsthand.

quest:547.text: Humbert's Sword. While scouting the Ironforge stronghold of Dun Garok under orders from High Executor Darthalia, Deathguard Humbert stepped away from his camp to collect firewood. Dwarven scouts looted his campsite and made off with his personal weapon, leaving the humiliated sentry desperate to recover it before his commanding officer notices. Tasked by High Executor Darthalia with keeping a watchful eye on Dun Garok, Deathguard Humbert took up a concealed vigil near the dwarven fortress. When morning broke, he briefly left his outpost unguarded to gather firewood for boiling water. That lapse was all the opportunistic Ironforge dwarves needed. Upon his return, Humbert found his camp looted and his trusty sword gone, taken deep into the heavily defended bunker. Losing a weapon to the very enemy one is supposed to surveil is an embarrassment punishable by death under Forsaken command. Humbert knows full well that High Executor Darthalia would string him up from the rafters of Tarren Mill if she ever learned of his blunder. Unable to storm the stronghold alone, he depends on passing Horde adventurers to plunge into Dun Garok and reclaim his blade before Darthalia realizes anything is amiss.

quest:549.text: WANTED: Syndicate Personnel. Posted on the Tarren Mill bounty board under the authority of Lady Sylvanas, this decree condemns all members of the Syndicate to death. The Forsaken seek to purge the brigands gathering in the ruins of Durnholde Keep before they threaten Horde operations in the foothills. The Syndicate's sudden presence southeast of Tarren Mill has not gone unnoticed by the Forsaken. Rather than offering parley or treating them as mere displaced nobles, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her commanders view the Syndicate as an active pestilence. The bounty dictates immediate death, specifying that any prisoners brought in will be executed without trial. Once an infamous internment camp fortress, Durnholde Keep now lies shattered and lawless. Syndicate Rogues and Watchmen have crept into its crumbled ramparts and towers, using the historic stronghold as an operations hub. For High Executor Darthalia, ridding the ruins of these armed bandits is essential to securing the road and safeguarding Tarren Mill's southeastern approach.

quest:55.text: Morbent Fel. This quest is the final reckoning with Morbent Fel, the necromancer haunting the heights above Raven Hill Cemetery. Armed with the enchanted relic Morbent's Bane, heroes are sent by the grieving Sven Yorgen to shatter the sorcerer's wards and end his reign of terror over western Duskwood. Morbent Fel makes his lair in an abandoned house perched atop a rocky ridge just east of Sven's camp, overlooking the sprawl of Raven Hill Cemetery. From this grim vantage, the necromancer has directed waves of undead to terrorize the surrounding forest and defile the graves of Duskwood. Protected by formidable dark magic and attended by loyal undead thralls, he has remained untouchable to ordinary steel. Direct assault against Morbent Fel is suicide without supernatural aid; his defensive sorceries deflect conventional attacks. To bypass these wards, Sven entrusts adventurers with Morbent's Bane, an enchanted artifact designed specifically to unravel the necromancer's magical shielding. Once invoked, the barrier collapses, leaving Fel vulnerable to a mortal strike.

quest:550.text: Battle of Hillsbrad. This mission marks the conclusion of the Forsaken campaign against the human township of Hillsbrad. Having shattered the local Alliance forces, you are sent by High Executor Darthalia to present an official commendation to Varimathras in the Undercity. The campaign in the Hillsbrad Foothills represents a brutal struggle for southern Lordaeron. Across a protracted series of strikes coordinated from Tarren Mill, Horde champions dismantled the human township's farmers, militia, blacksmiths, and civic leaders. With the Alliance presence crippled and the territory secured for the Forsaken, High Executor Darthalia drafts an official commendation to ensure the champion's exploits reach the highest ranks of command. Carrying Darthalia's sealed commendation leads directly to the Royal Quarter of the Undercity, into the presence of Varimathras. Standing alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the dreadlord oversees military operations across Lordaeron. While the Scourge descending from the northern Plaguelands remains the Dark Lady's paramount existential threat, securing the southern borders against surviving human enclaves is vital for the nascent Forsaken nation.

quest:5501.text: Bone Collector. At Kormek's Hut in Desolace, the goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle is certain that kodo bones are about to transform the world. Ten of them are wanted from the Kodo Graveyard, south of the hut, and something is promised in return. Bibbly insists the hut is sitting on a goldmine. Customers make furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder from kodo bones. Bibbly sends you south to the Kodo Graveyard to bring back ten of them, with something promised in return. A caravan comes by to pick up Bibbly's kodo bones, then sells them at Shadowprey Village. It is due any moment, and Bibbly is ten bones short of what is called a career high.

quest:552.text: Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand in Tarren Mill means to avenge Master Helcular, a great wizard on the brink of becoming a lich, who was killed by a human lynch mob after it found his ritual lair. Before vengeance can fall on Southshore, Thaivand needs Helcular's Rod, which one of the yeti there must hold. Master Helcular was on the brink of becoming a lich when he was found and killed by a human lynch mob, who had discovered the ritual lair he kept in the hills. They then buried the body in the Southshore cemetery. His apprentice, Thaivand, finds this disregard for a great wizard unacceptable and vows that the rains of vengeance will fall upon the town of Southshore. Thaivand says Helcular's Rod is needed first. Yeti have overtaken the ritual lair, and Thaivand is sure one of the beasts has the rod. There are so many yeti in the region that finding it will be difficult. Growless Cave and Darrow Hill are among the places they can be found.

quest:553.text: Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand hands you the Rod of Helcular. Three ceremonial pyres that Helcular fashioned for his most powerful spell must each charge it, and then it is to be driven into Helcular's grave in Southshore. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell, and the rod must be charged from each one. The flames of Azel and Veraz lie within the Foothill Caverns, in the yeti cave at Darrow Hill. The third, the Flame of Uzel, is found in a small cave above the caverns, farther north in the mountains, near Growless Cave. Once the rod is charged from all three flames, it is to be driven into Helcular's grave at Southshore, a heavily guarded human town. The graveyard sits in the northeast corner of the town, by the river, and the grave lies at the graveyard's southeastern corner.

quest:555.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. Chef Jessen of Southshore prides himself on preparing the finest cuisine north of Stormwind, but recent unrest has cut off his supply of fresh snapjaw turtle meat. To restore his famous Soothing Turtle Bisque to the tavern menu, he asks culinary-minded travelers to brave the dangerous northern waters near Dalaran and Lake Lordamere. Southshore remains one of the Alliance's last intact coastal towns in Lordaeron, clinging proudly to civilian life amidst mounting regional strife. Chef Jessen claims that his cooking rivals any tavern north of Stormwind, with patrons supposedly trekking from as far as Darkshire in Duskwood just for a taste of his specialty: Soothing Turtle Bisque. The rich, restorative soup depends entirely on fresh meat from the snapjaw turtles indigenous to the rivers and lakes of the northern mountains. In calmer years, Jessen gathered turtle meat himself by journeying up past Dalaran to the eastern shores of Lordamere Lake. However, rising tensions, hostile wildlife, the Syndicate, and Forsaken incursions have made foraging outside town lethal for ordinary townsfolk. To keep his pot simmering and his patrons satisfied, the chef relies on armed adventurers willing to harvest meat from the snapjaws lurking along the riverbanks and northern shores.

quest:556.text: Stone Tokens. Stone Tokens is a Horde assignment issued by Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill to retrieve magical binding artifacts from Dalaran agents in the Alterac region. The Forsaken seek to study the arcane methods Dalaran's mages use to enslave and command powerful elementals. Gathering these inert tokens serves as the foundation for the Magus's research into elemental subjugation. The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized conduits and enchanted foci to bind creatures from other dimensions into servitude. While the city itself is still rebuilding, its agents and remnant forces patrol the surrounding territory, relying on elementals as laborers and defensive shock troops. Magus Voidglare, an arcane researcher working on behalf of the Forsaken in Tarren Mill, seeks to dissect the precise sorcery Dalaran uses to compel these entities into obedience.

quest:5561.text: Kodo Roundup. At Scrabblescrew's Camp in Desolace, Smeed Scrabblescrew is expecting a caravan and wants five tamed kodos ready for it. You carry Smeed's kodo kombobulator out among the ancient, aged and dying kodos, and lead the ones it tames back to the camp. Bibbly believes no other goblin in Desolace knows how to turn a profit. Smeed Scrabblescrew disagrees: the one caravan willing to brave this land depends on Smeed, and Smeed has formed a partnership with Cork and Rigger. The caravan is due at the camp shortly. Smeed built a device that can rejuvenate and bring under control aged and dying kodos. Aimed at an ancient, aged or dying kodo, it jolts the beast into a tamed kodo that follows you. You bring five of them back to Scrabblescrew's Camp, along with the device.

quest:557.text: Bracers of Binding. Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill says the Magus, busy with the stone tokens you gathered, will eventually want their counterpart: bracers of binding. You are to collect four Bracers of Earth Binding from elementals among the ruins of Dalaran. While the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Bel'varil expects a further wish: samples of the matching piece, bracers of binding. Worn on an elemental's wrists, they tie it to a mage's service. Among the ruins of Dalaran, elementals wear them. Bel'varil wants four Bracers of Earth Binding brought to Tarren Mill.

quest:5581.text: Portals of the Legion. After Hand of Iruxos, Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village shows you the Hand and asks you to banish six demon portals at Mannoroc Coven, warning you to be wary of the portal guardians. Taiga Wisemane holds up the Hand of Iruxos, a grisly thing to look at, and says you must carry it if the demon portals around Mannoroc Coven are ever to be closed. The demon threat is increasing, and shutting the portals will check the number of demons crossing into this world. She wants all six portals banished, and she warns you to be wary of their guardians.

quest:559.text: Farren's Proof. Farren's Proof is an Alliance assignment in Southshore given by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Tasked with proving his coastal patrol efforts to his superior, Marshal Redpath, Farren sends recruits out to harvest severed murloc heads along the Western Strand. Following initial sweeps along the coastline in Down the Coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle finds himself under scrutiny by Marshal Redpath and town leadership. Claiming credit for clearing out the local murlocs is one thing; presenting undeniable evidence to skeptical superiors is quite another. Unwilling to soil his own hands with gruesome butchery, Farren tasks wandering Alliance adventurers with returning to the shoreline to collect tangible proof of the kill. The task takes fighters west of Southshore along the Western Strand, where coastal murlocs nest along the shallows. The lieutenant requires ten severed murloc heads to appease the town garrison's officers. Farren himself detests the creatures, admitting that the repulsive sight and smell of amphibious fish-men has utterly ruined his appetite for Southshore's primary export and staple food.

quest:56.text: The Night Watch. Tasked by Commander Althea Ebonlocke in Darkshire, this mission enlists adventurers to thin the ranks of undead rising in the nearby Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Abandoned by Stormwind's official garrison, Darkshire's local militia relies on traveling mercenaries to stem the encroaching horrors. Duskwood once stood under the shield of Stormwind, but as royal resources stretched thin and political discord gripped the capital, the crown withdrew its commissioned soldiers. Darkshire was left largely defenseless against the encroaching shadows. In response, the people of the forest formed the Night Watch, a homegrown militia now led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke, standing between the cursed forest and the town's remaining residents. South of Darkshire lies the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, a once-peaceful resting place now crawling with restless skeletons and reanimated spellcasters. With the Night Watch spread perilously thin across Duskwood's borders, Commander Ebonlocke directs incoming adventurers to strike down Skeletal Warriors and Skeletal Mages before the cemetery's dead spill onto the roads.

quest:560.text: Farren's Proof. Farren's Proof is a short delivery mission in Southshore where an adventurer carries a grisly bounty of murloc heads from Lieutenant Farren Orinelle to Marshal Redpath. Having let someone else do the bloody work of hunting the coast, the squeamish lieutenant delegates the actual reporting as well. It marks an intermediate step in securing town recognition along the Hillsbrad coast. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is tasked with patrolling and securing the southern coastline of Hillsbrad Foothills, yet he has little stomach for the brutal realities of frontier warfare. After sending an adventurer out to cull the rampant murlocs infesting the beaches, he balks at actually touching the severed heads brought back as proof. Rather than personally marching the dripping trophies to Southshore's town command, Farren gladly dumps the errand right back onto the bearer. Across Southshore, Marshal Redpath oversees the town's defensive operations and military readiness amidst mounting threats from Tarren Mill and wild beast populations. Receiving a sack of murloc heads via courier rather than directly from his lieutenant hardly surprises him. While recognizing that the adventurer has become Farren's errand runner, Redpath is pragmatic enough to accept the assistance, knowing Southshore requires all the diligent labor it can muster to keep its borders intact.

quest:561.text: Farren's Proof. Farren's Proof is an Alliance courier mission within the harbor town of Southshore. Acting on behalf of Marshal Redpath, an adventurer delivers orders directing Lieutenant Farren Orinelle to focus his military attention on the naga encroaching upon the Eastern Strand. Southshore's military leadership is hard-pressed by surrounding threats, yet Marshal Redpath remains attentive to maritime dangers along the southern coast. Having received fresh intelligence concerning naga incursions upon the Eastern Strand, Redpath dispatches a runner across town to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle with direct orders: abandon peripheral distractions, eliminate the amphibious menace, and deliver his progress reports directly to the Marshal in person.

quest:562.text: Stormwind Ho!. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is desperate to escape his posting in Southshore and return south to Stormwind City. Sensing a career opportunity after hearing Alliance High Command fears the rising threat of the naga, he hires an adventurer to exterminate the serpent-folk so he can claim the credit and secure a reassignment. Southshore sits on the knife-edge of Lordaeron, hemmed in by Forsaken forces, syndicate brigands, and relentless sea fiends. For Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, an ordinary guardsman accustomed to city drunks and petty brawls in Stormwind, the posting is nothing short of miserable. When word arrives from his former mentor that Alliance High Command is increasingly anxious about the naga encroaching on the coasts, Farren spots his golden opportunity to leave the north behind. Despite his lofty ambitions, Farren is candid about his cowardice: facing ferocious Daggerspine sirens and shorehunters in open combat is far beyond his courage and ability. Instead of risking his neck, he commissions an adventurer to scour the beaches southeast of Southshore, cull the naga ranks, and provide the martial feats he needs to draft an impressive dispatch to Major Samuelson in Stormwind.

quest:563.text: Reassignment. Reassignment is the culmination of Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's campaign to escape his posting in Southshore. Having compiled an exaggerated report of his deeds against the coastal naga, Farren dispatches an adventurer all the way to Stormwind Keep to deliver the documents to his former mentor, Major Samuelson. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle has made no secret of his disdain for his station in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tucked away in Southshore, far from the comforts of the capital and under the stern watch of Marshal Redpath, Farren has spent his days scheming for a transfer back south. By taking credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga, he hopes to present himself as an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ripe for promotion. To secure his reassignment without arousing the suspicion of Marshal Redpath, Farren bypasses the local chain of command entirely. He relies instead on his personal ties to Major Samuelson, a senior officer in Stormwind Keep who once mentored him. Delivering the polished report directly into Samuelson's hands ensures that Farren's alleged accomplishments land on the desk of someone with the authority to reassign garrison personnel.

quest:564.text: Costly Menace. Darren Malvew of Southshore hates losing the town's beautiful horses. Undead, the Syndicate gang and assorted scoundrels have cost plenty, but Darren says nothing threatens them more than the mountain lions that keep coming down from the hills of Alterac. Darren Malvew of Southshore cannot stand losing the beautiful horses there. Quite a few have been lost to undead creeps, the Syndicate gang and the scoundrels poking about the region. By Darren's own word, though, no menace to the horses is bigger than the mountain lions up in Alterac, forever coming down from the hills. Darren wants the lions dealt with: eight Mountain Lions and ten Hulking Mountain Lions. Mountain Lions are found in the lower hills of the Alterac Mountains.

quest:5643.text: Shadowguard. Shadowguard is a priestly calling issued to Darkspear troll priests who find themselves far from home in the Forsaken capital of Undercity. Aelthalyste recognizes that the young troll has matured enough for their tribe's sacred rites and sends them back to Orgrimmar. In the Valley of Spirits, the priest trainer Ur'kyo awaits to guide them into a vital tier of spiritual protection. Even in the gloom of the Undercity, the bonds of faith and tribal tradition remain strong. Forsaken priest trainer Aelthalyste observes visiting troll priests closely, noting when an initiate has grown potent enough to face their culture's trials. Rather than imposing the bleak philosophy of the Forsaken priesthood upon them, she directs the troll back across the Great Sea to the ancestral ways of their own elders. Upon arriving in Durotar, the priest makes their way to the mystic enclave of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. There, Ur'kyo tends to the spiritual needs and ancient rituals of the Darkspear tribe. He welcomes the returning initiate, preparing them for an essential rite of passage that bridges the priest's bond to the loa with practical spells vital for warding off harm.

quest:5644.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of passage quest for Forsaken priests journeying far from Lordaeron. Guided by the Forsaken priest trainer Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff, the adept is directed back across the seas to Aelthalyste in the Undercity to unlock a signature manifestation of Shadow magic. While visiting Thunder Bluff, Forsaken priests who have honed their mastery over divine and shadowy disciplines are evaluated by Miles Welsh, a Forsaken priest posted among the tauren. Recognizing that an acolyte has grown sufficiently in power, Miles bids them return to the Ruins of Lordaeron rather than attempt to impart these higher mysteries himself in Kalimdor. Awaiting beneath the city ruins within the Undercity's War Quarter is Aelthalyste, one of the foremost mentors of Forsaken priesthood. She watches over the development of shadow-weaving acolytes, ensuring that the potent, draining blight known as the Devouring Plague is entrusted only to those capable of wielding its corruptive force without succumbing to it.

quest:5645.text: A Lack of Fear. A Lack of Fear is a rite-of-passage summons for dwarven priests, calling promising disciples back to the grand halls of Ironforge. High Priest Rohan awaits in the Mystic Ward to test their discipline and bestow teachings tailored to their growing resilience. Priests serving the Alliance abroad are routinely directed by their local mentors to report back to their order's senior clergy. For dwarven disciples, that guidance leads straight to High Priest Rohan in the heart of Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The summons marks a turning point where basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper, trial-tested applications of holy magic. High Priest Rohan does not simply teach liturgy; dwarven tradition views the Light as a shield and an unyielding bulwark in physical conflict. Reporting for this test acknowledges that the initiate has survived baptism through fire in the wider world and possesses the mettle required to master fear itself on the front lines.

quest:5646.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite-of-passage quest for Forsaken priests who have ventured to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear tribe. The troll priest trainer Ur'kyo in Orgrimmar directs promising Forsaken initiates to return home to Undercity, where Aelthalyste waits to impart deeper teachings of shadow. While the orcs and tauren have little inclination toward priestly worship, the Darkspear trolls and the Forsaken share a curious theological bond within the Horde. In Orgrimmar, the troll priest trainer Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power. Yet he recognizes that Forsaken initiates must ultimately master the sinister arts unique to their own condition. In a mutual show of respect between their peoples, Ur'kyo directs wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to complete their training. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Priestess Aelthalyste tends to the flock in the Undercity's War Quarter. Forsaken priests walk a solitary, grueling path shaped by their turn toward shadow, tempering the painful touch of the Holy Light with the devastating affliction of Shadow magic. When an initiate attains sufficient prowess, Aelthalyste gathers them close to bestow the affliction known to their kind as the Devouring Plague.

quest:567.text: Dangerous!. Posted on the wanted board in Tarren Mill, this bounty marks four prominent Hillsbrad humans for execution. High Executor Darthalia has declared them dangerous enemies of the Forsaken due to specific assassinations and supply ambushes. The front lines across the Hillsbrad Foothills are brutal and personal. To High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, ordinary citizens of Hillsbrad have become lethal combatants. The wanted notice singles out four specific figures whose resistance has cost Forsaken lives and valuable shipments from the Undercity. The bounty names Clerk Horrace Whitesteed for the killing of Deathguard Toma, Citizen Wilkes for the murder of Apothecary Eli, Miner Hackett for taking the life of Deathstalker Fry, and Farmer Kalaba for sabotaging supply convoys sent from the Undercity. Each target operates from different pockets of Hillsbrad resistance, remaining elusive amid the chaos of the broader conflict.

quest:5672.text: Elune's Grace. Elune's Grace is a rite of recognition offered to devout night elf priests in Darnassus. Upon proving their faith and discipline through their early journeys, priests are called before Priestess Alathea to receive deeper instruction in the divine mysteries of the Moon Goddess. Within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, the Sisterhood of Elune guides young acolytes from their first prayers to mastery of lunar magic. Night elves do not look upon the Holy Light in the same manner as humans or dwarves; their faith is inextricably tied to the Mother Moon, Elune. When a novice priest reaches a significant milestone in their devotion, senior mentors take notice, marking the disciple as ready to shoulder greater divine power. Priestess Alathea extends this summons on behalf of the Sisterhood. She acknowledges that the acolyte's dedication has elevated them beyond the common flock, granting them access to traditions preserved across millennia. Accepting the rite seals the priest's bond to Elune, unlocking specific protective wards and lunar invocations unique to the kaldorei faith.

quest:5674.text: Elune's Grace. Elune's Grace is a rite of advancement for developing night elf priests, marking their readiness to wield divine talents unique to their people. Guided from local outposts like Dolanaar back to the sacred Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, candidates present themselves before Priestess Alathea to prove their devotion. Within the Sisterhood of Elune, a priest's journey involves more than simply mastering standard prayers of mending and smiting. As acolytes grow in experience, they reach a threshold where they are deemed ready to receive blessings granted exclusively to the kaldorei. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar lack the authority to bestow these deeper arts, directing promising disciples back to the cultural and spiritual heart of their order. The quest directs initiates across Teldrassil to the grand Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. There, beneath the gaze of the high priesthood, Priestess Alathea evaluates whether the petitioner is truly prepared to bear the goddess's defensive mantle. Learning Elune's Grace symbolizes reaching true maturity within the priesthood, bridging the gap between raw potential and formal service to the goddess.
