After the initial inquiries in Darkshire, Clerk Daltry pulls the town registry to locate Stalvan Mistmantle. To his surprise, the ledger hasn't been updated in years and lists Stalvan's last known residence far to the west, at the schoolhouse in Moonbrook. Unaware of the sinister nature of the investigation, Daltry treats it as routine bureaucratic upkeep, asking travelers to look into the address and gather whatever records might bring Darkshire's dusty archives up to date. Following the trail means venturing beyond the gloom of Duskwood into the lawless dust of Westfall. Moonbrook, once a thriving agricultural settlement, now crawls with Defias Brotherhood outlaws. Near the center of the derelict town stands its abandoned schoolhouse, standing quiet amid the bandit occupation. Inside, an old footlocker holds the first tangible clues to Stalvan's past life as an educator, as well as a lingering, restless sorrow bound to the chest.

quest:671.text: Foul Magics. Foul Magics is a Horde quest originating in Hammerfall within the Arathi Highlands. Tor'gan senses a disturbing demonic presence to the west and discovers traces of dark summoning rituals at Northfold Manor. He asks adventurers to venture into the manor and retrieve bloodstone amulets used in these summonings so he can study their dark magic. Tor'gan, an orc stationed at the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, began noticing an unsettling disturbance drifting through the Arathi Highlands. For an orc, demonic energies are not merely an abstract threat; they evoke a visceral, biological reaction rooted in the history of the blood curse. As Tor'gan tracked the source of his agitation westward toward Northfold Manor, the ambient corruption caused his blood to boil and stoked an involuntary rage within him. Recognizing the telltale aftermath of demonic summoning, he retreated before the dark influence overwhelmed his senses, seeking outside help instead of returning himself. At Northfold Manor, Tor'gan discovered physical evidence of dark rituals: an amulet carved from bloodstone lying on the ground. These magical charms are actively employed to facilitate and stabilize demonic summoning rituals. The specific amulet Tor'gan managed to recover was already depleted of its magical reserves, making thorough magical analysis impossible. In order to investigate the full extent of the summoning and determine what entities were brought forth, he charges Horde travelers with heading into Northfold Manor to retrieve ten intact bloodstone amulets from the practitioners residing there.

quest:672.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands where Tor'gan seeks to lift the spirits of a despondent orc named Gor'mul. When tales of Orgrimmar and Warchief Thrall fail, Tor'gan turns to newly rediscovered shamanic traditions to craft a revitalizing amulet from highland raptor eyes. At the remote outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, the orcs face enemies from without and quiet battles within. One of their own, Gor'mul, has fallen into a deep, unshakable melancholy. His companions attempted to rally him with proud tales of Kalimdor, the mighty fortress city of Orgrimmar, and the visionary leadership of young Warchief Thrall. Yet none of these grand victories or distant wonders could pierce Gor'mul's gloom or give him reason to hope. Recognizing that mere words are powerless against Gor'mul's despondency, Tor'gan turns to the Horde's revived spiritual heritage. By gathering the eyes of fierce highland raptors roaming Arathi, Tor'gan crafts an amulet blessed with the predators' spirits. Rather than relying on brute force or fel power, this ritual invokes the restorative strength of newly embraced shamanistic traditions, hoping the beast's vital flame can awaken a brother's dormant will to live.

quest:674.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest aimed at rekindling the fighting will of Gor'mul, a broken warrior consumed by despair. An emissary delivers a Raptor Talon Amulet in hopes of awakening the fierce spirit he once possessed. However, Gor'mul remains bitter, questioning whether any simple trinket could ever mend his sorrow or restore glory to the Horde. Raising Spirits involves delivering a Raptor Talon Amulet to an orc named Gor'mul. His allies hope that the wild strength and ferocity of raptors, channeled through the talisman, will reawaken the warrior's flame that once burned fiercely within his veins.

quest:675.text: Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live. In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.

quest:676.text: The Hammer May Fall. Dispatched by Tallow from Tarren Mill, Horde champions are directed across the mountains into the Arathi Highlands to relieve the embattled settlement of Hammerfall. Before reporting to Drum Fel, adventurers must prove their battle readiness against the brutish Boulderfist ogres lurking near the ruins of Stromgarde. In Tarren Mill, Tallow harbors little patience for untested adventurers wandering through the Foothills. Seeing undisciplined recruits standing idle while distant allies bleed, he directs capable fighters east through Thoradin's Wall into the Arathi Highlands. The Horde outpost of Hammerfall stands besieged on multiple fronts, but Tallow refuses to send warm bodies unless they have proven their worth against substantial opposition first. Rather than allowing recruits to stumble blindly into Hammerfall, Tallow demands a demonstration of martial strength at the ogre mound northeast of Stromgarde. The Boulderfist tribe maintains a heavy presence in Arathi, their hulking ogres and enforcers posing an immediate threat to anyone traveling the highland trails. Slaying these brutes serves both to thin the hostile forces flanking the road and to ensure that only capable warriors arrive at the outpost.

quest:677.text: Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde military initiative directed by Drum Fel from the outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Threatened by an alliance between the local Witherbark forest trolls and Boulderfist ogres, the Horde launches a preemptive campaign against the Witherbark to secure their foothold in the region. From the fortified sanctuary of Hammerfall, Drum Fel organizes a preemptive military strike against the hostile native powers of the Arathi Highlands. Surrounded by old human ruins and aggressive local factions, the Horde settlement faces an imminent threat from a cooperative pact formed between the indigenous Witherbark forest trolls and the brute Boulderfist ogres. Rather than allowing their enemies to dictate the terms of survival, Drum Fel calls on champions to take the offensive. The initial offensive focuses south of Hammerfall, targeting the heart of Witherbark territory. The Witherbark have turned their backs on any diplomacy, choosing instead to conspire with the Boulderfist ogres to purge the Horde from the highlands. By culling their specialized axe throwers, headhunters, and witch doctors, Hammerfall seeks to shatter their martial leadership and demonstrate that the Horde is here to stay.

quest:678.text: Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde martial trial issued by Drum Fel at the Hammerfall outpost in the Arathi Highlands. Having proven their basic combat readiness, adventurers are ordered southwest toward the dwarven bridge to engage the dangerous Boulderfist ogres. Eliminating both front-line brutes and spellcasting magi tests the warrior's resolve while protecting the Horde's vulnerable foothold in Arathi. At the isolated Horde redoubt of Hammerfall, survival demands unwavering martial strength. Drum Fel, recognizing the growing capabilities of travelers aiding the outpost, refuses to let anyone rest on easy victories. Rather than facing minor skirmishers, warriors must prove their mettle against what Fel considers a genuine threat: the hulking Boulderfist ogres. These brutes have consistently harassed the Horde expedition and tested the resolve of Hammerfall’s defenders. Fel offers simple terms for the task—warriors are expected to return successful in flesh or honorably in spirit, with praise promised for sheer tenacity in battle. The Boulderfist clan has established an entrenched lair southwest of Hammerfall, extending their territory toward the grand dwarven bridge connecting Arathi to the Wetlands. Unlike undisciplined beasts, the ogres command both crushing physical power and lethal mystical arts, fielding durable brutes alongside cunning magi. Their aggressive presence poses a direct challenge to the Horde's supply lines and regional dominance. By ordering the destruction of ten Boulderfist brutes and four magi, Drum Fel seeks to blunt their strength, ensuring the Boulderfists understand that the warriors of Hammerfall will neither yield ground nor tolerate rivals in Arathi.

quest:68.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This investigation unearths a forgotten chapter in the dark tale of Stalvan Mistmantle. A dusty, unsent letter pulled from a neglected footlocker in Moonbrook provides tangible proof of where he stayed before his vanished trail turned cold, leading back to Darkshire's records. While tracking down the history of Stalvan Mistmantle, an old footlocker tucked away in Moonbrook yields a vital piece of the puzzle: a dusty, unsent letter. Moonbrook, once a thriving agricultural settlement, fell into ruin and now teems with outlaws and restless specters. Stalvan's presence here was brief enough to escape common memory, but this neglected missive definitively places him in the hamlet. Delivering the letter back across the border to Darkshire gives Clerk Daltry the missing documentation he needs. While Daltry finds it peculiar that the letter was never mailed, the evidence is indisputable. With the Moonbrook connection verified, the bureaucratic paper trail can finally guide the investigation toward where Stalvan fled next.

quest:681.text: Northfold Manor. Captain Nials, at Refuge Pointe, asks for help against the Syndicate holding Northfold Manor. Their hold on the land between the defenders of Stromgarde and Southshore makes it hard for supplies to arrive. Stromgarde has been carved up between the ogres, the Syndicate and the Alliance, and every faction fights the others to a bloody stalemate. The Alliance's forces dwindle while their enemies grow. The defenders need help from Southshore, but supplies are slow to arrive. The Syndicate holds the ground between the defenders and Southshore. Captain Nials wants you to go to their base at Northfold Manor and cut down their highwaymen and mercenaries, in the hope that the pressure on the supply trains eases and more get through.

quest:683.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. Sara Balloo's Plea is a somber errand undertaken on behalf of a grieving dwarven widow in Ironforge. Unable to face her monarch directly in her state of sorrow, Sara entrusts a personal appeal to King Magni Bronzebeard regarding her fallen husband, Sully Balloo. After receiving the tragic final letter recovered from the watery depths of the Thandol Span, Sara Balloo finds herself paralyzed by mourning. Rather than let her husband Sully's sacrifice fade into obscurity, she writes a plea addressed directly to the throne of Ironforge. Too overwhelmed by heartbreak to appear before court etiquette herself, she entrusts the sealed parchment to a trusted champion of the Alliance to petition King Magni Bronzebeard on her behalf.

quest:684.text: WANTED: Marez Cowl. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty quest issued against a high-ranking Syndicate operative entrenched within the ruins of Stromgarde. As both an influential advisor and a dark warlock trafficking with demons, Cowl represents a severe threat to the Alliance forces attempting to secure the Arathi Highlands. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty decree posted to eliminate one of the Syndicate's key leadership figures in the Arathi Highlands. Marez Cowl serves as a high-ranking advisor and field operative within the organization, orchestrating their activities in the ruined capital of Stromgarde. By placing a price on her head, Alliance commanders at Refuge Pointe aim to decapitate the Syndicate's local command structure. Unlike typical brigands or dispossessed nobles among the Syndicate, Marez Cowl is a practitioner of dark sorcery. She is known as a cunning warlock who openly traffics with demonic powers to enforce her will and defend Syndicate territory. Approaching her lair within Stromgarde requires confronting not only cutthroats and conspirators, but the fell entities she commands.

quest:685.text: WANTED: Otto and Falconcrest. A bounty posted by the Stromgarde Militia marks Lord Falconcrest, leader of the local Syndicate forces, and his deadly bodyguard Otto for death. Eliminating them strikes a crucial blow against the criminal organization's foothold in the Arathi Highlands. Proof of their demise must be delivered to Captain Nials at Refuge Pointe. The Stromgarde Militia has issued an official bounty targeting two key figures in the Arathi Highlands: Lord Falconcrest and his ferocious bodyguard, Otto. Stationed out of Refuge Pointe, the beleaguered defenders of Stromgarde seek to break the Syndicate's hold over their ancestral lands. Hunters must bring the heads of both targets to Captain Nials to claim the reward. Lord Falconcrest serves as the mastermind behind the Syndicate's coordinated push into the Arathi Highlands. His death represents a vital strategic victory for the Alliance, promising to severely disrupt the criminal network's operations in the region. Beside him stands Otto, a brutally effective bodyguard whose blades have already cut down dozens of Stromgarde's remaining militia soldiers.

quest:686.text: A King's Tribute. A King's Tribute is an Alliance quest offered by King Magni Bronzebeard in the High Seat of Ironforge. Deeply moved by the grief of Sara Balloo, whose husband Sully fell defending the Thandol Span, the King decides to honor the fallen soldier with a lasting monument. He dispatches an adventurer to relay his royal commission to Grand Mason Marblesten. When King Magni Bronzebeard receives the plea of Sara Balloo, he does not dismiss the grieving widow. While he acknowledges that common folk may struggle to understand the brutal necessities of war, the loss of every soldier fighting beneath the Alliance banner weighs heavily upon his conscience. Unable to reverse the grim finality of death on the front lines, Magni chooses to ensure Sully Balloo's sacrifice is never forgotten. Rather than issuing empty platitudes, the King resolves to raise a physical memorial in Sully's honor. He appoints the adventurer as custodian of his royal will, sending them across Ironforge to confer with Grand Mason Marblesten. Entrusted with the King's personal commission, the master stonemason prepares to carve the memory of a fallen defender into stone.

quest:689.text: A King's Tribute. King Magni Bronzebeard has commissioned a monument to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who perished defending the Thandol Span. To honor the fallen warrior with enduring dignity, Grand Mason Marblesten dispatches travelers to Hillsbrad to retrieve pristine Alterac Granite. When King Magni Bronzebeard decided that fallen soldier Sully Balloo deserved a lasting memorial, the task fell directly to Ironforge's finest craftsman, Grand Mason Marblesten. Balloo lost his life during the disaster at the Thandol Span, a vital artery connecting the dwarven lands to northern kingdoms that has suffered brutal attacks by Dark Iron saboteurs. To Marblesten, fulfilling the king's royal decree means creating a sculpture that will withstand both time and war, ensuring that dwarven sacrifice is neither overlooked nor forgotten in the Great Forge. A master dwarven mason will not settle for ordinary quarry rock for a king's project. Marblesten insists that Sully Balloo's likeness can only be captured in Alterac Granite, a dense, resilient stone prized for its durability and clean texture. The challenge lies in securing it: the best deposits lie around Darrow Hill within the contested foothills of Hillsbrad. Venturing deep into the troubled north is dangerous, but dwarven stonework demands materials worthy of the heroism they commemorate.

quest:69.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This errand marks a pivotal turn in the search for the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle, leading investigators out of the gloom of Duskwood and back toward the heart of the kingdom. A hasty, scratched-out entry discovered in Darkshire's town registry points across the river to Goldshire. Following the paper trail to the bustling Lion's Pride Inn is the next step in uncovering where the mysterious tutor went. While reviewing Darkshire's records, Clerk Daltry catches an oversight in the town registry. Tucked beneath an earlier entry for Stalvan Mistmantle lies a second destination, hastily written and partially scratched out as if someone had second thoughts or meant to obscure their movements. The note indicates that Stalvan intended to travel northwest toward Elwynn Forest, specifically to the Lion's Pride Inn. Departing the shadowed groves of Duskwood for the sunny roads of Goldshire offers a stark contrast, but the shadow of Stalvan's past reaches even here. The Lion's Pride Inn serves as the bustling crossroads of Elwynn Forest, welcoming travelers, merchants, and soldiers alike. Innkeeper Farley presides over the busy taproom, making him the ideal person to ask about an educated wanderer seeking lodging.

quest:690.text: Malin's Request. Malin's Request is an Alliance task offered by Archmage Malin in Stormwind City's Mage Quarter. Malin asks seasoned adventurers to travel far north to Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands, where an expedition attempts to recover valuable magical relics left behind during the fall of Stromgarde. Archmage Malin, stationed in the Wizard's Sanctum of Stormwind, acts on behalf of his former mentor, Archmage Trelane. When the martial kingdom of Stromgarde collapsed into chaos and ruin, Trelane made a desperate stand at the Tower of Arathor. Forced to abandon his post as the city fell to hostile forces, Trelane left behind powerful enchanted possessions. Eager to reclaim these lost artifacts before hostile hands seize them, Malin directs capable mercenaries north to reinforce his operatives in the field. The road to recovering Trelane's relics leads through Refuge Pointe, the beleaguered bastion of Stromgarde loyalists in the central Arathi Highlands. Malin's primary contact among the defenders is the dwarf Skuerto. However, Refuge Pointe is severely hard-pressed by surrounding Syndicate outlaws, Witherbark trolls, and Boulderfist ogres. Arriving travelers quickly find that Skuerto and the outpost garrison are stretched far too thin to offer a warm reception without immediate assistance.

quest:691.text: Worth Its Weight in Gold. At Refuge Pointe, Apprentice Kryten is after Witherbark tusks, medicine pouches and a shadow hunter's knife, all reagents for Archmage Malin, who sent him and Skuerto to gather them. He asks you to seek them among the Witherbark trolls in the southeast of Arathi. Archmage Malin sent Kryten and Skuerto to Arathi to collect reagents, and Kryten had no idea how to gather them until you arrived. He needs ten Witherbark tusks, four medicine pouches and one shadow hunter knife. The Witherbark trolls make their home in the southeast of Arathi. By Kryten's research, any Witherbark troll should have tusks, and the witch doctors carry the medicine pouches. The knife belongs to the mightiest shadow hunters, handed to them after they finish their rites of passage. Only battle will show which of them has one.

quest:6921.text: Amongst the Ruins. Tasked by Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost, Horde adventurers delve into the flooded temple of Blackfathom Deeps to recover a fathom core. The Earthen Ring seeks this relic to uncover the dark elemental plots of the invading Twilight's Hammer cult. The ancient night elven temple of Blackfathom Deeps, once sacred to Elune, has fallen under the dominion of sinister forces. Deep within its submerged passages, the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer have established a stronghold. Stationed at the windswept shore of Zoram'gar Outpost in Ashenvale, the Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea observes the growing taint with rising alarm, recognizing that the cult intends to subjugate the local elements against the land and its defenders. To counter the cult's designs, Je'neu tasks Horde champions with securing a fathom core from the underwater fathom stone within the Moonshrine Ruins. When correctly deciphered by skilled shamans, the core reveals an exhaustive chronicle of elemental currents and disturbances. With this artifact in hand, the Earthen Ring hopes to pierce the veil of the Twilight's Hammer's operations and shield the region from elemental catastrophe.

quest:6922.text: Baron Aquanis. Upon vanquishing the water elemental Baron Aquanis within Blackfathom Deeps, adventurers recover a Strange Water Globe containing tainted, putrid fluid. Brought to Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring, the artifact provides crucial evidence of the elemental corruption spreading beneath Ashenvale. Je'neu believes it will prove what corrupted the baron, and he wouldn't be surprised if it were the Twilight's Hammer cultists lurking in the submerged ruins. Baron Aquanis was no ordinary water spirit, but a powerful elemental corrupted by foul sorcery within the flooded grottos of Blackfathom Deeps. When destroyed, the elemental leaves behind a Strange Water Globe—an impervious orb holding a sloshing, putrid fluid that seemingly sustained and warped the creature's natural essence. The object defies physical damage, harboring energies that are deeply distressing to those attuned to the balance of the elements.

quest:693.text: Wand over Fist. Skuerto at Refuge Pointe has worked out where the first of Trelane's items ended up. Kor'gresh has Trelane's Wand of Invocation in Boulderfist Hall, and Skuerto wants it brought back. After your work for Apprentice Kryten, Skuerto has found where Trelane's first item went. Kor'gresh holds it in Boulderfist Hall, and has been throwing blasts of ice at his own kin to keep them in line. Skuerto reckons the ogre must be close to figuring out all of the wand's powers. Boulderfist Hall lies south of Refuge Pointe and then east of Thandol Span.

quest:694.text: Trelane's Defenses. With the wand in hand, Skuerto turns to the ogres that surround the Tower of Arathor. To bring the tower's defenses to life, he needs an azure agate from the Boulderfist shaman, to be taken to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe. Ogres surround the Tower of Arathor in Stromgarde. Skuerto says the tower's defenses must be activated if you are to stand a chance against them and still reach the items alive. Certain gems from the tower have caught the fancy of the Boulderfist shaman, who carried them off, though Skuerto says they will not keep them for long. Bring one azure agate to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, who knows the spell to enchant it so that it works as a key.

quest:695.text: An Apprentice's Enchantment. Apprentice Kryten has enchanted the agate you brought him from the Boulderfist shaman. Touched to a pedestal at the foot of the tower, it will wake the tower's defenses. Before you leave, he sends you to Skuerto for the rest. Kryten hands you the enchanted gem. He explains that touching it to a pedestal at the foot of the tower will wake the tower's defenses, and that you should use it when you are ready to go in after the rest of Trelane's items. He will await your return at the camp. First, speak to Skuerto, who will fill in whatever else you need to know.

quest:696.text: Attack on the Tower. With the tower's defenses awake, Skuerto at Refuge Pointe sends you into the ogre-held tower for Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. They should lie in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be more than pleased if you bring them back. After Kryten's enchantment, Skuerto tells you what to look for: Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three should be sitting in chests inside the tower, and you should have no trouble opening them yourself, though the ogres call for care. The tower's defenses will not deal with them on their own, and if the ogres find you stealing from them, they will put the hurt on you.

quest:697.text: Malin's Request. Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin, who is found in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It tells Malin that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon, and Skuerto is certain Malin will repay you well for helping them in Arathi. After the work in Arathi, Skuerto hands you a letter to take back to Stormwind. Its message for Archmage Malin in the Mage Quarter is that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto has no doubt that Malin will repay you well for helping them, and sends you off with a wish for a safe journey.

quest:6981.text: The Glowing Shard. The Glowing Shard is a mysterious emerald-hued gem plucked from the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Swirling with smoky essence beneath its polished surface, this disturbing relic drives adventurers to seek answers in Ratchet and beyond. Drawn from deep within the Wailing Caverns, the glowing shard immediately unnerves those who hold it. Brilliant green and seemingly solid, it holds churning, mist-like shadows beneath its crystalline face. The crystal exerts a subtle pull, demanding attention while exuding a deeply unsettling aura that hints at the corrupted nature of the slumbering druids and their nightmare-infested sanctuary.

quest:70.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation directs searchers to an abandoned letter left behind at Goldshire's inn years ago. Following the trail of Stalvan Mistmantle leads out of Elwynn Forest and into Stormwind's Canal District. When Innkeeper Farley of the Lion's Pride Inn is asked about Stalvan Mistmantle, he recalls a stormy night years ago. A traveling courier had sought shelter from the pouring rain, only to rush downstairs around midnight in sheer panic. Dressed in only his sleepwear, the courier bolted straight out into the dark storm and was never seen again. In his panicked flight, the courier abandoned his satchel and personal chest in the upstairs room. Among the forgotten cargo lay an unsent letter bearing the name Stalvan, addressed to someone residing in the Canal District of Stormwind City. The chest remained untouched at the foot of the bed until Farley permitted it to be opened.

quest:700.text: A King's Tribute. A King's Tribute marks the final step in honoring the sacrifice of the fallen dwarven soldier Sully Balloo. After fine granite is gathered from the ruins of Lordaeron, Grand Mason Marblesten sculpts a solemn memorial monument in Ironforge on the orders of King Magni Bronzebeard. King Magni Bronzebeard commissioned a permanent monument to honor Sully Balloo, a brave dwarf who lost his life in service to his people. Crafted by Grand Mason Marblesten using high-quality granite transported from the war-torn lands of Lordaeron, the finished memorial stands in Ironforge as an enduring testament to fallen soldiers whose sacrifices preserve the dwarven kingdom. When presented with news of the monument's completion, Magni reflects somberly on the limits of stone and mortality. While acknowledging that carved rock can never truly equate to a brave dwarf's life, he hopes the memorial endures so future generations walking Azeroth will never forget the heroes who bled to secure their tomorrow.

quest:701.text: Guile of the Raptor. Guile of the Raptor is a quest in which Tor'gan seeks to awaken the dormant warrior spirit within Gor'mul. By harvesting the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers, Tor'gan plans to fashion an enchanted item imbued with the cunning and predatory power of the raptor. Tor'gan works to restore a listless compatriot named Gor'mul, whose warrior spirit has fallen dormant. Rather than relying on simple persuasion, Tor'gan turns to primal magic to shock Gor'mul back into action. By crafting a charm imbued with the essence of wild predators, he hopes to reintroduce Gor'mul to martial resolve and demonstrate the strength of their new power. To channel the predatory instincts of the wild, Tor'gan requires the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers. In shamanic and primal traditions, the heart of a cunning hunter carries its ferocity and guile. Tor'gan weaves both a physical token and a spell from these trophies, aiming to infuse Gor'mul directly with the predator's cunning so he can rediscover his true calling.

quest:702.text: Guile of the Raptor. After the earlier Guile of the Raptor, Tor'gan hands you an orb and sends you to Gor'mul at Hammerfall. Its energy carries the essence of the raptor, meant to stir Gor'mul's spirit and give him new purpose. Tor'gan gives you an orb whose energy is meant to fill Gor'mul with the raptor's essence. He hopes it will rouse the warrior's spirit and set him on a fresh course in life. Once Gor'mul is himself again, Tor'gan means to explain the current state of the Horde to him and gain a great warrior's help in the unceasing battles. Gor'mul greets your return with sourness, saying he wants nothing more than more of Tor'gan's pity and mocking you with talk of brightly colored string.

quest:7162.text: Proving Grounds. Proving Grounds is an initiation rite given by Lieutenant Haggerdin to Alliance recruits enlisting with the Stormpike Guard in Alterac. To earn an official Stormpike Insignia, aspirants must venture into the harpy-infested Icewing Caverns and recover a planted battle standard. Proving one's courage in the cavern marks the first step toward rising through the expedition's military ranks. The Stormpike Guard wages a relentless campaign in Alterac Valley against the Frostwolf Clan. Lieutenant Haggerdin, coordinating forces from the Alliance encampment in the Alterac Mountains, refuses to send green recruits onto the battlefield without a test. Before granting any soldier an official place in the guard, Haggerdin demands proof of skill and nerve by sending them into the treacherous Icewing Caverns southwest of Dun Baldar. The trial is straightforward in concept but deadly in execution: a Stormpike banner stands planted deep within the subterranean ice tunnels. The caverns are not empty; vicious frost harpies nest in the frostbitten recesses and eagerly tear apart unwary trespassers. Returning with the banner intact demonstrates that a recruit can navigate dangerous terrain, withstand brutal predators, and maintain discipline under pressure. Surviving the cavern and returning the standard earns a soldier the Stormpike initiate's insignia, welcoming them officially into the expeditionary force. As Haggerdin promises, the insignia is not merely a trinket—it is a mark of rank that can be enhanced as a soldier earns greater honor on the battlefield, aspiring toward legendary honors such as the Eye of Command.

quest:72.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation directs searchers to the Canals of Stormwind City, where Caretaker Folsom watches over the remaining possessions of the ruined Flintridge family. Looking for answers regarding the mysterious Stalvan Mistmantle, adventurers must dig through crated estate goods while confronting restless spirits tied to a past massacre. Tracking Stalvan's movements leads out of the shadowed groves of Duskwood and into the heart of Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom looks after what little remains of the Flintridge household. According to Folsom, his father served the estate before him and had the grisly task of mopping up blood in the wake of a horrific household slaughter—a tragedy somehow tied to the name Stalvan. With the Flintridge trust funds entirely drained and royal tax vultures circling, the family's surviving heirlooms and packed belongings are slated for auction. Whatever keepsakes and papers survived the bloodshed sit piled into shipping crates along the canal embankment. Uncovering Stalvan's trail requires prying open these sealed boxes before the estate's remaining worldly goods are scattered to collectors across the kingdom.

quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. Deep in the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel refuses to abandon his dig site without a prize to show the Explorers' League. Despite his severe forgetfulness and an infestation of hostile troggs, he insists on uncovering a mysterious fossil before retreating. Ensuring the dwarven researcher survives his erratic search allows word of his safety to reach his assistant back in Auberdine. Remtravel's Dig lies far to the south of Darkshore, nestled among ancient ruins that were supposed to hold forgotten secrets. Instead, the dwarven excavators struck into pockets of savage troggs, driving out the workers and leaving the camp under siege. While most would flee for Auberdine immediately, Prospector Remtravel became fixated on salvaging his findings. Refusing to leave empty-handed, he wanders right into the teeth of danger to recover an elusive fossil to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:7321.text: Soothing Turtle Bisque. Soothing Turtle Bisque is a culinary task offered by Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill. The Forsaken cook aims to disprove the notion that the undead lack culinary talent by preparing a hearty broth from local snapjaw meat. Players must hunt freshwater turtles around the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the shores of Lordamere Lake to master his prized recipe. It is widely assumed that the Forsaken have entirely abandoned the comforts of life, including the art of fine dining. Christoph Jeffcoat, stationed in Tarren Mill, vigorously rejects that assumption. Boasting that his rich, soothing turtle bisque is good enough to tempt souls back from beyond the grave, Jeffcoat seeks to prove that undead hands are capable of delicate, heartwarming craft even in a land tainted by plague and war. Ordinarily, Jeffcoat gathered his own ingredients from the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the eastern shores of Lordamere Lake in neighboring Alterac. However, duties in Tarren Mill and the encroaching presence of Alliance forces have pinned him down. He relies on passing Horde cooks to hunt the snapjaws, harvest their meat, and bring it back so the culinary tradition can endure.

quest:736.text: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. The Star, the Hand and the Heart is an Undercity quest wherein Keeper Bel'dugur tests an aspiring leader seeking to establish a new chapter of their order. To earn the essential Yagyin's Digest, the petitioner must track down three items of power whose names Bel'dugur dares not speak aloud. Within the shadowed corridors of the Undercity, ambitious practitioners seeking to lead their own circle turn to Keeper Bel'dugur. To establish a new flock and open a chapter of their order, an aspiring leader requires Yagyin's Digest, an authoritative text of ritual lore guarded by the keeper. Bel'dugur stands ready to support his fellow brother, but demands proof of worthiness before yielding such authority. Keeper Bel'dugur will not part with Yagyin's Digest lightly. He requires three distinct items of power to fulfill his side of the exchange. These relics carry such perilous or sacred significance that their names cannot even be spoken aloud; Bel'dugur instead pens them onto a private note. Only a practitioner capable of tracking down and retrieving all three unspoken artifacts proves worthy of founding their own chapter.

quest:74.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This step in the investigation leads deep into an old crate of Flintridge heirlooms left beside the canals of Stormwind City. Sifting through the dusty relics uncovers a torn journal page, offering a vital handwritten clue to the past life of Stalvan Mistmantle that leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. While digging through a sealed crate filled with musty heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits, investigators uncover a lone torn journal page hidden beneath a ceramic vase. Written in Stalvan Mistmantle's own hand, this remnant provides an intimate glimpse into the mind of a reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. This errand delivers a strange petrified specimen recovered from the wild beaches of Darkshore to the Explorers' League outpost in Darnassus. Archaeologist Hollee refuses to abandon her distracted colleague in the field, entrusting the specimen's transport to a passing adventurer instead. The fossil's arrival in the night elven capital immediately captures the keen interest of Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Prospector Remtravel's excavations along the misty coast of Darkshore have unearthed a curious fossil, but digging deeper matters more to him than protocol. Archaeologist Hollee, unwilling to leave the wandering prospector alone amidst the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists, remains behind to watch over him. In order to get the discovery documented, she requires an Alliance traveler to ferry the specimen up to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild maintains a scholarly delegation. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea in force under the banner of the Explorers' League, eager to unearth ancient relics and lost history beneath the soil of Kalimdor. Receiving the artifact in the elven capital, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker wastes no time in marveling over Remtravel's knack for uncovering ancient treasures. While night elves view their forests as living sanctuaries, the League views the ancient lands as an expansive archaeological dig waiting to be deciphered.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a summons dispatched to young Horde champions visiting Thunder Bluff, urging them north into the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Delivered by the city's heralds, the call directs travelers to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to take part in a proving hunt. Within the serene heights of Thunder Bluff, runners keep the burgeoning Horde informed of opportunities beyond the borders of Mulgore. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation aimed at proven adventurers looking for greater challenges. With the Horde establishing footholds deep in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, young warriors are called upon to bolster those outposts and test their survival skills in a far harsher environment. Ashenvale represents both rich resources and severe peril for the Horde. Two prominent encampments anchor the faction's presence in the territory: Splintertree Post along the main road, and a remote outpost perched upon the western coast at Zoram Strand. Arriving at Splintertree Post puts incoming recruits directly under the wing of Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman organizing a massive hunt designed to tame the wilderness and claim glory for the Horde.

quest:75.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle leads out of Duskwood to an isolated home in southeastern Elwynn Forest. Marshal Haggard, an aging veteran whose eyesight has deteriorated, directs you to an upstairs chest containing an old bundle of papers left behind when he moved in. Marshal Haggard lives far from town on the southeastern fringes of Elwynn Forest, near the borders of Duskwood and Redridge. When he moved into his secluded home, he found a chest tucked away upstairs packed with old parchments. With his failing eyesight clouding over, he abandoned any effort to read them, leaving the documents undisturbed until an investigator comes asking about Stalvan.

quest:750.text: The Hunt Continues. The Hunt Continues is an early rite of passage assigned by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. It tasks aspiring hunters with gathering mountain cougar pelts from the southern hills to clothe the tribe's children and mend their tents. In Camp Narache, young hunters are taught that taking a beast is never an idle pursuit or a search for trophies. Grull Hawkwind charges fledgling adventurers with venturing into the southern hills of Red Cloud Mesa to track down mountain cougars. Rather than proving martial prowess alone, the task emphasizes responsibility to the community, showing that true hunters must provide essential provisions for their people. Life on the mesa demands durable materials to withstand the open elements. Grull explains that the cougar hides are urgently needed to sew clothing for the tribe's children and to mend worn hide tents throughout Camp Narache. Proving oneself capable of securing these prized pelts earns the gratitude of the elders, and Grull promises to bring word of the hunter's selfless contributions directly to his father, Chief Hawkwind.

quest:755.text: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the beginning of an initiate's spiritual journey on Red Cloud Mesa. Directed by Chief Hawkwind, travelers seek out Seer Graytongue in the southern hills of Camp Narache. Undertaking these venerable ceremonies is considered a vital trial of passage for tauren coming of age. Upon the Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind directs young tauren seeking to prove themselves to Seer Graytongue. Residing in the quiet hills directly south of Camp Narache, Graytongue oversees the spiritual beginnings of the youth. This simple journey marks the formal threshold between everyday camp life and the serious commitments demanded by tribal custom. The Earthmother is central to the creation beliefs and everyday existence of the tauren. Her rites serve as sacred trials of maturity, resilience, and spiritual depth. As Seer Graytongue cautions all who arrive at his sanctuary, embarking upon the Rites of the Earthmother is no light endeavor, requiring total dedication to the traditions of the mesa.

quest:78.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This errand marks a turning point in uncovering the history of Stalvan Mistmantle, sending investigators from Elwynn Forest back into the shadowed town of Darkshire. Guided by Marshal Haggard's memory of his service days, you bring a recovered journal page to Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to identify the chilling handwriting. After recovering a weathered, torn journal page from Marshal Haggard's chest in Elwynn Forest, the retired commander cannot read the faded script due to his failing eyesight. Recognizing that the trail leads back across the river, Haggard recalls his past commanding the Stormwind Guard and remembers spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He directs you to Tavernkeep Smitts, a barkeep whose long tenure has made him an unofficial custodian of local history and rumors.

quest:7807.text: A Donation of Wool. A Donation of Wool is a material requisition organized by the Gnomeregan Exiles to gather essential textile supplies. Displaced from their technological home city, the exiled gnomes rely on sixty pieces of wool cloth from generous adventurers across the realm to sustain their community. Contributing to the drive grants formal recognition among the gnome refugees. Following the fall of Gnomeregan to trogg invaders and radioactive contamination, the surviving gnomes found themselves displaced from their high-tech metropolis. Operating as refugees primarily hosted by their dwarven cousins in Ironforge, the Gnomeregan Exiles face severe logistical strain. Routine material drives for basic goods like cloth are essential to keep their people clothed, supplied, and organized while surviving outside their ancestral halls. To avoid overtaxing individual benefactors, the organizers of the drive request exactly sixty pieces of wool cloth per volunteer. By pooling modest contributions from across the realm, the exiles can amass the bulk textiles required for bedding, bandages, and clothing without placing an unsustainable burden on any single supplier. In exchange, the gnomes offer formal recognition among their people to anyone willing to aid their recovery effort.

quest:789.text: Sting of the Scorpid. Sting of the Scorpid is an early trial assigned by Gornek to Horde recruits at the Den in the Valley of Trials. Novices are challenged to hunt venomous scorpid workers northwest of camp and return ten tails to prove their combat readiness. The task serves as a vital lesson in surviving battlefield hazards and respecting even the smallest adversaries. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Gornek tests novice Horde recruits by sending them against the local wildlife. The venomous scorpids roaming the arid dirt northwest of the Den have humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. To prove their battlefield competence, young champions must venture into the rocks, slay scorpid workers, and return with ten of their severed tails as proof of prowess. While deadly, the venomous predators also supply the very salvation of injured initiates. The Den maintains stockpiles of antivenom brewed directly from extracted scorpid venom to treat fallen novices. Beyond surviving the venom, Gornek emphasizes a core tactical truth: in the chaos of battle, arrogance is fatal, and even the smallest foe wields enough lethal venom to bring down a mighty warrior.

quest:79.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This quest marks the moment where scattered rumors about Stalvan Mistmantle solidify into undeniable proof of a brutal crime. Tavernkeep Smitts hands over long-hidden muddy journal pages, directing the investigator straight to Night Watch Commander Althea Ebonlocke. For years, the grim fate of a visiting noble family remained an unresolved tragedy in Duskwood. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard, then a leader of the Stormwind Guard, originally investigated the massacre site and discovered a handful of torn, muddy journal pages. Without handwriting samples or corroborating papers, the notes sat cold, unable to officially implicate the recluse rumored to dwell in the wilderness. The evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood finally connects the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle, turning town gossip into an open-and-shut case of murder.

quest:79008.text: ... and that note you found. Discovered among the embers of a dying campfire in Westfall, this blistered note leaves behind a cryptic and solitary clue. Its scorched message hints at a destination waiting elsewhere in the world, urging whoever finds it to seek out a 'twin land.' Amid the abandoned fields, scavenged farmsteads, and wind-scoured plains of Westfall, travelers frequently come across the camps of vagrants, outlaws, or desperate vagabonds. Yet this small campsite was left in haste or secrecy, its provisions abandoned and its embers still faintly glowing. Left among the scattered debris lies a scorched slip of parchment that survived the flames. The blistered note bears only two short sentences: 'Not all that burns is lost. Find the twin land, find the place.' Shrouded in mystery, the words serve as both an enigmatic riddle and an invitation, pointing away from the desolate fields of Westfall toward another realm connected by name, geography, or fate.

quest:79092.text: Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal. Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal is an arcane volume documenting the investigations of the master mage of the Tower of Azora. Delivered to the scholars of the Ironforge Library, the journal adds valuable magical insights to the great dwarven archive. Archmage Theocritus is known throughout the Alliance as an esteemed spellcaster stationed at the Tower of Azora in the eastern reaches of Elwynn Forest. Over years of solitary study, Theocritus has investigated curious artifacts, ley line anomalies, and nearby magical threats, recording his findings within detailed journals. Recovering such a volume represents a rare opportunity to study the personal observations of a senior Kirin Tor archmage. The Explorers' League and the caretakers of the Ironforge Library maintain one of the greatest archival repositories on the continent. By delivering Archmage Theocritus' Research Journal to their care, adventurers ensure that its arcane insights are safely preserved and cataloged alongside the historic volumes of Khaz Modan. The librarians actively welcome any further magical discoveries that can broaden their collective wisdom.

quest:79192.text: Stepping Stones. Stepping Stones is an investigation launched from a weathered note posted in the rugged wilds of the Barrens. The scrawled parchment says two couriers had been making deliveries for the New Plague, and calls what befell them simple apothecary accidents. The mysterious writer urges whoever finds it to seek out a secluded mountain refuge tucked along the border of Desolace. Pinned haphazardly to a wooden plank in a backcountry camp, the message stands out against the harsh elements of the Barrens. Campgrounds here often see a quiet rotation of mercenaries, cutthroats, and drifters seeking temporary shelter far away from the prying eyes of the Crossroads or Ratchet. The torn note immediately cuts through mundane wilderness chatter, offering an invitation laced with intrigue and dark undertones.

quest:79236.text: Cherry for Your Thoughts?. In Booty Bay, a mercenary named Tokal is seeking a drink in exchange for the truth behind recent attacks on human and dwarven outposts. While rumors point the finger at the Horde, Tokal insists her group was operating under a private mercenary contract. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, an individual named Tokal is keeping a low profile while watching out for law enforcement. A series of aggressive raids recently devastated human and dwarven camps, fueling rumors that the Horde had orchestrated the attacks. When approached by travelers who clearly do not work for the inquiring marshal, Tokal is quick to push back against the widespread narrative, offering a different version of events in exchange for a drink.

quest:80.text: The Legend of Stalvan. This crucial step in the investigation of Stalvan Mistmantle brings the gathered evidence before Darkshire's authorities. With a bloodstained journal page in hand, Commander Althea Ebonlocke directs the investigator to Clerk Daltry to authenticate the handwriting once and for all. Following the trail of journal pages recovered across Duskwood and the surrounding human territories, the Night Watch finally holds what appears to be damning evidence against the elusive tutor, Stalvan Mistmantle. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has harbored suspicions about the man for some time, but bringing formal judgment requires absolute certainty. A single bloodstained page is not enough to pass sentence until it can be proven beyond doubt that the macabre scribblings originated from Stalvan's own hand.

quest:815.text: Break a Few Eggs. Break a Few Eggs is an errand assisting a harried cook who must keep up with endless meal preparations. Securing fresh, fragile ingredients without breaking them keeps the kitchen running and the cooking on schedule. Feeding a crowd is an exhausting, never-ending endeavor. Between breakfast, lunch, and dinner, there is scarcely any time to step away from the stove, let alone leave the kitchen to scrounge for raw provisions. In Break a Few Eggs, a hard-pressed cook turns to passing adventurers to secure fresh eggs before the next meal service falls behind. Transporting eggs requires a gentle touch that brute force cannot replace. The cook may offer sharp words and little praise, but intact ingredients speak for themselves. Once the eggs are delivered safe and unbroken, the cook wastes no time sending the gatherer off and returning straight to work over the fire.

quest:822.text: Chen's Empty Keg. Following the creation of the potent Stormstout, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet offers to craft another esoteric recipe learned from the elusive pandaren wanderer Chen Stormstout. This potent concoction, known as trogg ale, requires rare organs and glands harvested from the native beasts of the Barrens. After assisting Brewmaster Drohn with reproducing the legendary Chen Stormstout's initial draught, the orc brewmaster reveals that the wandering pandaren shared more than one secret. Drohn possesses the formula for an eccentric beverage known as trogg ale. Unlike mundane spirits distilled from grains, this peculiar brew relies entirely on potent organic reagents scavenged from the fiercest wildlife in central Kalimdor. To brew this pungent and invigorating draught, Drohn requires thunderous components: lightning glands from stormhides, a thunderhawk saliva gland from greater thunderhawks, and a hearty liver from the roaming kodos of the plains. Once distilled, the mixture produces a fiercely stimulating beverage tailored for survival in the wilderness.

quest:824.text: Je'neu of the Earthen Ring. This errand directs Horde adventurers to deliver a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals to Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring. As a shaman dedicated to elemental harmony, Je'neu seeks to understand the spreading corruption along the Zoram Strand and within Blackfathom Deeps. Studying the relic offers hope of halting the unnatural blight poisoning the region's waters. When strange, contaminated elementals began surfacing across Ashenvale, scouts took notice of the unnatural power animating them. Among the remains lay a befouled water globe, an intact vessel pulsing with corrupted magic. Knowing standard soldiers and scouts lacked the spiritual insight to diagnose such an anomaly, Mastok Wrilehiss directed Horde travelers to seek out someone with deep knowledge of ancient legends and elemental lore: Je'neu Sancrea. Je'neu Sancrea belongs to the Earthen Ring, an order of shamans committed to preserving balance among the primal forces of Azeroth. While Horde forces guard the frontier along the Zoram Strand, Je'neu concentrates on the spiritual wound festering in the nearby temple ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. To him, an elemental drawing power from a tainted vessel is not merely an isolated threat, but an alarming omen that unseen, ancient powers are perverting the natural order.

quest:8249.text: Junkboxes Needed. At Ravenholdt Manor, Fahrad maintains an endless demand for sturdy, locked containers to train the guild's rising rogues. Because the practice locks provided by the manor's own craftsman are too simple for advanced students, Fahrad trades specialized throwing knives to anyone willing to supply authentic heavy junkboxes. Within the hidden redoubt of Ravenholdt Manor, nestled in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, training never ceases. Master thief Fahrad oversees instruction for the guild's operatives, placing high value on practical lockpicking mastery. While Zan provides practice contraptions for new recruits, Fahrad considers that crude work entirely unfit for experienced operatives who must crack real, stubborn mechanisms in the field. To keep the manor supplied with real-world mechanisms, Fahrad contracts out for heavy junkboxes swiped from dangerous targets across Azeroth. Though only skilled thieves can lift these boxes from marks in the wild, Fahrad does not restrict his business solely to rogues. Anyone who delivers batches of these locked chests—even if already picked clean of major valuables—earns Fahrad's favor and a supply of the manor's lethally balanced throwing blades, provided a token coin remains inside to motivate the initiates.

quest:837.text: Encroachment. Encroachment is a Horde quest directed by Gar'Thok at Razor Hill in central Durotar. It charges champions with striking deep into the western bramble dens to eliminate the entrenched Razormane quilboar threatening the borders of the young orc nation. When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor and founded Durotar, they found much of the harsh, arid land already inhabited by the Razormane quilboar. These aggressive, boar-like creatures proved a constant thorn in the side of the new settlement. Through sustained military efforts, the Horde drove back the bulk of their numbers, yet fortified pockets of Razormane continue to cling stubbornly to their thorned redoubts west of Razor Hill. Gar'Thok, an officer stationed at Razor Hill, oversees the effort to purge the lingering Razormane threat once and for all. He tasks seasoned defenders with striking directly into the western bramble camps to eliminate their scouts, warriors, and dustrunners. For Gar'Thok and the Horde leadership, allowing the quilboar any foothold near Razor Hill invites disaster, and striking them here is seen as the first step toward securing Kalimdor. Eliminating the quilboar defenders clears the path for Horde forces to torch the bramble dens, preventing the Razormane from reclaiming the western foothills. By burning these structures to the ground, the Horde removes an enduring menace and secures the western perimeter of Durotar, safeguarding vital supply roads between Razor Hill and the wider realm.

quest:843.text: Gann's Reclamation. Gann's Reclamation is a Horde quest offered by the wandering tauren exile Gann Stonespire in the southern Barrens. Deeply aggrieved by the dwarven archaeological dig at Bael Modan that displaced his tribe, Gann enlists travelers to strike back by slaying the site's workers and retrieving their leader's journal. Before the Prospector's cannons and pickaxes broke the earth, the red bluffs south of the Barrens were the ancestral birthplace and hunting grounds of Gann Stonespire's clan. When the dwarves arrived from Ironforge to establish Bael Modan, the tauren were violently pushed out or killed to make room for massive quarries and trenches. With peaceful protests ignored and diplomacy exhausted, Gann now walks the dust of the southern road in solitude, plotting a bloody restitution for his fallen kin. The dwarven operation at Bael Modan spares little thought for the land or its stewards. Ripping open hillsides with steam engines and heavy explosives, the expedition under Prospector Khazgorm tore deep into the earth. Gann's task is simple and uncompromising: thin the ranks of the Bael'dun excavators and foremen tearing up the sacred soil, slay Khazgorm himself, and seize the prospector's personal excavation notes to discover what the Alliance invaders are truly after.

quest:846.text: Revenge of Gann. Revenge of Gann is a Horde quest in the southern Barrens where the grieving tauren exile Gann Stonespire plans retribution against the Bael Modan expedition. Having eliminated Prospector Khazgorm, Gann directs travelers into the dwarven fortress to gather volatile munitions for an explosive counterattack. Prospector Khazgorm's death delivered a setback to the Bael Modan dig site, but Gann Stonespire knows it is merely temporary. Dwarven operations rarely pause for long, and a new foreman will soon arrive to oversee the machines gutting his ancestral territory. Refusing to watch the earth suffer further excavation, Gann resolves to strike back using the invaders' own technology. By turning their demolitions gear into an instrument of sabotage, he plans to rupture their stronghold from within. Bael Modan's fortress serves as both an excavation base and a fortified garrison, outfitted with soldiers, riflemen, and officers protecting dwarven interests in the Barrens. Gann discovers that the defenders stockpile materials suited for industrial demolition: nitroglycerin, wood pulp, and sodium nitrate. He tasks Horde allies with infiltrating the perimeter to strip these volatile components directly from dwarven ranks, stockpiling enough raw material to assemble a devastating satchel charge.

quest:847.text: Guile of the Raptor. After Tor'gan's orb gave Gor'mul the raptor's essence, the power he felt has him wondering about the shamans' magic. He sends you to tell Tor'gan he has been convinced, for the time being, and will listen. Gor'mul wonders aloud whether the power coursing through him is the shamans' power that Tor'gan tried to show him. He finds it interesting. He asks you to tell Tor'gan that he has been convinced, for the time being, and will hear what Tor'gan has to say.

quest:849.text: Revenge of Gann. Revenge of Gann marks the final strike in Gann Stonespire's vendetta against the dwarves of Bael Modan. Armed with a tailored explosive charge crafted from stolen dwarven plans, an agent of the Horde is tasked with detonating the expedition's prized flying machine to avenge the fallen Stonespire tribe. The Bael Modan excavation is more than an intrusive mining operation; it is an armed fortress planted directly atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. Key to the Prospectors' operational reach and military prowess is their gyrocopter flying machine. Stationed on a watchtower above the dig, the mechanical aircraft surveys the surrounding Barrens, protects supply lines, and acts as a hovering symbol of the Alliance's brazen intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

quest:857.text: The Tear of the Moons. High above the southern Barrens, a crazed dwarf named Feegly the Exiled demands the return of a mysterious relic unearthed at Bael Modan. Known as the Tear of the Moons, the artifact drove Feegly into madness and obsession before General Twinbraid had it locked away as an ill-omened curse. When the dwarves began cutting into the hills of southern Kalimdor to build Bael Modan, the Tear of the Moons was their first major discovery. The strange artifact immediately exerted a powerful and unsettling influence over Feegly, one of the expedition's workers. Feegly claimed the Tear granted him immense personal power, violently turning on his comrades to protect his prize. Recognizing the relic's corrupting influence, General Twinbraid branded it cursed, wrested it from Feegly's clutches, and secured it inside the keep. Banished from the excavation camp, Feegly took refuge among the cliffs, festering in bitter obsession and begging wandering travelers to steal it back.

quest:862.text: Dig Rat Stew. Dig Rat Stew is a culinary task offered by Grub, an orc camping east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. To satisfy a hearty desert appetite, Grub sends hungry adventurers south to the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan to gather a batch of plump dig rats for a dubious pot of stew. Survival in the arid expanse of the Barrens demands an unpretentious palate. While seasoned hunters bring down zhevras, plainstriders, and raptors, the lone orc Grub has developed a peculiar craving for subterranean rodents. Claiming to be famished all day long, Grub promises to share his personal recipe with any traveler willing to do the undignified legwork of rat-catching. The chosen source for these creatures is Bael Modan, the vast Alliance excavation site located deep in the southern Barrens. As dwarven prospectors tear into the red earth, their deep quarrying has inadvertently stirred up nests of prolific dig rats. While the dwarves view the tiny rodents as an infestation, Grub considers the overrunning critters an unmissable feast right under the enemy's nose. Preparing Dig Rat Stew requires a sturdy stomach. According to Grub, the rodents are actually best when allowed to rot for several weeks to draw out their pungent taste. Though he settles for fresher specimens to satisfy a starving adventurer on the spot, his cooking techniques illustrate just how rough-hewn and forgiving roadside cuisine can be on Kalimdor's frontier.

quest:868.text: Egg Hunt. Egg Hunt is a Horde task assigned by the scholar Korran at the Crossroads. Disturbed by the emergence of intelligent, insectoid creatures in the southern Barrens, Korran recruits adventurers to excavate intact silithid eggs from the mounds in the Field of Giants for study in Orgrimmar. Stationed at the dusty crossroads of the central savannah, the troll Korran serves as an observer reporting back to masters in Orgrimmar. While tribal conflicts and Alliance incursions occupy the Horde military, Korran pays attention to strange disturbances across the ecosystem. Chief among these oddities is the emergence of alien, hive-minded insectoids burrowing into the southern reaches of the Barrens. To learn where these insect creatures come from and what drives them, Korran requires biological samples before they mature. Armed with an excavation claw, adventurers head down to the Field of Giants to harvest eggs straight from the silithid dirt mounds. Disturbing these brooding pods triggers frantic defense from the surrounding brood, hinting at the unnatural intelligence and shared will uniting the swarm.

quest:8682.text: Skyseer the Elder. Skyseer the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit residing atop Freewind Post during the Lunar Festival. Travelers seek out his presence high above Thousand Needles to pay their respects to the ancestors and receive his ancient blessing. Perched upon the lofty wooden bluffs of Freewind Post, Elder Skyseer appears bathed in a radiant pillar of celestial light. Positioned near the bridges leading toward the massive mechanical lifts, his ghostly presence offers a quiet sanctuary amid the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles. Elder Skyseer receives visiting adventurers who come to honor the past during the celebration of the Lunar Festival. Beyond acknowledging their homage, the venerable elder can guide travelers toward his kin scattered across Kalimdor, including Elder Morningdew and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8724.text: Morningdew the Elder. Morningdew the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. Illuminated by a radiant beam of starlight, she offers ancient wisdom and directs pilgrims toward other elders scattered across Kalimdor. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their blessings with travelers. Elder Morningdew appears bathed in a shaft of lunar light, standing out starkly against the dusty red stone and noisy industrial hubbub of Thousand Needles. She reminds mortal travelers to look beyond earthly concerns to the starry expanse above. When approached, Morningdew encourages seekers to look toward the countless stars for answers to earthly mysteries. Beyond her contemplative greetings, she serves as a guide for festival pilgrims, sharing knowledge of the locations of other venerated spirits walking the lands, including Elder High Mountain, Elder Grimtotem, Elder Mistwalker, Elder Moonwarden, and Elder Windtotem.

quest:87288.text: Soft Saber Pelts. Soft Saber Pelts represents a trade agreement aimed at keeping wilderness roads secure from predatory cats. Hunters bring in the thick furs of local sabers so they can be crafted into warm, protective blankets and shawls. Traversing the untamed paths of Azeroth requires constant vigilance against prowling predators. Large sabers frequently roam near well-traveled thoroughfares, presenting a persistent hazard to couriers, merchants, and lone adventurers. While local inhabitants admire the grace and majesty of these great cats, allowing their numbers to swell unchecked along trade routes invites deadly ambushes. Gathering hunters to keep the local roads safe serves as a necessary measure for communal survival. Hunting such impressive beasts is not done merely for sport or eradication. In frontier encampments, every resource is valued, and the dense, velvety coats of wild sabers are prized for their warmth and durability. Once brought in by capable hunters, the pelts are tailored into fine shawls and heavy blankets capable of fending off harsh weather, ensuring that nothing taken from the wild goes to waste.

quest:873.text: Isha Awak. Isha Awak is a sacred rite of the hunt issued by the mystic Mahren Skyseer along the Merchant Coast. Brave Horde wanderers are charged with diving into the Great Sea to track down and slay a fearsome aquatic predator known as the Deep Doom. By claiming the beast's heart, the hunter partakes in an ancient bond of spirit and respect. Off the coast south of Ratchet, lurking beneath the waves, roams Isha Awak. Known as the Deep Doom, this immense sea creature commands the coastal waters with formidable strength and predatory solemnity. The human encroachers encamped along the shoreline have learned to dread the waters, having lost many of their scouts and soldiers to the creature's relentless hunger. Unlike the terrified humans ashore, Mahren Skyseer holds deep reverence for the leviathan. To the tauren mystic, Isha Awak is not a curse or simple pest, but a gift: a worthy and honorable foe whose might tests the resolve of true hunters. Slaying the beast is not merely about culling a predator; it is an act of spiritual communion, claiming the heart wherein the beast's essence dwells and carrying its untamed spirit forward.

quest:874.text: Mahren Skyseer. Mahren Skyseer is a Horde journey that directs proven hunters from Camp Taurajo out toward the eastern shores of the Barrens. After mastering the plains' predators, adventurers are sent by Jorn Skyseer to learn coastal tracking from his sister. Finding her requires braving the waters and human encampments dotting the Merchant Coast. Through the trials set by Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, hunters prove their tenacity against the most dangerous beasts stalking the red plains of the southern Barrens. Yet Jorn teaches that a true predator never limits themselves to dry earth and rolling savannas. To truly master the craft, a tracker must be ready to stalk prey through swamps, sheer crags, and the crashing waves of the Great Sea. Jorn's sister, Mahren Skyseer, makes her camp far to the east along the coast. While Jorn studies the spirits of thunderhawks and plains stalkers, Mahren dedicates herself to the elusive creatures dwelling in the salt spray. Traversing the region to find her is perilous, as Kul Tiras marines and Theramore expedition forces maintain fortified outposts and watchtowers across the coastal lowlands.

quest:876.text: Serena Bloodfeather. This bounty task charges Horde adventurers with slaying Serena Bloodfeather, the matriarch driving harpy raids against Crossroads supply lines. Her campaign is a personal blood feud stemming from the Champion of the Horde Rexxar slaying her sister. Putting an end to Serena aims to shatter the coordination behind the harpy flock in the northern Barrens. The Witchwing harpies infesting the crags northwest of the Crossroads do not strike solely out of animalistic hunger. Their leader, Serena Bloodfeather, wages an explicit blood feud against the Horde. Years ago during the founding of Durotar, the wandering beastmaster Rexxar struck down Serena's sister, a notorious matriarch named Bloodfeather. Consumed by hatred for the nascent Horde, Serena has rallied her flock into an organized scourge intent on butchering supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

quest:878.text: Tribes at War. Tribes at War is a Horde quest offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. Trapped behind bars by the tauren, Mangletooth barters critical intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the slaughter of rival Bristleback spiritual leaders. Caged in Camp Taurajo, the Razormane quilboar Mangletooth proves that captivity does not blunt old hatreds. The Barrens has long been contested between two dominant quilboar factions: the Razormane and the Bristleback. While the Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes, Mangletooth offers valuable insight into who is truly tormenting Thork's outpost—provided a champion of the Horde first cuts down the Bristleback's most revered casters. Mangletooth directs adventurers north against the Bristleback's mystical core: their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw raw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. By eliminating their casters, the Horde strikes a crippling blow to Bristleback ritual strength, leaving them vulnerable to Razormane rivals and reducing pressure on nearby trails.

quest:879.text: Betrayal from Within. Betrayal from Within is a task offered by Mangletooth, an imprisoned quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo. Spurned and left for dead by his own kin, Mangletooth seeks bloody vengeance against the trio of Razormane warlords who emerged from Razorfen Kraul to organize assaults across the Barrens. Languishing in captivity beneath the sun at Camp Taurajo, the quilboar Mangletooth harbors no remaining loyalty toward his Razormane kin. Left behind in defeat and facing certain execution, his only surviving ambition is vengeance against the leaders who abandoned him. To achieve this, he offers Horde travelers vital intelligence on the true architects behind the ruthless raids tormenting the plains. While Horde leaders at the Crossroads like Thork struggle to curb the constant quilboar aggression, Mangletooth reveals the core of the problem: three seasoned commanders from deep within Razorfen Kraul. Led by the formidable warrior Lok Orcbane, accompanied by the tracker Nak and the spellcaster Kuz, this trio directs Razormane raiders from encampments far to the south. Mangletooth demands their severed skulls as proof that his betrayers have fallen before his own end arrives.

quest:883.text: Lakota'mani. Lakota'mani is a rite of the hunt initiated by claiming the hoof of Lakota'mani, a massive roaming kodo of the Barrens. Bringing this trophy to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo honors the spirit of the mighty beast and marks the hunter as an equal to its thunderous strength. In the Taur-ahe tongue, Lakota'mani translates to 'Earthshaker.' Among the herds that wander the sun-baked plains of the Barrens, he stands apart—a kodo of tremendous size and endurance whose footsteps echo like gathered thunder. To tauren hunters, tracking and defeating such a creature is not an act of wanton slaughter, but a sacred communion with the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife. Carrying the hoof of the fallen beast to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo brings spiritual closure to the hunt. Jorn recognizes the change immediately, noting a newfound power and stride in any hunter who returns from the encounter. By presenting the trophy, the hunter receives Jorn's blessing, acknowledging that Lakota'mani's enduring courage and primal spirit now walk alongside them.

quest:884.text: Owatanka. Owatanka is a legendary thunder lizard known among the tauren as Bluebolt, roaming the southern plains of the Barrens. Slaying this swift, electrified beast yields a crackling tailspike that carries its bound lightning to the camp elders. Delivering this trophy to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo honors the tradition of learning from the primordial beasts of Kalimdor. Across the arid expanses of the southern Barrens walks Owatanka, a rare thunder lizard spoken of with reverent respect by tauren hunters. While most of his kin are massive and plodding, Owatanka possesses sudden, blinding speed. The tauren name him Bluebolt, marking him as a creature fundamentally altered by the storm. According to lore kept by Jorn Skyseer, Owatanka was struck directly by lightning long ago. Rather than perishing, the thunder lizard absorbed the celestial strike, fueling an endless wellspring of energetic fury. Even in death, the creature's tailspike crackles violently with stray sparks when handled, a tactile remnant of the storm's power. Carrying Owatanka's Tailspike back to Camp Taurajo is treated as a rite of prowess and spirit. Jorn Skyseer recognizes the mark of the encounter immediately in the eyes of any hunter who manages to outmatch the beast's speed. In presenting the trophy, the hunter symbolically draws upon Bluebolt's enduring velocity.

quest:885.text: Washte Pawne. This quest begins upon claiming a quill from Washte Pawne, a rare and revered thunderhawk drifting through the skies of the southern Barrens. Its plumage radiates an unnatural sting, compelling hunters to bring the relic to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. For the tauren, felling this legendary avian is not a simple trophy hunt, but a profound spiritual trial of pain and regret. Thunderhawks are elusive creatures of the Barrens, treated with superstitious reverence by wandering nomadic tribes. Among them, Washte Pawne—translated into the Taurahe tongue as 'Spirit Biter'—holds a distinct and fateful place. Unlike ordinary quarry, its demise is not taken lightly; shamans whisper that striking down such a creature carries omens that teeter dangerously between triumph and misfortune. Those who slay Washte Pawne quickly discover that its dropped feather burns with a piercing, lingering discomfort upon touch. When presented to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the seer reveals that this ache is not physical poison, but the spiritual sting of regret. Taking a magnificent life bears a heavy burden, and the trial asks whether the hunter will succumb to the pangs of remorse or temper that grief into lasting wisdom.

quest:8852.text: Ten Signets for War Supplies. Ten Signets for War Supplies is a logistical exchange coordinated by Warlord Gorchuk in Orgrimmar. Champions of the Horde can trade surplus commendation signets for practical battlefield equipment and supplies. While this trade forfeits official glory and recognition, it directly equips front-line soldiers for the looming conflicts ahead. As the Horde mobilizes its legions for war, gathering supplies is just as vital as assembling warriors. Warlord Gorchuk oversees logistics in the Valley of Spirits, ensuring that crates of weapons, rations, and armor flow toward the front lines. Those who have proven their dedication can surrender commendation signets to draw useful equipment from the army's reserves. Horde Commendation Signets are typically surrendered as proof of service, earning a soldier prestige and renown among the leadership. Exchanging them directly for gear bypasses this formal recognition in favor of raw survival. Gorchuk understands that an extra satchel of supplies or a sturdy weapon can mean the difference between life and death once the clash of armies begins.

quest:889.text: Spirit of the Wind. Spirit of the Wind is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By channeling the residual power within Agamaggan's blood shards, Mangletooth infuses travelers with swiftness to outpace the vast savannas of the Barrens. In the arid sprawl of the Barrens, crossing open territory quickly can mean the difference between survival and falling to predatory beasts or wandering centaur warbands. The captive quilboar Mangletooth, imprisoned within Camp Taurajo, understands the latent power sleeping within the red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. When handed ten of these relics, he draws upon their primeval resonance to bestow the Spirit of the Wind, granting travelers a burst of fleet-footed momentum to outrun the howling drafts of the plains. Quilboar tradition reveres Agamaggan, the Great Boar who shed his blood across central Kalimdor during the ancient War of the Ancients.
